description: Linear A lexicon: one entry per word, logogram or sign group, with its reading, meaning, root, Proto-Semitic root (proto_semitic: the semitic_roots id and form, a list for a compound), cognates, confidence tier and attestations. Readings are di Mino's unless the source field names another scholar.

confidence_levels.CONFIRMED: Ideographic + phonetic + mathematical convergence (e.g., KU-NI-SU next to WHEAT ideogram)
confidence_levels.PROBABLE: Gordon reading with external attestation or strong structural evidence
confidence_levels.CANDIDATE: A close root match or strong contextual support, not yet independently confirmed
confidence_levels.SPECULATIVE: Analogical reconstruction or weak match, included for completeness

entries.meaning: abundance, a counted entry; rival dam 'blood'

cognates.Arabic: ṭamma, of water, 'to abound, rise high' (Lane 1877)

entries.note: ZA 21a: *118-MI 2 closes a quantity list (PI-MU 40, TE 2, PA 5, TA-MA-PI 3); a counted entry favours a commodity. With *118 = ṭa, √ṭ-m-m (#2104): Ar. ṭamma, of water, 'to abound, rise high' (Lane 1877); no case is assigned (Fischer 2002, §140). Rival: dam 'blood', Heb. דָּם (HALOT 224), Ug. dm (DULAT 270), with *118 for plain d. One attestation, two signs. See DA-ME.
entries.source: di Mino; HALOT; DULAT; Fischer 2002; Lane

entries.meaning: commodity ideogram, a Pistacia/terebinth product (resin, mastic or nuts)

cognates.Akkadian: buṭnu 'terebinth' (CAD B 358); buṭuttu A 'pistachio tree, wood, nut' (CAD B 359)
cognates.Hebrew: boṭnîm 'pistachio nuts', among the choice products of the land sent down to Egypt, Gen 43:11 (HALOT 121)

entries.note: HT 123+124b, damaged, has three forms: *188-*308 11, *188 1 and *188-DU 10, quantities with no recoverable relation. *308, pressed oil, also follows OLIV on HT 123+124a. *188 stands with VIN on HT 98b, on the Khania roundels, and as *188-DU-SE on PSI Za 1, a ritual text. buṭnu, a Pistacia product: Heb. boṭnîm 'pistachio nuts' (Gen 43:11; HALOT 121), Akk. buṭnu 'terebinth' (CAD B 358), Arb. buṭm 'terebinth, its fruit' (Lane 219). Ebla writes the word bù-da-ma-tim and GIŠ.EŠ₁₁ = buₓ-du-du 'pistachio' (GlOS 1, 131), and has bu₃-du-du as a name (Pagan 1998, row 1278). Weak point: PA₃-*188 (HT 8b) supports a b-initial reading only with PA₃ as a phonetic complement, and Soldani's derivation of *188 from CH 009 (Ferrara, Montecchi and Valério 2022, 96) fixes neither the commodity nor its name. Twenty-eight attestations.

entries.meaning: terebinth oil, the Pistacia product *188 with *308 'pressed oil'

cognates.Akkadian: buṭnu 'terebinth' (CAD B 358); šamnu 'oil, fat, cream' (CAD Š/1 321)

entries.note: HT 123+124b .1 *188-*308 11, the first entry, before *312 1¾: terebinth oil, *188 buṭnu 'terebinth' (CAD B 358) with *308 šamni 'oil' (CAD Š/1 321), the oil modifier that follows OLIV four times on HT 123+124a. The tablet is damaged, and its preserved quantities do not sum to KU-RO 20, KI-RO 5. See *188 and *308.
entries.source: di Mino; CAD B; CAD Š/1; HALOT; DULAT

entries.meaning: wheat; rivals ḫaṭṭu 'sceptre', ḥaṯ 'unleavened bread'
entries.note: KH 88 QA-NU-MA · *21F-*118 · NI 10, before figs; ZA 5a heads a ration list, *21F-*118 · VIN-SU over KI-NI-MA 7 and O-TA-NI-ZA-SE 6; ZA 14 an entry of 1; ARKH 2 .3–4 ZU-*301 SE-DE *21F-*118 6, ṯannān ṣēd ḥiṭṭa 'the chariot soldiers: provision of wheat', written as one group under SI-DA-TE (GORILA III 6–7). Ug. ḥṭt 'wheat' (DULAT 372), Heb. ḥiṭṭâ (HALOT 306), the final -t unwritten. *21F writes ḥi, as in A-DA-*21F-RI dāhiru. Egyptian group writing does the same with this very word: ʿa=di=na, *ḥiṭṭina 'a variety of wheat', where the a-sign ʿa writes ḥi, not the expected ḥa, and d writes ṭ (P. Anastasi IV 8, 11; Hoch 1994, 85, no. 104). Rivals: ḫṭ 'sceptre, rod' (DULAT 410; Akk. ḫaṭṭu), and ḥṯ 'unleavened bread' (DULAT 373) with *118 = ṯa.

entries.meaning: bridegroom, son-in-law

cognates.Ugaritic: /ḫ-t-n/ 'to become a son-in-law, to marry', with the PN ḫa-at-ni, PRU 3 142 (DULAT 408); ḫtn 'relationship by marriage, wedding' (DULAT 409)
cognates.Akkadian: ḫatānu 'relative by marriage' (CAD Ḫ 148)
cognates.Amorite: ḫatanum 'son-in-law' (Gelb AS 21, 20); names ʾAB-I+ḪATAN (Gelb AS 21 no. 81), ḪATAN+PI+ʾIL (no. 2200)
cognates.Arabic: ḫātana 'he allied himself to him by marriage' (Lane 704)

entries.note: HT 87: *21F-TU-NE · MA-KA-RI-TE · heads six men at one unit each (PI-TA-KE-SI 1 … KU-RU-KU 1, A-RA-[?]-A-TU 1); HT 117b: *21F-TU-NE · over KU-RE-JU 1, DI-KI-SE 1; HT 7b: *21F-TU-NE 1 before DA-RU-*329 2. A rubric or personnel category in all three. √ḫ-t-n 'bridegroom, son-in-law' is pan-Semitic: Akkadian ḫatānu (CAD Ḫ 148), Ugaritic ḫtn (DULAT 408–409), Hebrew ḥātān (HALOT 364–365) and Arabic ḫatan (Lane 703–704). Syllabic controls are Ugaritic {LU₂}ḫa-ta-nu and Neo-Assyrian ḫa-tu₂-nu /ḫatunu/ (WVDOG 152, P514187.11.1), the latter the closest spelling to the Linear A, though much later. ḫa-tu-ne writes /ḫatun-/, final E a dead vowel. Three attestations.

entries.meaning: pastureland, pastoral product (commodity logogram: nawum in administrative register, nawā in ritual/general)

cognates.Akkadian: nawûm 'steppe, uncultivated pastureland' (CAD N/1, 249–51)—administrative land-use category in OB economic texts
cognates.Amorite: nawûm 'steppe; encampment (man and beast)' (Huffmon, APNM 237); nawijum 'nomadic encampment' (Gelb, AS 21)
cognates.Hebrew: nāweh 'habitation, pasture-land' (KB); cultic sense 'shrine, temple' at Exod 15:13 (ʾel nəwēh qodšeḵā 'to Thy holy shrine')

entries.note: A commodity logogram: 242 standalone occurrences on 240 documents, 89% of its 272 uses, concentrated at Haghia Triada on nodules and tablets, 231 of them on HT nodules. It takes the commodity-label slot of GRA (dagān), OLE (šamnu), VIN (wayn) and CYP (cyperus) and names the pastoral class: nawum, with mimation (Mari na-wu-um, GlOS 2, 116), the land-use term for uncultivated pastureland and its goods, livestock, wool and dairy, against cultivated cereals (GRA) and orchard products (OLE, OLIV, VIN). In ritual use the same root gives nawā 'dwelling, abode', compared with Greek ναός 'temple'. The syllabic value na is acrophonic, the first syllable of nawā(n), as cuneiform É bītu 'house' gives bi; the formula verb A-TA-I-*301-WA-JA, from the same √n-w-y, writes *301 where NA would serve. See NU-WI.

entries.meaning: light, radiance (personal name or epithet)

cognates.Amorite: NWR 'shine': janūr, nawarum, Nawar (Gelb AS 21, 28); PN NAWAR-I, written NA-WA-RI (Gelb AS 21 no. 5018)
cognates.Akkadian: namru, older nawru 'bright, shiny, brilliant' (CAD N/1 239)
cognates.Arabic: nawwara, anāra 'it gave light, shone'; nawr 'blossoms' (Lane 2864)

entries.note: HT 115a, an accounting tablet with GRA+BOSm; in erasure on .2 (GORILA I 188–91). √n-w-r 'to shine, give light': Ug. nwr /nāra/, /yanūr-/ 'to be bright, shine' (Huehnergard 2012, 50), nrt 'lamp'; Heb. נוּר nūr, nēr 'lamp'; Ar. nūr. 'Light' is a common name element: Amorite Niwru and ʾAbu-niwra (Gelb 1980, nos. 5026, 162), Ebla nu-ru₁₂-ud 'light' (Pagan 1998, row 3919). Rival: *301 = r, which gives r-u-ra, an awkward reduplication. See NU-RO.

alternative_readings.note: servant, retainer (root n-ʿ-r): Heb. נַעַר naʿar 'lad, servant, retainer'. Suits a tablet listing people and grain just as well.

entries.meaning: fat, tallow (an oil/fat-register commodity)

cognates.Hebrew: peder 'kidney fat, suet', burnt on the altar with the head, wəʾet-happāder, Lev 1:8 (HALOT 914)

entries.note: Commodity ideogram on 38 tablets, regularly among GRA, OLE, OLIV and related commodities, most often before a quantity. pidru 'fat': Central Semitic *pidr- 'fat', Heb. peder 'suet from the kidney' (Lev 1:8; HALOT 914), JArm. pidrā 'fat', Arab. fidra 'piece of meat'. *304+PA is A 629 in SigLA, a sign Schoep separates from A 304 (Schoep 2002, 123). Rival: an agricultural commodity booked between oil and olives, Palmer's pulses or a spice such as cyperus or coriander (Schoep 2002, 123–124).

entries.meaning: administrative heading or transaction marker
entries.note: Three Haghia Triada tablets, each time set off by dividers at the head of a list: HT 35 TI-TI-KU · *326 ·, before I-KU-TA CYP 1 and the oils; HT 91 I-KA · *326 · GRA .3, before *304, the oils, OLIV, NI and VIN at ≈⅙ each; HT 128a opens *326 ·, before PA-RA and the grain entries of TU-RU-NU-SE-ME, WA-TU-MA-RE and MI-TA. After a heading word or opening the tablet, *326 marks the transaction the list records.

entries.meaning: fat (*304) with the PA adjunct, a qualified grade
entries.note: The *304 commodity logogram with a PA adjunct, in seven administrative attestations: a phonetic complement or a commodity qualifier, as in other logogram-plus-sign compounds. SigLA codes the sign A629. GORILA takes it as A 304 + PA; Schoep finds A 629 in other contexts than A 304 (HT 100.1, among signs for groups of people; KH 7b.3, 73.2), beside A 303 and A 316, a qualifier or adjunct (Schoep 2002, 123). PA can write the onset p of pidr, as WA writes the wa- of wayn in VIN+WA. Weak point: its a stands against the i of pidr- (Heb. pädär, suff. pidr-, HALOT 914).

entries.meaning: personnel-category logogram, a counted class of persons
entries.note: A logogram in standalone counted entries, a syllabogram inside sign groups. HT 89 counts *305 23 in the headcount 23+22+24+13+5, KU-RO 87, and on HT 100 *305 5 is a subcategory of the personnel total KU-RO 97 (Uchitel 2003, 85). Uchitel takes it for an age group (Uchitel 2006, 75), Montecchi for a group of persons, never counted in fractions (Montecchi 2008, 315). Ten documents. See KA-*305.

entries.meaning: seed-grain
entries.note: HT 10a .3–4 *305-RU 2½, whole and undotted at the end of .3, the side written over an erasure (GORILA I 21), in the list headed KU-NI-SU 'emmer'. Ug. d/ḏrʕ 'seed-grain' (DULAT 277–278), Heb. zeraʿ, OSArb. ḏrʾ (HALOT 282), the ʿ unwritten. One attestation. See ZE.

entries.meaning: Dawana (personal name)

cognates.Linear B: da-wa-no, a man's name at Knossos, KN As 1517.4, Ga 423 v., Mc 4454.A, Mc 4461.B (DMic I 159)

entries.note: ZA 6a .1 *305-WA-NA *171 19, the first entry of face a, intact and undotted (GORILA III 157). KN Mc 4454.A writes the name the same way, da-wa-no *150 29: name, logogram, number (DMic I 159). *305 writes da, as Linear B d; the -o is the Greek nominative. *171 has no reading. One attestation.

entries.meaning: Wisa (personal name)

cognates.Linear B: wi-so, a woman's name at Knossos, KN Ap 639.4 wi-so MUL 1, in a catalogue of women; wi-sa[, the start of a man's name, PY Cn 328.12, cf. wi-sa-to (DMic II 436)

entries.note: HT 113 .2 WI-SA ·, whole, then a gap and O 2½, a recipient entry (GORILA I 184–185). Linear B writes the same spelling in wi-sa[, a man at Pylos, broken after SA (PY Cn 328.12), and wi-so, a woman at Knossos (KN Ap 639.4; DMic II 436). Cf. Safaitic WS 'to reward' (Harding 1971, 641). One attestation.

entries.meaning: Sleepy (personal name); rival √y-š-š 'aged'

cognates.Linear B: ja-sa-no, KN As 1516.4, which West compares with Ugaritic yšn (DULAT 973)

entries.note: KH 5 .2 WI-SA-SA-NE CYP+E 2, intact, a recipient of cyperus in the section headed A-DA-KI-SI-KA · A-RA-U-DA · (GORILA III 25). wiššān, a qittāl of √w-š-n 'to sleep', as SI-DA-RE Siddāri; SA-SA writes šš as in JA-SA-SA-RA-ME (di Mino, Ya Diktu). Initial w- as in Arabic and Safaitic, where Ugaritic and Hebrew have y-; cf. WI-DI-NA. The Ugarit and Hebrew names take the pattern qatil. Rival: √y-š-š 'aged', the name Yəšîšay (HALOT 447), with no w- in any cognate. One attestation.

entries.meaning: thus, likewise (ditto heading)

cognates.Hebrew: zeh 'this', with Ug. d and Arb. ḏā (HALOT 264)

entries.note: HT 9b .2 KA-*305 ·, unnumbered, below the ruling, over a roster that repeats the names of HT 9a in whole units (KU-RO 24); *305 drawn whole at the edge of worn surface, undotted (GORILA I 19). k 'like, as' (DULAT 415) with the demonstrative ḏā 'this' (Heb. zeh, Ug. d, Arb. ḏā; HALOT 264), as Arb. kaḏā 'like this, thus' (Lane 948): a ditto heading over the repeated roster. The ḏ- demonstrative is a West Semitic innovation. One attestation. See DU.

entries.meaning: gift, offering (votive label)
entries.note: ARKH Zc 8 (FO Zc 1 is the same object), the sole word on an inked object from Arkhanes: a votive label. ʿaṭāye 'gift': Arb. ʿaṭāʾ 'a gift' (Lane 2085), √ʿ-ṭ-w 'to give', with TA for ṭ and the glide of the III-weak noun *ʿaṭāy- written JE. Weak point: the root is attested in Arabic alone. One attestation.

entries.meaning: the ancient, the noble (heading); rival 'became fertile'

cognates.Hebrew: *ʿattîq 'old, ancient', wəhaddəbārîm ʿattîqîm 'and the records are ancient' (1 Chr 4:22; HALOT 903)

entries.note: HT 4: heads a short allocation list (DU-RI-TE 2, PA-RE, TA-PI-SI-DI 1). With *306 = ʿa, NWS √ʿ-t-q 'be old, noble' (Heb. ʿātīq, Arab. ʿatīq), with -A-RE a nominal suffix. Rival: Sabaic ʿtkr 'become fertile (of land)' (Beeston et al. 1982, 14; Ry 522/2), a t-infix stem of √ʿ-k-r, which covers the whole sequence, ʿa-ti-ka-(a)-re for ʿ-t-k-r, and suits a heading over an allocation list. The ʿ-t-q reading leaves -RE unexplained but has the broader NWS pedigree. Weak point: *306 = ʿa is a proposed value, which *306-TU ʿAttu (HT 9a, HT 9b, HT 119, HT 122a) and *306+MI ʿAmmī (HT 115b) also carry. See A-TI-KA.

entries.meaning: pressed oil, oil derivative—commodity modifier indicating oil extraction from base commodity

cognates.Akkadian: šamnu 'oil, fat, cream' (CAD Š/1 321)

entries.note: Oil-derivative modifier, on the tablets of HT, KH and ARKH always among oil and liquid commodities (OLE+X, CYP, VIN); on the metal object HT Zf 167 it stands alone. HT 123+124a sets it after OLIV four times: 8¼ of 31, 8¾ of 31½ and 4¼ of 15 give 26.6–28.3%, and the fraction after OLIV 16, 4 […], is damaged. šamnu 'oil', Akk. šamnu 'oil, fat, cream' (CAD Š/1 321), Heb. šemen (HALOT 1567). Weak point: the commodity function is firmer than the word, and OLE also carries šamnu.

entries.meaning: seal, signet; rivals 'he sealed' (3ms perfective), buṭma 'pistachio'

cognates.Hebrew: ḥôtām 'seal, signet', Judah's ḥōtāmkā, Gen 38:18 (HALOT 300); ḥātam 'to seal' (HALOT 364)
cognates.Egyptian: ḫtm 'seal, signet ring; to close, seal', the source of the Semitic word (HALOT 300)

entries.note: PH Wc 38, a Phaistos roundel (MM II), the sole word on it; TA is dotted (GORILA II 94). With *314 = ḤA, √ḥ-t-m 'to seal, stamp': Heb. ḥōtām (חותם) 'seal, signet ring' (HALOT 300), Arb. ḫatama 'he sealed' (Lane 702); Akk. ḫatāmu means only 'to muzzle, block' (CAD Ḫ 152). Either the noun 'seal', naming the sealing device, or the 3ms perfective 'he sealed', a performative inscription. Egyptian ḫtm 'seal, contract' extends the family. Rivals: Egyptian ḥtm 'provide, supply', which suits a roundel as receipt but lacks the pharyngeal ḥ of *314; with *314 = bu, a PU₂ variant, bṭm 'pistachio' (DULAT 249), Arb. buṭm 'fruit of the terebinth' (Lane 219), Ebla bù-da-ma-tim 'pistachio' (GlOS 1, 131), a roundel commodity, cf. *188 BUṬNU. Weak point: *314 = ḤA is a proposed value, and DU-*314-RE (KO Za 1) writes *314 for PU₂ in dubur, the value that gives the rival buṭm.

entries.meaning: bean or legume; food commodity in ration allocations

cognates.Akkadian: kiššanu, kiššenu 'a leguminous plant' (CAD K 456)

entries.note: Commodity ideogram *316, six occurrences on five documents at Khania and Phaistos. On the nodules KH Wa 1001 and KH Wa 1002 the KI complement (*316+KI) gives the initial syllable /ki/. Akk. kiššanu, a leguminous plant, issued in the Alalakh ration lists (CAD K 456). On KH 91 *316 1 13/20 follows VIN (wine) in a rations list with GRA, NI (figs), *401+RU and *401+RA; on PH 1a it is allocated to named individuals (DI-RA-DI-NA, JA) with CYP. Weak point: the comparison is Akkadian alone.

entries.meaning: commodity logogram counted in whole units; in A542 (HT 89) a personnel-class composite

cognates.Akkadian: leqû, laqû "to take, receive" (CAD L 138); liqtu "collection, gleaning"

entries.note: ARKH 3a counts *317 2 twice, after OLIV 3⅕ and *131B 2 and again beside *312 2, among grain and olive entries; HT 96a has the group *323-*317 1 among SI-MI-TA GRA 5, RU-SA 4 and *323-*344 1; PH 9a has *317-QE-*353 ¼. A commodity sign counted in whole units, and a sign inside groups. On HT 89 it forms the composite JU+*317+QE, A542 in SigLA, a count of 22 among four other human categories in Uchitel's personnel-list analysis (Uchitel 2006). Three attestations. See JU+*317+QE.

entries.meaning: a counted class of men, the composite A542
entries.note: HT 89 JU+*317+QE 22, after *305 23 and before MA-I-MI 24: 22 persons in the total 23+22+24+13+5, KU-RO 87. GORILA decomposes the unit as JU+*317+QE, SigLA catalogs it as the single composite sign A542. One attestation.

entries.meaning: personnel-class logogram, counted beside VIR (men)
entries.note: HT 97a .1–2 *327 33 after VIR+KA 82 under KA-RU · *307+*307 (foot broken, no KU-RO). HT 119 .1 *327 34 beside VIR 68; the entries sum to 159 with *327 against KU-RO 160, so it counts persons (Montecchi 2008, 317: summed with VIR/MUL). Cf. *327-JU 8 (HT 119 .4–5), 'forse un gruppo sillabico' (Montecchi 2008, 318). A closed rectangle, left upright projecting, crossing interior strokes (GORILA I 159, 203); what it depicts is not determinable. No Linear B counterpart (Montecchi 2024, 172). No sound value.
entries.source: HT97a; HT119; GORILA I 159, 203; Montecchi 2008, 317–18; Montecchi 2024, 172

entries.meaning: aromatic preparation, compounded ointment—commodity ideogram for perfumed/refined oil products

cognates.Akkadian: ruqqû 'to prepare perfume'; ruqqû adj. 'perfumed (oil)' (CAD R 420); raqqû 'oil presser, perfume maker' (CAD R 173)
cognates.Ugaritic: rqḥ 'perfumer, druggist', in šmn rqḥ 'perfumer's oil', KTU 4.91:5 (DULAT 734); rqḥ 'perfume, ointment' (DULAT 735)
cognates.Hebrew: rōqaḥ 'mixture of ointments'; reqaḥ 'spice mixture' (HALOT 1290); šemen mišḥat-qōdeš rōqaḥ, Exod 30:25
cognates.Phoenician: rqḥ 'ointment mixer, perfumer'; rqḥ 'ointment, perfume, spice' (Krahmalkov 447)

entries.note: A commodity ideogram with three riders and a compound: +RU on seven documents (KH 12 twice, KH 63, KH 83, KH 84, KH 85, KH 91, KN Zg 57a), +RO on KH 31 and KN Zg 57a (twice), +RA on KH 91 and MI 2, and +*304 on HT 33, KH 12 and KN Zg 57a. KH 91 writes +RU beside +RA and KN Zg 57a +RU beside +RO, so they are distinct products. √r-q-ḥ 'mix aromatics, compound ointment': Akk. ruqqû 'perfumed (oil)' (CAD R 420); Heb. rōqēaḥ 'perfumer' (BDB 955), riqqūḥîm 'perfumes' (Isa 57:9); Ug. rqḥ 'perfumer' (DULAT 734). +RU names refined oil by the ru- of ruqqû, +RO compounded ointment by the rō- of rōqaḥ (HALOT 1290), and +*304 (pidru) a fat-based aromatic. The ideogram keeps company with CYP (cyperus), OLE, *308 (šamnu) and *304, the aromatic and oil register, and its fractions (¹⁄₅, ¹⁄₁₆) suit a concentrate. Nine of its twelve documents are from Khania, as Mycenaean perfumery centred on Pylos (PY Un 267). +RA writes the ra- of raqḥ 'spice mixture' (Heb. reqaḥ, HALOT 1290), as on VIN+RA. Weak point: both +RA witnesses, KH 91 and MI 2, break off after the rider. See RO-QA.

entries.meaning: cup, drinking vessel—commodity ideogram for a specific vessel type, with KE phonetic complement indicating initial syllable of Semitic *kaʾs-

cognates.Akkadian: kāsu 'goblet, cup; cup as measure' (CAD K 253)

entries.note: HT 26 (Haghia Triada, Villa Magazine, LM IB): a vessel ideogram with the phonetic complement KE, heading both faces. *406VAS draws a vessel and is a compound or ligature component, and KE narrows it to one type, as Linear B vessel ideograms take phonetic complements. Akk. kāsu, Heb. kōs, Arab. kaʾs, Ebla ga-sa-a-tum kāsāt 'cups' (GlOS 1, 322): KE writes its first syllable, E for a. KA-SI (skeleton k-s) on HT Wa 1027, a nodule from the same site, is a candidate for the word in syllables. HT 93a has the bare *406-VS beside DA-RI-DA with quantity 2, a vessel-class commodity sign on a second tablet. HT 26b opens with *406VAS+KE, then VIR+[?] 9 and named allocations (RO-NI 3, KA-U-ZU-NI 4, KI+MU 12): personnel and commodities distributed by vessel type. Weak point: KE writes the a of kās with E.

entries.meaning: large open bowl or basin for liquids; wine bowl

cognates.Akkadian: agannu 'a large bowl' (CAD A/1 142)
cognates.Hebrew: ʾaggān 'large bowl'; Moses puts half the blood bāʾaggānōt 'in the basins', Exod 24:6 (HALOT 11)

entries.note: Commodity logogram: *412+E three times on MA 10, TI+*412VAS once (MA 10b), *412-VS-VIN once (PH 9b); VIN on PH 9b marks a wine vessel. Akk. agannu 'basin', Heb. ʔaggān (Exod 24:6, Song 7:3, Isa 22:24), Arb. ʔiggānat-, syllabic a-ga-nu at Qatna and Amarna (GlOS 1, 12): a larger basin than *406VAS kās 'cup'. The complement E writes /ʔē-/: Arabic keeps the i-class vowel, Northwest Semitic lowers it to ē, ʔēgān, and the aleph is unwritten. TI+*412VAS is a subtype, TI for ṭīn- 'clay bowl'. See A-KA-NU.

entries.meaning: account, register (šipru), a transaction logogram

cognates.Ugaritic: spr (II) 'tablet, register, list, inventory; in accounting, record of tribute' (DULAT 756); spr (III) 'number, inventory' (DULAT 757)

entries.note: An administrative logogram, a transaction sign on HT 118 (SigLA). Ten occurrences at Haghia Triada, Khania and Zakros: nine stand alone, several head quantified entries, and two are on sealed Khania roundels. SI-*516 reads as an s-onset phonetic complement, the ground for Ugaritic spr 'tablet, register' and Heb. sēper/sōpēr. Weak point: no full phonetic spelling is attested.

entries.meaning: Addu/Haddu (heading); rival adû 'work stint'

cognates.Ugaritic: hd(d) 'Haddu (Hadad), storm god, byname of Baal'
cognates.Akkadian: Adad (OB Addu) 'storm god'; adû 'a (day's) work, stint'
cognates.Amorite: Haddu/Addu as a divine name and theophoric element (Huffmon; Howard)
cognates.Hebrew: Hădad (הֲדַד) 'Hadad' in names: Ben-Hadad, Hadadezer 'Hadad is help'

entries.note: A-DU occurs in 8 documents at two sites, regularly in initial or heading position: a heading or an entity. Gordon's Addu/Haddu (Gordon 1966 §129): the spelling fits Old Babylonian Amorite and Akkadian Addu without initial h, and second-millennium syllabic forms such as eḫ-li-a-du keep the divine element (Howard 2023, 5). Ebla has ʾa₃-du, the DN Ḫaddu as a personal name (Pagan 1998, row 27). HT 92 places A-DU between TE and the commodities, the slot of a named recipient such as Addu. Rival: Akk. adû 'work quota per man-day, work assignment' (CAD A/1 135), which fits allocation and roster contexts. HT 95b sets A-DU over the items HT 86a divides between A-KA-RU and A-DU. Weak point: one reading must serve all eight headings, and only HT 85a, with *307+*307, selects the god. See A-DU *307+*307, A-DU-NI-TA-NA and A-DU-KU-MI-NA.
entries.source: di Mino; Gordon 1966; Howard 2023; Pagan 1998; CAD A/1

entries.meaning: Addu's sanctuary (Storm God + doubled sanctuary sign)

cognates.Akkadian: Addu (= Adad) 'storm god'

entries.note: HT 85a .1 A-DU · *307+*307 · VIR+[?] ·, heading a personnel register of 66 workers. The middle sign is *307 written twice, joined by a top bar (A 638; GORILA I 131), as Montecchi also reads A 638 (2008, 316 n. 30). KA-RU · *307+*307 · VIR+KA heads HT 97a. The entry keeps the attested phrase whole: the theonym A-DU with the doubled *307. See DU-PU₂-RE.

entries.meaning: the one of Addu's cella (cult title as a roster name)

cognates.Akkadian: kummu A 'cella, private room (of a temple)'; zamār kummi ana Adad 'a cella-song for Adad' (CT 15 3 i 3, OB); Ištar of Agade adi kummiša 'with her cella', its personnel (Maqlû II 195) (CAD K 533–534)
cognates.Ugaritic: kbm 'a cult installation', set beside Akk. kummu (DULAT 423)

entries.note: ZA 10a: a roster entry counted 1, beside A-KU-MI-NA. A-DU Addu + KU-MI kummi 'cella', as in SI-DU-QI-KU-MI Ṣiduqi-kummi, god first + -NA, the gentilic -ān of KI-RE-TA-NA Kretan: 'the one of Addu's cella'. Akkadian sings a cella-song for Adad (CT 15 3 i 3) and once sends Ištar 'with her cella', its staff (Maqlû II 195). Weak point: kummu names personnel only there. Rivals: A-DU + √k-m-n 'Addu has sheltered' (#3237), Amorite Ka-mi-nu-um (Gelb 1980, no. 3970); A-DU + KU-MI-NA 'cumin', which is measured (MY Ge 605 ku-mi-no Z 2), where this entry is counted 1.
entries.source: di Mino; CAD K; DULAT; Gelb 1980

entries.meaning: given by Addu (compound theophoric PN)

cognates.Akkadian: nadānu N innadin 'was given'; active names Adad-iddinam, Bēl-ittannu
cognates.Amorite: yantin-DN 'DN gave' (active prefix conjugation; Gelb AS 21)

entries.note: ARKH 5 A-DU-NI-TA-NA 41, before A-DA-RO GRA 40 and *131B 6: a named recipient and its quantity, in the Arkhanes ration format of ARKH 2 and ARKH 3a, which also list *131B must. A-DU, Addu the storm god, + NI-TA-NA nittāna, N-stem perfect of √n-t-n 'to give', from *nintan: 'given by Addu'. Both elements stand elsewhere: A-DU heads the HT 88 register and detaches as a theophoric prefix on ZA 10a (A-DU-KU-MI-NA beside A-KU-MI-NA), and √n-t-n underlies NA-TU-*301-NE (SKO Zc 1). Names of god and verb: Akk. Adad-iddinam and Iddin-Dagan, of the type DN-iddin(am) (CAD N/1 49), Mari Yantin-Addu (ARM 26/1, 602), Amorite Yantin-Haddu (Gelb 1980, nos. 2990, 2992). Weak point: West Semitic Adda-natan (SAA 14 014) has the G perfect natan, which the NI- spelling does not fit. One attestation.

entries.meaning: 'the Living One', title of the Goddess (√ḥ-y-y)
entries.cognates: Hebrew חַי ḥay "alive", חַיִּים ḥayyīm "life"; Ugaritic ḥyw "to live"; Mari West Semitic ḥaya "lives" is written both ha-ia- and a-ia-; Late Old Babylonian Alalakh likewise alternates ha-ia- and a-ia- in the same name (Weeden 2009, 96–100). The Mesopotamian god Haya is written dḫa-ià; Aya is an independently attested goddess.
entries.note: PE Zc 4 A-JA ≈ JA-SI, inked, and SY Za 2, the last group of the formula, after U-NA-KA-NA-SI-OLE; MA 4b A-[?]-[?]-[?]-JA is a longer word. A for ḥ has its control at Old Babylonian Mari, where West Semitic ḥaya 'lives' is written both ha-ia- and a-ia-, and at Alalakh VII, where a-ia- and ha-ia- alternate in one name, a-ia- on Weeden's account reproducing an unrepresented /ḥ/ (Weeden 2009, 96–100). /ḥayyā/ 'the Living One', as Amorite Ḥajja, a divine name (Gelb 1980, 19), in Milki-Ḥayya (Gelb 1980, no. 4724). Rivals: the god Haya, dḫa-ià from Early Dynastic Fara on, whom the Old Babylonian Hymn to Haia for Rim-Sin calls the god who loves the petition 'Give me life!' (line 59; ORACC AMGG, 'Haya'; ETCSL 2.6.9.2.59); the goddess Aya; Davis's 'much', modifying the oil (Davis 2013, 41). Two attestations.

entries.meaning: Ḥayyu 'Living' (personal name)

cognates.Ugaritic: ḥy (III) PN, syll. fḫé-ia-PI, bn ḥy (KTU 4.366:4); ḥy (I) 'alive' (DULAT 376)
cognates.Amorite: ḤAJJ-UM, ḪA-IU-UM (Gelb 1980, no. 2044)

entries.note: HT Zd 155, a graffito on stucco: A-JU · NA-MA-MA-TI-TI-A319, A-JU whole and undotted before the divider (GORILA IV 131), where HT Zd 157 has a single stroke before its divider; NA-MA holds WI-JA-SU's slot before MA-TI-TI-A319. A writes ḥa, JU yu: Ḥayyu, the masculine of A-JA ḥayyā, as the Ugaritic name ḥy (DULAT 376) and Amorite ḤAJJ-UM (Gelb 1980, no. 2044). One attestation. Cf. A-JA.

entries.meaning: island
entries.note: THE Zb 7, a clay vessel from Thera: the sole word on it, inscribed on an island, a label of origin or dedication. A dialect form of I-JA /ʾiya/ (Knossos) and I-JA-TE /ʾiyyate/ (Phaistos): A-JE at Thera against I-JA at East Cretan sites is regional vowel variation, as the libation formulae differ between Phaistos and East Crete. Ug. ỉht 'islands, coastal region' (DULAT 31). One attestation.

entries.meaning: cup, bowl

cognates.Akkadian: agannu 'a large bowl' (CAD A/1 142)

entries.note: Hebrew/Aramaic ʾaggān 'bowl'; Qatna and Amarna write a-ga-nu (GlOS 1, 12). Rendsburg sets a-ka-nu beside Heb. ʾaggān, Ph. and Aram. ʾgn, Akk. agannu 'bowl' (2026, 204). Gordon 1966 §119: 'opens with the word a-ka-nu = Hebrew and Aramaic ʾaggan bowl, which happens to be applied specifically to a magic bowl in an Aramaic incantation.' Self-referential vessel label: the bowl names itself. GORILA writes A-KA-NU-ZA-TI as one sign group, but Gordon segments A-KA-NU as a standalone noun. GORILA IV 125 begins the transcription with A-KA-NU-ZA-TI and marks no lacuna before it. The following ZA-TI is /zāt/ 'this' (older *zāʾt), giving ʾagānu zāt 'this bowl.' Cf. Hebrew zōʾt. Phoenician ʾGN is feminine, as zāt requires, and FK D 35 has the postposed demonstrative construction hʾgn hz, 'this bowl' (Krahmalkov 2000, 31). A Sarepta jug handle in Ugaritic script reads agn z pʿl yd[--] 'this bowl PN made' (KTU 6.70 1; Rendsburg 2026, 204), and Egypt lists *ʾaguna among Syrian tribute, written a-ku-nu at Amarna (Hoch 1994, 42–43 no. 36). Rival: one word, a verb of √k-n-s, which is written KA-NA-SI everywhere else. TI's vowel is dead, as the final TI of MA-TI-TI. Weak point: ZA-TI is a hapax, its first sign is disputed ZA/ZE. See *412.

entries.meaning: field, estate (heading); rival the Ugaritic god Ugaru

cognates.Ugaritic: ugr 'field, soil' (DULAT); DN Ugaru, paired with Gapnu as gpn-w-ugr 'Vine and Field'
cognates.Akkadian: ugāru 'open field, meadow, arable land'

entries.note: Linear A writes A-KA-RU, hence Agaru; Ugaritic supplies Ugaru (ugr II), 'Field,' paired with Gapnu ('Vine') as one of Baal's two messenger-deities (DULAT 27; KTU 1.3; 1.5). A-KA-RU heads accounts at HT 2 and HT 86a/b as a field or estate heading. Rival: a divine or cult-institutional sense, since on HT 86a its section stands beside one headed A-DU (Addu). Initial a/u: the Aegean field word is a-initial, Myc. a-ko-ro, Grk. ἀγρός, which Rendsburg sets beside Ug. ugr and Akk. ugāru as one IE–Semitic lexeme (2026, 205). Rival with initial a: ʾ-g-r 'hire', Ebla a-gàr-du, Ugarit a-ga-ru-ta 'hire contract' (GlOS 1, 12–13). Akk. ugāru is a Sumerian loan, attested at Ras Shamra and Emar (CAD U/W 27); in Old Babylonian it names an administrative unit of fields with its own overseer, UGULA A.GÀR (CAD U/W 29). See U-KA-RE.

entries.meaning: axe(s), weighed in *118 units; Wanderwort, Hittite kullupi; rivals: a personal name, *kVlūb- 'basket'

cognates.Akkadian: kalappu 'axe', counted by weight: ka-la-pu ša 2 GÍN 'an axe of two shekels' (CAD K 66)
cognates.Hittite: kullupi 'a kind of hoe', ᵁᴿᵁᴰᵁ (KBo 3.33 II 10′; KUB 7.41 obv. 5)

entries.note: PA 1: A-KU-JU-PA-*118 35, the tablet's only entry (GORILA I 284). *118 closes the group before the numeral, as in SI+ME-KI-*118 1¾ and *539-*118 1 on HT 24b, where it takes fractions; Linear B writes the talent with *118. KU-JU writes kul, as in I-KU-JU-TI ʾukulti (ZA 6b), SU-JU-TA sulta (KN 22a) and ZU-JU-PU₂ ṯulpu (HT 25a). Hittite ᵁᴿᵁᴰᵁkullupi, a copper hoe or axe (KBo 3.33 II 10′; KUB 7.41 obv. 5), and Aramaic kulbā share the kul-; Akk. kalappu has kal-. Rabin 1963, 124f. (cited by HALOT 472) derives the word from the Hittite. A Wanderwort of the metal trade. One attestation.
entries.source: di Mino; CAD K; HALOT; CAL; TLHdig

entries.meaning: the one of the cella (cult title as a roster name)

cognates.Akkadian: kummu A 'cella, private room (of a temple)' (CAD K 533)
cognates.Ugaritic: kbm 'a cult installation', set beside Akk. kummu (DULAT 423)

entries.note: ZA 10a: a roster entry counted 1, beside A-DU-KU-MI-NA. The article ha- written A- (as A-TU-RI-SI-TI ha-Turisīt) + KU-MI kummi 'cella' + -NA, the gentilic -ān of KI-RE-TA-NA: 'the one of the cella', the title A-DU-KU-MI-NA ties to Addu. Rivals: ʾa- + √k-m-n 'I shelter' (#3237), Amorite Ia-ak-me-ni (Gelb 1980, no. 2909); A- + KU-MI-NA 'cumin', which is measured (MY Ge 605 ku-mi-no Z 2), where this entry is counted 1. One attestation.
entries.source: di Mino; CAD K; DULAT; Gelb 1980

entries.meaning: people, kinfolk—social/kinship term
entries.cognates: Hebrew ʿam "people, nation" (HALOT 837), Ugaritic ʿm "lineage, ancestors" (DULAT 160), Akkadian ummānu "people, army" (CAD U/W 106), Phoenician ʿm "people" (Tomback 255)
entries.note: HS Zg 1, a stone object, has A-MA alone; MA 1b has A-MA · *47 over QE-DE-MI-NU; ZA 7b has A-MA, the rest broken. Three attestations, at three sites. ʿamma 'people, kinfolk': Heb. ʿam 'paternal uncle; kin, clan; people' (HALOT 837). On MA 1b, A-MA stands beside QE-DE-MI-NU (Qēdmīnu 'primordial, eastern', cf. Kadmos), a kinship term beside a Semitic personal name, as in the NWS names ʿAmminadab (Exod 6:23; Num 1:7; HALOT 844) and ʿAmmišadday (Num 1:12). Ebla has the name a-ma ʿamma 'the uncle' (Pagan 1998, row 672). Plain A writes the ʿ, as in A-MA-JA ʿAmmaya and A-PA₃-DI ʿAbdī; *306+MI writes the same name element with *306. Rivals: ʾammat- 'cubit' and ʾam(a)t- 'maidservant', on the same two consonants. See *306+MI.

entries.meaning: handmaid (of the goddess)

cognates.Akkadian: amtu 'slave woman, handmaid'

entries.note: ZA 10b: A-MI-TA 3 in a quantified list of names. Ug. àmt /ʾamatu/ 'woman slave, handmaid' (Huehnergard 2012, 41), as in amt aṯrt 'handmaid of Asherah' (Gordon 1966b, 91); Akk. amtu, Heb. ʾāmāh. Mari names the same formation: ʾAmat-ʿAštar-an and ʾAmat-Labwa, 'handmaid of Ashtart' and 'of the Lioness' (Gelb 1980, nos. 782–783).

entries.meaning: grace, favor

cognates.Akkadian: unnīnu 'prayer, supplication'

entries.note: KN Zc 7, an inked vessel: GORILA prints JA-SA-RA-A-NA-NE as one group; read JA-SA-RA · A-NA-NE. ḥanān 'grace, favour', the qatāl pattern of the geminate root, A- writing ḥa with the guttural unwritten: Amorite Ḥanana (Gelb 1980, no. 475), ḥanan 'gracious' (GlOS 1, 245). With JA-SA-RA, yašara ḥanān 'righteous is (thy) grace'. See A-NA-NU.

entries.meaning: the crosser, the one from beyond (√ʿ-b-r, the ʿApiru word); rival 'creator' (√b-r-ʾ)

cognates.Hebrew: ʿābar (עָבַר) 'to cross over' → ʿibrī (עִבְרִי) 'Hebrew'; bārāʾ (בָּרָא) 'he created' (Gen 1:1)
cognates.Akkadian: ebēru 'to cross over'

entries.note: HT 96a and b (Scribe 8, Casa Room 7, LM IB). HT 96b heads a major allocation: QA-*118-RA-RE qaṭara 'incense', *516 SIPRU, GRA 40¾, OLE+U 4, NI 2. The short form PA-RA-NE stands on HT 115a and b, by the same scribe. ʿabrāne, √ʿ-b-r with agentive -āne, 'the crosser, the one from beyond', as ʿibrī 'Hebrew', PA writing b. Amorite Ḥa-pí-ra-an, of the element ḤPR ḥapir-, *ʿapir-, the ʿApiru/Ḥabiru word (Huffmon 1965, 36, 202), matches A-PA-RA-NE with initial A for ʿa and -ān, cuneiform ḫ writing ʿ; so ḪABIR-AN (Gelb 1980, no. 1997). AP-RA-AN (Gelb 1980, no. 863) is a separate name, ʾApran, since cuneiform AP- writes ʾ and ʿ alike. Borger derives ʿapīru from ʿ-p-r 'dust' (apud Huffmon 1965, 202); PA writes p and b alike. Rival: √b-r-ʾ with -āne, 'creator', the aleph unwritten.

entries.meaning: personal name, ʿAbdī 'my servant'; rival the head of an ʿAbdi-DN name

cognates.Ugaritic: ʕbd (I) 'servant, slave' (DULAT 136); ʕbdy PN, syll. ÌR-ya (DULAT 141)

entries.note: PK Zb 26, a pithos sherd written retrograde, A-PA₃-DI[ broken after DI (Younger, Linear A Texts). ʿAbdī, as the Ugaritic PN ʿbdy, syll. ÌR-ya (DULAT 141), or the head of an ʿAbdi-DN name, as ʿbdyrḫ (DULAT 141) and Amarna ÌR-a-ši-ir-ta (EA 71:17). Amorite ḫa-ab-di-ia ʿabdiya at Tuttul (Buck 2018, 328). One witness.

entries.meaning: personal name; Ugaritic ålnr (Hurrian), Linear B a-ra-na-ro

cognates.Hurrian: Allanšeridanu, {1}al-la-an-še-ri-da-ni, a man at Ugarit, RS 16.251:5 (Kinlaw 1967, 19)
cognates.Linear B: a-ra-na-ro, a man on the Knossos roster KN As(2) 1516

entries.note: HT 1 A-RA-NA-RE 105, the last of the counted names, whole (GORILA I 3). Ugaritic ålnr, a personal name classed Hurrian and set beside Linear B a-ra-na-ro (DULAT 57); first element allai 'the Lady' (Laroche, GLH 42–43), as in Allan-šeridani at Ugarit (Kinlaw 1967, 19). Hurrian r and l alternate; RA writes r here, as the same scribe writes RA₂ for la in QE-RA₂-U. Linear B a-ra-na-ro is a man, VIR 1, on KN As 1516.11. HT 47b ]RA-NA-RE[, room for one sign before (GORILA I 91), is the same name if the lost sign is A. Rival: Gordon's Egyptian ꜥꜣ-rn-Rꜥ 'Great-is-the-name-of-Re' (Gordon 1966 §127).
entries.source: di Mino; DULAT 57; Laroche 1980; KN As 1516.11; Gordon 1966 §127

entries.meaning: earth (feminine noun—PS *ʾar(V)ṣ̂- "earth")

cognates.Akkadian: erṣetu(m) "earth, land, ground"—standard citation form erṣetum carries feminine mimation, supporting ʾarṣ̂atum as regular East-Semitic-style case marking

entries.note: ZA 7a, a Zakros allocation tablet: A-RA-TU 4, beside A-RE-TU-MI, which words or a number may have followed, ʾarṣ̂-ummī 'Earth is my mother'. ʾarṣ̂atu 'earth', PS *ʾar(V)ṣ̂-, -TU the feminine -at(u); the emphatic lateral ṣ̂ is unwritten, as in A-RE-TU-MI. A-RA-TU keeps the a of the absolute state, and A-RE-TU-MI reduces it to e in the construct before -ummī: the noun and the theophoric name stand on one tablet. A-RA-TU-ME, a hapax heading on the roundel HT Wc 3024, is ʾarṣ̂atum with mimation, as Akkadian erṣetum. Mimation marks the nonbound singular in both genders in Proto-Semitic, *ṭāb-at-u-m beside *ṭāb-u-m (Huehnergard 2019, 59–60, Table 3.7), and in Amorite, a-še-ra-tum, ḫa-na-tum, ni-iḫ-ma-tam, where it is 'common but apparently optional' (George and Krebernik 2022, 131). Minoan writes it on three masculine singulars, RI-SU-MA, MA-RU-ME and JA-SA-SA-RA-ME, against more than 200 without, so at that rate the eight other feminine -at common nouns are expected bare.

entries.meaning: earth (feminine noun with mimation—cf. Akk. erṣetum)

cognates.Akkadian: erṣetum "earth, land, ground"—standard fem. citation form with mimation (ORACC freq. 62)

entries.note: Hapax heading on the roundel HT Wc 3024. Mimated form of A-RA-TU (ZA 7a). Feminine mimation is the Proto-Semitic nonbound singular, *ṭāb-at-u-m (Huehnergard 2019, 59–60, Table 3.7), kept in Akk. erṣetum 'earth' (CAD E 308), Amorite a-še-ra-tum and ḫa-na-tum (George and Krebernik 2022, 131), and the names Ḥananatum, Ḥayyatum (Gelb 1980, nos. 477, 1809). The corpus's only feminine with mimation; masculine singulars take it rarely too (RI-SU-MA, MA-RU-ME). A roundel is a sealed receipt, and its heading names the item in citation form, where mimation stands. See A-RE-TU-MI.
entries.source: di Mino; Huehnergard 2019; CAD E; George and Krebernik 2022; Gelb 1980

entries.meaning: Earth is my mother (NWS theophoric compound PN; pre-Greek Artemis)

cognates.Ugaritic: ʾarṣ 'earth'; ủm 'mother' (DULAT 67); X-ummī name Anati-umme, RS 14.16:7 (Kinlaw 1967, 24)
cognates.Akkadian: erṣetu 'earth'; ummu 'mother'
cognates.Greek: Ἄρτεμις (Artemis)—widely agreed pre-Greek; no convincing Greek etymology
cognates.Lydian: Artimuś (dat. artimuλ)—u after the m, not in TU's slot; Aramaic (Letoon) ʾrtmwš likewise
cognates.Linear B: a-te-mi-to (PY Es 650, genitive)—drops pre-consonantal /r/ per standard LB orthography
cognates.Etruscan: Artumes (oldest), Artam[e]s, Aritimi, gen. Artmsl (Nielsen & Rathje 2009: 261–262)—u before the m, as in TU-MI; Cristofani's cited Aretume unverified

entries.note: ZA 7a: U-JU 5, A-RA-TU 4, A-RE-TU-MI; MI opens line 3, which runs on into the break, so words or a number may have followed it. ʾarṣ̂-ummī 'Earth is my mother': √ʾ-r-ṣ̂ 'earth', Heb. ʾereṣ, Ug. arṣ, Akk. erṣetu (HALOT 90), with ʾummī 'my mother', its glottal elided in sandhi. TU writes ṣu, as TE writes ṣe in TA-NA-RA-TE-U-TI-NU, and MI writes mmī, the geminate unmarked. Cf. the sentence names Mari Eštar-ummī (ARM 23 610:7) and Ugaritic Anati-umme (RS 14.16:7). Cf. Artemis, LB a-te-mi-to and a-ti-mi-te, Greek Ἄρτεμις and West Greek Ἄρταμις, a scatter Beekes explains as adaptation from an a/i/u vowel system (Beekes 2014, 8, 25). RE has the e of Akk. erṣetu and Heb. ʾereṣ (#768), where A-RA-TU on the same tablet writes A-RA-. Weak point: the tablet breaks after MI, so the word can run on. One attestation. See A-RA-TU-ME.

entries.meaning: healer, of the Rephaim (√r-p-ʾ); rival ʿarpa 'clouds' (√ʿ-r-p)
entries.note: PE 2, in a list of fractional entries: A-RI-PA ¼, after A-*325-ZA ¼ and before QA-QA-DA ½. ʾaripāʾ, √r-p-ʾ 'to heal': Ug. rpum, the Rephaim, ancestral healers and shades (KTU 1.20–22; DULAT 731), Amorite Rapiʾum (Gelb 1980, no. 5238), r-p-ʾ names at Mari and Alalakh (GlOS 2, 168). Rival: Ug. ʿrpt 'clouds', from rkb ʿrpt 'Rider of Clouds', Baal's epithet (Ps 68:5), with the ʿ unwritten. One attestation. See RP-33-Y and A-RE-PI-RE-NA.

entries.meaning: Eshmun (healing deity)

cognates.Phoenician: ʾšmn ʾEšmūn, god of Sidon and of healing: bt lʾšmn 'a temple for Eshmun' (KAI 14:16–17; KAI 15–16); ʾšmn mʾrḥ 'Eshmun the Host', who healed the dedicant (KAI 66:1–2) (Krahmalkov 2000, 82–84)
cognates.Punic: ʾšmn in names from Sidon, Cyprus, Sardinia, Carthage, Spain and Italy: ʾšmnytn 'Eshmun has given', ʾšmnʿzr 'Eshmun, help!', ʾšmnʾdn 'Eshmun is lord', ʿbdʾšmn 'servant of Eshmun' (Benz 1972, 70–73, 278–279)
cognates.Ugaritic: šmn (III) DN Šamnu, the noun 'oil' as a god's name, two birds l šmn 'for Šamnu' (KTU 1.164:9; Pardee 2002, 75, 283), the later Eshmun (DULAT 817)
cognates.Akkadian: ᵈIa-su-mu-nu beside ᵈMi-il-qar-tu in Esarhaddon's treaty with Baal of Tyre (SAA 2 5 r. iv 14′); ᵈIa-su-mu-na (SAA 2 2 r. vi 22); /ʾAsmūn/ (Krahmalkov 2000, 82)

entries.note: ZA Zb 3 (Zakros, LM IB), with VIN 32, an offering context. The skeleton (ʾ)-š-m-n is Eshmun, the Sidonian healing god, Ph. ʾšmn; the initial a is archaic, ʾAšmūn, as Assyrian ᵈIa-su-mu-nu keeps it (SAA 2 5 r. iv 14′; Krahmalkov 2000, 82). The name is šmn 'oil': Ugarit already has the god as šmn Šamnu, the noun as a name (Pardee 2002, 283), the later Eshmun (DULAT 817). Eshmun is a Phoenician god carried abroad from his cult centre at Sidon, and theophoric names are common in Linear A accounts. Rivals: šamnu 'oil, fat' as a commodity; *ṯamāniy- 'eight', Eshmun as the eighth son of Sadykos (Brown 1995, 36); Woudhuizen's Akkadian assammû 'a large drinking vessel' (2016, 229–230; CAD A/2 339–340), the pithos's own name. PK Za 12 A-NE is damaged between A and NE, with no sign loss established; a restoration there favours A-[KO-A]-NE (PK Za 11) over A-[SA-MU]-NE. One attestation. See OLE and *308.
entries.phonological_notes: Initial A- = laryngeal (ʾ). SA = /šV/ under sibilant neutralization. MU = /mū/ (long vowel). NE = /n/ with dead vowel. Archaic /a/-vocalism preserved in Linear A spelling.

entries.meaning: locked house, work-house (of the sanctuary), heading its personnel classes; rivals ʾasīr- 'captives', aššum šarra 'concerning the queen'

cognates.Eblaite: ʔa₅-za-ru₁₂ ʔas(ā)r 'locked house (for female weavers)' (GlOS 1, 46, after ARET 12 517)
cognates.Alalakh: LÚ.MEŠ asirū, bonded household staff in the grain-delivery lists of Alalakh VII (Niedorf 2008, 80 n. 305, after Zeeb 2001, 235–41)
cognates.Ugaritic: åsr 'prisoner, captive', pl. åsrm (KTU 4.382:6; 2.31:24; DULAT 111); RS Akk. LÚ a-sí-ru
cognates.Akkadian: asīru 'prisoner of war, captive used as worker' (OB administrative and western texts, Mari to Boğazköy); bīt asīri 'prisoner compound', kurummat bīt asīri 'food rations for the prisoner compound' (CAD A/2 331–32)
cognates.Egyptian: group writing ʔa₂-ṯi₂-ra 'captive' (GlOS 1, 46, after Hoch, SWET 45f., no. 40)

entries.note: HT89 A-SA-RA₂ · *307 (dubur 'sanctuary') heads five personnel classes, KU-RO 87, then rations of cyperus, figs and wine. Written as one group, with no divider or space between A and SA (GORILA I 141). A-SA-RA₂ writes ʾasāra with the vowels of Ebla ʔa₅-za-ru₁₂ ʔas(ā)r 'locked house' (GlOS 1, 46): the sanctuary's work-house, named over the classes it holds, as VIR+*307 names sanctuary personnel. Its staff are of the kind of the asirū of Alalakh VII, bonded household staff in grain-delivery lists (Niedorf 2008, 80 n. 305); cf. the Gibeonites made hewers of wood and drawers of water for the house of God (Josh 9:23, 27) and the captives given to the Levites (Num 31:47); compare MA-I-MI, TA-RA. Rivals: ʾasīr- 'captives' (Ug. åsr, Akk. asīru), which wants SI for /sī/; A + SA-RA₂ 'concerning the queen', A as abbreviated Akkadian aššum (EA 287:34; Huehnergard 2008: 285, 399), a cut the tablet does not mark. One witness.
entries.source: HT89; GORILA I 141; GlOS 1; Niedorf 2008; DULAT 111; CAD A/2 331–32; Josh 9:23, 27; Num 31:47; Montecchi 2008, 321; Huehnergard 2008: 285, 399

entries.meaning: uprightly, in righteousness (variant of yaššaram, ʾa- for ya-)

cognates.Hebrew: yāšār (יָשָׁר) 'upright, straight, righteous' (Deut 32:4, Ps 119:137, 1 Kgs 9:4, Prov 2:7); yōšer (יֹשֶׁר) 'uprightness, equity' (Ps 111:8, Prov 2:13); √y-š-r 'to be straight'; Yeshurun (יְשֻׁרוּן) poetic name for Israel = 'the upright one' (Deut 32:15, 33:5, 33:26, Isa 44:2); cf. Num 23:10 yĕšārīm (Balaam's pun on Yeshurun)
cognates.Ugaritic: yšr 'straight, upright' (DULAT 973); yšr in ritual context = moral/cultic fitness
cognates.Akkadian: ešēru 'to be/go straight, prosper' (CAD E 354); išaru 'straight, just, normal'; mīšaru 'justice, equity' (CAD M/II 116)—Hammurabi's mīšarum edicts: royal debt-release decrees that 'set things straight'
cognates.Arabic: yasara (يسر) 'to be easy, smooth'; yasār 'ease, prosperity'

entries.note: IO Zb 10, PR Za 1 and PK Za 11: the Iouktas, Prassa and Palaikastro spelling of JA-SA-SA-RA-ME, with ʾA- for JA- (ya-), whose reading and cognates it shares. On PR Za 1 RA is drawn reversed, the A802 form, normalized RA (GORILA IV 48); PK Za 11 writes · A, then SA-SA-RA-ME · on the next line, with no divider between. Ebla writes the same base with a- for ya-: the names a-sa-ar, a-sa-ra /yaSar/, beside Amorite ia-sa-rum and a-ša-ru-um (GlOS 2, 377). The JA-/A- alternation runs through the formula verb too (A-TA-I-*301-WA-JA, JA-TA-I-*301-U-JA): a person marker or article variant on one root.

entries.meaning: fine flour, semolina

cognates.Akkadian: šawīqu 'fine flour, semolina'

entries.note: HT 28a: A-SI-JA-KA heads a list of grain and oil, GRA+QE 5, OLE+U 2, OLE+KI ½, OLE+MI 1, OLE+TU, VIN 3, where a flour category fits a commodity allocation; HT 28b writes it again. Skeleton syk against šwq: š is written s and ḳ is written k. Arabic sawīq 'parched barley meal' keeps the trade commodity.

entries.meaning: I make myself a dwelling (Palaikastro dialect variant, 1cs tG-stem middle-reflexive of √NWY)

cognates.Hebrew: nāweh (נָוֶה) 'comely habitation, pasture' (Exod 15:13, Ps 23:2 [nĕʾōt, pl. construct], Isa 33:20, Jer 25:30); nāʾwāh (נָאוָה) 'comely' (Song 1:5); √n-w-y 'to dwell, settle'
cognates.Amorite: nawûm 'steppe; encampment (man and beast)' (Huffmon, APNM 237); nawijum 'nomadic encampment' (Gelb, AS 21)
cognates.Akkadian: namû A (nawû) 'pasture land … and its population and flocks; outlying area around a city' (CAD N/1, 249–51)
cognates.Arabic: nawā (نوى) 'to intend, set out for'; nawan, an-nawā (النَّوَى) 'the abode, the place one sets out for'
cognates.Greek: ναός (naos) 'temple' < *nawos, same √n-w-y (Bernal 1987, Rendsburg 1989); cf. Exod 15:13 nəwēh qodšekhā 'Thy holy shrine'

entries.note: PK Za 11: the Palaikastro spelling of A-TA-I-*301-WA-JA, whose reading and cognates it shares. -WA-E for -WA-JA writes ay as ē, as the Palaikastro scribes do.

entries.meaning: I make myself a dwelling (1cs tG-stem middle-reflexive denominative of √NWY)

cognates.Hebrew: nāweh (נָוֶה) 'comely habitation, pasture' (Exod 15:13, Ps 23:2 [nĕʾōt, pl. construct], Isa 33:20, Jer 25:30); nāʾwāh (נָאוָה) 'comely' (Song 1:5); √n-w-y 'to dwell, settle'
cognates.Amorite: nawûm 'steppe; encampment (man and beast)' (Huffmon, APNM 237); nawijum 'nomadic encampment' (Gelb, AS 21)
cognates.Akkadian: namû A (nawû) 'pasture land … and its population and flocks; outlying area around a city' (CAD N/1, 249–51)
cognates.Arabic: nawā (نوى) 'to intend, set out for'; nawan, an-nawā (النَّوَى) 'the abode, the place one sets out for'
cognates.Greek: ναός (naos) 'temple' < *nawos, same √n-w-y (Bernal 1987, Rendsburg 1989); cf. Exod 15:13 nəwēh qodšekhā 'Thy holy shrine'

entries.note: The verb that opens the libation formula: eleven attestations at five peak sanctuaries, Iouktas, Kophinas, Troullos, Palaikastro and Syme. A- is the 1cs prefix, -TA- the tG prefix, I an epenthetic i, and *301-WA-JA (*301 = na) the root √n-w-y: /ʾatainawaya/ 'I make myself a dwelling', denominative from nāweh 'abode', as hitnabbēʾ 'make oneself a prophet' from nābîʾ (di Mino, Ya Diktu). The tG is the stem of what the worshipper does to herself before the deity. Hebrew keeps it only in relics such as tirgaltî (Hos 11:3; Hutton and Marzouk 2012), Moabite has Gt wʾltḥm 'and I fought' (KAI 181:11, 15), and the act matches the Hitpaʿel wāʾetnappal lipnê YHWH 'and I prostrated myself before YHWH' (Deut 9:18), the same frame. A-TA-I- puts the -t- before the root, as Hebrew Hitpaʿel, Arabic Form V ta-faʿʿala and Geʿez tä-qätlä do; Akkadian infixes it (Gt). Exod 15:2 zeh ʾēlî wə-ʾanwēhû is 1cs √n-w-y with the deity as object, and Targum Onkelos renders it wə-ʾebnē lēh maqdəšā 'I will build Him a sanctuary'. Rival sense 'glorify him', beside wa-ʾărōməmennhû: HALOT files it under II נוה, and the Peshitta and Palestinian Targumim read 'praise'. Hebrew nāweh joins divine habitation to pasture (Exod 15:13; Ps 23:2; Isa 33:20; Jer 25:30; Ezek 34:14), and Amorite nawûm is 'steppe; encampment (man and beast)' (Huffmon 1965, 237). Same paradigm: Palaikastro A-TA-I-*301-WA-E (PK Za 11a), which weakens JA to E as A-SA-SA-RA-ME and A-DI-KI-TE-TE do there, and JA-TA-I-*301-U-JA (AP Za 1, 3ms). A-TA-I-*301-DE-KA and TA-NA-I-*301-(U-)TI(-NU) share the frame but are √ʿ-n-y 'answer' (di Mino, Ya Diktu). The root noun *301-WA nawā 'dwelling' stands on IO Za 4. Rival: Davis's functional gloss 'gives' (Davis 2026, in Salgarella and Petrakis eds., The Wor(l)ds of Linear A, 43–60). See TA-NA-RA-TE-U-TI-NU, the closing petition.

entries.meaning: Athirat (divine name: the Goddess)

cognates.Akkadian: Ašratu 'the goddess Ašratu' (HALOT 99)
cognates.Amorite: ʔaθeratum 'the Favourite, Lucky One', a-še-ra-tum = DINĜIR.MAḪ (Sanmartín 2026, 140; Hess 2025, 3–4)

entries.note: KN Zc 7, an inked vessel: A-KA-NU-ZA-TI · DU-RA-RE · A-ZU-RA ·, the divine name after 'this bowl' and DU-RA-RE, before JA-SA-RA-A-NA-NE. ZU, AB 79, is the one sign dedicated to ṯ and covers the whole ṯ-series, as Old Babylonian PI writes wa, we, wi and wu (Huehnergard 2011, 69); elsewhere scribes wrote ṯ in the T-series (di Mino, Ya Diktu 16–17 n. 27). A-ZU-RA writes ʾAṯirat (di Mino, Ya Diktu 40). Final RA writes the live /a/ of the feminine ending, which rules out ʾaṯirt- (Amarna a-ši-ir-te, Aramaic ʾăšērtā). ʾAṯirat is the West Semitic form: Ugaritic ʾaṯrt /ʾaṯiratu/ (Huehnergard 2012, 142) and Amorite a-še-ra-tum, whose second vowel 'is not elided as in Akkadian' (George and Krebernik 2022, 130). Rival: ʾAṯrat, with the middle vowel syncopated, as ᵈaš-ra-tu at Ugarit (RS 20.24: 20), a god list in Akkadian forms, ᵈaš-ra-tum in Old Babylonian, and 18 of the 95 Amarna spellings of ʿAbdi-Aširta, his own EA 60 among them (Hess 2025, 1–2, n. 14). Final -t is unwritten, and the ṯ is kept against the š of Akkadian and Hebrew.
entries.source: di Mino; Huehnergard 2011; George and Krebernik 2022; Hess 2025; Huehnergard 2012; Sanmartín 2026

entries.meaning: luminous one (feminine)

cognates.Amorite: ʾWR 'shine': ʾūrum 'light', jāʾwir (Gelb AS 21, 14)

entries.note: KH 6, a Khania cyperus distribution tablet: a personal name or epithet. √ʾ-w-r 'to shine, be light', Heb. ʾōr < *ʾawr 'light', with feminine -ēt. Rival: -t also forms abstracts and unit nouns (Fischer 2002, §64), so ʾawrēt is 'light' itself, and the feminine rests on the name slot alone. See U-RE-WI.

entries.meaning: 'our beloved …', the opening of a longer word

cognates.Amorite: dādum 'beloved', with dawd(ān)um (Gelb AS 21, 17); PN DAWD-UM (Gelb 1980, no. 1437)
cognates.Akkadian: dādu A 'love-making; darling, favorite' (CAD D 20)

entries.note: DRA Zg 1, a five-sign retrograde graffito on a clay reel from Drama-Kajrjaka, Bulgaria: DA-DU-*301̣-[?]-[?], the last two signs unread; RILA-S1 D 24 classes the inscription as doubtful. DA-DU opens DA-DU-MI-NE on KN Zf 31 and DA-DU-MA-TA on HT 95a. With *301 = na, dādu-nā 'our beloved': Amorite dādum, dawdum 'beloved' (DAWD-UM, Gelb 1980, no. 1437), with Ugaritic -nā 'our' after the case vowel, as malku-nā 'our king'. No divider follows *301, so the word runs on into the two lost signs. Rival: the Amorite name type dawdān- (Gelb 1980, nos. 1397, 1407–1408, 1416–1419; Da-da-nu-um, Huffmon 1965, 28). See DA-DU-MI-NE and TA-DI.
entries.source: Fol and Schmitt 2000, 56–62; Gelb 1980; Huffmon 1965; Huehnergard 2012, 33–34; RILA-S1 D 24

entries.meaning: settlement(s), district (heading of a grain list); rival 'beloved land'

cognates.Akkadian: dadmū pl. tant. 'the inhabited world (settlements and inhabitants)' (CAD D 18)
cognates.Amorite: dadmum, fem. dadmītum (Gelb 1980, 17); PN Da-ad-mi-tum (Gelb 1980, no. 1394)

entries.note: HT 95a .1 DA-DU-MA-TA · GRA, heading the grain list DA-ME 10, MI-NU-TE 10, SA-RU 20, KU-NI-SU 10, DI-DE-RU 10, QE-RA₂-U 7; HT 95b gives the same list under A-DU ·. A band of lost surface between MA and TA is wider than the other gaps but holds no sign position. dadmatu 'settlement(s)', feminine of *damdam- 'inhabited land': Akkadian dadmū 'the inhabited world (settlements and inhabitants)' (CAD D 18), Amorite dadmum and fem. dadmītum (Gelb 1980, 17), the Mari name Da-ad-mi-tum (Gelb 1980, no. 1394), Old Syrian dadm 'totality; country' (GlOS 1, 141); cf. Punic ʾdmt 'land' (KAI 145.3; DNWSI 14–15). Woudhuizen (2016, 226–227) reads the same word but takes it as 'goddesses of the dwellings'. The U of DU echoes no vowel of the word. Rivals: dādu-mātu 'beloved land' (√d-w-d + Akk. mātu), though both languages put the head noun first (māt dādi); Hadad-mattān 'gift of Hadad', parallel to A-DU on side b, with Ha- lost and final -n unwritten. One attestation.
entries.source: di Mino; CAD D; Gelb 1980; GlOS 1; DNWSI; Woudhuizen 2016

entries.meaning: good, sufficient—commodity quality designation on oil/fat allocation tablets
entries.note: HT 12 closes with DA-I 50 after OLE+DI 5, *304 5, QA₂+[?]+PU 1, E 30, *118 5, CYP+E 3 and NI 1; on KH 13 DA-I 3 follows *304-CYP ⅓. dayu 'enough': Heb. day 'enough, sufficiency' (HALOT 219), Aramaic day. Rival: a total; the 50 after DA-I on HT 12 equals the sum of the entries without the fraction (Schoep 2002, 162; Pope 1960, 204).

entries.meaning: fish
entries.note: The sole word on five Haghia Triada nodules (HT Wa 1001–1005), a commodity label. Heb. dāg 'fish' (דָּג), Ug. dg; KA writes g, as the velar series does not mark voicing.

entries.meaning: personal name on Dagan, Daguna

cognates.Akkadian: Daguna, Dagana, the Babylonian forms of the god's name (HALOT 213)
cognates.Amorite: Dagān DN (Gelb AS 21, 17)

entries.note: HT 103: DA-KU-NA 1, after *188 13 and before DA-KU-SE-NE 1, in a counted list under U-TA₂ · NI 40. DA-KU-NA writes Da-gu-na, Linear A marking no voicing. Daguna is an Old Akkadian personal name in lists (JCS 35, 211, 2; SANTAG 7, 062), and Babylonian Daguna, beside Dagana, is the god Dagan, frequent in personal names (HALOT 213). Gordon reads da-gu-na 'Dagon' at Haghia Triada (Gordon 1966, 24). On a counted list the bearer is a person or recipient, the name formed on Dagan. One attestation. See GRA.

entries.meaning: Hurrian personal name, 'the brother is beautiful'; cf. Boğazköy Tagu(b)-šini, Ugaritic Taki-šenni

cognates.Ugaritic: tgḏn PN, Hurrian, syllabic ta-gi₅-ša-na, RS 16.140:8, and ták-ša-na, RS 16.257 II 3 (DULAT 848); Tak-Šana, {1}ta-ki-ša-na (Kinlaw 1967, 115)
cognates.Hurrian: Tagup-šeni, Ḫatti (de Martino 2011, 86); Ta-ku, Ta-gu, Nuzi (Gelb, Purves and MacRae 1943, 262); šenna- names, Še-en-na-a-a, Še-en-ni-ia (ibid., 255)

entries.note: HT 103 lists DA-KU-SE-NE twice, on .2–3 as PA₃-DA-KU-SE-NE[ ]6½, broken after NE, with a possible divider after PA₃ (GORILA I 171), and again with 1, beside DA-KU-NA 1; HT 104 has DA-KU-SE-NE-TI 45½ with I-DU-TI 20½ and PA-DA-SU-TI 29, KU-RO 95: a name. DA-KU writes taku under stop neutralization, with the u of tagu-. Boğazköy Tagu(b)-šini (KBo XXII 114, 7), under the themes tagi- and tagu- (Laroche 1980, 250); Ugaritic tgḏn, syllabic ta-gi₅-ŠA-na, Hurrian Taki-šenni (NPN 262, printed Tgz̄n; Tropper 2000, 119, §32.144.35); Nuzi Aku-šenni, Takku and Takuja (NPN s.vv.). Hurrian šēna 'brother' with the individualizing -ni, šen=ni, gives the element -šenni (Giorgieri 2000, 199, 202; Wilhelm, Hurrian, 103; Laroche 1980, 225–26, s.v. šeni). GORILA I 171 allows the final TI of HT 104 to be an ideogram or classifier; Finkelberg 2002/03, 96–97 takes it as a dative of the recipient. tagi, tagu- is Hurrian 'beautiful' (Laroche 1980, 250–51): 'the brother is beautiful'.
entries.source: Gordon 1966; NPN; Tropper 2000; Laroche 1980; Giorgieri 2000; Wilhelm, Hurrian; Finkelberg 2002/03

entries.meaning: blood (ritual allocation category); rival dam 'kinfolk'

cognates.Akkadian: damu 'blood' (CAD D 75)

entries.note: HT 95a/b and HT 86a: DA-ME with MI-NU-TE, always together, in the set SA-RU, KU-NI-SU, DI-DE-RU, QE-RA₂-U (QA-RA₂-WA on HT 86a). HT 120: DA-ME GRA+K+L 74, GRA+PA 62 J A, beside DA-U-*49, KI-RE-TA-NA and PA-I-TO. Ug. dm (DULAT 270), Heb. dām (HALOT 224), Akk. damu 'blood' (CAD D 75), which DA-ME spells: a ritual category drawing grain. Rival: Old Syrian dam 'kinfolk' (GlOS 1, 147), a kin group drawing grain. Four attestations, all Haghia Triada. See *118-MI.
entries.source: di Mino; DULAT; HALOT; CAD D; GlOS 1

entries.meaning: the (district) of Qīr, the walled town; heading opposite KA-PA 'village'; rival diḳaru 'pot'

cognates.Hebrew: qîr קִיר 'wall' (HALOT 1099); qîr Môʾāb beside ʿār Môʾāb (Isa 15:1)
cognates.Akkadian: diqāru 'round-bottomed bowl' (CAD D 157), the rival

entries.note: KA-PA and DA-QE-RA head the two sections of HT 6a; DA-QE-RA heads HT 120, grain to DA-ME, KI-RE-TA-NA and PA-I-TO, against HT 102 under KA-PA (Uchitel 2003, 82). ḏā 'the one of' (cf. DA-NA-SI) + qīr 'walled town', Moabite qr 'city' (HALOT 1099); towns beside villages, Heb. ʿārîm // kᵊpārîm (1 Chr 27:25). Qīr is a town name, as Heb. Qîr Môʾāb, Qîr-Ḥereś (HALOT 1100); a town name is diptotic, genitive -a (Fischer 2002, §§152–153; Ug. ʾugarita, Huehnergard 2012, 40), as Amorite ḏū before a name: ZU-I-LA, ZU-ᵈIŠ-ḪA-RA (Gelb 1980, nos. 6596, 6598). Rivals: diqāru 'bowl' (CAD D 157), Ug. dqr 'pot' (DULAT 276). See KA-PA.
entries.source: di Mino; Uchitel 2003; HALOT; Fischer 2002; Huehnergard 2012; Gelb 1980; CAD D; DULAT

entries.meaning: estate, household (a unit receiving men and grain); rival 'kin group, clan'

cognates.Ugaritic: dr 'circle, group, assembly' (DULAT 277), the rival sense

entries.note: Seven documents at Haghia Triada, Khania and Palaikastro: a head count on three rosters of men (HT 7a, 85a, 122b), beside named men and work groups, and a grain or goods share on four lists (HT 10a, 10b, KH 104, PK 3), the largest on HT 10a (16½) and PK 3 (72). dār 'dwelling, house': Heb. dôr 'dwelling' (Isa 38:12), Arab. dār 'house'. Rival: *dawr- 'clan, group of relatives' (#40), Ug. dr 'circle, group, assembly' (DULAT 277). See DI-RI-NA.
entries.phonological_notes: Skeleton d-r, as in dār. Dead vowel on RE. No neutralization required.

entries.meaning: those of Acacia (gentilic, a roster unit); rival the unglossed Dasiṭa

cognates.Egyptian: šnd.t 'acacia', the source of the Semitic loan
cognates.Hebrew: šiṭṭâ, pl. šiṭṭîm 'acacia' (HALOT 1473); place names Beth-Shittah (Judg 7:22), Abel-Shittim (Num 33:49)
cognates.Akkadian: šamṭu, šanṭu (HALOT 1473)

entries.note: HT 13 DA-SI-*118 19 (wine list, beside KU-ZU-NI 18); HT 85a 24 (men, under A-DU · *307+*307, beside KU-ZU-NI 5); HT 122a 2 (men); HT 99b 2. Three scribes count it as a unit. ḏā 'those of', as in DA-NA-SI Ḏā-Naśiʾ, + ši-ṭa, Heb. šiṭṭâ 'acacia' (HALOT 1473), from *šint-, the n unwritten or assimilated. *118 = ṭa: s-t and s-d give no acacia. Weak point: *118 = ṭa is a proposed value. Four attestations.

entries.meaning: the enduring one (personal name)

cognates.Arabic: dāma, inf. n. dawm 'it continued, lasted, endured' (Lane 935)

entries.note: HT 120: DA-U-*49 · A517 20 under the heading DA-QE-RA, between DA-ME (GRA+K+L 74, GRA+PA 62) and KI-RE-TA-NA (GRA+B 60, GRA+PA 48): a recipient. *49 is read mi, a proposed value: Dawmi 'the enduring one', √d-w-m 'last, endure' (Arb. dwm 'to last', HALOT 216), as in Hebrew Dūmah (HALOT 216) and Assyrian Adummatu. DA-U writes daw analytically, as KA-U-ZU-NI writes Kawṯuni. Weak point: *49 = mi is a proposed value. Rival: *49 as the logogram PALM/TREE after DA-U. One attestation. See DU-ME-DI.

entries.meaning: Diʿa 'Knowledge' (personal name)

cognates.Amorite: daʿum, diʿ(atān)um, fem. daʿatum, diʿatum 'knowledge' (Gelb 1980, 17); DAʿ-UM, DA-UM (no. 1491); DIʿ-ATAN-UM, DI-ḪA-TA-NU-U[M] (no. 1507)

entries.note: HT Wc 3017, a roundel, face a QA-KU-RE · DI-*306 ·, face b CYP+D · *304+PA, DI-*306 whole and undotted (GORILA II 77); SigLA reads NA; the hanging strokes are DI's. DI writes di, *306 the ʿa: Diʿa 'Knowledge', Amorite diʿum, fem. diʿatum 'knowledge' (Gelb 1980, 17), as in the name DIʿ-ATAN-UM (Gelb 1980, no. 1507). Rival: HT 20 has the same frame, QE-KU-RE · DI ½, with DI a commodity; DI-*306 would then be that commodity written out. One attestation.

entries.meaning: nobles, notables; rival ʾadr 'granary'

cognates.Akkadian: adāru 'to be afraid, to fear' (semantic shift from 'awe-inspiring')

entries.note: HT 95a DI-DE-RU 10, HT 95b and HT 86a, in the Haghia Triada allocation set, always with SA-RU, MI-NU-TE and QE-RA₂-U, in the same order. ʾaddīru 'nobles', DI-DE- writing the geminate -dd-: Ug. adr 'strong, of good quality; noble, notable' (DULAT 21). Rival: Ug. ʾadr 'granary, barn' (GlOS 1, 10), a store drawing grain. Three attestations. See A-DA-RO.

entries.meaning: personal name ("El judges"—Ugaritic hero-king Dāniʾēlu)

cognates.Ugaritic: Dāniʾēlu—hero-king of KTU 1.17-19 (Tale of Aqhat). √d-y-n "to judge" + ʾēl "God."
cognates.Hebrew: Dāniyyēʾl (דָּנִיֵּאל)—Ezekiel 14:14, 14:20, 28:3; likely same figure as Ugaritic Danel
cognates.Akkadian: Da-ni-ilu—PN attested in Amarna letters (EA 256)

entries.note: HT 108 (Scribe HT 2, LM IB), a grain ration list headed by KI-RE-TA-NA 'Cretan': DI-NA-RO 2, DU-SU-NI 5, RA₂-TI 10. Dānīlu 'El judges', the Ugaritic hero-king Dāniʾēlu: √d-y-n with theophoric ʾēl contracted to -lo, RO writing lo. DI for the a of Dāniʾēlu writes the i of the root's noun dīnu 'judgment' (CAD D 150). DI-NA-U Dīnāyu shares the base. HT 108 thus holds the roots of both Ugaritic epic heroes' names, Keret and Danel. One attestation.

entries.meaning: personal name: hypocoristic of a √d-y-n name ('Judge')

cognates.Akkadian: dīnu 'judgment' (CAD D 150)

entries.note: Five documents at Haghia Triada and Knossos: a personnel list (HT 25a, twice, among names with quantity 1) and commodity allocations (HT 9a under VIN, DI-NA-U 4; HT 9b under AROM, DI-NA-U 4; KN Zb 27, VIN 17), a common NWS name at both sites. A √d-y-n 'judge' name, with -U after NA writing the hypocoristic -āyu/-āʾu (Amorite -ay-um: ʾAhlul-ay-um, Gelb 1980, no. 690; cf. Diyn-i-Baddu, no. 1512). Huffmon's glossary gives dyn 'judge', Common Semitic, as a Mari name element: the G imperfect Ya-di-nim (yaqtil class), the precative La-di-nam, I-di-AN (Huffmon 1965, 182; Noth IPN 187–188). Rival: √ʾ-d-n 'lord' with the laryngeal lost, ʾadōnū 'our lord', on the same d-n skeleton at the cost of one more assumption. See DI-NE.

entries.meaning: mighty is the verdict (compound sentence name); rival a simplex recipient name

cognates.Hebrew (PN): עַדְרִיאֵל Adriel (1 Sam 18:19), אֲבִידָן Abidan (Num 1:11), דָּנִיֵּאל Daniel
cognates.Akkadian: addiru "mighty" + dāyānu "judge"

entries.note: HT 98a DI-RE-DI-NA ½, a recipient between TA-NA-TI ¾ and TE-*301 ¾. ʾaddīr-dīnā 'mighty is the verdict': ʾaddīr as in DI-DE-RU ʾaddīru (√ʾ-d-r), dīn 'verdict', the name element diyn (GlOS 1, 155), as in DI-NA-U Dīnāyu and DI-NA-RO Dānīlu (√d-y-n). The NWS sentence name of predicate adjective and noun, the Ebla type ʾaddīr-X 'X is powerful': ʾaddīr-ʾIl, ʾaddīr-Malik (Pagan 1998, rows 848, 852), Punic ʾDRBʿL, ʾDRMLK (Benz 1972, 262). DI-RE leaves ʾa- unwritten, as DI-DE-RU and Punic BALDIR, BALIDDIR for bʿl ʾdr (Benz 1972, 262). Rival: a simplex recipient name. Weak point: Punic drops the ʾa- inside the name, DI-RE-DI-NA at its head. One attestation.

entries.meaning: households, granaries (grain recipient); rivals the Amorite place name Dīr, a personal name

cognates.Amorite: dīrum (noun), Dīr, Dīrum (GN), Dīrītum (DN), under DWR 'to turn around' (Gelb 1980, AS 21, pp. 17–18)

entries.note: A grain recipient in two Scribe 5 lists: HT 93a DI-RI-NA · DA+RE+SE 43½; HT 102 DI-RI-NA 10, beside SA-RA₂ GRA 976, PA₃-NI, VIR, MA-ZU and I-KA. DI-RI = dīr-, the base of Amorite dīrum and Dīr under √d-w-r (Gelb AS 21, 17–18); -NA = masculine plural -īna: households. Rivals: the place name Dīr ('the people of Dīr'), a personal name. Two attestations. See DA-RE.

entries.meaning: that, of (relative pronoun)
entries.note: ḏū 'he of, that of', the West Semitic determinative-relative (PWS *ḏū), kept apart from Akkadian ša. Gordon read it as a word in du ra-re, 'the cup of this night-demon', on the Knossos cup KN Zc 7 (Gordon 1966, §156); DU-RA-RE there reads as one word, durāru 'release'. As a bound element it opens DU-RU-WI ḏu-luwwī. Alone it stands in lists with a quantity, ZA 10b TA 2 / DU 1 and ZA 31 DU 2: Ebla and Amorite names open with ḏū 'he of' (ḏū-ʾIl, Pagan 1998, row 1609; ḎU+DAWD-I, Gelb 1980, no. 6583), so the roster DU abbreviates such a name, as KI abbreviates in the accounts. HT 122a ]DU 1 is broken before, and HT 47a ]DU 2̣0[ ends a word begun on the line before (GORILA I 91). The relative marker also heads genitives, nominative ðū (Huehnergard and Pat-El 2018, 191–92, Table 1). Weak point: no Linear A clause shows DU heading a relative. See DU-RA-RE, DU-RU-WI, KA-*305 and SE-WA-AU-DE.

entries.meaning: sanctuary, inner sanctum; proposed variant spelling of DU-PU₂-RE

cognates.Hebrew: dəbîr 'back room, holy of holies' (HALOT 208); wəladdəbîr, 1 Kgs 6:5
cognates.Arabic: dub(u)r 'back, hind part', the base HALOT gives for dəbîr (HALOT 208)

entries.note: KO Za 1 .2 TU-RU-SA · DU-*314-RE · I-DA-A ·, after A-TA-I-*301-WA-JA; GORILA IV 20 dots DU and RE, and *314 is whole. Facchetti (1999, 132) and Davis (2013, 44 n. 46) take *314 here as an orthographic variant of PU₂, and Thomas (2020, 8) admits the comparison: DU-*314-RE writes DU-PU₂-RE, the word of PK Za 15 and HT Zb 160 in the same ritual corpus, an equation for this word alone. dubur 'sanctuary, inner sanctum', Heb. dəbîr 'rear room, holy of holies' (1 Kgs 6:5), on Arb. dub(u)r 'rump' (HALOT 208): dubur ʾIda 'the sanctuary of Ida'. Rival: *314 = RI, √d-r-r, which gives no parse in context. One attestation. See DU-PU₂-RE.
entries.source: Facchetti 1999, 132; Davis 2013, 44 n. 46; Thomas 2020, 8; di Mino

entries.meaning: sanctuary, inner sanctum (dubur)

cognates.Linear B: da-pu₂-ri-to-jo po-ti-ni-ja (KN Gg 702), identified with λαβύρινθος (Chadwick–Baumbach 1963, p. 216)

entries.note: PK Za 15 JA-DI-KI-TE-TE-DU-PU₂-RE 'O Diqqitīt of the sanctuary' and HT Zb 160 PA-TA-DA-DU-PU₂-RE. PK Za 11 reads A-DI-KI-TE-TE-[··]-RE (GORILA IV 34), two signs lost before RE, the slot DU-PU₂ fills on PK Za 15, and PK Za 8 writes it JA-DI-KI-TE-TE-*307-PU₂-RE. Three spellings write dubur: *307 alone, *307-PU₂-RE and DU-PU₂-RE. Hebrew dəbîr 'rear room, holy of holies' of the temple (HALOT 208); Linear B da-pu₂-ri-to-jo po-ti-ni-ja (KN Gg 702); Egyptian group writing d-bi₄-r dabīr 'naos, inner sanctuary' (GlOS 1, 140, after Hoch, SWET 376, no. 561). DU-PU₂ keeps the u-u of the base noun dubur 'back, hind part' (Arabic dubur, Akkadian dubur, #151), of which the holy of holies is the later back-room sense. See DU-*314-RE.
entries.source: di Mino; Facchetti 1999; Thomas 2020; GlOS 1; HALOT

entries.meaning: dove, swallow (offering bird)

cognates.Hebrew: dərôr (דְּרוֹר) 'a kind of bird, swallow or dove', Ps 84:4, Prov 26:2 (HALOT 230)

entries.note: KN Zc 7 · A-KA-NU-ZA-TI · DU-RA-RE · A-ZU-RA ·, between 'this bowl' and the Goddess. durār 'dove, swallow': Hebrew dərôr, the bird nesting at the altars (Ps 84:4) and in flight (Prov 26:2; HALOT 230), Deir ʿAlla drr (DNWSI 262), Arabic durrat 'parrot', DU writing the u. The cups lay above the crypt of the dove vase (Evans, PoM I 146, 587); the Knossian Goddess bears a dove and her votary offers one (PoM II 337, 339); doves attend Asherah and Tanit (Dever 2005, 232). Gordon read ḏū-layli 'that of the Night', the night-demon (1966 §§146, 156); night is contracted lēl in the period (EA 243:13; GlOS 2, 20), which Linear A writes with E. Weak point: drr 'bird' has no Bronze Age witness. See MI-RU-TA-RA-RE.
entries.source: di Mino; HALOT; DNWSI; Evans, PoM I–II; Dever 2005; Gordon 1966

entries.meaning: the Levite (ethnonymic designation)

cognates.Ugaritic: d determinative-relative 'the one(s) of, he who' (DULAT 252)
cognates.Amorite: LWJ 'surround, accompany': lājum, lījum (Gelb AS 21, 24)

entries.note: HT 25a .4, at the end of the line after ZU-JU-PU₂ 1, with no numeral. WI is complete at the preserved right edge; .5 opens I-KI-RA 1 after the lost lower-left margin, where DU-RU-WI's 1 can stand, as DI-NA-U's 1 opens .3 (GORILA I 44–45); the break leaves unconfirmed whether a divider followed it. DU writes ḏu 'the one of', and RU-WI luwwī 'joined', with the u of the D-stem of l-w-y 'to accompany': Ebla lu-wu, lu-a (GlOS 2, 19); cf. Gen 29:34 yillāweh 'will be joined'. U-RE-WI on the same tablet writes the e of Hebrew lēwî; the names lāwiy, lawuy (GlOS 2, 19) would need RA-WI. Rival: DU-RU-WI-I-KI-RA as one name. Niesiołowski-Spanò derives the Levites from Mycenaean ra-wo, λαοί (2020, 444–452).

entries.meaning: He of the Lord (personal name; ḏū 'he of' + ṯuwāʕ 'lord'); rival 'the noble one'

cognates.Amorite: zu, *ḏū 'he of' in names: Zu-ḫa-di-im, Zu-ḫa-at-nim (Huffmon 1965, 186)
cognates.Akkadian: šuʾû A (šuwāʾu) 'master, lord'; šu-ʾ-u = šarru (LTBA 2 2:30); Old Akkadian appellative su-wa-um, a recipient of land (BIN 8 203:9) (CAD Š/3 417)
cognates.Ugaritic: ṯʕ (II) 'Hero, Noble', title of Kirta: krt ṯʕ (KTU 1.14 IV 37) (DULAT 879–880); Gordon reads 'Kret of Thaʿ', a tribe the scribe Ilimilku shares as 'the Thaʿite' (Gordon 1966, 74 n. 30, 120 n. 75)

entries.note: HT 36 .2 DU-ZU-WA at the end of the line after the 44 ½ of the .1 heading JE-DI *307+*307-GRA+QE, its 7 ½ on .3 over an erasure (GORILA I 69). All three signs whole and undotted. DU ḏū 'he of', as in DU-RU-WI and the Amorite names Zu-ḫa-di-im, Zu-ḫa-at-nim (Huffmon 1965, 186); ZU-WA ṯuwā(ʕ) 'lord', the w written and the final ʕ unwritten, as Akkadian šuwāʾu 'master, lord' and the Old Akkadian appellative su-wa-um, borne by a recipient of land (BIN 8 203:9; CAD Š/3 417). A recipient of grain in the Idaean's account: the lord's man. Rival: ḏū 'possessor of', 'the noble one', as Arabic ḏū. One attestation. Cf. QE-SI-ZU-E.
entries.source: di Mino; Huffmon 1965; CAD Š/3; DULAT; Gordon 1966

entries.meaning: He of the Spring (personal name; ḏū 'he of' + maʿīn 'spring, flowing water'); rival a product, '(the drink) of the spring'

cognates.Hebrew: maʿyān 'spring, source; place of origin, headwaters'; maʿyan mayim (Lev 11:36) (HALOT 612)
cognates.Arabic: maʿīn 'spring' (HALOT 612); rabwatin ḏāti qarārin wa-maʿīnin 'a high ground having level areas and flowing water' (Q 23:50); kaʾsin min maʿīn 'a cup from a flowing spring' (Q 37:45, 56:18)

entries.note: HT 123+124b .5 DU-MA-I-NA ⅜, after SI-DU and before KU-RO 20, on a face written over an erasure; I underdotted, whole in the facsimile beside the break that crosses NA (GORILA I 212–213). DU ḏū 'he of', as in DU-ZU-WA and DU-RU-WI; MA-I-NA maʿīna, the ʿ unwritten, I for ī, as Syriac meʿīnā. A recipient named for his spring, as the ḏāti … maʿīn of Q 23:50. Rival: a product, '(the drink) of the spring', after TU-PA-DI-DA. Weak points: I is dotted; Arabic maʿīn and Syriac meʿīnā are late. One attestation. Cf. DU-ZU-WA.

entries.meaning: She of (…), a woman named by her house (personal name; feminine of ḏū 'he of'); rival daṯʾu 'spring pasture'

cognates.Sabaic: PNf ḏt + clan name, the woman married into the clan (Sabaweb lemma 1281, after Stein 2012, 77)
cognates.Ugaritic: dt, f. of the functor d 'the one(s) of': pldm dt šʕrt 'cloaks of wool', KTU 4.270:8 (DULAT 252)
cognates.Arabic: ḏātu, fem. of ḏū 'a possessor, an owner, a lord' (Lane 984)

entries.note: HT 123+124a .6 DA-TU OLIV 15, *308 4¼, KI-RO ¾, the fourth holder after KI-TA-I gittī, PU-*131A and SA-RU šarru (GORILA I 211); TU (AB69) in the SigLA crop, which labels it KI. DA ḏā as in DA-NA-SI Ḏā-Naśiʾ, TU the nominative -tu: ḏātu stands alone with its quantities, as DU ḏū does (ZA 10b, ZA 31), the woman of a house as the Sabaic PNf ḏt + clan name. Side b of the tablet lists DU-MA-I-NA ḏū-maʿīna. Rival: daṯʾu 'spring pasture', a field name; dīšu, esikti dīšim nisik 'we have assigned the spring grass (for pasture)' (ARM 6 23:8; CAD D 163–164). Weak points: ḏāt is elsewhere bound to a following noun; ZA-TI zāt writes the demonstrative with Z at Knossos. One attestation. Cf. DU-MA-I-NA.
entries.source: di Mino; DULAT; Lane; Sabaweb; CAD D

entries.meaning: men, people (section heading); rival copper, bronze
entries.note: KH 7a (Khania, LM IB): the heading over VIR+*313b 10, men of the *313b class, who draw ½ unit of CYP+D; each of the tablet's three sections draws CYP+D. ʾenāš 'men, people' (semitic_roots 4), E- the root's own initial, as JArm. ʔēnāš, SI writing the final š. Rival: naḥāši 'of copper' (semitic_roots 2745), the interior ḥ unwritten, as no *314 sign occurs on any KH tablet: Emar naḫšu 'bronze(-vessel)', Amarna nuḫuštu (GlOS 2, 87); it leaves E- unexplained, since nəḥōšet and its cognates begin with n-. Weak point: the heading names the men VIR already counts. One witness.

entries.meaning: parīsu, the half-gur grain measure (CAD P 186; DULAT 671–672 prś)

cognates.Akkadian: parīsu B 'measure of capacity, half a gur' (CAD P 186)

entries.note: GRA with PA, the initial of parīsu, at four sites, often over large dry measures: Akkadian parīsu B '(a measure of capacity) one-half of a gur' (CAD P 186), Ugaritic prś/prs, a dry measure of half a gur (DULAT 671–672), and Biblical Aramaic pĕrēs 'half-portion' (Dan 5:28); Ebla writes it ba-rí-zu, Mari and Alalakh VII pa-ri-si (GlOS 2, 135). HT 102 has PA₃-NI GRA+PA 33 and, after a lacuna, ]VIR GRA+PA 33, broken before VIR (GORILA I 169). HT 120 keeps GRA+PA apart from GRA+K+L and GRA+B. Fourteen documents.

entries.meaning: flour/meal as a grain subtype; processed grain product for rations and offerings

cognates.Akkadian: qēmu 'flour' (CAD Q 204)

entries.note: GRA with the adjunct QE on four Haghia Triada tablets, in dry-measure quantities beside OLE+KI, OLE+MI, VIN and plain GRA: HT 18 PA-SE GRA+QE 20, HT 28a JA-*21F · GRA+QE 5, HT 101 ZU-*22F-DI GRA+QE 40, HT 99a GRA+QE without a number. HT 36 heads JE-DI *307+*307-GRA+QE 44½ (20 erased from 64½), flour issued under the *307 dubur 'sanctuary' sign, with DU-ZU-WA 7½. QE writes the first syllable of Akk. qēmu(m) 'flour, meal' (CAD Q 204), Heb. קֶמַח qemaḥ 'flour' (Gen 18:6; Num 5:15), Ug. qmḥ (KTU 1.14 II 29). GRA+QE is a processed subtype, distinct from plain GRA, whole grain.

entries.meaning: Ida, 'the Hand' (sacred mountain—toponym/theonym)

cognates.Akkadian: idum 'arm, side; strength' (Old Assyrian idu)

entries.note: A complete sign group on ritual stone vessels at three sites, Nerokurou, Palaikastro and Zakros; on PK Za 18 it alone is bounded by dividers, between the broken groups ]-TE and JA-JA-[. The distribution and the dedicatory genre fit a sacred-mountain name, Mt Ida and the Idaean cave. PH 6 (MM IIB, Phaistos), the earliest witness, has it inside the phrase I-DA-PA₃-I-SA-RI ʾIdā bi-ʾišarī; Phaistos lies under the mountain. Ida 'the Hand': Linear A writes the *ʾid- variant, with the initial i of Eblaite i-da 'hand' (GlOS 2, 371), Akk. idu, Soqotri ʔed, Tigre ʔǝde. The Idaean Daktyls, 'fingers', are the Greek doublet, 'fingers of the hand' (Pollux, Onom. 2.156), and Chantraine calls Ἴδη pre-Hellenic (DELG s.v. Ἴδη; di Mino, Ya Diktu); JE-DI yedī 'the Idaean' (HT 8a, HT 36, HT 122b, HT 140) is the gentilic. Rival: ἴδη 'wood, forest' (DELG s.v. ἴδη), attested only after the toponym. The w- is Cretan only: Βίδα (IC IV 80.2), Zeus Ϝιδάτας (IC II v 35), Koine Ἰδάτης (Staatsverträge III 552), Linear B wi-da-jo (KN V 60); epic Ida has none (Il. 8.170 ἀπ' Ἰδαίων). The w- is a Greek reshaping after ϝιδ- 'see': Helbig equates Βιδάτας with Παντόπτης 'all-seeing' (Bürchner, RE Suppl. I 250–51), while Linear A, which has WI (WI-DI-NA, HT 28b), writes Ida only as I-DA-. Weak point: the toponym class rests on behaviour.

entries.meaning: of Ida (diptotic genitive after DU-*314-RE); rival 'toward Ida'

cognates.Hebrew: hāhārāh (הָהָרָה) 'toward the mountain' (Gen 19:17, the hē locale -āh); yad (יָד) 'hand, arm' (HALOT 386)
cognates.Ugaritic: ʾugarita, diptotic genitive 'of Ugarit' in ḥmyt ugrt /ḥāmiyātu ʾugarita/ 'the walls of Ugarit'; yd 'hand'
cognates.Akkadian: idum 'arm, side; strength' (Old Assyrian idu)

entries.note: The diptotic genitive in dubur ʾIda, 'the sanctuary of Ida', as Ugaritic /ḥāmiyātu ʾugarita/ 'the walls of Ugarit', where a diptotic place name has genitive -a (Huehnergard 2012, 40, §IV.B.3). Rival: 'toward Ida', with the directive of Ugaritic -h /-ah(a)/ and Hebrew -āh, which final A alone does not show. Bare I-DA is attested. Ida 'the Hand' (see I-DA): Ebla spells 'hand(s)' i-da-a, sign for sign (A.ŠU.LUḪ = ma-wu i-da-a 'water of the hands', GlOS 2, 27, 371); Cretan Greek writes the name Βίδα.

entries.meaning: the Tower, a sacred title (DA-MA-TE with prothetic I-)
entries.cognates: Cf. Ugaritic dmt "tower", in "the tower of the mother of(?) the god[s(?)" (KTU 2.31:46), and dmtqdš "Tower" (DULAT 272); Akkadian dimtu "tower; fortified area, settlement; district" (CAD D 144–147; Huehnergard 1997). The unprefixed DA-MA-TE is independently attested at KY Za 2. Cf. Linear B da-ma-te, PY En 609.1, read δάμαρτες 'household estates' or Δαμάτηρ (DMic I 151), and Greek Δαμάτηρ (Dor., Arc., Boeot.), Δωμάτηρ (Aeol.), Δημήτηρ (Hom.) 'Demeter' (DELG 272–273).
entries.note: AR Zf 1 and AR Zf 2, separate one-word inscriptions on votive double axes from Arkhalkhori, AR Zf 2 broken after TE (I-DA-MA-TE[). I-DA-MA-TE alternates with DA-MA-TE on KY Za 2, prothetic I- before the same base, Ug. dmt 'tower' (DULAT 272), as Heb. ʾezrōaʿ (Jer 32:21, Job 31:22) beside zərōaʿ 'arm' and BArm. ʾedrāʿ beside dərāʿ (HALOT 28), Ug. udmʿt beside dmʿt 'tears' (Tropper 2000, §33.423a), and Ebla iš-ba-um /ʾiṣbaʿum/ 'finger' (Lipiński 1997, §27.17). A sacred title: Ug. dmt stands in 'the tower of the mother of(?) the god[s(?)' (KTU 2.31:46). Cf. Magdalene, read as the epithet 'the Tower' since Jerome, Ep. 127 (turritae) (Taylor 2014; Schrader and Taylor 2021). Rival: a personal name, as for DA-MA-TE. Weak point: single words, with no sentence around them. Two attestations. See DA-MA-TE.
entries.source: di Mino; DULAT; HALOT; Tropper 2000; Lipiński 1997

entries.meaning: the Tower; the unprefixed base of I-DA-MA-TE

cognates.Akkadian: dimtu 'tower; fortified area; district' (CAD D 144)
cognates.Linear B: da-ma-te, PY En 609.1 (pa-ki-ja-ni-ja to-sa da-ma-te DA 40), read δάμαρτες 'household estates' or Δαμάτηρ (= Δημήτηρ) as a unit of land (DMic I 151)
cognates.Greek: cf. Δαμάτηρ (Dor., Arc., Boeot.), Δωμάτηρ (Aeol.), dat. Δαμμάτηρ (Thess.), Δημήτηρ (Hom.) 'Demeter' (DELG 272–273)

entries.note: KY Za 2, a stone vessel from Kythera, DA-MA-TE alone. The base of I-DA-MA-TE (AR Zf 1, 2), read 'the tower': Ug. dmt (I) 'tower', in 'the tower of the mother of(?) the god[s(?)' (KTU 2.31:46; DULAT 272), Akk. dimtu 'tower; fortified area; district' (CAD D 144–147). Rival: a personal name on the same noun, as Ugarit dmty, dmtn (GlOS 1, 147) and Ebla ti-ma-ti 'pillar' (Pagan 1998, row 4489). One attestation.
