entries.meaning: Ida, 'the Hand', the sacred mountain, with emphatic enclitic -mi
entries.cognates: see I-DA
entries.note: SY Za 1 A-TA-I-*301-WA-JA · I-DA-MI · JA[, formula position 2, where Kophinas has dubur ʾIda (I-DA-A) and Iouktas JA-DI-KI-TU. ʾIda with the emphatic enclitic -mi, as I-PI-NA-MI-NA /ʾippina=mi=na/ (di Mino, Ya Diktu, 11); Ugaritic -m, /-mi/ or /-ma/ (Huehnergard 2012, 79); Ps 68:17 hārī-m gabnunnîm 'O many-peaked mountain' (Dahood, Psalms II, 142). One witness.

entries.meaning: island

cognates.Hebrew: ʾî (אִי) 'island, coastland', šəʾērît ʾî Kaptôr 'the remnant of the island of Caphtor' (Jer 47:4)
cognates.Ugaritic: ỉht (pl. cstr.) 'islands, coastal region' (KTU 1.3 VI 8; DULAT 31; GlOS 1, 60)

entries.note: CR Zf 1 A-MA-WA-SI · KA-NI-JA-MI · I-JA · QA-KI-SE-NU-TI · A-TA-DE: I-JA complete, after KA-NI-JA-MI qāniy-yammi 'Creator of the Sea'; KN Za 10 I-JA[ breaks after JA. ʾiy 'island', as Hebrew ʾî Kaptôr, Crete itself (Jer 47:4). Rivals: the vocative yā; the name element ʾIyya 'where?' (Emar i-ia; GlOS 1, 59). See A-JE.

entries.meaning: and behold (contracted conjunction + h-n presentative)

cognates.Hebrew: hinnēh (הִנֵּה) "behold" (< *han + emphatic); ha- definite article (< *han with n-assimilation)
cognates.Akkadian: annû "this" (demonstrative, same *han base)

entries.note: /wannā/ 'and behold', comparing Ugaritic w hn beside contracted wn (KTU 1.23:46; 1.4 IV 50; Watson 1996, 285–87; Sivan 2001, 34, 186) and Lipiński's *wa-hanna/u > wn (1997, §27.25). Hebrew wəhinnē keeps /h/; Ebla a-na, an-na, i-na, in-na and Ugarit syllabic a-né-en-na write the presentative without h- (GlOS 1, 218). Rival: /winnā/, since alphabetic Ugaritic leaves the vowels open; Tropper 2000, §33.142.23 allows */wa-hinnV/ > /winnV/, though he prefers w with enclitic -n. See U-NA-A, I-NA.

entries.meaning: brother-in-law (kin title); I-JA-PA-ME · TA-TA 'the brother-in-law of Tatta'; rival ybmt 'sister-in-law', Anat's epithet

cognates.Ugaritic: ybm 'brother-in-law' (DULAT 937); ybmt 'widowed sister-in-law', Anat's epithet ybmt limm, the rival

entries.note: KH 7a: sections under E-NA-SI 'men', I-JA-PA-ME · TA-TA and SE-*305 'provisions'; the second holds QA-TI-KI, *313b men 4, cyperus ⅓ (GORILA III 29). yabam 'brother-in-law', as Tell Rimah ia-ba-mi-ša and Ugaritic ybm (GlOS 2, 341; DULAT 937); before TA-TA, yabam Tatta 'the brother-in-law of Tatta', a woman's name at Mari and Tuttul (Monti 2017, 302, 335): her husband's brother, as ia-ba-mi-ša 'her brother-in-law'. Rival: ybmt 'widowed sister-in-law', Anat's epithet ybmt limm (DULAT 937; Huehnergard 2012, 87). One witness.
entries.source: di Mino; GlOS 2; DULAT; Huehnergard 2012; Monti 2017

entries.meaning: island (genitive after SI-MA 'name of'; -i written with an E-series sign)
entries.note: PH Zb 4, a clay vessel from Phaistos: SI-MA · I-JA-TE, šima ʾiyyate 'name of the island'. Heb. ʾî 'coast, island' (HALOT 38), pl. ʾiyyîm: the base ʾiyy- with the feminine -at-, and the genitive -i after the construct SI-MA written with an E-series sign. A-JE ʾaye (Thera) and I-JA ʾiya (Knossos) spell the same noun. One attestation. See SI-MA and I-JA.

entries.meaning: farmer, plowman (recipient)

cognates.Akkadian: ikkarum 'farmer, farm laborer, plowman' (Huehnergard 1997, glossary)

entries.note: HT 91 opens with I-KA over grain and small rations of oil, olives, figs and wine; HT 102 I-KA 5 (KA dotted) in a grain ledger, KU-RO 1060 after SA-RA₂ GRA 976. ʾikkār 'farmer': Akk. ikkaru 'plowman, farmer' (CAD I/J 49), Heb. ʾikkār, a loan from it (HALOT 47), Syr. ʾakkārā; the geminate and final r unwritten. Rival: the personal name Ikkaru (ORACC QPN). Two attestations. See I-KI-RA and A-KI-RO.

entries.meaning: at the horn, the promontory (place name)

cognates.Hebrew: qeren 'horn', and of a hill in qeren ben-šāmen 'a fertile hill', Isa 5:1 (HALOT 1144)
cognates.Akkadian: qarnu 'horn, ... protruding part' (CAD Q 134)
cognates.Phoenician: qrn 'horn' (Krahmalkov 432); Carne, a city in Phoenicia named from it (Krahmalkov 433)

entries.note: HT 90 (Haghia Triada): heads a distribution of GRA 20 and OLE+DI 3. i-k-r-n: ʾi- 'at' with √q-r-n, 'at the horn', a promontory toponym; KA-RO-NA on HT 11a has the same k-r-n. A preposition would govern the genitive qarni, not -NA (Fischer 2002, §292), so I-KU-RI-NA is a fixed place name, not a phrase. Rival: a personal name on √q-r-n. One attestation.

entries.meaning: behold, she who reveres… (broken)

cognates.Hebrew: yārēʾ (יָרֵא) "fearing", f. cs. yirʾat, Bab. yərēʾat (HALOT 433; Prov 31:30); hēn yirʾat (הֵן יִרְאַת) "behold, the fear of" (Job 28:28); yirʾā (יִרְאָה) "fear, reverence, awe"

entries.note: AP Za 2 .2 I-NA-JA-RE-TA[ ]QA, no divider after TA. hinna yarēʾat… 'behold, she who reveres…': I-NA- as in I-NA-JA-PA-QA hinna yapqaḥ (PK Za 11), Ebla i-na, in-na (GlOS 1, 218); yarēʾat the feminine construct of yārēʾ 'in fear of', Babylonian yərēʾat (HALOT 433), as ʾiššâ yirʾat YHWH 'a woman who fears YHWH' (Prov 31:30), JA writing ya and RE the ē. Rival: yārēʾtā 'you have feared' (2 Sam 1:14), the finite verb of I-NA-JA-PA-QA. Rival: the noun yirʾat 'the reverence of' (Job 28:28; di Mino, Ya Diktu). Weak point: no divider follows TA, and the genitive is lost in the lacuna. One attestation.

entries.meaning: my Anat—theonym plus 1cs -ī; proposed "She Who Answers" (√ʿ-n-y)

cognates.Ugaritic: ʿnt /ʿanatu/ "Anat"; syllabic ᵈa-na-tu₄ = /ʿanatu/; btlt ʿnt "the young woman Anat"
cognates.Hebrew: ʿAnāt (עֲנָת) in Shamgar ben Anath (Judg 3:31); Beth-Anath (Josh 19:38); Anathoth (Jer 1:1)
cognates.Akkadian: Antu "Anu's consort" (CAD A2, 148)
cognates.Egyptian: ꜥntjt "Anat" (NK warrior goddess, adopted from Canaan)
cognates.Amorite (Mari): Ḫanat (cult goddess at Mari, early 2nd millennium, with initial ḫ- instead of ʿ-)

entries.note: IO Za 6, position 2. The vessel is chipped, but the complete group I-NA-TA-I-ZU-DI-SI-KA has no internal lacuna. Segmented I-NA-TA-I + ZU-DI + SI-KA, 'my Anat, Breast-Who-Gives-Drink.' Initial I carries the laryngeal ʿ, not a separate particle: Ugaritic has three vowel-conditioned aleph signs (Huehnergard 2012, 21), and syllabic Ugaritic writes ᵈa-na-tu₄ for /ʿanatu/ and ša-i for /šāʿi/ (Huehnergard 2008, 18 n. 78, 208, 249). Final I is the 1cs suffix -ī. IO Za 8 ]A-NA-TI-*301-WA-JA[ is broken at both edges. See TA-NA-I-*301-U-TI-NU, DA-RU-NE-TE, KA-KU-NE-TE.

entries.meaning: my Anat, Breast-Who-Gives-Drink—theonym plus compound divine epithet

cognates.Ugaritic: ʿnt "Anat" (DULAT 167); ṯd "breast" (KTU 1.23: b-ṯd aṯrt 'at the breast of Athirat'; yiṯdyn 'they suckle')
cognates.Akkadian: šaqû "to give to drink, to irrigate" (CAD Š2 20)

entries.note: IO Za 6, complete and undivided, between TA-NA-I-*301-U-TI-NU and JA-SA-SA-RA-ME: I-NA-TA-I + ZU-DI + SI-KA. Ugaritic btlt ʿnt 'the young woman Anat' (KTU 1.3 III 11; Huehnergard 2012, 86) and Middle Babylonian Ištar-ṣēri give deity-plus-epithet controls. ZU-DI is ṯudī 'breast', Ug. ṯd 'breast, bosom' (DULAT 886); SI-KA is šiqā 'she who gives drink'. Ugaritic gives Anat the title ṯd lʾimm 'the breast of the people' (KTU 1.13:19), and pairs mṣṣ ṯd btlt 'he sucks the breasts of the Virgin' with ḥlb aṯrt (KTU 1.15 II 27; DULAT 886): the same divine nursing context. One attestation. See ZU-DI.

entries.meaning: Who Gives Drink (proposed second member of a divine epithet; participial/verbal noun of √š-q-y)

cognates.Hebrew: hišqā (הִשְׁקָה) "to give drink, to water" (HALOT 1640); šiqqūy (שִׁקּוּי) "drink, watering"; mašqeh (מַשְׁקֶה) "cupbearer, drink"
cognates.Akkadian: šaqû "to give to drink, to irrigate" (CAD Š2 20); šāqû "cupbearer"
cognates.Arabic: saqā "to water, give drink" (BK 1 1076); sāqī "cupbearer"; siqāya "the providing of water" (Q 9:19 siqāyat al-ḥājj)

entries.note: IO Za 6, inside the undivided group I-NA-TA-I-ZU-DI-SI-KA, segmented after ZU-DI: the second member of ṯudī-šiqā 'Breast-Who-Gives-Drink'. √š-q-y 'give drink': the participle sāqiy 'waterer' (GlOS 2, 245), Ebla saqat 'libation' (GlOS 2, 246) and the Ebla name si-gi-da-mu 'give drink, Damu!' (Pagan 1998, row 4205). The same šiqā closes A-DA-KI-SI-KA (KH 5). Cf. administrative SI-KA (√š-k-n) on the HT nodules. Weak point: no divider stands before SI-KA. One attestation. See TE-SU-DE-SE-KE-I.

entries.meaning: in the presence of

cognates.Hebrew: pānīm (פָּנִים) 'face, presence' (Gen 32:31, Exod 33:14–15, Lev 1:3–4, Ps 19:15, Mal 1:8); lipnê (לִפְנֵי) 'before the face of' = standard cult-approach formula; √p-n-y 'to turn, face'
cognates.Ugaritic: pnm 'face, presence' (DULAT 664); pn ilm 'face of the gods' in ritual texts
cognates.Akkadian: pānu 'face, front, presence' (CAD P 92); ina pāni 'before, in the presence of'
cognates.Arabic: fanā' (فناء) 'courtyard, forecourt'; related to approaching a presence
cognates.Amarna Canaanite: pa-ni-mu /panīmū < paniy=humu/ 'before them' (Moran: 'before him'), 'face' as a preposition (GlOS 2, 130)

entries.note: Complete at three peak sanctuaries: IO Za 2 and IO Za 15 (Iouktas), KO Za 1 (Kophinas), VRY Za 1 (Vrysinas). Damaged at Troullos (TL Za 1 […]NA-MA) and Apodoulou (AP Za 2 I-PI-NA-MA[, to a broken edge), and I-PI[ at the break of PK Za 8. ʾippina=ma 'in the presence of': pnm, Heb. pānîm 'face, presence' (HALOT 938), Ug. pnm 'face, countenance' (DULAT 664). Biblical cult pairs approach before the divine presence with acceptance (Lev 1:3–4; Ps 19:15; Mal 1:8), as I-PI-NA-MA stands beside the √r-ṣ-y verb of the fuller formula. PI writes pin- against Heb. pānîm and Akk. pānu, a different vowel in one root: Hebrew shifted *a > *i more than once (Suchard 2016, 189), Punic writes Tinnit's epithet pn bʿl as Θινιθ-Φανεβαλ and Θεννειθ-Φενηβαλ (Krahmalkov 2000, 398, 495), and SED reconstructs *yad- 'hand', of the same noun pattern as *pan-, 'with a variant *id- … probably for PS too' (SED I, CXXX). Rival: Davis's functional gloss 'a favor, a blessing' (Davis 2026, 55). See PI-*310-A.

entries.meaning: face, presence (of)—expanded variant of I-PI-NA-MA

cognates.Hebrew: pānīm (פָּנִים) 'face, presence' (Gen 32:31, Exod 33:14–15, Lev 1:3–4, Ps 19:15, Mal 1:8); lipnê (לִפְנֵי) 'before the face of' = standard cult-approach formula; √p-n-y 'to turn, face'
cognates.Ugaritic: pnm 'face, presence' (DULAT 664); pn ilm 'face of the gods' in ritual texts
cognates.Akkadian: pānu 'face, front, presence' (CAD P 92); ina pāni 'before, in the presence of'
cognates.Arabic: fanā' (فناء) 'courtyard, forecourt'; related to approaching a presence

entries.note: PK Za 10 and PK Za 11, Palaikastro stone vessels, beside the formula words A-TA-I-*301-WA-E and A-SA-SA-RA-ME: a reduplicated expansion of I-PI-NA-MA ʾipinama 'face, presence' (√p-n-m), whose reading and cognates it shares.

entries.meaning: divide! (imperative of √q-ṭ-ʿ), heading over mixed commodities
entries.note: Heads a mixed commodity section: HT 44a I-QA-*118 · GRA, OLE+KI, OLE+U, OLE+RA, OLIV, NI, VIN, over an erasure, QA over an erased I (GORILA I 85). iqṭaʿ 'divide!', the imperative of √q-ṭ-ʿ 'cut, divide' (semitic_roots K0337), with *118 = ṭa and the final ʿ unwritten: Arb. wa-qaṭṭaʿnāhum 'and We divided them' into twelve tribes (Q 7:160); JPA Pa. qaṭṭaʿ 'divide (a Sidra)' (Jastrow 1351). Hebrew, Ugaritic and Sabaic have q-ṣ-ʿ (HALOT 1124; DULAT 705); the ṭ follows Arabic and Aramaic. Rivals: ʾiqṭaʿ 'I divide', the 1 sg. prefix, since the prefixed i- of the imperative is Arabic only; a personal or institutional name. Weak point: *118 = ṭa is a proposed value. One attestation.

cognates.Arabic: qaṭaʿa 'cut'; D qaṭṭaʿa 'divide' (Q 7:160); qaṭīʿa 'portion of land held in fee' (Lane 2990)
cognates.Aramaic: JPA qəṭaʿ 'cut off', Pa. qaṭṭaʿ 'divide (a Sidra)' (Jastrow 1351)
cognates.Hebrew: MHeb. qāṭaʿ 'cut off' (Jastrow 1351); BH II qṣʿ, pu. məquṣṣāʿôt 'made with corners' (Ex 26:23; HALOT 1124)

entries.meaning: goddess; rival ʾila 'god'

cognates.Akkadian: ilat 'goddess'

entries.note: HT Wa 1006–1013: eight sealings bearing only I-RA₂, in two hands (scribes 52 and 53), from one deposit, Portico 11 and Room 13, LM IB; one context. I ʾi, RA₂ la: feminine ʾilat- 'goddess' (Akk. ilat, Ug. ỉlt 'goddess', DULAT 63), the final -t unwritten. Rival: masculine ʾila 'god', Ug. il /ʾilu/ 'god; El' (Huehnergard 2012, 41), the Amorite name element *ilāh, almost always first in a name (Huffmon 1965, 162; I-la-sa-lim, Sa-mu-ū-i-la, 165), and Ebla's bare i-la 'the god' as a name (Pagan 1998, row 2700). See SA-RE-JU, PI-RU-E-JU and DI-NA-RO.
entries.source: di Mino; GORILA II; DULAT; Huehnergard 2012; Huffmon 1965; Pagan 1998
entries.phonological_notes: I = /ʾi/ (initial laryngeal). RA₂ = /la/ (proposed). Quiescent feminine -t not written—NWS ʾilāt → ʾilā in absolute state.

entries.meaning: O Diqqitu! (vocative invocation of the proposed goat-goddess Diqqitu)

cognates.Ugaritic: dqt 'female head of small cattle for sacrifice', a ewe or she-goat (Gordon UT §19.695, cited by Astour 1966, 283 n. 74); DN dqt, KTU 1.102:8 (Astour 1966, 283–84; DULAT 276)

entries.note: IO Za 2, position 2 of the libation formula. JA- is the vocative ya-, and DI-KI-TU spells diktu with the -TU vowel written, against Greek Δίκτη. The goddess named here is the addressee of the verb at position 1, A-TA-I-*301-WA-JA ʾatainawaya 'I make myself a dwelling', the worshipper settling before her; each peak sanctuary invokes its mountain, Diktu at Iouktas and Palaikastro, Ida at Kophinas and Syme. Astour's etymology: Ug. dqt 'female head of small cattle for sacrifice' (Gordon UT §19.695), *daqqatu, *diqqatu, a divine name in a Ugaritic god-list (Astour, 'New Evidence for the Semitic Derivation of the Greek Name of the Mountain Dikte', 1966). Hesiod calls the mountain Αἰγαίῳ ἐν ὄρει, 'Goat's Mountain' (Theog. 481–482 West), a Graeco-Semitic doublet, and Amenhotep III's list spells it Di-qa- with the determinative 'high' (Astour, 'Aegean Place Names', 1966). Clay goats are the commonest votive at peak sanctuaries, and Amalthea, the goat who nursed Zeus in the Dictaean Cave, is the goddess brought down to a wet-nurse. Palaikastro, of Proto-Phoenician dialect, writes the nisbe -TE-TE: A-DI-KI-TE-TE, and the vocative JA-DI-KI-TE-TE in JA-DI-KI-TE-TE-DU-PU₂-RE 'O Diqqitīt of the sanctuary' (PK Za 15) and JA-DI-KI-TE-TE-*307-PU₂-RE, with the *307 DUBUR logogram (PK Za 8). See A-DI-KI-TE-TE.
entries.source: di Mino; Astour 1966 (New Divine Names, Aegean Place Names)

entries.meaning: personal name: Amorite-type yaqtul name + feminine -at (cf. Yadwiratum, Gelb 1980, no. 3209; Ya-du-ra-an, Ya-du-ri-im, Huffmon 1965, 38)

cognates.Amorite: JA-DWIR-AT-UM Yadwiratum (Gelb 1980, no. 3209); JA-DWIR-UM, JA-DWIR-I, JA-DWIR-AN (nos. 3210–3214); Ya-du-ra-an, Ya-du-ri-im (Huffmon 1965, 38); element jadūr, B stem of DWR 'to turn around, to dwell' (Gelb glossary)

entries.note: KN 1b JA-DU-RA-TI E 105, laid out as the recto's JA-KU-TI E 240, so both are names. ya- patterns 'figure almost exclusively in animal, plant, and personal names' (Fischer 2002, §66d). JA-DU-RA-TI writes Yadurat-i, the feminine Amorite Yadwiratum, [IA-DI]-RA-TUM (Gelb 1980, no. 3209), with another case ending; cf. Ya-du-ra-an, Ya-du-ri-im (Huffmon 1965, 38). One attestation.

entries.meaning: O Radiant One (vocative + elative of √n-w-r 'light'), divine epithet

cognates.Arabic: ʾanwaru 'lighter, brighter', hāḏā ʾanwaru min ḏāka 'this is brighter than that' (Lane 2866)
cognates.Amorite: NWR 'shine': janūr, nawarum, Nawar (Gelb AS 21, 28)
cognates.Akkadian: namru, older nawru 'bright, shiny, brilliant' (CAD N/1 239)

entries.note: SY Za 4, word 2, after the formula verb A-TA-I-*301-WA-JA, in the deity or recipient slot. RILA-S1 (84) reads JA-I-NWA-RO with RO underdotted and rates GORILA's JA-I-NWA-ZA 'moins probable' (cf. SY Za 11; for ZA cf. KN Zf 31). Sign 3 is NWA (AB48) in both RILA-S1 lines, its only occurrence in the corpus, with the value of Linear B B48 (pe-ru-si-nwa ~ pe-ru-si-nu-wa). JA is vocative ya, as in JA-DI-KI-TU; I writes the aleph, here ʾa (cf. I- for ʾu in I-KU-JU-TI); NWA writes /nw/; -RO writes final /-ru/. ʾanwaru is the ʾaqtal elative of √n-w-r 'light': Arb. 'hāḏā ʾanwaru min ḏāka' (al-Zamakhsharī, Asās al-Balāgha, s.v. nwr). The epithet stands before PA₃-NI-WI 'the Builder', as Ugaritic pairs El's titles ṯr il dpid // bny bnwt 'Builder of Built (Ones)' (KTU 1.4 III 30–32; Smith & Pitard 2009, 39, 447). Same root as NU-RO nūr; Akkadian nawir 'is bright' names a god in OB personal names, Sîn-nawir 'The Moon Is Shining' (CAD N/1 212). Rival: ʾaṣwaru 'Fashioner' (√ṣ-w-r; Q 59:24 al-muṣawwir beside al-bāriʾ), which needs AB48 to be a sibilant + w sign. One attestation. See *301-U-RA.

entries.meaning: 'the Living One', title of the Goddess

cognates.Amorite: ḤJJ 'live': ḥajjum, ḥajja, jaḥī (Gelb AS 21, 19)

entries.note: PK Za 18 I-DA · JA-JA-[…], on a stone vessel, after the fully delimited I-DA, and SY Za 8 A-TA-I-*301-WA-JA · JA-JA-[…], after the libation-formula opener. Both positions take a theonym or divine epithet. √ḥ-y-y 'live': Heb. ḥāyâ 'to be alive' (HALOT 310), ḥayyā 'the Living One'. No HA precedes JA-JA, and Aegean spelling leaves h unwritten: Linear B e-qe-ta /hekwetās/, e-qe-ta-i /hekwetāhi/, a-mo-ta /harmota/ and a-u-po-no /ahupnos/ (Chadwick and Baumbach 1963, s.vv. ἕπομαι, ἅρμα, ἀ-/ἀν-). Weak point: both stand on fragments that break after the second JA, where a divider may follow. Two attestations.
entries.source: di Mino; HALOT; Chadwick and Baumbach 1963
entries.phonological_notes: Only /ja-ja-/ is graphically preserved. HA is absent; an initial /ḥ/ and every sign after the second JA remain hypothetical.

entries.meaning: personal name, Amorite type (yaqtul of √m-w-t)

cognates.Amorite: IA-MU-UT-DA-DU, IA-MU-UT-LI-IM (Gelb 1980, nos. 3370, 3375); bare JA-MWUT-UM, IA₃-A-MU-TUM (no. 3625)
cognates.Egyptian: mꜣʿt 'Maat' (rival)

entries.note: MA 2c: ]-U-NA-NA 3, then ]JA-MA-U-TI 6 at the broken left end, sign groups possibly lost before it. Yamwut + -i, the Amorite JA-MWUT names (Gelb 1980, nos. 3370, 3375, 3625): MA-U writes the w of yamwut-, as DA-U-MI writes dawmi, where the cuneiform contracts it (IA-MU-UT-DA-DU); TI writes the root's t with the -i of JA-KU-TI and JA-DU-RA-TI. Rival: JA- + Egyptian mꜣʿt 'Maat'. One attestation. See MI-TU.

entries.meaning: He-from-the-hand-of-Re (Egyptian theophoric)
entries.note: HT 122a, intact, 1 in a list of names totalling 31. Gordon reads Egyptian Ỉmy-d(t)-Rꜥ 'He-who-is-from-the-hand-of-Re' (Gordon 1966a, 31, §127), comparing Ugaritic bdil 'From-the-hand-of-El'. Rival: a Minoan name. One witness.

entries.meaning: personal name ("he shines"—Amarna Yapaḫu)

cognates.Amarna: Yapaḫu (EA 297-300)—ruler of Gezer; cuneiform -ḫ- renders ʿ, √y-p-ʿ "he shines/appears"
cognates.Hebrew: yāpaʿ (יָפַע) "to shine forth" (Hiphil hôpîaʿ, Deut 33:2); PN Yāpîaʿ, king of Lachish (Josh 10:3)
cognates.Amorite: JPʿ "to shine" (B stem jāpaʿ); bare name IA-A-PA-AH Yaypaʿ at Mari, beside Yaypaʿ-Addu, Yaypaʿ-Lim (Gelb 1980, nos. 2792–2794, p. 595)

entries.note: ZA 4a .3–4 JA-PẠ 1̣[, PA dotted, the numeral dotted and broken after (GORILA III 149), the only JA-PA standing alone: JA-PA-QA, I-NA-JA-PA-QA and JA-PA-RA-JA-SE are other words. Yapaʿ, √y-p-ʿ with ʿ unwritten: Amarna writes the ʿ with -ḫ- in Yapaḫu, ruler of Gezer (EA 297–300), Hebrew keeps the name as Yāpîaʿ (Josh 10:3), Alalakh has bare ia-pa yapaʿ (Buck 2018, 334), and Gelb files JA-JPAʿ at Mari and Alalakh (Gelb 1980, nos. 2792, 3395). ARKH 3b […]-JA-PI is a damaged ending. One witness. See A-WA-PI.
entries.source: di Mino; GORILA III; Buck 2018; Gelb 1980

entries.meaning: Moon (personal name, after the moon god); rival yarē 'he instructs'

cognates.Amorite: Jaraḫ, divine name (Gelb 1980, glossary); JARAḪ-T-UM, IA-RA-AḪ-TUM (no. 3419)
cognates.Hebrew: yārēaḥ (יָרֵחַ) 'moon', wə-yārēaḥ ʿāmād 'and the moon stayed' (Josh 10:13); yeraḥ (יֶרַח) 'month', bə-yeraḥ zīw 'in the month Ziv' (1 Kgs 6:37)

entries.note: KN Wc 30, an MM IIIB roundel, JA-RA its only word. Yaraḫ with ḫ unwritten: the moon god's name, borne by men as Amorite JARAḪ-T-UM (Gelb 1980, no. 3419). Rival: yarē 'he instructs', √y-r-h. One witness.

entries.meaning: personal name, '(DN) is exalted' (Amorite type)

cognates.Amorite: JA-RWIM names, IA-RI-IM-LI-IM Yarim-Lim, IA-RI-IM-D-IM (Gelb 1980, nos. 3432–3442)
cognates.Ugaritic: yrm PN, syll. ia-ri-mu/mi, gen. ia-ri-mi (PRU 3 66 [RS 16.252]:12; DULAT 965)

entries.note: HT 87: JA-RE-MI 1 in a roster of men under *21F-TU-NE · MA-KA-RI-TE. Yarīm, the yaqtul of √r-w-m, a hypocoristic of the Amorite Yarim-DN names (Gelb 1980, nos. 3432–3442: Yarim-Lim, Yarim-Addu); Ugarit has the bare name, yrm, ia-ri-mi (DULAT 965); cf. Heb. Yirmᵉyāhû. RE writes ri, as KI-RE-TA₂ beside KI-RI-TA₂. Rival: √y-r-ḫ 'moon', the god Yariḫ (Huehnergard 2012, 42, 87). One attestation. See RU-MA-TA.

entries.meaning: personal name, '(DN) is exalted', with hypocoristic -ān (Amorite type)

cognates.Ugaritic: yrmn PN, syll. ia/ya-ri-ma-nu/na (RS 8.146:26; DULAT 966; Kinlaw 1967, 132)
cognates.Amorite: JA-RWIM names, IA-RI-IM-LI-IM Yarim-Lim, IA-RI-IM-D-IM (Gelb 1980, nos. 3432–3442)

entries.note: PH 7a .3 JA-RU-MA-NE (GORILA I 295), at the head of a line whose left edge is broken through JA: sign-groups may have stood before it, as well as a divider. The line breaks after NE, where a trace may be a dotted unit stroke (note .3). Yarīmān, the yaqtul of √r-w-m with the hypocoristic -ān: Ugarit has the name, yrmn, syllabic ia/ya-ri-ma-nu/na (DULAT 966; Kinlaw 1967, 132), beside bare yrm, the JA-RE-MI of HT 87, both clipped from the Amorite Yarim-DN names (Gelb 1980, nos. 3432–3442: Yarim-Lim, Yarim-Addu). Weak point: RU for the ri of ia-ri-ma-nu. Rival: a yaqtul from rummān 'pomegranate' (semitic_roots 2699). One attestation. See JA-RE-MI.

entries.meaning: personal name, '(he) lives', the bare form of the Amorite Yawi-DN names

cognates.Amorite: Ya-wi-dIM, Ya-wi-AN, Ya-wi-i-la, Ya-wi-dD[a-gan], hypocoristic Ya-wi-ya (ARM VII 169.5) at Mari (Huffmon 1965, 39, 70–72)
cognates.Amorite (rival): ia-wi-AN yahwî-ʾilu 'ʾIlu shall exist', √h-w-y 'be' (ARM 25 48; Buck 2018, 336; Gelb 1980, no. 3591)

entries.note: ZA 14 .4 JA-WI, the last group on the line, against the original right edge, with no numeral; the surface beneath it is blank, .5 keeps only traces at the broken lower left and .6 is vacat (GORILA III 180–181). It is the last word of the inscription, though signs may have followed on the lost lower left. Yawī, the bare form of the Mari names Ya-wi-dIM, Ya-wi-AN, Ya-wi-i-la and Ya-wi-dD[a-gan], beside the hypocoristic Ya-wi-ya (Huffmon 1965, 39, 70); Huffmon takes ya-wi with ya-ah-wi from *ḥwy 'live, give life' (1965, 71–72). Rival: √h-w-y 'be, become', ia-wi-AN yahwî-ʾilu 'ʾIlu shall exist' (Buck 2018, 336; semitic_roots 1546), the alternative Huffmon names. One attestation.

entries.meaning: righteous, upright (clipped form of yasaramu; may converge with *y-s "to heal" in onomastic contexts—cf. Greek ἰάομαι, Iāsōn, no secure IE etymology)

cognates.Amorite: JŚR 'be straight': jaśar, jīśar, jaśarum (Gelb AS 21, 22)
cognates.Akkadian: išaru 'normal, prosperous, just' (CAD I/J 224)

entries.note: MA Zb 8, bare JA-SA on a clay vessel, and PH 16b, on a fragmentary lame: two standalone witnesses at two sites, the clipped yašar 'righteous, upright' without the mimated -am of the formula word JA-SA-SA-RA-ME, an epithet in short votive texts. SA writes both s and š, so standalone JA-SA also admits *y-s 'to heal'. Rival: the healer, from Greek ἰάομαι 'to heal'; Beekes counts Ἰᾱ́σων among the words in which Pre-Greek initial ya- may stand as ἰα- (Beekes 2014, 7). Iāsōn and Iasion derive from it (Astour 1965, 276–282), and the agentive -ān (Gordon 1966 §155) gives *yasā-ān > Iāsōn, as Rpan from √r-p-ʾ (Astour 1965, 252); LB i-ja-te iatēr 'surgeon' at Pylos has the root. Against the rival, neither Malia nor Phaistos has an Iasion cult. Cf. SI-RU-TE, where the same merger joins √š-r-t and √š-y-r. See JA-SA-RA, JA-SA-SA-RA-ME and JA-SA-SA-RA-MA-NA.

entries.meaning: 'He hears'—yaqtal hypocoristic personal name with frozen nominative -ū

cognates.Hebrew: יִשְׁמָעֵאל (Yišmāʿēl / Ishmael) = "El hears"—√š-m-ʿ + ʾēl; שִׁמְעוֹן (Šimʿōn / Simeon) = "hearing"; שְׁמוּאֵל (Šəmūʾēl / Samuel) = "name/heard of El"
cognates.Ugaritic: yšmʿ—theophoric PN element in KTU personal names; šmʿ "to hear" in Ba'al cycle
cognates.Akkadian: šemû "to hear"; Šamû-Adda (EA 325) = "Addu has heard"—same root reversed
cognates.Punic: √š-m-ʿ in ŠMʿ-BʿL "Baal has heard" (Benz 1972); one of the productive PN roots in Carthaginian epigraphy
cognates.Amorite: Ya-ás-ma-ḫu-um, Yasmaḫ-Addu (Mari, APNM p. 132)

entries.note: ZA 15a, a Zakros wine allocation list: JA-SA-MU 5, beside SI-PI-KI and SA-MI-DA-E. yaśmaʿū 'he hears', √š-m-ʿ, the bare verbal element of a sentence name, as Yišmāʿēl 'El hears' without the god; SA writes s and š alike, and the final ʿ is unwritten. Cuneiform writes the guttural (Ya-ás-ma-aḫ-{d}IM) and Linear A drops it: JA-SA-MU is the Linear A shape of the Yašmaʿ hypocoristicon, Ya-ás-ma-ḫu-u[m] (Huffmon 1965, 132). The form is the yaqtal theme-vowel class with the frozen nominative -ū, the citation form of an independent name (Huffmon 1965, 104–15); the yaqtul yašmuʿ is the rival parse, both G imperfects with one Linear A surface. Rivals: yasamu with sāmek; Ya-ʾAšmu, an Eshmun short form, though the short forms of ʾŠMN write ʾŠM-, not *YŠM-. One attestation.

entries.meaning: righteous is (predicate before A-NA-NE ḥanān 'grace')

cognates.Hebrew: yāšar (יָשָׁר) 'straight, just, upright'; יְשֻׁרוּן Yəšurûn 'Jeshurun', Israel's name of honour, ישׁר + -ûn (HALOT 450), Dt 32:15, 33:5, 26, Isa 44:2
cognates.Akkadian: išaru 'straight'
cognates.Ugaritic: yšr 'uprightness' (DULAT 973); the verb is Hebrew yāšar 'to be straight, right' (HALOT 450)

entries.note: KN Zc 7, an inked vessel: JA-SA-RA-A-NA-NE, written without a divider. JA-SA-RA | A-NA-NE yašara ḥanān 'righteous is (thy) grace', the predicate before its noun, as kî-yāšār dəbar-YHWH 'for righteous is the word of YHWH' (Ps 33:4) and kî-yāšār YHWH 'for YHWH is righteous' (Ps 92:16). Ebla has the form as a name, a-sa-ra yašara 'the just one' (Pagan 1998, row 804). Weak point: no divider marks the boundary. One attestation. See JA-SA-SA-RA-ME and JA-SA.

entries.meaning: line-broken first portion of JA-SA-SA-RA-ME / yaššaram 'uprightly; in righteousness'; not independently attested as a bare lemma

cognates.Hebrew: yāšār 'straight, upright' (HALOT 450); mêšārîm 'uprightly', mêšārîm tišpəṭû, Ps 58:2 (HALOT 578)
cognates.Amorite: JŚR 'be straight': jaśar, jaśara (Gelb AS 21, 22)

entries.note: IO Za 16, a fragmentary square serpentine libation table from the Iouktas peak sanctuary (HM 5317), reads JA-SA-SA-RA- / -ME across a line break without a divider: the break falls inside the word, which is JA-SA-SA-RA-ME yaššaram. PK Za 4 preserves only A-SA-SA-RA-[ at a broken edge. Compare Amorite IA-SA-RA-AM (Gelb 1980, no. 3448). One attestation. See JA-SA-SA-RA-ME and JA-SA-SA-RA-MA-NA.

entries.meaning: in righteousness indeed; uprightly indeed

cognates.Akkadian: mīšaru 'redress; justice' (CAD M/2 116)
cognates.Amorite: JŚR 'be straight': jaśar, jaśara (Gelb AS 21, 22)

entries.note: KN Za 10 writes JA-SA-SA-RA-MA / NA across the side break without a divider, so the sequence is one graphic word. Amorite IA-SA-RA-AM attests accusative /yašaram/ (Gelb 1980, no. 3448), the Semitic manner accusative 'uprightly, in righteousness'. NA is the emphatic or topical clitic =na, as Ugaritic -n or -(Vn)na (Tropper 2000, §§89.1–2). SA-SA writes the geminate šš, as in JA-SA-SA-RA-ME. Weak point: /yaššaram=na/ is unattested outside Crete. One attestation. See JA-SA-SA-RA-ME, JA-SA-SA-RA and JA-SA.

entries.meaning: in righteousness (adverbial accusative in -am of √y-š-r; also 'righteously'); rival: substantivized "the upright/proper [thing]" in an object slot. Polysemic layer: masculine divine name Yasharam (Akk. Mīšarum, Phoen. Misor)

cognates.Hebrew: yāšār (יָשָׁר) 'upright, straight, righteous' (Deut 32:4, Ps 119:137, 1 Kgs 9:4, Prov 2:7); yōšer (יֹשֶׁר) 'uprightness, equity' (Ps 111:8, Prov 2:13); √y-š-r 'to be straight'; Yeshurun (יְשֻׁרוּן) poetic name for Israel = 'the upright one' (Deut 32:15, 33:5, 33:26, Isa 44:2); cf. Num 23:10 yĕšārīm (Balaam's pun on Yeshurun)
cognates.Ugaritic: yšr 'straight, upright' (DULAT 973); yšr in ritual context = moral/cultic fitness
cognates.Akkadian: ešēru 'to be/go straight, prosper' (CAD E 354); išaru 'straight, just, normal'; mīšaru 'justice, equity' (CAD M/II 116)—Hammurabi's mīšarum edicts: royal debt-release decrees that 'set things straight'
cognates.Arabic: yasara (يسر) 'to be easy, smooth'; yasār 'ease, prosperity'

entries.note: √y-š-r 'to be straight, upright, righteous.' SA writes š (cf. SA-SA-ME sesame on HT 23a: LB sa-sa-ma, Ug. ššmn); SA-SA writes the geminate šš (di Mino, Ya Diktu); the same root takes one SA, with no gemination written, in JA-SA-RA (KN Zc 7) and I-MI-SA-RA (HT 27a). RA writes the accusative -am, against RU for nominative -um, and ME the mimation: yaššaram 'in righteousness', as Amorite JAŚAR-AM, IA-SA-RA-AM, classed accusative (Gelb 1980, no. 3448). Rival: the object of the verb, 'an offering, a gift, a dedication' (Davis 2026, 55; Thomas 2020). Whole on IO Za 6 (GORILA V 25), PS Za 2 (IV 54), TL Za 1 (IV 59) and IO Za 12, one line, second SA and ME dotted (Karetsou, Godart and Olivier, Kadmos 24, 1985, 143); IO Za 2 has JA-SA-SA-RA-[, ME restored by GORILA (V 19), IO Za 9 ]JA-SA-SA-, RA-ME restored (V 33), and PK Za 14 JA-SA-SA-[ at the broken edge (IV 40). Cf. PL Zf 1 JA-SA-SA-RA-[ME?], a damaged vertical trace after RA; SAM Wa 1 (Samothrace) JA-SA SA-RA, without -ME, on a nodule with TE 10 ¹⁄₁₆; and KH Zc 106 ]-SA-SA-RA-MI (RILA-S1), broken before SA, the formula in LM IIIA1 with MI for ME.
entries.source: Gordon 1966; di Mino; Gelb 1980; Davis 2026; Thomas 2020; GORILA

entries.meaning: O Šumāt! (vocative yā + divine name, plural of *šum- 'name')
entries.cognates: Amorite Šumat-Yaraḥ, Šumat-ʾIlī, Šumatān, and Šumatānum (Gelb 1980, AS 21, nos. 5581–5582, 5588–5589); Common Semitic *šum-/šim- ‘name’ and Amorite sum- ‘name (> posterity)’ (Huffmon 1965, pp. 247–249, 252).
entries.note: JA SU-MA-TU: JA is the vocative yā, as JA-DI-KI-TU /yā Diktu/ in the same formula position. Huffmon lists Amorite sumat- as an unexplained name element and reports Birot's proposal that it is a plural of sum- ‘name (> posterity)’: *šum- with *-āt gives Šumāt. SU-MA-TU writes /šu-mā-t/, TU carrying a dead vowel after final /t/ and the long vowel unmarked. Amorite has the element in Šumat-Yaraḥ, Šumat-ʾIlī, Šumatān and Šumatānum (Gelb 1980, nos. 5581–5582, 5588–5589; Huffmon 1965, 57, 247–249, 252). GORILA V 64–65 and Davis read the next sign as OLIV, giving yā Šumāt | OLIV 1; Metaxa-Muhly 1984 and Finkelberg 1990 read syllabic RE, which would lengthen the name. The slot names the deity addressed, and Phoenician makes 'Name' divine in Astarte-Šembaal, Ug. ʿṯtrt šm bʿl (Krahmalkov 2000, 392), and Šem-ʾIl 'Il is the Name' (468). Weak point: no held form names a deity Šumāt; the element stands only in Amorite personal names. See SI-MA.
entries.source: di Mino; Birot, TEM III, p. 29, apud Huffmon 1965, p. 252; Gelb 1980
entries.root_meaning: name, posterity (proposed Amorite plural; Birot, apud Huffmon 1965, p. 252)

entries.meaning: gentilic 'the Idaean' (of Mount Ida); rivals the personal name 'He knows' and the gentilic 'Judean'

cognates.Hebrew: yād 'hand' (HALOT 386), the root of Ida (see I-DA); for the rivals, Yĕdîʿăʾēl (יְדִיעֲאֵל), a y-d-ʿ name (1 Chr 11:45; 26:2), and yehūdī (יְהוּדִי) 'Judean'
cognates.Amorite: for the rival, JDʿ 'to know' as a name element (Gelb 1980, glossary); JADAʿ+JAT-UM (Gelb 1980, no. 3168); bare JID-I, written I-DI (no. 2432)
cognates.Akkadian: for the rival, ia-ú-du 'Judah' (Sennacherib, 701 BCE)

entries.note: HT 8a: JE-DI OLE+KI 10, heading the list; HT 36: JE-DI GRA+QE 44½; HT 122b: JE-DI · *346 · VIR+[?], heading a roster of men; HT 140: JE-DI · OLE+KI 1½ in mid-line, JE damaged, with room for a lost sign before it. A recipient on three tablets. yedī 'the Idaean', gentilic of Mount Ida. Rivals: yēdīʿ 'he knows' as a personal name, with ʿ unwritten (Hebrew Yĕdîʿăʾēl, 1 Chr 11:45; Amorite JADAʿ+JAT-UM, Gelb 1980, no. 3168); yehūdī 'Judean', which leaves the ū of -hū- unwritten (U writes /hu/ in U-NA, so the expected spelling is JE-U-DI) and needs Judah, first attested under Tiglath-pileser III (c. 734 BCE), some 700 years after LM IB. See I-DA and JA-DI.

entries.meaning: He gave (PN, qatal 3ms of √y-t-n 'to give')—straight theophoric truncation: Yatana-DN 'DN-gave,' same root as Hebrew Nāṯān, Ugaritic Yattin-Haddu, Amorite Yantin-Dagan, Yattin-Dagan (Gelb 1980, nos. 2986, 3555)

cognates.Ugaritic: ytn (II) PN, syllabic ia-ta-nu, PRU 3 94 (RS 16.245):4 (DULAT 977); /y-t-n/ 'to give, grant' (DULAT 974); Yatanu, Milki-Yatanu in the Akkadian texts of Ugarit (Kinlaw 1967, 135, 81)
cognates.Phoenician: ytn PN 'gave', Ia-a-tu-na; YTNʾL Ia-ta-na-e-li 'God gave' (Krahmalkov 220)
cognates.Amorite: NTN 'give': jantin, natūnum (Gelb AS 21, 27)

entries.note: HT Wa 1020, its only attestation; HT 88 has none. Yatana 'he gave', the G 3ms perfect of √y-t-n in a name or title slot, a theophoric name element, Yatana-DN. Ugaritic keeps ytn where Hebrew has n-t-n: G /yatana/, prefix /yittinu/ with the n assimilated (Huehnergard 2012), BH nātan. The masculine of A-TA-NA-TE ʾAtanat, the feminine of the root with I-y > ʾ. Ugarit writes the same name ia-ta-nu and ia-te-nu (DULAT 977; Kinlaw 1967, 135), E for a within it. Weak point: there the e falls on the second syllable; every held form has ya in the first.

entries.meaning: wine-lords, wine-stewards (personnel category)

cognates.Akkadian: māru 'son/lord', plural mārē/mārū

entries.note: ZA 4a *28B-NU-MA-RE 13, ZA 5b *28B-NU-MA-RE 20, ZA 15a *28B-NU-MA-RE 6, each followed by SI-PI-KI 'pourings' on the Zakros wine tablets, among personal names: a personnel category, the stewards who administer the palace wine. A compound of yīnu 'wine', √y-y-n (Heb. yayin, HALOT 409; Ug. yn, DULAT 954), and mārē 'lords, sons', √m-r-y, cf. Aramaic mrʾ 'lord, master' (DNWSI 682); *28B writes ji, a proposed value, and WE reads the word as well, wēnu-mārē, wēnu < *wayn. Rival: a personal name, from its recurring slot beside SI-PI-KI (Negri, SMEA 43/1, 2001, 82). Three attestations. See VIN.

entries.meaning: food, provisions (section heading)

cognates.Akkadian: ukultu 'food, fodder'

entries.note: ZA 6b: heads the first section, over GRA+PA 50¼, VIN+RA 40, VIN+KA 10; *312-TA₂ heads the second. ʾukulti 'food, provisions': Akk. ukultu 'food, fodder' (CAD U/W 62). KU-JU writes kul (JU = lu, as in KU-RE-JU), and initial I- the ʾu. The line reads I-KU-JU-TI-*28B: the word spans a fragment join, with a gap at the crack in the diplomatic copy (GORILA III 158–159), and *28B stands as a separate sign before GRA+PA. Cf. AB 28 (I), a different sign, as a single or transaction sign before GRA+PA (Salgarella 2020, 73 n. 55; Steele 2024, 58). One attestation.
entries.source: di Mino; CAD U/W; GlOS 1; Salgarella 2020; Steele 2024

entries.meaning: until, as far as (preposition)

cognates.Ugaritic: ʿd /ʿad(ē)/ 'up to, as far as, until' (Huehnergard 2012)
cognates.Hebrew: ʿad (עַד) 'until'; ʿad ʾăšer dāq 'until it was fine' (Exod 32:20, Deut 9:21)
cognates.Phoenician: ʿd 'as far as, up to', Phoenician and Punic (Krahmalkov 2000, 360)

entries.note: KN Zc 6 .2 opens with A-DI after .1 QI-TI-RI and governs DA-KI-TI: ʿadi daqqati '(ground) until fine', as Hebrew grinds the golden calf ʿad ʾăšer-dāq 'until it was fine' (Exod 32:20; Deut 9:21); Phoenician ʿd 'as far as, until' (Krahmalkov 2000, 360). Evans (PoM I 615 n. 1) reports a dividing mark before DA, which GORILA IV 121 does not print. Initial A- writes ʿa-, the ʿ unwritten. One attestation.

entries.meaning: fine (powder), ground fine

cognates.Hebrew: daq, f. daqqâ (דַּקָּה) 'fine, crushed': qəṭōret sammîm daqqâ 'finely ground sweet incense' (Lev 16:12); hādēq 'very fine', of the sanctuary incense (Exod 30:36)

entries.note: KN Zc 6 register .2, after QI-TI-RI 'my incense' and A-DI 'until': incense ground fine, the Hebrew qəṭōret … daqqâ (Lev 16:12), Ug. dqt 'small, tiny, fine' (DULAT 276). Written as one unit with PA-KU 'flask' (DA-KI-TI-PA-KU, closed by a divider before NI-JA-NU). QI-TI-RI is masculine, so DA-KI-TI is a noun 'fine powder'. Rival: genitive of the divine name, 'of Daqqatu' (Ugaritic dqt, DN 'the Little One', DULAT 276), cf. JA-DI-KI-TU and A-DI-KI-TE-TE. Younger reads A-DI-DA-KI-TI-PA-KU as a muddled A-DI-KI-TE (Younger, Linear A Texts, Other Texts: Knossos). Cf. SKO Zc 2 ]DE-KI-TI[ (Skoteino cave, a painted vessel), broken on both sides.
entries.source: di Mino; DULAT; Younger, Linear A Texts

entries.meaning: thin bread, wafers (qualifier of *309C KIKKARU)

cognates.Arabic: ruqāq (الرُقاق) 'thin bread'; ruqāqa 'a single thin, round cake of bread' (Lane 1131)
cognates.Hebrew: rāqîq (רָקִיק) 'wafer', beside kikkar leḥem 'round of bread' (Exod 29:23)
cognates.Akkadian: raqqatu D '(a type of bread)', Emar (CAD R 171)
cognates.Old Syrian: Emar NINDA ru-qa-nu ruqqānu, Ebla ra-ga-gu raqaq 'thin cake, waffle' (GlOS 2, 166)

entries.note: TY 2 .5 *309C-[?]-RU-KA 30, one of eight qualifiers joined to *309. RU-KA writes ruqāq, the final q unwritten. Exod 29:23 sets rāqîq beside kikkar leḥem, the pairing TY 2 shows; Akk. raqqatu, a bread at Emar (CAD R 171). Sign order follows GORILA's facsimile, RU over KA (GORILA I 324–325). Rival: a place or recipient name, as the other qualifiers can be read. The hook atop *309C is joined to the circle, as the curl on *309 at .3 and .6 (GORILA I 325). Weak point: *309 = KIKKARU is a proposed value. One attestation.

entries.meaning: personal name ('Where are you?')

cognates.Amorite: ʾAjak-u, written A-JA-KU (Gelb 1980, no. 320); ʾAjak-um, A-IA-KU-UM (no. 300); the ʾAja- 'where?' names, nos. 285–319

entries.note: KN Zf 13, the last four signs of an undivided 19-sign spiral, ending at the centre of the bezel; the start of the word is not marked and KU is underdotted (GORILA IV 152–153). Amorite ʾAjak-u (Gelb 1980, no. 320). Rival: Akk. ajakku, a temple structure (CAD A/1 224–225). See A-RE-NE-SI-DI-*301-PI-KE-PA-JA-TA-RI-SE-TE-RI-MU-A-JA-KU.

entries.meaning: personal name; Egyptian kꜣḥs, a name under Senusret III; rival kabsi 'young ram'

cognates.Egyptian: kꜣḥs, a personal name (PNM v6, personal_names_id 142607804; Ranke II, 322.3)
cognates.Akkadian: kabsu 'young male sheep' (CAD K 23), the rival

entries.note: PH Wc 37 KA-*314-SI *320, a Phaistos roundel (MM II), all three signs whole (GORILA II 94). Egyptian kꜣḥs, a name under Senusret III (Ranke II, 322.3; PNM v6, Louvre C 173), with *314 read ḥa and the final vowel dead. Rival, *314 as a variant of PU₂: kabsi 'young ram', Akk. kabsu (CAD K 23), Heb. kebeś, a roundel commodity. One witness.
entries.source: Ilin-Tomich 2025 (PNM v6), s.v. kꜣḥs; di Mino

entries.meaning: the Easterner, √q-d-m + -ān (Gordon: Cadmos + -ān)

cognates.Amorite: qadmānum 'eastern' (Gelb AS 21, 29); PN QADM-AN-UM (Gelb AS 21 no. 1704)
cognates.Akkadian: qudmu, qadmu 'early times; front' (CAD Q 295)

entries.note: HT 29: KA-DU-MA-NE 1, the last entry of a list of names counted in ones and twos (RU-MA-TA 2, PA-JA-RE 1, DI-JA-I 2, SA-*323-MI 1, A-RE-DA-I 2). Qadmān 'the Easterner', √q-d-m 'front, east' with -ān: Amorite ga-ad-ma-nu-um Qadmānum 'eastern' (Gelb 1980, no. 1704; GlOS 1, 341); Ug. qdmn 'eastern; leader' (GlOS 1, 341). One attestation. See QE-DE-MI-NU.

entries.meaning: the Canaanite (ethnonymic designation)

cognates.Ugaritic: knʕny GN 'Canaanite'; Mari LÚ Ki-na-aḫ-num, Alalakh LÚ URU Ki-in-a-nim (AT 48:5) (DULAT 444)
cognates.Punic: chanani, the people's name for themselves, and knʿny (Krahmalkov 236)

entries.note: KH Wc 2005, a Khania roundel, the only word: an ethnic designation in a record of trade or personnel. kanaʿanītī 'the Canaanite': -NI-TI writes the gentilic -ītī, the nisbe of DU-RU-WI ḏu-luwwī 'the Levite', and the ʿ goes unwritten. Heb. kənaʿănî 'Canaanite' (HALOT 485), Amarna Kinaḫḫi 'Canaan' (EA 8:15), with the gentilic 'Canaanite' at EA 9:19; Punic Chanani, the people's name for themselves (Augustine, apud Krahmalkov 2000, 236). One attestation.

entries.meaning: place name, 25 men in the HT 97a roster beside PA-I-TO

cognates.Eblaite: ga-nu-ti, a personal name (EbDA, ARET 20 15 r. 3, 11)

entries.note: HT 97a: KA-RU VIR+KA 82 heads *327 33, KA-NU-TI 25, PA-I-TO 6, DI 4, NA-TI 4, MA-DI 5, TA-TI 2, DE-[ ] 3, men by place, KA-RU 82 their total (Younger, Linear A Texts). Ebla has the name ga-nu-ti (ARET 20 15 r. 3, 11). One witness.

entries.meaning: village, settlement (kapar); rival an institution

cognates.Akkadian: kapru A 'village, farm' (CAD K 189)

entries.note: Six Haghia Triada attestations. First word on HT 102 (SA-RA₂ GRA 976 follows; KU-RO 1060), HT 94a (VIR+[?] 62 follows on the line; KU-RO 110), HT 6a (divider, then DA-TA-RA) and HT 105 (broken after PA; VIR+[?] 234 below). An entry with ½ on HT 8b and HT 140; KA-PA-QE 5¾ on HT 6a. Abbreviated KA on HT 140 (Montecchi 2010, 15). Hebrew and Aramaic kĕpar 'village', with final /r/ unwritten; Bronze Age kapr 'village' at Ebla, Alalakh VII and on the Euphrates, Ug. kpr (GlOS 1, 315). The ½ entries make an institution or entity the rival to a place. Rival: Akkadian gabbu 'all' (Gordon, via Rendsburg 1996, 38), spelt ka-pa-šu-nu and qa-pa-šu-ma at Nuzi, where it follows a total of men (Gordon 1934, 20 §100). It fits the heads of HT 94a and HT 105, but not the ½ entries, and HT 94a closes with KU-RO. See KU-PA-RI.

entries.meaning: bowl; rival kubburu 'extra share'

cognates.Hebrew: kəpôr 'bowl', kəpôrê zāhāb šəlōšîm 'thirty golden bowls' (Ezra 1:10); among the temple vessels (1 Chr 28:17)
cognates.Emar: 1 DUG kap-pár-ra, 2 DUG kap-[pár-ru], a vessel (GlOS 1, 315)

entries.note: HT 115a .5 KA-PO-RU 1, whole and undotted, on its own line after A-SE-JA ⅔ 'portion of the fire offering' and before RI-SU-MA · SU, under GRA+BOSm (GORILA I 189). kapōru 'bowl': PO keeps the ō of the Canaanite shift, as Hebrew kəpôr 'small metal bowl' (Ezra 1:10; HALOT 492). Rival: kubburu 'extra (payment), preferential (share)', Emar ka₄-ku-bu-ru, Alalakh ku-ub-bu-rum (GlOS 1, 299), which needs PO for bu. One attestation.

entries.meaning: 'Companion' (personal name)
entries.note: HT 98a: KA-RI-*310-I ¼, the last of the fractional issues, after RO-KE ½. Qarīnī 'Companion': *310 = in joins RI as it joins KI in KI-*310-RE kinnār, so KA-RI-IN-I writes qa-rīn-ī; Arabic qarana 'be someone's companion', Sabaic qrn 'guard' (Biella 467), with the -ī of a personal name. Rival: Qarnī 'horn', as KA-RO-NA Qarna and Mari Qarni-Lim (ARM 26/1, 599). Rival: Akk. karānu 'wine' (CAD K 202). Weak point: *310 = in is a proposed value. One attestation.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'horn'

cognates.Akkadian: qarnu "horn" (CAD Q 136)

entries.note: HT 11a (Haghia Triada, Villa Magazine, LM IB): A-RU-RA ]3, KA-RO-NA 2, *322-RI 1, KU-RO 10, three entries in one total, so a recipient. KA writes /qa/: the k-signs cover k, g and q (Gordon 1966, §142). Horn names are common across Semitic: Amorite Qar-ni-li-im (Huffmon 1965, 58; element qarn- 'horn, strength', 259), Middle Babylonian Qarni-Ana (ORACC P503266), Middle Assyrian Qarna-Adad (ORACC P282214), Neo-Assyrian Qarnaya (ORACC P336263), and Hebrew Qeren-happûk, a daughter of Job (Job 42:14). One attestation. See I-KU-RI-NA.

entries.meaning: carafe, drinking vessel (Akkadian karpatu; Ugaritic krpn)

cognates.Ugaritic: krpn 'cup, goblet' (DULAT 452), where DULAT records Stieglitz 1971's equation with Minoan ka-ro-pa₃
cognates.Akkadian: karpatu 'earthen pot; a measure' (CAD K 219); karpu 'pot, earthen container' (CAD K 221)

entries.note: HT 31: after the vessel ideogram *416-VS (quantity 10), one of Gordon's HT 31 vessel quartet (Gordon 1966, §115). Gordon read ka-ro-pa as karpu, Akk. karpatu 'earthen container, pot' (CAD K 219), one of the commonest vessel words in cuneiform. PA₃ = ba writes k-r-b, but the root is √k-r-p: a single p is voiced between vowels, here between o and a. Stieglitz took up the identification with the Akkadian and Ugaritic cognates (Stieglitz 1971, 110). Rendsburg cites 'Min. ka-ro-pà (HT 31.3) (Gordon, EML, 26, 30, 39; Stieglitz 1971)' as cognate with Ugaritic krpn 'carafe, goblet, flagon' (Ugaritic Dictionary, forthcoming). Its six Ugaritic passages (El blessing Kirta, ʿAnat drinking wine, Baʿal's feast) make it a drinking vessel. Ugaritic krpn 'cup, goblet' (DULAT 452) carries the afformative -n (Dahood 1965, 161, apud Stieglitz 1971, 110 n. 2) that Minoan karp- lacks. Weak point: PA₃ = ba is a proposed value; Gordon's p (PA₃ as PA) gives √k-r-p without the voicing. One attestation.
entries.source: Gordon 1966; Stieglitz 1971; Rendsburg, Ugaritic Dictionary; DULAT; CAD K; di Mino

entries.meaning: Kothar (divine craftsman god)

cognates.Hebrew: kōšēr (כּוֹשֵׁר) "skill, success" (Eccl 2:21, 4:4; BDB 507); keter (כֶּתֶר) "crown" (Esth 1:11, 2:17; Kabbalistic Keter, highest sefirah)
cognates.Akkadian: kašāru "to restore, repair" (CAD K 282)

entries.note: KH 41 (Khania, clay tablet, LM IB): 3 · KA-TA-RE · [, broken at both ends, the numeral before the name as in the HT 86a allocations. Kothar, √k-ṯ-r: KA, not QA, which writes √q-ṭ-r in QI-TI-RI, and TA, not *118 ṬA, set it apart from qṭr 'incense'; TA writes its ṯ, as scribes wrote ṯ in the T-series beside ZU (di Mino, Ya Diktu 16–17 n. 27). Khania is western Crete's second archive, with strong Near Eastern exchange. Rival: √k-t-r 'crown', which TA writes the same way; it shares a biconsonantal *K-T with √k-ṯ-r, as √k-n-s does with √k-n-š. One attestation.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Disk, Round loaf'

cognates.Amorite: KAKKAR-I (KA-KA-RI), personal name (Gelb 1980, AS 21, no. 3957)
cognates.Akkadian: kakkaru 'metal disk (a talent); round loaf' (CAD K 49)

entries.note: HT 94b under KI-RO: TU-MA 1, PA-TA-NE 1, DE-DI 1, KE-KI-RU 1, SA-RU 1, KU-RO 5, one unit each with no commodity sign: a name. *kikkar- 'disk, round loaf' (semitic_roots 1097) as a name, with the i of Heb. kikkār, KE writing ki as RE writes ri in KI-RE-TA₂; Akk. kakkaru (CAD K 49), Amorite KAKKAR-I (Gelb AS 21 no. 3957). Weak point: KI for the a of kikkar-. Rival: a title. KI-KI-RA-JA (HT 85b) is on the same root. One attestation. See QA-KU-RE and QE-KU-RE.

entries.meaning: lyre (Hebrew kinnōr כִּנּוֹר)

cognates.Akkadian: kinnāru 'lyre', Mari and Ugarit (CAD K 387)

entries.note: HT 37, an inventory tablet: KI-*310-RE with quantity 1. With *310 = in the word reads ki-in-re, kinnār 'lyre', the anchor for that value. Heb. kinnōr (כִּנּוֹר), the lyre David played before Saul (1 Sam 16:23). Emar writes the lyre ki-in-na-ru, in closing the first syllable as *310 does (Pentiuc 2001, 98). Weak point: *310 = in is a proposed value; /ni/ gives the same k-n-r. One attestation.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Dark' (√ḳ-d-r 'be dark'; cf. Hebrew Qēdār)

cognates.Hebrew: Qēdār (קֵדָר) 'Kedar', son of Ishmael, an Arabian people; qādar (קָדַר) 'be dark, mourn' (HALOT 1072)

entries.note: HT 117a: KI-DA-RO 1 in the SA-TA roster, beside KU-KU-DA-RA, KO-SA-I-TI, DA-MI-NU and DA-NE-KU-TI, each counted once; HT 47a: KI-DA-RO 5 after KU-PA₃-NA-TU 20, DU 20 and PI 10. A personal name, Qidaru 'Dark', from √ḳ-d-r 'be dark', as Heb. Qēdār, Ishmael's son and an Arabian people (Gen 25:13), from qādar 'be dark, mourn'. Rival: PS *ḳidr- 'earthenware' (Ar. qidr, Heb. qədērā, Aram. qidrā), the noun of A-KI-DA-RO (KH Wa 1002) ʾa-qidrū 'the earthenware', with A- the article or a prosthetic aleph. Two attestations, both lists of people.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'protection (of the god)' (Akk. kidinnu)

cognates.Akkadian: kidinnu "divine protection"; OB personal names Ki-din-Amurrum, Ki-di-nu-um (CAD K 342–343)

entries.note: HT93a .3 KI-DI-NI 5 J H, in a grain list of recipients with DI-RI-NA, A-SE, SA-RA₂ and QA-QA-RU. Akkadian kidinnu 'divine protection', in Old Babylonian personal names Ki-din-Amurrum and Ki-di-nu-um (CAD K 342–343); the bare name is Middle Assyrian ki-di-ni Kidinni (ORACC tcma/assur, Assur 3/1 no. 2, r. 27). Rival: kittini 'linen' (Akk. kitû, Ug. ktn), which needs DI for ti and a textile in a grain list. One attestation.

alternative_readings.note: linen: Akk. kitû "flax, linen" (CAD K 473); Ug. ktn "a type of tunic" (DULAT 464); Heb. kuttōnet (Gen 3:21; 37:3). Needs DI for ti and a textile entry in a grain list.

entries.meaning: priests (plural + mimation)
entries.note: ZA 5a, under the heading *21F-*118 · VIN-SU: KI-NI-MA 7, then O-TA-NI-ZA-SE 6. kihinīma 'priests', the plural with mimation: Heb. kōhănîm, sg. kōhēn (HALOT 461), Ugarit khn 'priest' (GlOS 1, 302), the qātil participle, Ug. khn /kāhinu/, pl. khnm /kāhinūma/ (Huehnergard 2012, 59, 149). KI writes the i of Arb. kihānat 'divination' (Lane 3004). Ugarit lists priests the same way: khnm 3 GUR ZÌ.KAL.KAL 'priests: 3 kor of fine flour' (KTU 4.38:1; DULAT 428–29). The medial h goes unwritten, as in A-KO-A-NE, RA-ME raḥmē, JA-JA ḥayyā and Neo-Punic hknt 'the priestess' beside hkhnt (Tomback 1978, 139–40). Weak point: one attestation. See A-KO-A-NE.
entries.source: di Mino; GlOS 1; HALOT; Huehnergard 2012; DULAT; Lane; Tomback 1978

entries.meaning: garden, orchard; rival qīru 'hot bitumen'

cognates.Akkadian: kirû 'garden, orchard, palm grove' (CAD K 411); qīru 'hot bitumen' (CAD Q 270), the rival

entries.note: HT 103 KI-RA 5½, after DA-KU-SE-NE 1; ZA 8 opens KI-RA · A-TA-RE · NI 'figs' ½. kirû 'garden, orchard' (CAD K 411), base kiri- (Huehnergard 1997, 126), fits these horticultural entries. Rival: qīru 'hot bitumen' (CAD Q 270), spelled qi-ra in the Middle Assyrian Laws (KAV 1 v 76), with KI writing qi.
entries.source: di Mino; GORILA I; CAD K; CAD Q; Huehnergard 1997

entries.meaning: Kret (eponym of Crete)

cognates.Ugaritic: krt Kirta, king of bt ḫbr and hero of KTU 1.14–1.16; krt ṯʿ 'Kirta the Hero' (KTU 1.15 II 8; DULAT 453)
cognates.Hebrew: kārat (כָּרַת) 'to cut', wəhikrattî ʾet-kərētîm 'and I will cut off the Kerethites' (Ezek 25:16); negeb hakkərētî 'the Negeb of the Kerethite' (1 Sam 30:14)
cognates.Akkadian: karātu 'to cut off' (CAD K 215); Ki-ir-ta, a king of Mitanni and a man of Alalakh (Niedorf 2008, 489)
cognates.Linear B: ke-re-te-u Krētheus, a man's name (PY Ea 59; Ventris and Chadwick 1956, 420), set beside krt by DULAT 453

entries.note: HT 85b and HT 129 (GORILA): Kret, the eponym of Crete, as in the Ugaritic Epic of Kret (KTU 1.14–16). The word uses TA₂ (AB 66), where the gentilic KI-RE-TA-NA has plain TA (AB 59); RE alternates with RI in KI-RI-TA₂. √k-r-t 'to cut, make a covenant' has plain PS *t in every branch: Akk. karātu, Ug. krt with t, which Ugaritic keeps apart from ṯ, and Heb. כָּרַת with taw, where PS *ṯ would give š. TA₂ then marks either a Cretan pronunciation of the island's own name, interdental, aspirated or palatal, which foreign scribes fitted to plain t, or a substrate place name with a non-dental stop, later heard as √k-r-t. Ug. krt is /kirta/, the protagonist Kirta, and lkrt /li-kirta/ 'belonging to the story of Kirta'; Huehnergard rejects the vocalization 'keret' as non-Ugaritic, and BH kərētī 'Kerethite' differs in its vowels (Huehnergard 2012, 60, 68). Kret here is the consonantal name krt; Linear A Kirēta shares the i of /kirta/. Ki-ir-ta is a Bronze Age name: Kirta, an early king of Mitanni, on his son's seal (Šu-ut-tar-na DUMU Ki-ir-ta LUGAL Ma-i-ta-ni), and Kirta son of Belata at Alalakh (Niedorf 2008, 489; ATmB 31.1–2, 353.3).
entries.source: Gordon 1966; Niedorf 2008; DULAT; Ventris and Chadwick 1956

entries.meaning: Cretan (gentilic: 'of Crete')

cognates.Hebrew: kərētîm (כְּרֵתִים) 'Kerethites': gôy kərētîm 'nation of Kerethites', beside kənaʿan ʾereṣ pəlištîm 'Canaan, land of the Philistines' (Zeph 2:5); wəhikrattî ʾet-kərētîm 'and I will cut off the Kerethites' (Ezek 25:16); hakkərētî wəhappəlētî 'the Kerethite and the Pelethite', David's guard (2 Sam 8:18)
cognates.Linear B: ke-re-te Krētes 'Cretans', an ethnic (PY An 128.3; Ventris and Chadwick 1956, 147); ke-re-si-jo we-ke 'of Cretan workmanship', of tripods (PY Ta 641, 709; Ventris and Chadwick 1956, 396)

entries.note: HT 2, HT 8a, HT 108 and HT 120, all at Haghia Triada: Kretan 'Cretan', the gentilic -ān on the name written KI-RE-TA₂ and KI-RI-TA₂, twice each; cf. Heb. kərētī 'Kerethite' (כְּרֵתִי). Ug. krt is /kirta/, the protagonist Kirta, and lkrt /li-kirta/ 'belonging to the story of Kirta'; Huehnergard rejects the vocalization 'keret' as non-Ugaritic, and BH kərētī differs in its vowels (Huehnergard 2012, 60, 68).

entries.meaning: Kret (variant spelling)
entries.cognates: see KI-RE-TA₂
entries.note: A spelling of KI-RE-TA₂ with RI for RE; the corpus form has TA₂. HT 114a and HT 121 both pair it with SA-RA₂ in one administrative template, SA-RA₂ read as a recipient or institution, the queen or the royal establishment. Huehnergard gives Ugaritic krt /kirta/ 'Kirta' and lkrt /li-kirta/ 'belonging to the story of Kirta', and rejects 'keret' as a Ugaritic vocalization (Huehnergard 2012, 60, 68). Biblical Hebrew kərētī 'Kerethite' differs in vocalism. For Bronze Age Ki-ir-ta, see KI-RE-TA₂. See KI-RE-TA-NA.

entries.meaning: owed, outstanding balance (deficit)—transaction term heading deficit sections

cognates.Akkadian: kalû 'hold back, detain'; adj. kalû 'held (back)' (ORACC CAMS/GKAB)

entries.note: KI-RO marks what is owed or outstanding, against KU-RO 'total'. HT 15: 684 + 570 = 1254 beside KI-RO 400, outstanding 400. KI-RO heads sections that close in KU-RO with exact sums (HT 88, six entries of 1, KU-RO 6; HT 117a, ten of 1, KU-RO 10; HT 94b, five of 1, KU-RO 5), and a total cannot head a list. On HT 1, KI-RO 197 stands before four quantities that sum to 336. HT 30's KI-RO section re-lists the main section's commodities in smaller quantities, the delivered and outstanding split. HT 34.6 balances: SA+MU+KU 100, then PA₃ 70 and KI-RO 30 (30 written over an erased 7), 70 handed over and 30 outstanding (Schrijver 2014, 7). Schoep reads 'deficit', clearest where KI-RO follows KU-RO with a smaller entry (HT 123a.9; less clearly HT 93b.1), with Killen's caveat (Schoep 2002, 163–164). KI-RO quantities are not summed into KU-RO; where a tablet marks the split, the residual is delivered less owed, and none of the 13 gives KI-RO the exact sum of the items above it. *kilʾu 'what is held back', from √k-l-ʾ 'hold back, withhold' (2998), RO for l, the glottal stop unwritten, -u the case ending: Heb. kālāʾ 'withhold, keep back', Akk. kalû 'hold back'. KU-RO kull- (√k-l-l) differs in vowel and third radical.

entries.meaning: cumin (Cuminum cyminum)

cognates.Akkadian: kamūnu / kammūnu—OB ration lists, medical texts
cognates.Linear B: ku-mi-no (𐀓𐀖𐀜)—Knossos/Pylos palatial spice inventories, 15th c. BCE

entries.note: On the HT Wc 3014 roundel, KU-MI-NA (side a) and QE (side b, the standalone qab-measure √q-b-b before the CAP caprid logogram) are separate entries. A Wanderwort: Sumerian U.GAMUN, Akk. kamūnu, Ug. kmn, Linear B ku-mi-no, Greek κύμινον; KU-MI-NA has the skeleton of ku-mi-no, a Semitic loan in Linear B. HT 54a.2 reads ]KU-MI-NA-QE[, broken at both ends (GORILA I 105). A-KU-MI-NA and A-DU-KU-MI-NA on ZA 10a are roster titles on the homograph kummi 'cella' + -ān, as SI-DU-QI-KU-MI.

entries.meaning: emmer (Akkadian loan)

cognates.Akkadian: kunāšu (kunīšu, kunšu) 'emmer' (CAD K 536); Nuzi ku-ni-šu, ku-ni-ši (HSS 14 163:1ff.; HSS 16 114:1; JEN 427:9; CAD K 537); Boğazköy ZÍD ku-ni-ši 'emmer flour' (AfO 16 48:21)
cognates.Ugaritic: polyglot [ÁŠ = ku-na]-šu = Hurrian ut-te = Ugaritic ku-sú-mu (GlOS 1, 323)

entries.note: HT 10a KU-NI-SU · heads a list of issues with no commodity logogram (SA-MA 4, DA-RE 16½, *305-RU 2½, DA-RI-DA 8, ME-ZA 3); HT 86a/b A-KA-RU · KU-NI-SU GRA+K+L 20, SA-RU 20, DI-DE-RU 20, QA-RA₂-WA 10, the grain sign after the word; HT 95a/b the same set with DA-ME, MI-NU-TE and QE-RA₂-U. kunīšu 'emmer', an Akkadian loan (Gordon 1966, §116): CAD K 536 lists kunīšu beside kunāšu, and Nuzi writes ku-ni-šu in grain issues, 1 imēr ku-ni-šu ana PN (HSS 14 163:1; CAD K 537). S writes the Akkadian š of PS *kunaṯ- (#1604), and the Ugarit polyglot sets [ku-na]-šu beside Ugaritic ku-sú-mu (GlOS 1, 323). GRA+KU abbreviates the word, and MI-NU-TE minūtu stands in the same set. Weak point: on HT 95a/b the word stands in a fixed set whose DA-ME and SA-RU take commodities elsewhere, as recipients do. Five attestations. See GRA+KU.
entries.source: di Mino; Gordon 1966; CAD K; GlOS 1

entries.meaning: priestess (fem. singular)
entries.note: KH 92 .1 A-DA-QIf-RI · KU-NI-TE 10[ (Younger, Linear A Texts): a counted entry, with ]NA-KI 1 on .2. kuhnēt 'priestess': Punic khnt 'priestess' (Krahmalkov 2000, 224), Ug. khn 'priest' (DULAT 428). KU writes the ū of Punic kūhen (KAI 159.6/7; Krahmalkov 2000, 419). Of the √k-h-n group with KI-NI-MA. One attestation. See A-KO-A-NE.

entries.meaning: personal name, hypocoristic of Kubaba in -aya, cf. Amorite Kubbiya
entries.root: Kubb-, short base of Kubaba (Sumerian Kug-Baba, Haas 1994, 406) + -aya

cognates.Amorite: KUBB-IJA (KU-UB-BI-IA), Mari (Gelb AS 21 no. 4149); KUBB-AN-UM (no. 4148)

entries.note: HT 116a: KU-PA-JA GRA 16, first of six grain recipients under U-TA-RO · TE ·, with PU-RA₂, SI+SE, PI-*34-TE, SI-KI-NE and QA-NU-MA. KU-PA-JA writes Kubbaya, the geminate unwritten, -aya the hypocoristic ending on Kubaba's short base, as -ān- on KU-PA₃-NU Kubānu; cf. Amorite KUBB-IJA at Mari, KUBB-AN-UM (Gelb AS 21 nos. 4148–4149) and the goddess Kupapa (Gelb 1980, 23). Rival: KU-PA quppa 'box, basket' (HT 110a, KH 29, ZA 11a/b) with -ya. One attestation.

entries.meaning: the villages, a group of men drawing grain; rival kaparrī 'junior shepherds'

cognates.Hebrew: kōper 'village', wᵉʿad kōper happᵉrāzî 'and to the village of the open country' (1 Sam 6:18); pl. kᵉpārîm, beʿārîm ûbakkᵉpārîm 'in the cities and in the villages' (1 Chr 27:25)
cognates.Akkadian: kaparru 'shepherd of low rank': ŠE.BA 7 LÚ ka-pa-ar-ri 'grain rations of 7 k.-shepherds' (Chagar Bazar, AOAT 1 206 A 931:16); rations ša LÚ.NA.GADA.MEŠ u LÚ ka-pa-ar-ri (ARM 5 71:6, 14) (CAD K 177), the rival

entries.note: PE 1 .2 KU-PA-RI VIR 5̣0[, whole, under the heading U-KA-RE A-SE-SI-NA; .3 GRA+PA 26½; .3–4 E-KA[ VIR 72, .4–5 GRA+PA 36: grain rations at ½ unit a head, VIR 53 restored from 26½ (Younger, Linear A Texts, after Tsipopoulou & Hallager 1996, 25–30). ku-pa-rī, plural oblique of *kupr 'village', Hebrew kōper (1 Sam 6:18), with the a of the qutl plural, as bōqer, pl. bᵉqārîm (Lam 3:23). KA-PA kapa(r) heads VIR+[?] 62 on HT 94a in the same frame. Rival: Akkadian kaparru 'shepherd of low rank', whose men draw grain rations at Chagar Bazar and Mari (CAD K 177), which needs KU for ka. One witness.

entries.meaning: the field (of), meadowland (heading of a grain-ration list); rivals ʾikkār 'ploughman', the personal name Ugār

cognates.Akkadian: ugāru 'grassland, meadow, arable land', a Sumerian loanword: construct ina ú-ga-ar ekallim 'from the meadow of the palace' (ARMT 23 244:10); kurummat 27 ṣābī ša ú-ga-re-e īpušū 'provisions for 27 men who worked the meadowlands' (BE 14 56a:26); DUMU.MEŠ ú-ga-ri-im 'the participants in the u.' (BIN 7 7:12) (CAD U/W 29–31)
cognates.Ugaritic: ủgr (I) 'field, soil', sg. suff. ủgrm (1.12 I 25); PN ủgr, syll. ú-ga-a[r (Ug 5 51:8), the rival (DULAT 27)

entries.note: PE 1 .1–2 U-KA-RE A-SE-SI-NA, two groups, the heading over KU-PA-RI kuparī VIR 5̣0[ and E-KA[ VIR 72, each with grain at ½ unit a head (Younger, Linear A Texts, after Tsipopoulou & Hallager 1996, 25–30). u-gā-r, the construct before A-SE-SI-NA ḥašīšin 'of hay', RE's vowel dead, as Mari ina ú-ga-ar ekallim 'from the meadow of the palace' (ARMT 23 244:10; CAD U/W 31). Men of the ugāru draw provisions in Akkadian: kurummat 27 ṣābī ša ú-ga-re-e īpušū 'provisions for 27 men who worked the meadowlands' (BE 14 56a:26; CAD U/W 30). Rivals: ʾikkār 'ploughman', Hebrew ʾikkār (2 Chr 26:10, pl. ʾikkārîm), U for ʾi a vowel mismatch; the PN Ugār (DULAT 27). One witness. See A-KA-RU, A-SE-SI-NA.

entries.meaning: of dry grass, of hay (genitive with nunation; ʾugār ḥašīšin 'the hay meadow', the field's name)

cognates.Arabic: ḥašīš 'dry herbage; dry pasture, or fodder … cut herbage', 'one of the best pastures for camels, or for camels and sheep and goats' (Lane 573); ḥašša 'to mow' (HALOT 363)

entries.note: PE 1 .1–2 U-KA-RE · A-SE-SI-NA, the divider after RE in the photograph and the facsimile; the heading over KU-PA-RI VIR 5̣0[ and E-KA[ VIR 72, each with grain at ½ unit a head (Younger, Linear A Texts). ḥa-šī-ši-n: A for ḥa, the ḥ unwritten, as A-NA-NE ḥanān; SI the genitive -i after the construct ʾugār; NA the nunation -n, its vowel dead. A hay meadow worked by the crews it feeds, as the men who worked the ugāru draw provisions (BE 14 56a:26; CAD U/W 30). SE writes šī, as A-SE beside A-SI. One attestation.

entries.meaning: devotee(s) of Kubaba (Kubaba + -ān- + feminine -atu), a counted personnel group

cognates.Anatolian/North Syrian: Kubaba, divine name (Ugarit, Carchemish); Hurrian Kubaba (Laroche 1980, 150)
cognates.Amorite: Kupapa, fem. DN (Gelb glossary); ʾAlli-Kupapa, Baʿli-Kupapa (nos. 708, 2094); short base in Kubb-ān-um (no. 4148) and Kuba-ʾEl (nos. 4099–4100), which Gelb segments kubb-, kuʾb-
cognates.Akkadian: ištarītu 'a priestess', named from Ištar; Kubabat (Old Assyrian; Haas 1994, 406, 614)

entries.note: Feminine of KU-PA₃-NU Kubānu, on the base of KU-PA₃-PA₃ Kubaba (HT 88, where KU-PA₃-NU also stands). HT 119 KU-RO 160 includes *327 34 and VIR 68, so KU-PA₃-NA-TU 7 counts persons. HT 47a KU-PA₃-NA-TU 20[ is broken. Amorite has the short base with the same -ān- in Kubb-ān-um (Gelb 1980, no. 4148), and in Kuba-ʾEl (Gelb 1980, nos. 4099–4100), so the name need not write Kubaba's second BA. Akkadian ištarītu, a priestess named from Ištar, is the same type. AP Za 2 ]-KU-PA₃-NA-TU-NA-TE-[ carries the stem.
entries.source: di Mino, Ya Diktu; Gelb 1980, AS 21, nos. 708, 2094, 4099–4100, 4148; Laroche 1980, 150; Haas 1994

entries.meaning: devotee of Kubaba (Kubaba + -ān-), personal name or title; rival Ugaritic Gupana/Gupan

cognates.Anatolian/North Syrian: Kubaba, divine name (Laroche 1980, 150; DULAT 419); base of Kubānu
cognates.Amorite: Kubb-ān-um (Gelb, AS 21, no. 4148)
cognates.Ugaritic: rival {m}gu-pa-na, personal name gpn(y) (RS 11.839 r. 8, ORACC P503288; PRU 3 195:18, DULAT 301); gpn, Baal's messenger, gpn w ugr (KTU 1.3 III 36; DULAT 301)

entries.note: Kubānu 'devotee of Kubaba', masculine of KU-PA₃-NA-TU Kubānatu, the counted personnel group of HT 119 (di Mino, Ya Diktu). HT 88 sets it beside KU-PA₃-PA₃ Kubaba. Amorite has the short base with this ending, Kubb-ān-um (Gelb 1980, no. 4148), so the form need not write Kubaba's second BA. A name or title, entered once on each of HT 1, HT 3, HT 49a, HT 88, HT 117a and PH(?) 31a and twice on HT 122a. Rival: Gupana/Gupan, the Ugaritic personal name gu-pa-na (RS 11.839) and the god gpn of gpn w ugr (KTU 1.3 III 36; DULAT 301), which Gordon compares with KU for g (Gordon 1966, §142), with Linear B ku-pa-nu-we-to. HT 101.4 KU-PA₃-[…] OLE+U 2 stands in an entry-heading position and restores as KU-PA₃-[NU]. See KU-PA₃-NA-TU.
entries.source: di Mino, Ya Diktu; Gelb 1980, AS 21, no. 4148; Gordon 1966; DULAT; ORACC P503288; Laroche 1980; Jiménez Delgado 2024, 439; Haas 1994

entries.meaning: Kubaba, Sumerian Kug-Baba 'Pure is Baba' (divine or personal name)
entries.root: Kubaba (Sumerian Kug-Baba 'pure Baba', Haas 1994, 406; kug = ellu 'pure', CAD E 102)

cognates.Sumerian: ku₃-ᵈba-ba₆ Kug-Baba, the woman tavern-keeper (munus lu₂-kurun-na) who made firm the foundations of Kish and reigned 100 years (Sumerian King List 224–227, CDLI P479895); Ur III PN Ku-ba-ba-e (Monti 2017, 179)
cognates.Akkadian: Old Babylonian awat Kubaba ša šarrūtam iṣbatu 'the case of Kubaba, who seized the kingship' (CAD Ṣ 32); ᵈNIN ku-ba-ba GAŠAN KUR.URU kar-ga-miš 'Lady Kubaba, Lady of the land of Carchemish' (RS 17.146; DULAT 208); ᵈku₃-KA₂ ᵈ15 ša uru gar-ga-mis 'Kubaba, Ištar of Carchemish' (SAA 2 6:469; CAD R 359)
cognates.Old Assyrian: Kubabat (ku-ba-ba-at), with the Semitic feminine -t, in the pantheon of Kaneš (Haas 1994, 384, 406, 614); PNN Ṣilli-Kubabat, Ummi-Kubabat (CDLI P357798, P360824)
cognates.Ugaritic: kbby PN 'Kubaba' (KTU 4.695:7), syllabic {f}ku-ba-ba, wife of Arḫalba, king of Ugarit (RS 16.144:6) (DULAT 419; Watson 2012, 332; Kinlaw 1967, 74); Hurrian kbbd 'for Kubaba' (KTU 1.116:23; Pardee 2002, 94–95)
cognates.Amorite: Kupapa fem. DN (Gelb 1980, 23); ʾAlli-Kupapa, Baʿli-Kupapa (Gelb 1980, nos. 708, 2094); Mari ḫa-ià-ku-ba-ba 'Kubaba is alive' (Weeden 2009, 96 n. 118)
cognates.Hurrian: ᵈKu-pa-pa, gen. Ku-ba-ba-be, with Adamma and Ḫašuntarḫi (Laroche 1980, 150); Alalakh fKubaba-danni (AT 364:7; Draffkorn 1959, 39)
cognates.Hittite: ᵈKu-pa-pa, ᵈKu-ba-ba, in the circle of Ḫebat (van Gessel 1998, 264–266; Haas 1994, 406–407)
cognates.Luwian: the 'Queen' of Carchemish, her name written with rhombus, bird and vessel (Haas 1994, 406)

entries.note: HT 88, under KI-RO ·: KU-PA₃-PA₃ 1, then KA-JU 1 and KU-PA₃-NU 1, in a list of single units totalled KU-RO 6. Kubaba sign for sign, with PA₃ in its proposed value ba. The name is Sumerian Kug-Baba 'Pure is Baba': the Sumerian King List writes ku₃-ᵈba-ba₆ for the tavern-keeper who founded Kish (SKL 224–227), an Old Babylonian omen already calls her Kubaba (CAD Ṣ 32), and Haas reads the goddess of Carchemish the same way, 'reine Baba', the Sumerian Kar 'trading place' in her city's name supporting it (Haas 1994, 406). Haas holds her identity with Phrygian Kybele and Lydian Kybebe secure (Haas 1994, 408). The goddess and women bear the name alike, and on HT 88 it names the goddess, a woman or a cult institution. Rival: an Old Syrian-Anatolian name of unknown meaning (Haas 1994, 406), with Assyrian KÙ.KA₂ kù-bābu 'holy gate' a folk etymology at most (Haas 1994, 406). One attestation.
entries.source: di Mino; Haas 1994; CAD E, Ṣ

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Vineyard' (√k-r-m)

cognates.Akkadian: karmu "ruin" (different sense; CAD K 220)

entries.note: HT 117a (Haghia Triada, Casa Room 9, LM IB): one of ten entries counted 1 each under MA-KA-RI-TE 'merchants' (KU-RO 10), a name on the noun 'vineyard', as Tēnā 'Fig' (TE-*301). Heb. kerem 'vineyard' (HALOT 498); Ebla has the same noun as a name, gar₃-mu karmu 'vineyard' (Pagan 1998, row 1991). One attestation. See KU-RU-MA.

entries.meaning: in all, total (accounting term), the -a form of KU-RO kull; rival a recipient

cognates.Amorite: be-el-ku-ul-la, ab-du-ku-ul-lim, ia-mu-ut-ku-lu-ú (GlOS 1, 305)
cognates.Akkadian: kalu (kulu) 'whole, entirety, all'; OA nom. kulu, acc. kala, gen. kili (CAD K 87)

entries.note: ZA 20 .4 KU-RA 130, the last line of the text, .5 vacant; the tablet is broken above, and .1–3 keep 26 (GORILA III 193). A totaling word for Younger (Linear A Texts, ZA 20) and for Raison and Pope, Meriggi and Brice (Schoep 2002, 162). ARKH 2 .1–2 SI-DA-TE KU-RA *131B 5, 'provisions in all: must 5', at the head, over A-SI-DA-TO-I 12, ZU-*301-SE-DE-*21F-*118 6 and A-SU-PU-WA 4, which carry no logogram (GORILA III 6–7). kulla, the -a form of KU-RO kull: Amorite be-el-ku-ul-la (GlOS 1, 305); Old Assyrian nom. kulu, acc. kala (CAD K 87). RA for la, as RO for lu in KU-RO. Rival: a recipient, as ZA 10b DU-RE-ZA-SE *131B 5; the Alalakh place Ku-ra (AT 238:4, 66:17; Wiseman 1953, 155). Weak point: ARKH 2's must 5 stands against the 22 under it (12, 6, 4), so the total rests on ZA 20, broken above. Two witnesses, two sites. See KU-RO.
entries.source: di Mino; GlOS 1; CAD K; Younger; Schoep 2002

entries.meaning: total, sum (accounting term)
entries.note: Function fixed corpus-internally by final or section-final position and by arithmetic. HT 89 is the control: 23+22+24+13+5=87, KU-RO 87. The Semitic comparison is *kull- 'all, entirety'; Rendsburg reads ku-ro /kull-/ 'all' (Rendsburg 2026, 203 n. 4). Linear B normally writes TO-SO for 'total'. Complements KI-RO 'owed, outstanding' in Linear A accounting. See KU.
entries.source: Corpus-internal arithmetic; Gordon 1966 for the Semitic comparison; Duhoux 2012; GlOS 1; Rendsburg 2026

entries.meaning: saffron, crocus (PN from plant term)
entries.note: HT 87: KU-RU-KU 1, fifth of six men at one unit each under the heading *21F-TU-NE · MA-KA-RI-TE ·, Scribe 9: a personal name from the plant word. kurkū 'saffron, crocus': Akk. kurkānû, an aromatic plant (CAD K 560), Heb. כַּרְכֹּם karkōm 'saffron' (Song 4:14; HALOT 497); Greek κρόκος is a Semitic loan. One attestation. See *21F-TU-NE.

entries.meaning: vineyard / mountain with vineyard
entries.note: HT 115b KU-RU-MA · I ½, in a list of small quantities (PA-RA-NE ½, DU-PA₃-NA 1, *306-TU-JA 1). kurma or gurma 'vineyard': Heb. kerem (HALOT 498), Ug. krm (DULAT 451); a place, or a name drawn from it, as KU-RA-MU Kurmu.

entries.meaning: water(-men), water-drawers of the sanctuary; rival Anatolian 'grown-ups'

cognates.Ugaritic: mh/y 'water', pl. mym; tkmt my 'who carries water on her shoulders' (KTU 1.19 II 6)
cognates.Akkadian: EA mi-e-ma, mi-ma /mēma/ < /mayma/ 'water' (CAD M/2 17)
cognates.Hebrew: מַיִם mayim 'water'; שֹׁאֲבֵי מַיִם 'drawers of water' (Josh 9:21, 27; Deut 29:10)

entries.note: HT 89 MA-I-MI 24, third of five classes under A-SA-RA₂ · *307 (dubur 'sanctuary'), KU-RO 87. mayimi 'water' (DULAT 529): the sanctuary's water-drawers, as the Gibeonites drew water for the altar (Josh 9:27), and the Nethinim stand beside the gatekeepers (Ezra 7:24); compare TA-RA. Rival: Uchitel's Anatolian 'grown-ups', from mai- 'to grow' (Uchitel 2006, 75); Hittite makes its participle mi(y)ant- (EDHIL 541–542), and the -mi participle is Luwian (Finkelberg 1990/91, 80 n. 86), which has no verb mai- (Melchert 1993, 146). One attestation. See MI-JA.
entries.source: di Mino; DULAT; Uchitel 2006; Finkelberg 1990/91; Kloekhorst 2008; Melchert 1993

entries.meaning: infants or young dependents (personnel category)

cognates.Ugaritic: mṯ (I) 'infant, baby boy' (KTU 1.69:2; 1.5 V:22; 3.7:15; Copenhagen Ugaritic Corpus/DULAT)

entries.note: HT 102 counts MA-ZU 3 in an administrative list, between DI-RI-NA 10 and WI 10, under KU-RO 1060. HT 6a writes MA-*321 10 under the same KA-PA heading, among ration entries (GORILA I 13). Ugaritic mṯ 'infant', after yld 'give birth' in KTU 1.5 V:22. ZU writes ṯ, a proposed value; the vowels of /maṯu/ come from the Linear A spelling, since alphabetic Ugaritic writes only mṯ. Weak point: the HT 102 sign has ZU's round hoop and two bars, as on HT 1, but stands on a foot, a feature of *321, perhaps a variant of ZU; GORILA dots it (GORILA I 169).

entries.meaning: personal name (f.), the feminine of Makī (MA-KA-I-SE); rival the Egyptian name mkj·t

cognates.Amorite: me-ki-im maqīm 'Established', the masculine (Buck 2019, 307; Gelb 1980 no. 4648 ME-QWIM, no. 4649 ME-KWIN)
cognates.Egyptian: mkj·t, women and men, Middle Kingdom (Ranke I, 166.17); mk·t (Ranke I, 166.19); rival

entries.note: PK 1 MA-KA-I-TA 1 closes a roster of names entered singly (A-DU-ZA, TA₂-TA-RE, O-KA-MI-ZA-SI-I-NA); ZA 5b MA-KA-I-TA 3 follows SI-PI-KI 1½ in the wine register, a recipient. The feminine of Makī (MA-KA-I-SE, ZA 8), TA the feminine t. Egyptian writes the name mkj·t, borne by women and men in the Middle Kingdom (Ranke I, 166.17), I for j sign for sign. Rival: the Egyptian name mkj·t as a loan.

entries.meaning: personal name: Makī with the Zakros -SE; Amorite maqīm 'Established'; rival the Egyptian name mkj

cognates.Amorite: me-ki-im maqīm 'Established', PN at Alalakh and Apišal (Buck 2019, 307; Gelb 1980 no. 4648 ME-QWIM, no. 4649 ME-KWIN)
cognates.Egyptian: mkj, men, Middle Kingdom (Ranke I, 166.12–13), one a ruler 'aus ḳdm' in Sinuhe B 219, Mkj⟨m⟩ 'semit. Königstitel' of Qatna in TLA; rival

entries.note: ZA 8 MA-KA-I-SE 2, in a roster of names with quantities (KU-TU-KO-RE, A-RI-NI-TA, TA-I-NU-MA-PA, DA-I-PI-TA, KA-I-RO). SE is the Zakros suffix of RU-MA-TA-SE beside bare RU-MA-TA; MA-KA-I is the base of MA-KA-I-TA (PK 1, ZA 5b). Makī, the Amorite name me-ki-im maqīm 'Established' (Gelb 1980, nos. 4648–4649; Buck 2019, 307), the final m unwritten. Egyptian writes the name mkj (Ranke I, 166.12–13), once for a ruler from Qedem in Sinuhe B 219, which TLA renders Meki⟨m⟩, a Semitic royal title. Rival: the Egyptian name mkj. One attestation.

entries.meaning: merchants (heading of a roster of men); rival 'red (wool)'

cognates.Ugaritic: mkr 'merchant, commercial agent', pl. mkrm, counted in rosters: ʿšr mkrm 'ten merchants', spr mkrm 'list of traders', ġr mkrm 'total of merchants' (DULAT 537); syllabic ma-ka-ri 'to trade' (Huehnergard 2008, 146)
cognates.Akkadian: makāru B 'to do business', OA and Ras Shamra (CAD M/1 126); mākiru, makkāru 'trader' (CAD M/1 129, 131); tamkāru 'merchant' (CAD T 125); tamkārūtu 'commercial transaction; (collective) merchants' (CAD T 141); rival makrū, fem. makritu 'red', of wool (CAD M/1 138)
cognates.Egyptian: *mākiruyu 'merchant', a Semitic loan after swty 'trader' (Hoch 1994, 169, no. 223)

entries.note: HT 87: *21F-TU-NE · MA-KA-RI-TE ·, then six men at 1 each. HT 117a: MA-KA-RI-TE · KI-RO · U-MI-NA-SI ·, then ten men at 1 each, KU-RO 10: 'merchants: owed'. One sign-group in both, divider after TE. √m-k-r 'to trade': Ugaritic counts mkrm in rosters with a total (ġr mkrm, DULAT 537), Akkadian has mākiru and makkāru 'trader', Punic mkr. TE writes the -t of a class noun, cf. the Akkadian collective tamkārūtu 'merchants' (CAD T 141). Hebrew has -t forms of the root, mimkeret 'sale' (Lev 25:42; HALOT 581) and hammōkeret 'she who sells' (Nah 3:4). Weak point: neither names a body of traders. Rival: makritu 'red', of wool (CAD M/1 138), which suits a commodity, not a roster of men.

entries.meaning: mina, portion (weight/measure unit)

cognates.Egyptian: group writing man-nu₂ 'mina', a Semitic loan (GlOS 2, 45, after Hoch, SWET 127, no. 162)

entries.note: KH Wc 2064 and KH Wc 2099, two Khania roundels, each with the ligature MI+*301 alone. minā 'mina, portion': Heb. māneh 'mina' (HALOT 599), Akk. manû 'mina' (CAD M/1 219), from manû 'to count' (CAD M/1 221), Ug. mn 'mina' (GlOS 2, 45). A weight label on sealed administrative roundels. Two attestations. See MI-NU-TE.
entries.source: di Mino; HALOT; CAD M/1; GlOS 2

entries.meaning: loins, hip meat—choice cut on sacrificial fat allocation tablet

cognates.Akkadian: matnu 'sinew, tendon' (CAD M/1 412)

entries.note: HT 41a, unquantified before PA-JA 2 on a tablet of *304 (fat) allocations: MI-DA-NI PA-JA 2, a weight. Heb. māṯnayim 'loins'. Ebla writes matn 'tendon' SA.ŠU = ma-da-nu, with DA for t (GlOS 2, 59). MI writes the i of the plural, as in Arabic mitān (Lane 3017). Rival: a heading or title before PA-JA. One attestation.

entries.meaning: water

cognates.Akkadian: mû 'water; liquid' (CAD M/2 149)

entries.note: SY Za 5, a stone libation vessel from the Syme peak sanctuary: ]MI-JA · JA-WA-PA₃[ (Muhly and Olivier 2008, 209). mayya 'water', the word on a vessel for pouring: Ug. mh/y 'water' (DULAT 529), Heb. mayim (HALOT 576), Akk. mû. Weak point: the rim breaks before MI, and traces of two or three signs stand ca 10 cm to the left (Muhly and Olivier 2008, 209). One attestation. See M'-Y3 and MA-I-MI.

entries.meaning: coverings, blankets
entries.note: HT 26a: MI-KI-SE-NA 15 under the *406VAS+KE heading, after *312-TE-TE and TA-TI 21. miksēna 'coverings', the miqtal of √k-s-y 'cover': *miksay- > miksē, Heb. miksê 'cover, covering', Ug. mks (HALOT 581); SE a sounded ē, -NA the plural *-īna. KI echoes the preceding i. One attestation. See JA-KI-SI-KI-NU.

alternative_readings.note: levy, tax on produce (√m-k-s): Akk. miksu, makāsu (also at Ugarit), mākisu 'tax-collector'; Heb. mekes (Num 31:28); Phoen. MKS 'customs official'. Fits the ledger slot, not the e-vowel.

entries.meaning: amount, number; counting, reckoning

cognates.Akkadian: minūtu 'amount, number; contingent; standard of coinage' (CAD M/2 98); minûtu, cross-reference to manûtu (CAD M/2 99); manû 'count'
cognates.Arabic: Manāt, a remote divine-name comparison from the same apportioning semantic field

entries.note: HT 86a under A-DU and HT 95a–b list MI-NU-TE after DA-ME in grain allocations (HT 86a DA-ME GRA+B 20, MI-NU-TE 20; HT 95a–b DA-ME 10, MI-NU-TE 10), and HT 106 opens MI-NU-TE CYP 6½. Akkadian minūtu: CAD M/2 98 gives 'amount, number', and mi-nu-te is written in Tiglath-pileser I's tally of game, itti mi-nu-te annite 'with this count' (AKA 143 iv 33), and in an obscure Middle Assyrian ana mi-nu-te (Ebeling, Parfümrez. 26 ii 20; both CAD M/2 99). Linear A does not mark vowel length, and final TE may carry a support vowel. Rival: a goddess, Amorite Ma-nu-tum (Gelb 1980, no. 4528) and Arabic Manāt (Q 53:20), both with a where MI writes i. See MI+*301.

entries.meaning: personal name (Mitanni Indo-Aryan type)

cognates.Nuzi: Mittar-atti (Mi-it-ta-ra-at-ti), name element mittar- (Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943, s.v. MITTAR-ATTI)
cognates.Amarna: Ša-mitta, filed with Indo-Aryan su- (Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943, element list, s.v. šu)

entries.note: Personal name on HT 128a, MI-TA GRA+PA ½. The closest name is Nuzi Mittar-atti, element mittar- (Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943, s.v. MITTAR-ATTI), which Gelb sets among the non-Hurrian names with apparent Kassite features (ibid., 196) and Gentile analyses as Mitanni Indo-Aryan *mitra-atthi- 'having Mitra [or a friend] as his guest' (Gentile 2019, 157); no Kassite element list has mittar- (Clay 1912, 36–41; Pinches 1917, 111–113). Rival: Indo-Aryan -mitta, as Amarna Ša-mitta (Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943, element list, s.v. šu). Bare MI-TA occurs only on HT 128a; SI-MI-TA (HT 96a), A-MI-TA (ZA 10b) and the Troy whorls contain the string but are separate words. See SI-MI-TA, MI-DA (t/d variant), A-MI-DA-O.
entries.source: di Mino; Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943; Gentile 2019; Clay 1912; Pinches 1917

entries.meaning: personal name, 'dead one'

cognates.Akkadian: mītu 'dead' (CAD M/2 140)
cognates.Amorite: rival: MUT-UM 'man' in names (Gelb 1980, nos. 4827–4831)

entries.note: HT 117a: MI-TU 1, a recipient in the roster under MA-KA-RI-TE · KI-RO, with U-SU, KU-PA₃-NU and TE-JA-RE. mītu 'dead one', a name of the substitute type. HT 135a ]-MI-TU is the end of a longer word. Weak point: two signs. Rival: *mi/ut- 'man' (semitic_roots 56), with i in Tigre mit and Heb. mətīm. One attestation. See JA-MA-U-TI.

entries.meaning: prefect, administrator (heading of a wine issue); rivals mōgun- 'regalement, gift', Dagan

cognates.Canaanite: su₂-ki-na 'prefect', gloss in EA 362 (ORACC aemw/amarna P270873)
cognates.Akkadian: sākinu 'a high official', Alalakh, Boğazköy, Ras Shamra (CAD S 76)

entries.note: ZA 15a .1 *47-KU-NA SA-VIN, all four signs whole and undotted (GORILA III 183), heading a wine issue with libation portions (SI-PI-KI) and groats. With *47 = so: sōkina 'prefect', the vowels of the Canaanite gloss su₂-ki-na (EA 362), with the ō of the Canaanite shift. Rivals: mōgun- 'regalement, gift' with *47 = mo, /m-g-n/ 'to wine and dine, regale' (DULAT 525); Dagan with *47 = do (DULAT 265). One witness. See SI-KI-NE.

entries.meaning: nẖnm-oil, one of the seven sacred oils (Egyptian loanword); rival personal name

cognates.Egyptian: nẖnm (also nḫnm, nšnm) 'one of the seven sacred oils', from the Pyramid Texts (PT 75) to the Middle Kingdom offering lists, as on the stele of Mery, Louvre C 3 (AED lemma 87760; Wb 2, 319.1–3)

entries.note: HT 115a .2–.3 NA-*21F-NE-MI-NA 1, NA-*21F at the end of .2 after the erased ⟦*301-Ụ-RA⟧, NE-MI-NA at the head of .3, all five signs whole and undotted, on a palimpsest (GORILA I 189).
