Egyptian nẖnm, one of the seven sacred oils of the offering lists (AED lemma 87760; Wb 2, 319.1–3): *21F writes ẖ as it writes Hurrian ḫ in A-SE-TU-*21F, NE and MI the n and m. NA is the noun ending in -n that Semitic adds to Egyptian loans: Hebrew ʾēṭûn 'linen' < jdm.j (HALOT 37), qîqāyôn 'castor-oil plant' < kꜣkꜣ (HALOT 1099), Akkadian kukkānītu (CAD K 498). HT 135a has ]NẸ-MI-NA 10 (.1) and NA-*21F-NE[ (.3), each matching one end of this word. Rival: a personal name, as Ritmā, Šakūtu and Barāne stand beside it. One whole witness.
entries.source: di Mino; AED; Wb; HALOT; CAD K

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Vow' (√n-d-r); rival Egyptian PN 'of-the-hand-of-Re'
entries.note: HT 117a, a personnel list: NA-DA-RE 1, beside MI-TU, KU-PA₃-NU and TE-JA-RE. Nadr 'Vow', √n-d-r 'to vow': G /nadara/, prefix /yaddur-/ with the n assimilated (Huehnergard 2012), BH nādar. Amorite NDR 'to vow' (Gelb 1980, §0.7) gives nadir- 'vowed one' as a name, which fits the roster slot, and LB no-da-ro (KN As(1) 609, personnel) keeps the n-d-r frame. Rival: Gordon's Egyptian name 'of-the-hand-of-Re'. One attestation.

entries.meaning: chief, prince (nasīʾ), broken before NA

cognates.Ugaritic: nšỉ, KTU 2.82:16, uncertain context, compared with Hebrew nāśîʾ (DULAT 639, s.v. /n-š-ʔ/, after Pardee)
cognates.Hebrew: nāśīʾ (נָשִׂיא) 'prince, chief, tribal leader' (HALOT 727–28); Num 1:16, Ezek 44:3; Deir Alla nsʾ 'leader' (ibid.)
cognates.Akkadian: našû 'to lift, carry, raise' (CAD N1 91)

entries.note: AP Za 2 line 1 begins at a broken edge with ]NA-SI, a divider after SI. nasīʾ 'chief, prince', Heb. nāśîʾ. Weak point: the start is broken, so the word can be longer, and its place in the line is unknown. E-NA-SI on KH 7a is a distinct form. One attestation. See DA-NA-SI and U-MI-NA-SI.

entries.meaning: the dedicated one (qatūl passive participle of √n-t-n + -ān); rival nātānān 'the giver'

cognates.Hebrew: nātīn (נָתִין) "temple servant, dedicated one"—singular of Nĕtīnīm (נְתִינִים), Ezra 2:43, 8:20; 1 Chr 9:2. Passive participle of √n-t-n. The Levites themselves called nĕtūnīm nĕtūnīm "given, utterly given" (Num 3:9)
cognates.Ugaritic: ytn / ntn "to give"—one of the most common Ugaritic roots
cognates.Amorite: the passive natūn 'given' in names: NATUN-UM Natūnum, ʾIL-I+NATUN Ilī-natūn (Gelb 1980, nos. 5014, 2756)
cognates.Akkadian: nadānu "to give"; nādinu "giver" (active participle)
cognates.Phoenician: Mattan (מתן) "gift"—common PN element (Mattan-Baal); institutional parallels in Phoenician temple servant classes
cognates.Athena: A-TA-NA = ʾatanā 'She-who-gives' (lexicon PROBABLE)—NWS feminine of √y-t-n (> ʾ- via I-y weakening). NA-TU-NA-NE with initial n- preserves √n-t-n; the coexistence of both allomorphs points to a pre-split isogloss stage

entries.note: SKO Zc 1, an inked inscription from the Skoteino cave, broken on both sides: NA-TU-*301-NE, with *301 = na (288 occurrences at 16 sites), so na-tū-nā-n(e), the final E dead. natūnān 'the dedicated one', the qatūl passive participle of √n-t-n 'to give' with -ān, TU for the ū. Compare Heb. nĕtūnīm 'given ones', the Levites given to sanctuary service (Num 3:9), and the post-exilic Nĕtīnīm, temple servants (Ezra 2:43; 8:20; 1 Chr 9:2), an institution traced to the Gibeonites (Josh 9:27). Ug. ntn, ttn /tatinū/ 'to give', BH nātan (Huehnergard 2012, 52; App. C, 6–7). Rival: nātānān 'the giver', the qātāl active participle with -ān, a title of the Goddess at a cave sanctuary, beside A-TA-NA-TE ʾAtanat 'She-who-gives' (√y-t-n). One attestation. See MA-TI-TI.

entries.meaning: offspring, descendants, posterity

cognates.Hebrew: nîn ‘offspring, descendants’ (Gen 21:23; Isa 14:22; Job 18:19); cf. the extended -ūn formation Yəšūrūn ‘Jeshurun, the Upright One’
cognates.Hebrew verb: rare n-w-n ‘produce shoots, get descendants’ at Ps 72:17; HALOT leaves open whether the noun derives from the verb or the verb is denominative
cognates.Semitic morphology: masculine nominative plural *-ūna (Huehnergard 2019, 60–61); Arabic indefinite nominative -un (Fischer 2002, §§141, 147)

entries.note: PL Zf 1, a silver pin: … TA-NU-NI-KI-NA · NI-NU-NI · [?]-I-[?]. NI-NU-NI follows TA-NU-NI-KI-NA tannî qînâ, the imperative and its object, as a vocative noun: nīnūn 'offspring, descendants', Heb. nîn 'descendants', with the verb nyn 'to get descendants' (Ps 72:17; HALOT 696). NI writes nī, NU nū, and the final NI the n with a dead vowel; -ūn is the plural or collective ending, as in Yəšūrūn. Rival: nīn-un, with the Arabic nominative nunation. Weak point: Hebrew has nîn only in the singular, beside neked (HALOT 696). One attestation.

entries.meaning: O Sokar (Egyptian Skr), the deity addressed; rivals Ušḫara the Snake, ʾAšqur

cognates.Egyptian: Zkr 'Sokar' (AED lemma 146890; Wb 3, 487.13)
cognates.Ugaritic: ủšḫr DN, from Akkadian Išḫara (DULAT 113), the rival

entries.note: TL Za 1 A-TA-I-*301-WA-JA · O-SU-QA-RE ·, the deity slot of the libation formula. ʾō Sukar: vocative ʾō (Geʿez ʾo-, Leslau 1987, 1) + Egyptian Skr 'Sokar', final E dead after r (di Mino, Ya Diktu). Rival: Ušḫara, Ugaritic úšḫr, only as úšḫr ḫlmẓ 'Ušḫara the Snake' (KTU 1.115:2, 12; DULAT 113), from Akk. Išḫara, with QA where KA writes ḫ. Rival: ʾAšqur, an Amorite DN in names at Mari and Alalakh (aš-kur-ᵈIM), with O for ʾa; Sanmartín derives it from |S-ḳ-r| 'the very high one' (GlOS 2, 195; cf. Akk. zaqāru), Gelb from ŚKR 'to remember' (AS 21, nos. 949–950). One witness.
entries.source: di Mino, Ya Diktu; DULAT 113; GlOS 2, 195; Gelb, AS 21

entries.meaning: honeyed oil (DI for dišpu 'honey')

cognates.Akkadian: dišpu 'honey' (CAD D 161)
cognates.Arabic: dibs 'the expressed juice of fresh ripe dates, date honey' (Lane 848)

entries.note: OLE with the adjunct DI: 12 tokens on 8 Haghia Triada tablets, beside OLE+MI on HT 14, HT 28a, HT 90 and HT 116a, a distinct oil class. DI writes the di- of dišpu 'honey' (CAD D 161), Heb. dəbaš 'honey' (HALOT 213): honeyed oil. Ugaritic uses nbt for honey (DULAT 610). Weak point: one adjunct sign stands for the whole word. See OLE+MI.

entries.meaning: oil with flour and honey, a compound (A623)
entries.note: HT 121 KI-RI-TA₂ OLE+QE+DI 10, heading the list, once. SigLA catalogs the sign as the single logogram A623; GORILA reads the ligature OLE+QE+DI. QE writes the qē- of qēmu 'flour', as in GRA+QE, and DI the di- of dišpu 'honey' (CAD D 161), as in OLE+DI: oil, flour and honey, as סֹלֶת וָשֶׁמֶן וּדְבַשׁ (Ezek 16:19). DI+QE on HT 101 joins flour and honey. Weak point: GORILA reads a ligature, SigLA the single sign A623.
entries.source: di Mino; GORILA I; SigLA; CAD D; CAD Q

entries.meaning: genuine, standard-grade oil (kīnu)

cognates.Akkadian: kīnu 'true, reliable, just, honest' (CAD K 389)
cognates.Amorite: KWN 'be firm': kīnum (Gelb AS 21, 23)

entries.note: OLE with the KI adjunct marks an oil subtype, 21 tokens on 17 documents at Haghia Triada, Tylissos and Zakros. kīnu 'true, standard': Akk. kīnu 'true, reliable, correct, normal, legitimate' (CAD K 389), Heb. kēn 'correct, right' (HALOT 482). Cf. KI-NU (ARKH 3a), read Kīnu, the full word or a personal name. Weak point: no Semitic text names a 'genuine' oil.

entries.meaning: anointing oil (mišḥā)

cognates.Hebrew: mišḥâ 'anointing, anointing oil'; šemen hammišḥâ 'the anointing oil', Exod 25:6 (HALOT 644)
cognates.Amorite: MŚḤ 'anoint': maśīḥum, maśḥatum (Gelb AS 21, 25)

entries.note: OLE with the complement MI, 19 tokens on 14 documents from Haghia Triada and Tylissos; it stands with OLE+U and OLE+KI on the allocation tablets HT 42+59, HT 91 and TY 3a, and with PA as PA-OLE+MI on TY 3b. MI writes mišḥ-, Northwest Semitic √m-š-ḥ 'to anoint': Ug. mšḥ 'to anoint, oil' (DULAT 582), Heb. māšaḥ. Biblical cult inventories name שֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה šemen ham-mišḥā 'the anointing oil' (Exod 25:6; 29:7; 31:11; HALOT 644) and שֶׁמֶן מִשְׁחַת קֹדֶשׁ šemen mišḥat qōdeš 'holy anointing oil' (Exod 30:25, 31), a commodity named by its m-š-ḥ noun, as OLE is by MI. Ebla has the verb, ma-zi-ʔà (ARET 11 160), and Akkadian muššuʔu 'to rub', muššuʔtu 'ointment' (GlOS 2, 55). Weak point: the single sign MI carries the whole reading.
entries.source: Hebrew Bible, Exod 25:6; 29:7; 30:25, 31; 31:11; DULAT 582; GlOS 2; corpus distribution

entries.meaning: oil designated for ritual libation; sacred oil poured as an offering

cognates.Hebrew: nesek 'libation' (HALOT 703); at Bethel Jacob wayyassēk ʿālêhā nesek and poured oil on the pillar, Gen 35:14

entries.note: OLE with the complement NE, on HT 23a, HT 32, HT 100 and TY 3b, at Haghia Triada and Tylissos, always in small quantities (¾, ≈⅙, 2 units), measured ritual portions. neseku 'libation': Akk. nasāku 'to pour a libation' (CAD N/2 26), Heb. נֶסֶךְ nesek 'libation, drink offering' (Num 15:5; Isa 48:5), √n-s-k, NE its first syllable. HT 32 issues it under a *307 dubur 'sanctuary' heading; on HT 23a OLE+NE, OLE+TU, OLE+RI and *308 stand at the same ≈⅙, a recipe of four oils; on TY 3b it is a minor entry (2 units) beside large quantities of OLE+MI, anointing oil. Rival: nēru 'lamp' (√n-w-r), lamp oil, against which tell the small quantities and the sanctuary contexts.

entries.meaning: aromatic/fragrant olive oil preparation

cognates.Akkadian: riqqu 'aromatic plant, aromatics' (CAD R 368)

entries.note: OLE with the complement RI, on HT 23a, HT 35, HT 60 and KH 82, at Haghia Triada and Khania; myrrh stands on three of the four tablets. riqqu 'aromatic substance' (CAD R 371), RI its first syllable. On HT 23a it stands with OLE+NE and OLE+TU, all at ≈⅙. The root is that of *401 RUQQÛ: Akk. rīqu, riqqu, Ebla GIŠ.NAGA = rí-ga-tum riqaḥt 'spiced, oily ointment' and Ug. rqḥ 'perfume, ointment' stand under one root |r-ḳ-ħ| (GlOS 2, 165).

entries.meaning: fine-grade olive oil; 'good oil' as an administrative quality designation

cognates.Hebrew: kaššemen haṭṭôb 'like the good oil', Ps 133:2; ṭôb 'good' (HALOT 370)
cognates.Akkadian: ṭābu 'good, sweet, fresh' (CAD Ṭ 19); šamnu ṭābu 'sweet oil' (HALOT 371)
cognates.Amorite: ṭābum 'good' (Gelb AS 21, 35)

entries.note: OLE with the complement TA, on HT 30 and HT 35 at Haghia Triada and on KH 19, 39, 55, 61 and 85 at Khania, in small fractions (⅕, ⅓, ½, 𐝓), a premium grade issued in measured amounts. ṭābu 'good': Akk. ṭābu, Heb. ṭōb, Ug. ṭb, TA writing ṭa as its first syllable. Ugarit issues šmn ṭb 'good oil' (KTU 4.14, 4.91, 4.158), and Ebla writes Ì.DU₁₀ = sa-ma-nu-um da-bù samnum ṭābu 'good oil', D for ṭ (GlOS 2, 311). See DA-I-PI-TA.

entries.meaning: sanctuary oil

cognates.Akkadian: šamnu 'oil, fat' (see OLE)

entries.note: PE Wy 5, a stone object from Petras: OLE *307 1½, the oil logogram with *307, the DUBUR logogram 'sanctuary'. Oil for the sanctuary. One attestation. See DU-PU₂-RE.

entries.meaning: Phaistos (place name)

cognates.Egyptian: byšt, recarved on the Kom el-Hetan Aegean list of Amenhotep III, identified with Phaistos (Cline and Stannish 2011, 7–9)
cognates.Linear B: pa-i-to, the town, on the Knossos sheep tablets (KN Da 1163, Da 1156, Db 1159 and others)

entries.note: HT 97a PA-I-TO 6, among the entries under KA-RU · *307+*307 · VIR+KA 82, after KA-NU-TI 25; HT 120 PA-I-TO 3⅕, the last entry, after KI-RE-TA-NA GRA+B 60 and GRA+PA 48. Linear B writes the same pa-i-to for Phaistos, the town of the Knossos tablets (DMic II 68).
entries.source: di Mino; Gordon 1966; DMic II; Cline and Stannish 2011; Beekes 2014

entries.meaning: Sukrita (place name; Linear B su-ki-ri-ta)

cognates.Linear B: su-ki-ri-ta, the town, KN Da 1091, Db 1324, Db 1327, Df 1325, Dn 1092, Dv 5232

entries.note: PH Wa 32, a Phaistos nodule: SU-KI-RI-TA alone, four signs, undotted (GORILA II 90). HT Zb 158b, a jar: SU-KI-RI-TE-I-JA, the gentilic in -TE-I-JA. Linear B spells the place su-ki-ri-ta in the Knossos sheep tablets (KN Da 1091, Db 1324, 1327, Df 1325, Dn 1092, Dv 5232), with the ethnic su-ki-ri-ta-jo (KN C 911); DMic II 303 n. 6 records Godart's reading of su-ki-ri-ta on this Phaistos sealing (PP 31, 1976, 42 ff.) and the scribe's change of su-ki-ri-ta to pa-i-to on KN Da 1163. Identified with Σύβριτα in the Amari valley; Chadwick takes the name as not Greek (DMic II 303 n. 5). √s-g-r 'shut, bolt' on Ventris and Chadwick's Sugrita, the vowel of KI dead: Heb. sāgar 'shut' (BDB 688), Akk. šigaru 'bolt' (HALOT 742), Pun. sgr 'lock'; Ugarit syllabic GIŠ sú-qi-ri 'bolt', the same SU-KI-RI frame (GlOS 2, 190). Ugaritic personal name śgryn /Sugriyānu/ (KTU³ 4.825 i 13), s̀ an allograph of {s} (Tropper & Vita 2019, §2). Rival: SU- + KI-RI-TA qrt 'town' (Phoen., Pun. qrt, HALOT 1142; Syr. ḳerīt-, Brock. 695), SU- unexplained; Greek writes Semitic q as κ, and Σύβριτα has β/γ.

entries.meaning: of Sukrita (Sybrita): origin label on a jar

cognates.Ugaritic: suGir 'bolt', the base of the town name (GlOS 2, 190)
cognates.Linear B: su-ki-ri-ta-jo, the ethnic of the town, KN C(2) 911

entries.note: HT Zb 158b, a jar: the only word on side b (GORILA IV 65); side a reads [·]-TU-SE-SU-KI. Gentilic on SU-KI-RI-TA (PH Wa 32), the vowel of KI dead before RI; Linear B has the ethnic su-ki-ri-ta-jo (KN C 911). Davis (Aura Suppl. 13, 46) pairs the two forms as alternating endings. -I-JA is the Semitic nisba *-iy- (fem. *-iyya), the gentilic suffix of Ugaritic ugrty /ʾugaritiyyu/ 'man of Ugarit' (Fischer 2002, §116). Rival: Anatolian -iya-. -TE-I-JA has no other Linear A witness; SE-TO-I-JA (PR Za 1) shares -I-JA. One document.

entries.meaning: He (of) Re: Egyptian personal name Pꜣ-Rꜥ (Gordon's Pꜣy-Rꜥ); Linear B pa-ja-ro

cognates.Egyptian: pꜣ-rꜥ 'he (of) Ra', a man's name, Thutmose III–Amenhotep III (PNM v6, personal_names_id 142613047; Ranke I, 114.11)
cognates.Linear B: pa-ja-ro, a man on the Knossos roster KN As(2) 1519

entries.note: HT 8b, HT 29, HT 88 and ZA 10b: a personal name in all four. Linear B pa-ja-ro is a masculine personal name in the Knossian roster KN As(2) 1519.6, and DMic compares it with Linear A PA-JA-RE. Gordon reads Egyptian Pꜣy-Rꜥ 'He-of-Re' (Gordon 1966a, 31, §127). PNM has the man's name pꜣ-rꜥ 'he (of) Ra' (Ranke I, 114.11, as PNM cites it), used from Thutmose III to Amenhotep III and spelled pꜣjj-rꜥ under Hatshepsut, the date of the LM IB tablets (Ilin-Tomich 2025); JA writes the jj. Amarna writes the same Re as -ri- in na-ap-ḫur-ri-ia, Nfr-ḫprw-rꜥ 'beautiful of form is Rē' (Hess 1993, 116). Rival: a Minoan name, as Davis treats the pair (Davis 2026, 44). Four attestations.
entries.source: di Mino; Gordon 1966a; Ilin-Tomich 2025; DMic II; Davis 2026; Hess 1993

entries.meaning: daughters (fem. pl.) / portions / Kubaba devotees (cf. KU-PA-NA-TU)
entries.note: KH 7b, a Khania vessel allocation tablet, standalone. Three readings: banātu 'daughters', a personnel category, PA for b (Akk. fem. pl. of bintu, Ug. bnt, Heb. bānōt); panātu 'faces, portions', share categories (Akk., Heb. pānîm); and (Ku)bānatu, a devotee title, the tail of KU-PA-NA-TU, the feminine of Kubaba, which Khania's Anatolian contact layer favours. KU-PA-NA-TU carries the KU- that PA-NA-TU lacks. One attestation. See PO-TO-KU-RO.

entries.meaning: short form of A-PA-RA-NE, 'the crosser'; rival 'creator'

cognates.Akkadian: ebēru A 'to cross (water)' (CAD E 10)

entries.note: HT 115a: PA-RA-NE 1 in a GRA+BOSm list beside *301-U-RA naura 'light', SE-KU-TU, KA-PO-RU and RI-SU-MA; HT 115b: ½; both by Scribe 8, who also writes A-PA-RA-NE (HT 96a and b). The short form of A-PA-RA-NE, without the initial ʿayin of √ʿ-b-r or the prosthetic aleph of √b-r-ʾ, 'the crosser', with 'creator' the rival. Amorite Ḥa-pí-ra-an, of the element ḤPR ḥapir-, *ʿapir-, the ʿApiru/Ḥabiru word (Huffmon 1965, 36, 202), and ʾAPR-AN AP-RA-AN (Gelb 1980, no. 863) match it with -ān, cuneiform ḫ writing ʿ. Borger derives ʿapīru from ʿ-p-r 'dust' (apud Huffmon 1965, 202); PA writes p and b alike.

entries.meaning: personal name; Egyptian Ptḥ-dj(⸗f) 'Ptah gives'; rival Hurrian pṭḏ (Ugarit)

cognates.Egyptian: ptḥ-dj⸗f, a man's name (PNM v6, personal_names_id 142614558)

entries.note: PH(?) 31a .3 PA-TA-DA[, after KU-PA₃-NU SUS+SI+RE 1, broken after DA at the line end; HT Zb 160 PA-TA-DA DU-PU₂-RE[, a vessel label 'Patada: to the sanctuary'. Egyptian ptḥ-dj⸗f, a man's name under Thutmose IV–Amenhotep III (PNM v6, Louvre C 277), the ḥ and the ⸗f unwritten; Amarna writes Ptah -ptaḫ in Ḫi-ku-up-ta-aḫ (EA 84:37; RGTC 12/2, 105). Rival: Hurrian pṭḏ, a man at Ugarit (KTU 4.357:23; DULAT 676).
entries.source: Ilin-Tomich 2025 (PNM v6), s.v. ptḥ-dj⸗f; DULAT 676; di Mino

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Viper'; rival Ptah-theophoric

cognates.Greek: Πύθων 'Python', from a Semitic form akin to Heb.-Aram. ptn (Rendsburg 2026, 208)

entries.note: HT 94b (KI-RO · TU-MA 1, PA-TA-NE 1, DE-DI 1 …), HT 122a (PA-TA-NE 1 after KU-PA₃-NU 1, in a roster with JA-MI-DA-RE) and the nodule HT Wa 1019 (PA at the edge). On HT 122a SigLA labels the second sign ri, and its own tracing, GORILA's facsimile and the photo show TA. *patn- 'viper' as a name: Heb. peten (HALOT 990), Ug. bṯn, Akk. bašmu. Rivals: Ptah with ḥ unwritten and -ānu, 'devotee of Ptah', and √p-t-ḥ 'open' with -ānu. Three attestations.

entries.meaning: a kind of *402 cup

cognates.Akkadian: patāqu B 'to drink', pa-ta-qu (Malku VIII 8), liptiqu (En. el. III 9) (CAD P 275)

entries.note: HT 31 .6, a vessel inventory: PA-TA-QE written over the *402-VS cup logogram, 3000, the largest allocation on the tablet; one of Gordon's HT 31 vessels (Gordon 1966 §115). pitqē: Stieglitz compares Aramaic pitqā 'winecup' (Lewy, Chaldäisches Wörterbuch, s.v.) and Akkadian naptaqu 'smelting-jar' (AHw, s.v.), both apud Stieglitz 1971, 111; Jastrow 1173 gives pitqā 'tablet, ballot, decree', and Targ. II Esth. 1:8 names a large goblet Pithka, 'Decree'. Stieglitz sets the ending -e beside the archaic Hebrew plural -ê and the Ugaritic dual construct (Stieglitz 1971, 110). Rival: Akkadian patāqu 'to cast metal', 'metal vessel' (Astour, JAOS 87, 1967, 292 n. 13, apud Stieglitz 1971, 111).

entries.meaning: terebinth (PA₃ a phonetic complement for the b-onset)
entries.note: HT 8b, Villa Magazine: PA₃-*188 2, PA₃ ba as a phonetic complement giving the b of buṭnu 'terebinth' (see *188). Rival: HT 8b .3 5 · PA₃ · *188 2, PA₃ a transaction sign opening the second section and *188 the item, as su-pu₂ *188 1 on b.1 (Schrijver 2014, 7). See *188 and PA₃-KA-RA-TI.

entries.meaning: cattle, heifers (fem.pl.)
entries.note: HT 8a .1–2 JE-DI · OLE+KI 10 PA₃ | KA-RA-TI 1½: PA₃ is the last sign of line 1, KA-RA-TI the first of line 2, in a list sharing out 10 units of oil. Hebrew bāqār, fem.pl. -āti. Rival: PA₃ a transaction sign closing line 1 and KA-RA-TI a recipient (GORILA V apud Schrijver 2014, 7 n. 6). HT 8b opens its second section the same way, 5 · PA₃ · *188 2, and PA₃ stands alone on HT 34.6 (PA₃ 70, KI-RO 30 = SA+MU+KU 100), HT 9b, 93a and 132. One attestation.

entries.meaning: builder (a personnel class)

cognates.Amorite: BANIJ-IM Baniyim, the active participle as a name (Gelb 1980, no. 1128)

entries.note: HT 85a PA₃-NI 12, a count of men under A-DU · *307+*307 · VIR+[?], beside DA-RI-DA 12 and U-*325-ZA 6; HT 102 PA₃-NI GRA+PA 33, after SA-RA₂ GRA 976. bānī 'builder', the active participle of √b-n-y, *bāniyu > bānī: Ug. bny 'architect, builder' (DULAT 231), Akk. bānû 'housebuilder' (CAD B 95). Two attestations. See PA₃-NI-NA and PA₃-NI-WI.
entries.source: di Mino; DULAT; CAD B; GlOS 1; Gelb 1980

entries.meaning: our builder

cognates.Ugaritic: bny 'architect, builder; maker, creator'; bny bnwt 'Creator of creatures', El's title, KTU 1.4 II 11 (DULAT 230–231)
cognates.Akkadian: bānû A 'creator, begetter' (CAD B 94)
cognates.Amorite: BNJ 'build, create': jabnī, bānijum (Gelb AS 21, 16)

entries.note: HT 6b and HT 93a: a personnel designation. √b-n-y 'build', the participle bāniyu with the 1pl possessive -na: banīna 'our builder'. See PA₃-NI. HT 93a writes it twice, heading the tablet on .1 and again on .8 before ]PA-SE-JA 20 and VIR+[?] 10. On .8, NA is damaged and GORILA I 147 prints a break after it, but SigLA's PA begins 0.4 sign widths after NA, so no sign is lost: the word is whole and legible in context.

entries.meaning: the builder (nisba/gentilic)

cognates.Akkadian: bānû B 'housebuilder' (CAD B 95)
cognates.Amorite: PN BANIJ-IM (Gelb AS 21 no. 1128); bānijum (Gelb AS 21, 16)

entries.note: SY Za 4, the Syme libation formula, beside A-TA-I-*301-WA-JA and JA-I-NWA-RO. √b-n-y 'build' with the NWS gentilic *-iy, written -WI: bānīy 'the builder'. The same nisba closes DU-RU-WI (*ḏu-luwwī 'the Levite', 'the attached one') and U-RE-WI (*ʾūr-lēwī), occupational adjectives from the gentilic *-iyy-; Linear A writes the glide of /iy/ as WI, where Hebrew contracts it to -î. The Merarite Levite Bānî (בָּנִי, 1 Chr 6:31) bears the name. RILA-S1 underdots WI and rates PA₃-NI-PI less plausible (RILA-S1 84). One attestation. See PA₃-NI.

entries.meaning: meal worked with oil or clarified butter (commodity)

cognates.Arabic: basīsa 'sawīq [meal of parched barley or wheat], and flour, &c., mixed with clarified butter, or with olive-oil' (Lane 201)

entries.note: MIL Zb 1, a clay vessel from Miletos, the Minoan settlement on the Anatolian coast, the only word. ba-si-so, with PA₃ ba, SI si and *47 so, as in *47-KU-NA sōkina 'prefect': basīsa, the vessel's contents, Arabic basīsa 'sawīq [meal of parched barley or wheat], and flour, &c., mixed with clarified butter, or with olive-oil' (Lane 201). Weak points: the root is Arabic only, and -so writes the final a. MIL Zb 1 has no GORILA or SigLA record. One attestation.

entries.meaning: face, front

cognates.Hebrew: *pāneh 'face, front', only in the plural pānîm (HALOT 938)
cognates.Ugaritic: pnm 'face, countenance', also as a preposition (DULAT 664)

entries.note: ZA 11a, after KU-PA · GRA+PA 1, heading OLIV 2. With *310 at the proposed value IN, PI-IN-A writes pīnā 'face, front', the pin- of I-PI-NA-MA ʾippina=ma 'in the presence of': Heb. pānîm 'face' (HALOT 938), Ug. pnm 'face' (DULAT 664).

entries.meaning: by the portions (broken before PI); rivals 'by the recitation', minḥâ 'offering'

cognates.Akkadian: kaspam ana maniātikunu … dināma 'give the silver according to the amount you establish' (TCL 17 14 r. 8, OB; CAD M/2 87)

entries.note: AP Za 2 line 2 preserves ]PI-MI-NA-TE from a broken left edge to a divider after TE; PI and MI are written over an erasure (GORILA IV 5). bi-mināti 'by the portions': PI the proclitic bi-, as in PI-KU-ZU bi-kuṯ, and mināt 'portion', Emar mināt (GlOS 2, 45), Ugaritic mnt (I) 'portion, ration' (DULAT 558), Akk. minītu, pl. mināti, 'amount' (CAD M/2 86), √m-n-y 'count, allot', TE writing the oblique. Rival: Ugaritic mnt 'enumeration; spell, incantation' (GlOS 2, 45). Rival: Hebrew minḥâ 'gift, offering' (Lev 2:1), Ugaritic mnḥt 'tribute' (DULAT 556), with ḥ unwritten. Younger restores I-]PI-MI-NA-TE and compares PI-*34-TE (HT 116a); no I survives before PI. Weak point: the left edge is lost, so a sign may stand before PI. One attestation. See MI+*301, MI-NU-TE and DA-DU-MI-NE.

entries.meaning: provisions, provisioning (allocation entry); rivals bayti 'house', a recipient name

cognates.Akkadian: piqittu 'provisioning, control, muster, charge' (CAD P 388)
cognates.Hebrew: piqqādôn 'deposit, stored goods', wəhāyâ hāʾōkel ləpiqqādôn lāʾāreṣ 'and the food shall be a store for the land' (Gen 41:36; HALOT 958)

entries.note: HT 116a PI-*34-TE GRA 5, then OLE 5, OLE+MI 1, *OLIV+TU 2: one of six entries under U-TA-RO · TE, each a sign group with GRA and a number, as KU-PA-JA, PU-RA₂, SI+SE, SI-KI-NE and QA-NU-MA. Read PI-QI-TE with *34 = QI. Akkadian piqittu(m), oblique piqitti, sense 1 'provisioning, provisions' (CAD P 388), from paqādu(m) 'entrust, assign, inspect' (Huehnergard 1997, 104, 614); the entry draws grain, oil and olives. Rivals: bayti 'house; temple, household, estate' (DULAT 243; HALOT 124; CAD B 282) with *34 = ai, an institution among recipients that include PU-RA₂ and SI+SE; a recipient name, as its neighbours. Younger compares ]PI-MI-NA-TE (AP Za 2.2), with *34 for MI-NA. One witness. Weak point: *34 = qi is a proposed value.
entries.source: di Mino; Huehnergard 1997; CAD P; DULAT; HALOT; CAD B; Younger, Linear A Texts

entries.meaning: and the gift (heading over oil and grain amounts); rivals uqīš 'he bestowed', a name

cognates.Akkadian: qāšu (qiāšu) 'make a donation, dedicate, give a present' (CAD Q 156); qīšu 'given as a present' (CAD Q 280)
cognates.Amorite: QJŠ, jaqīš 'to donate, to present'; qīšum 'given, gift' (Gelb 1980, 29)

entries.note: HT 140 opens both oil sections with U-*34-SI, each followed by a name (*86-SI-NI, *86-SI-*118-KA) and OLE amounts, the second broken after SI (GORILA I 237); HT 15 opens the grain account with it (684, 570, KI-RO 400). Never a recipient. u-qīš 'and the gift', *34 = qi: u- 'and' with qīš, Akk. qīšu 'given as a present' (CAD Q 280), Amorite qīšum 'given, gift' (Gelb 1980, 29), from √q-y-š 'give as a gift' (#3843), Akk. qāšu 'make a donation, dedicate' (CAD Q 156). Rivals: uqīš 'he bestowed', D preterite, written ū-qa-īš (CAD Q 156, mng. 3); a name, as U-MI-NA-SI in the same header slot (HT 117a, HT 28b). Weak point: *34 = qi is a proposed value.

entries.meaning: trade agents, deputies, a personnel group drawing grain; rivals bitāri 'portions' and the names Paṭir, Batūl

cognates.Ugaritic: bdl(m) 'substitute, lieutenant, a kind of (sales) representative'; syllabic LÚ.MEŠ DAM.GÀR : bi-da-lu-ma 'merchants' (GlOS 1, 110)
cognates.Amorite: rival PAṬIR-UM Paṭirum 'released' (Gelb 1980, no. 1151); BATUL-UM Batūlum 'bachelor' (no. 1153)

entries.note: HT 96a .4 PI-TA-RA · 1, whole, in a grain list after SI-MI-TA GRA 5, RU-SA 4, *323-*317 1 and before *323-*344 1 (GORILA I 157). bi-da-la, the sign sequence of Ugarit bi-da-lu-ma, glossing LÚ.MEŠ DAM.GÀR 'merchants', and of the name DUMU-bi-da-la-ya (RS 15.0009); Ebla ba-da-lum 'merchant' (GlOS 1, 110). A body of agents drawing grain, cf. MA-KA-RI-TE 'merchants' (HT 117a). Rivals: bitāri 'portions', Emar bi-ta-ri (GlOS 1, 130); the name Paṭir 'released' (Gelb 1980, no. 1151; Ebla ba-du-ri₂, Pagan 1998, row 1090), with PI for pa; the name Batūl 'bachelor' (Gelb 1980, no. 1153); Ug. btlt 'virgin' (DULAT 248), for which the slot gives no cue. One witness.
entries.source: di Mino; GlOS 1; Gelb 1980; Pagan 1998; ORACC aemw/ugarit

entries.meaning: grandtotal (lit. 'daughter of all')

cognates.Hebrew: בַּת כֹּל bat kol 'daughter of all', Gordon's reconstruction in Hebrew script (Gordon 1966 §118); Hebrew bat 'daughter', kōl 'all'
cognates.Akkadian: kullatu 'all, totality' (CAD K 504)

entries.note: HT 122b: PO-TO-KU-RO 97 follows KU-RO 65, a grand total over the subtotal, summed across both faces: HT 122a KU-RO 31 + KU-DA 1 + HT 122b KU-RO 65 = 97 (Schrijver 2014, 4). Gordon reads bat kol, bat 'daughter' with kol 'all', 'daughter of all', the grand total, deriving po-to from *butt- < *bunt-, the feminine of Ugaritic bun- 'son' (Gordon 1966 §118); the skeleton p-t-k-r gives bt with kr, the vowels dead. The structure is that of KU-RO kull 'total'.

entries.meaning: Baal, 'Lord' (allocation heading)

Amarna.meaning: lord, master / lord of the houses
Amarna.note: Baal theophoric ubiquitous in Amarna (Šipti-Baʿla, etc.). bʿl t bbtm "lord of the houses" (EA 11 n.22) parallels institutional usage.

entries.note: HT 28b and HT 116a: an allocation heading. Gordon's Baʿl/Bōl, with the proposed values PU = bV and RA₂ = l and the ʿayin lost. Ebla has bare ba-lu, ba₄-lum 'lord' as personal names (Pagan 1998, rows 1110, 1153). ZA 6a ]PU₂-RA₂ GRA+PA 20 is a candidate for the same name at Zakros, with PU₂ = bu, in the same name-with-grain slot; the line is broken before PU₂, so the word can be longer. RA₂ = l stands without this word: SA-RA₂ šarra writes the marked liquid, as Linear B ra₂ /rya, lya/ (Judson 2020, 72, 74), and KN 54 writes PU-RA with plain RA. Two attestations.
entries.source: Gordon 1966 §150; HT28b and HT116a corpus contexts; Pagan 1998

entries.meaning: incense, incense-offering (Semitic cultic term)

cognates.Akkadian: qatāru 'incense' (CAD Q 166)

entries.note: HT 96b (Haghia Triada, Casa Room 7, LM IB), a commodity tablet headed A-PA-RA-NE ·: QA-*118-RA-RE · *516 · GRA · 40¾, OLE+U 4, NI 2¹⁄₁₀, a large allocation of grain and oil. qaṭara(re) 'incense, incense-offering', √q-ṭ-r 'to smoke, burn incense', with *118 read ṭa, a proposed value: Heb. qəṭōret 'incense' (HALOT 1095), beside Akk. qutru 'smoke' and qutrinnu 'incense, censer' (HALOT 1095), Arabic qaṭara 'to drop, distill'. -RA writes the root's r and -RE an ending, or the noun pattern qaṭṭāra. Weak point: *118 = ṭa holds only once the DA and TA doublets are set aside, and standing alone before a numeral *118 is the talent sign. With t, the root is the same: Akk. qatāru 'to make an incense offering' (CAD Q 166) writes *q-ṭ-r with t by Geers' law (Huehnergard 1997, 588). One attestation. See QI-TI-RI.

entries.meaning: its portion (a measured share); rival qadaša 'holy portion'

cognates.Arabic: qaṭīʿa 'portion (of land) held in fee', VIII 'took a portion' (Lane 2990)

entries.note: HT 70 .2 ]QA-*118-SA 2¼, broken before QA, part of *118 dotted (GORILA I 123), after NI · TE 30 and before I 3. With *118 = ṭa there is no q-ṭ-s root; QA-*118 (KH 10) with the suffix -ša 'its, her' gives qaṭʿ-ša 'its portion' (Lane 2990), a pre-*s > *h suffix. Rival: qōdeš 'holy portion' (HALOT 1076), which needs plain d, a value only possible for *118. A lost sign before QA would change the word. One witness.

entries.meaning: smith or cultic administrator; occupational title

cognates.Sabaic: qyn 'administrator, governor,' including an administrator of a god or king (Biella 1982, 454)

entries.note: Four Haghia Triada lists: HT 8a, HT 8b, HT 85b, the last of its roster of single units, and HT 122a, QA-*310-I 3 after TE-KI 2. QA-IN-I qaynī, with *310 in its proposed value in. Arb. qayn 'smith' (HALOT 1097), Sabaic qyn 'administrator, governor', of a god or a king as well (Biella 1982, 454): a recurring occupational or administrative title. Cf. Heb. qênî 'Kenite' (HALOT 1097). Four attestations.

entries.meaning: personal name, Hurrian type in -šenni 'brother'

cognates.Hurrian: šēna 'brother' with the individualizing -ni, šen=ni, onomastic -šenni (Giorgieri 2000, 202; Wilhelm, Hurrian, 103; Laroche 1980, 225–26): Adal-šenni (RS 11.0839, a-dal-ŠEŠ) and Tulbi-šenni (RS 19.0063+, tul₂-bi-ŠEŠ) at Ugarit; Aku-šenni at Nuzi (NPN, s.v.)

entries.note: CR(?) Zf 1, a gold pin: A-MA-WA-SI · KA-NI-JA-MI · I-JA · QA-KI-SE-NU-TI · A-TA-DE. The name stands before the 1cs verb A-TA-DE, as the one who makes the pin ready. The second sign is KI, with GORILA IV 146–147, Younger and the photograph. KN Wb 33 joins QA-KI[ (a) and NU-SE (b, read leftward) as QA-KI-SE-NU-[ (Younger, Linear A Texts, other texts). The pattern is DA-KU-SE-NE Takušenni (HT 103) beside DA-KU-SE-NE-TI (HT 104), with the same final -TI. The first element is Hurrian Kakki (Mari, Kaneš), with Kakki-še at Karana (Monti 2017, 252, 453, 388). Rival: an Amorite name on kakka 'weapon', as KAKK-A+MANN-U (Gelb 1980, nos. 3905–3912). QA for the k as Nuzi Qa-ak-ki, var. Ka-ak-ki, Ga-ak-ki, and Kakkiše, Ka-ak-ki-še, ᶠQa-ak-ki-še (NPN 78). Two attestations.
entries.source: di Mino; Younger, Linear A Texts; Laroche 1980; Giorgieri 2000; Wilhelm, Hurrian; Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943; Monti 2017; Gelb 1980

entries.meaning: goblet, cup (vessel term on HT31 inventory)

cognates.Emar: qú-pa-ḫu, qu-bá-ḫu ZABAR qubbaʿ 'cup, goblet', written with PA (GlOS 1, 338)

entries.note: HT 31: written on the *402-VS vessel logogram, quantity 10, one of Gordon's four vessel words on the tablet (Gordon 1966 §115). PA₃ writes ba: Heb. qubaʿat (קֻבַּעַת) 'goblet, cup' (Isa 51:17, 22), a vessel term with an original b, the ʿayin unwritten. Rival: Gordon's qa-pa kappu (√k-p-p 'palm, vessel'; §115), whose geminate pp resists the voicing PA₃ would need. One attestation.
entries.source: Gordon 1966 §115; di Mino; GlOS 1; DULAT; cf. Stieglitz (Kadmos 10, 1971, 111) who proposed Akkadian qapūtu / Hebrew qūpāh as alternative

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Ground' (Akkadian qaqqarum)

cognates.Akkadian: qaqqaru(m) 'ground, earth, territory, plot of land'

entries.note: A recipient or listed person at all three intact witnesses: HT 93a QA-QA-RU · I GRA+PA 5; HT 118, 6 pigs with KI 4; HT 122b, 2 in a personnel list totalled KU-RO 65. HT 111a ]QA-QA-RU 8 is broken before, so the word there can be longer; it stays out of the count. Akk. qaqqaru 'ground': Ebla has the noun as a personal name, ga-ga-lum = qaqqarum 'ground' (ARET 8 539 v. 9, 13′; Pagan 1998, row 1936), and gar₃-ga-ri₂ = qarqari (Pagan 1998, row 1988), both on the base qarqar-.

entries.meaning: parched (roasted) grain; rival Ugaritic qrwn 'offering'

cognates.Hebrew: qālî 'roasted grain', eaten before the first-fruits offering, Lev 23:14 (HALOT 1102)
cognates.Akkadian: qalītu 'parched grain' (CAD Q 59); qalû 'roasted' (CAD Q 68)
cognates.Arabic: qalā 'he fried wheat, roasted it in a pan' (Lane 2993)

entries.note: HT 86a, intact: QA-RA₂-WA 10, where HT 95a/b write QE-RA₂-U (qelwu 'parched grain') in the same set (KU-NI-SU, SA-RU, DI-DE-RU, DA-ME, MI-NU-TE). With RA₂ = /la/, √q-l-w 'roast': Geʿez qalawa, Heb. qālî (Lev 23:14; Ruth 2:14), Aram. qəlā. Rival: Ugaritic qrwn 'offering' (DULAT 703; KTU 1.127:10–11), with RA₂ = /ra/ and final n unwritten. Cf. LB qa-ra₂-wo, a personal name (KN Ce 50; DMic II). One attestation.

entries.meaning: city of (Phoenician construct form)

cognates.Phoenician: qrt 'city' (Krahmalkov 433); construct in qrtḥdšt 'Carthage, New City' (Krahmalkov 434)

entries.note: HT 132: QA-RE-TO · *21F 27, between A-SE · A319 5 and PA₃ · *305 1, in a commodity allocation. qart- 'city (of)', the Phoenician construct, which Melqart, milk-qart 'king of the city' (#2772), shows. Ug. qryt /qar(i)yatu/, also qrt /qarītu/ 'city' (Huehnergard 2012, 44), BH qiryā; the Ugarit polyglot vocabulary has qa-ri-t[u₄] 'city' (GlOS 1, 354). One attestation.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Easterner, Ancient one'

cognates.Ugaritic: qdm 'east' (Huehnergard 2012, glossary); qdmy 'ancient; ancestral' (DULAT 684); personal name Qdmn (Astour 1965, 152)
cognates.Hebrew: qedem 'east, ancient time' (HALOT 1069); qadmōnî, the Kadmonites (Gen 15:19; HALOT 1071)
cognates.Akkadian: qudmu 'early times; front' (CAD Q 295)

entries.note: MA 1a and 1b, the faces of one bar from the Malia palace: I-DU-WI · *47 · QE-DE-MI-NU and A-MA · *47 · QE-DE-MI-NU (GORILA I 268–269). QE-DE-MI-NU writes Qēdmīnu, √q-d-m 'front, east, early' with the ē of Heb. qēdmâ 'eastward' and the Ishmaelite Qēdmāh (Gen 25:15; HALOT 1070), and -īnu, beside KA-DU-MA-NE Qadmān (HT 29) with -ān, the type of Amorite Qadmānum (see KA-DU-MA-NE). Astour sets Kadmos, Kadmōn and Kadmaiōn beside W-S qdm and the Ugaritic name Qdmn (Hellenosemitica 152); Heb. qadmōnî names the Kadmonites (Gen 15:19). Rival: a non-Semitic name, or a title after *47. One bar.

entries.meaning: parched (roasted) grain

cognates.Akkadian: qalû 'roasted' (CAD Q 68); qalītu 'parched grain' (CAD Q 59)
cognates.Arabic: qalā 'he fried wheat, roasted it in a pan' (Lane 2993)

entries.note: Heads HT1 (KI-RO 197, ZU-SU 70, DI-DI-ZA-KE 52, KU-PA₃-NU 109, A-RA-NA-RE 105), a list with no commodity logogram. Closes the fixed set DA-ME, MI-NU-TE, SA-RU, KU-NI-SU 'emmer', DI-DE-RU on HT95a (under DA-DU-MA-TA · GRA) and HT95b; QA-RA₂-WA closes the same set on HT86a. Hebrew קָלִי 'parched grain', listed with wheat, barley and flour (2 Sam 17:28; Lev 23:14); Syriac qelyātā, Geʿez qēlēw 'roasted' (HALOT s.v. קָלִי); Akkadian qalītu 'parched grain' (CAD Q 59), verb qalû 'burn, roast' (CAD Q 69; OB to NA, Boğazköy and El-Amarna included); Ebla ŠE.GIBIL₄ = ga-a-tum qalwat 'parched grain' (GlOS 1, 346). QE writes the e of qelyātā and qēlēw; RA₂ = /la/; U = /wu/. With KU-NI-SU 'emmer' it is one of two grain products in a set of parties (SA-RU, DI-DE-RU).
entries.source: HALOT s.v. קָלִי; CAD Q 59, s.v. qalītu; Dillmann 1865; GlOS 1; di Mino

entries.meaning: bow, incised on the Malia palace wall; rival 'throne, seat' (PS *kussīʾ-)

cognates.Akkadian: qaštu 'bow' (CAD Q 148); rival kussû 'chair, throne' (CAD K 587)
cognates.Hebrew: qešet 'bow' (קֶשֶׁת, HALOT 1155); rival kissēʾ 'throne, seat' (כִּסֵּא, HALOT 487)

entries.note: MA Ze 11, incised in the Malia palace south of the north-west court (GORILA IV 140), complete. qešet 'bow': QE writes qe, SI še, a vowel mismatch only, and TE the feminine -t, as Heb. qešet (HALOT 1155); Akk. qaštu (CAD Q 148), Ug. qšt (DULAT 707), Geʿez qast. Rival: kussīʾ 'throne, seat' (Akk. kussû, Ug. ksu, Heb. kissēʾ), which suits a palace but has no -t for TE. One attestation. Cf. QE-SI-ZU-E.
entries.source: di Mino; GORILA IV; HALOT; CAD Q; DULAT

alternative_readings.note: throne, seat (root k-s-ʾ); Akk. kussû, Ug. ksu, Heb. kissēʾ. Fits a palace label, but the word has no -t for TE and QE must stand for k.

entries.meaning: gift for the Heroes (construct: Amorite qīšum 'gift' + ṯuʿ 'Hero, Noble'), a recipient of wine; rival 'the noble's gift'

cognates.Akkadian: qīštu 'gift presented to gods, votive offering' 1, 'gift, gratuity' 2; construct qí-iš-ti šarrum ana rēdîm iddinu 'the gift the king gave to a soldier' (CH §34:59); qí-ša-at ⟨UKU⟩.UŠ 'the gifts to the soldiers', in an oil issue (ARM 7 14:10) (CAD Q 276, 278)
cognates.Amorite: qīšum, f. qīštum 'given' (Gelb 1980, glossary)
cognates.Ugaritic: ṯʕ (II) 'Hero, Noble', title of Kirta and of the dead, deified kings as recipients of offerings: dqt ṯʕ 'one ewe, (for) the Hero' (KTU 1.39:1); ṯʕ (I) 'offering' (KTU 1.40:24) (DULAT 879–880)

entries.note: ZA 15a .2 QE-SI-ZU-E 57, the first entry under *47-KU-NA SA+VIN; with I-TI-NI-SA 10, MI-ZA-SE 3, *28B-NU-MA-RE 6 and SI-PI-KI 2½ it makes the 78½ of KU-RO VIN 78 on 15b .2 (Younger, Linear A Texts). ZA 4a .5 QE-SI-ZU-E 4, again before *28B-NU-MA-RE and SI-PI-KI. QE-SI qīši, the construct of Amorite qīšum 'given, gift' (Gelb 1980, 29) with the linking -i, as Old Babylonian qīšti in qīšti šarrum ana rēdîm iddinu 'the gift the king gave to a soldier' (CH §34:59; CAD Q 278); ZU-E ṯuʿē, ZU ṯu and E for ʿe with the guttural unwritten, as U writes ḥu in U-DE-ZA; ṯuʿ- as Akk. šuʔu beside šuwaʔu (DULAT 879). An objective genitive, as Mari qīšat ⟨UKU⟩.UŠ 'the gifts to the soldiers' in an oil issue (ARM 7 14:10; CAD Q 278): wine for the Heroes, the dead kings who receive offerings at Ugarit (DULAT 880). Rival: the subjective genitive, 'the noble's gift', the lord's present to his men. Weak point: E for the genitive, where the singular wants -i; -ē fits a dual oblique (< -ay) or a contraction. Cf. QE-SI-TE, DU-ZU-WA.
entries.source: di Mino; CAD Q; DULAT; Younger

entries.meaning: in the charge of (list heading); Akk. qātu 'hand; charge'

cognates.Akkadian: qātu 'hand; authority, custody, charge' (CAD Q 183)

entries.note: HT 7a: QE-TI · VIR+[?] heads a list of five men with numbers. Akk. qātu 'hand; custody, charge' (CAD Q 183), the word that marks whose charge a list records; QE writes qā. Cf. QẸ-TI-RA-DU · VIR+[?] (HT 58), in the same slot. Rival: a personal name, as Ebla ga-ti qāti 'hand' (Pagan 1998, row 1975). One attestation. See KA-TI.

entries.meaning: small (portions)

cognates.Akkadian: qatnu 'thin, fine, narrow' (CAD Q 173)

entries.note: HT 41a .2 QE-TU 10, complete at the start (GORILA I 79), over *305 ·, *304 10, RE · *304 10, MI-DA-NI · PA-JA 2. QE-TU writes qaṭun 'small', the final n unwritten; QE-TU-NE (HT 12) writes it out. Ebla has the name ga-da-na qaṭana 'the small one' (Pagan 1998, row 1924); Ugarit qà-ṭú-na (GlOS 1, 358). Weak point: QE for qa. Rival: Ug. qṭ 'flax, flaxseed (?)' (DULAT 708), a commodity; or a heading over the *304 entries. One attestation.

entries.meaning: small, fine (amounts)—quality term over the QA₂-ligature entry

cognates.Akkadian: qatnu 'thin, fine, narrow' (CAD Q 173)

entries.note: HT 12: QE-TU-NE · QA₂+[?]+PU 1, after QA-TI-DA-TE · OLE+DI 5 and *304 5, before E 30 and MA+RU · *118 5 (GORILA I 25). QE-TU-NE writes qaṭunē, *qaṭun- 'small, thin' with -ē: Heb. qāṭōn, qāṭān; Akk. qatnu 'thin, fine'; Ug. qṭn. QE-TU (HT 41a) is the form without the ending. Ebla writes the name ga-da-ne beside ga-da-nu, ga-da-na (GlOS 1, 358); see QE-TU. Weak point: QE for qa. Rival: a heading or name over the QA₂ entry. One attestation.

entries.meaning: my incense (ritual term)

cognates.Egyptian: group writing qu₄-da-ru₂-ta 'incense' (GlOS 1, 359, after Hoch, SWET 305, no. 440)

entries.note: KN Zc 6, an ink-inscribed clay cup from a sanctuary deposit above the Basement of the Monolithic Pillars, Knossos: .1 *34-TI-RI, .2 A-DI DA-KI-TI 'until fine' (Lev 16:12 qəṭōret … daqqâ). qiṭrī 'my incense', *34 read QI, TI for ṭi, with the 1cs possessive suffix -ī: Heb. qiṭṭēr 'to burn incense' (HALOT 1094), qəṭōret 'incense' (HALOT 1095). Rival: ʿiṭrī 'my scent', *34 for ʿi: Heb. ʿătar 'smell (of incense)' (Ezek 8:11), Arb. ʿiṭr 'scent' (HALOT 906). Weak point: *34 = qi is a proposed value. One attestation. See QA-*118-RA-RE.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Ewe' (√r-ḥ-l), as Hebrew Rāḥēl; rival Egyptian Ḥr-Rꜥ 'Horus-Ra'

cognates.Akkadian: laḫru 'ewe, full-grown female sheep', with metathesis (CAD L 42)

entries.note: HT Wc 3006, a roundel: WA-O-MI / RA-*314-RA, no logogram. raḥil 'ewe', Heb. rāḥēl 'ewe' (HALOT 1216) and the name Rachel (Gen 29:6); *314 writes the ḥ, RA the final l as in KU-RO kull. Rivals: the commodity 'ewe'; Egyptian ḥr-rꜥ 'Horus-Ra' (Ranke I, 249.15; PNM v6, personal_names_id 142609473), Horus first. One attestation.

entries.meaning: to, for, as (preposition)
entries.note: RE writes le-, the preposition 'to, for', whose vowel goes with Arabic li (Gordon 1966 §161; Heb. lə-, HALOT 507). On administrative tablets it introduces quantities: HT 32 OLE+NE · RE 104, 'libation oil for 104'; HT 66 TA-MI · RE 1; PK Zb X RE ⅓. On HT 27a RE 20, and on HT 27b RE 14, RE 70[ and RE ]40, each after SA n (SA 1, SA 4, SA 4), RE n is a counted entry, with no reading there.

entries.meaning: dance (√r-q-d); rival raqqitt- 'female dancer'

cognates.Akkadian: raqādu 'to dance' (CAD R 166); raqqidu, f. raqqittu 'dancer' (CAD R 171); riqittu 'dance' (CAD R 367)

entries.note: PO Zc 1, inked: RI-QE-TI-A-SA-SA-RA-[·]. riqitt- 'dance': Akk. riqittu 'dance' (ri-qi-it-tum; CAD R 367), from √r-q-d with the d assimilated to t; QE writes qi. The same root gives raqqittu 'female dancer' (raq-qit-tum; CAD R 171, s.v. raqqidu), with RI for ra. The pair matches U-QE-TI · JA-SA-SA-RA-ME on PL Zf 1, a -QE-TI word before the Asasara name. Rival: RI- + QE-TI, the element of HT 7a. Weak point: the cut before A-SA-SA-RA is the reader's, with no divider. One attestation.

entries.meaning: head, chief quality; first quality
entries.note: HT 115a, a GRA+BOSm list: RI-SU-MA, then SU 2 ⅕, after KA-PO-RU 1; HT 81: RI-SU-MA with the fraction L4, after A-SE · MI+JA+RU ≈ ⅙. rīšum 'head, first quality', with the nominative mimation -um: Ug. rỉš /raʾšu/ 'head' (Huehnergard 2012, 41–42), Heb. rōʾš, Akk. rēšum. Cf. RE-SU (HT 37) and A-RI-SU (HT 118, in a list summing to KU-RO 30). Two attestations. See RO.

entries.meaning: setting, arrangement; a set/group (of vessels)—deverbal noun from √ś-y-m 'to place, set'

cognates.Amarna: sīm 'placing', under West Semitic influence (Moran, EA 155 n. 1); sīm lēb (EA 139 n. 8)

entries.note: HT 31 .3, after *416-VS-KA-RO-PA₃ 10: SA-JA-MA 30[, two tens visible and the surface lost after them. MA is the last sign. The five vessel names on the tablet stand over their logograms; SA-JA-MA stands without one, as KI-DE-MA-*323-NA does on .4. A noun /śaymā/ of √ś-y-m 'to set, place' (Heb. śîm, Amarna sīm); JA writes the y. Gordon (1975, 153 n. 13) read sa-ya-ma-n[a] 'silver', after Aramaic סים: the tablet has no NA, and Jastrow (1903, 980) derives סִימָא 'silver' from Persian. Rival: a vessel name written without its logogram. Hapax. See SI-MI-TA.

entries.meaning: Samarō, personal name, 'guard'

cognates.Amorite: samar, a name element 'guard, watch' (Huffmon 1965, 251); bare ŚAMAR-A, SA-MA-RA (Gelb 1980, no. 5437); ʾAbī-Śamar (no. 134)
cognates.Egyptian: smr 'courtier' (ORAEC)

entries.note: HT 88, one of six one-unit entries in the KI-RO roster. √š-m-r 'guard', the Amorite name element samar (Huffmon 1965, 251). Rival: Egyptian smr 'courtier'. One witness.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Harnessed'; cf. Amorite Ṣamidum

cognates.Amorite: ṢAMID-UM (ZA-MI-DU-UM), a woman's name (Gelb 1980, no. 6398); ṢMD 'to bind, to harness' (Gelb 1980, 34)
cognates.Akkadian: rival samīdu B '(a type of groats)' (CAD S 115)

entries.note: HT 39 .3 SA-MA-TI 10, then KU-RE[ (GORILA I 75), complete at the left edge. The list runs TA-I-*123 10[, KU-RE-JU 8, KU[, SA-MA-TI 10, KU-RE[, then KU-RO *414+A 100[. SA-MA-TI takes no commodity sign and stands among names. It writes Ṣamidi, cf. the Amorite woman's name ṢAMID-UM (Gelb 1980, no. 6398) and Amorite ṢMD 'to bind, to harness' (Gelb 1980, 34), Ug. ṣmd 'yoked pair'. Weak point: TI for di. Rival: Akk. samīdu B, a groats (CAD S 115), which needs a commodity slot. One attestation.
entries.source: di Mino; Gelb 1980; DULAT; CAD S

entries.meaning: groats, semolina, processed grain
entries.cognates: Akkadian samīdu/samiddu 'groats, coarse meal, semolina' (temple ration lists); Emar si-im-mi-da-ti simmidatu 'a kind of flour' (GlOS 2, 198; Pentiuc 2001, 156); related to SA-MA-TI (HT39) from same root
entries.note: ZA 5a and ZA 15a, both Zakros. samidē 'groats, semolina', a borrowed Akkadian commodity noun with a Minoan ending -E; it takes quantity 4 on ZA 15a, and its slot on ZA 5a, after KI-NI-MA 7 and O-TA-NI-ZA-SE 6, admits a commodity or a name. It shares the smt skeleton with JA-SU-MA-TU, with SA-MA-TI (HT 39), whose slot shows no commodity, and with Ug. ṣmd /ṣimdu/ 'pair, yoke, team', BH ṣemed (Huehnergard 2012, 130–135). Rival: a name of the kinship-theophoric X-dāʿ type, Šumī- or Šammī-dāʿē 'my Name knows', beside A-MI-DA-U and A-MI-DA-O ʿAmmī-dāʿ; Amorite has SA-MI-DA-ḪU-UM Śami-daʿum (Gelb 1980, no. 5450), and the Bible ʾĂbîdāʿ and ʾEldāʿā (Gen 25:4). Against the rival, its -U/-E endings need a final-vowel variation, and Howard (JSS 68.1) documents u > a only in √ypʿ names (Niqmī-yapuʿ > Niqmēpaʿ).

entries.meaning: personal name, from √š-q-l 'to weigh'

cognates.Akkadian: šaqālu 'to weigh, balance, pay' (CAD Š/2 1)
cognates.Amorite: ŠQL 'weigh': šiqlum (Gelb AS 21, 33); PN ŠIQL-AN-UM (Gelb AS 21 no. 5532)

entries.note: HT11b SA-QE-RI · KA 30, the last of five KA entries summed to KU-RO 180: a recipient, so a name. Šaqeli on √š-q-l 'to weigh': SA writes š, and RI the l, as Linear A writes r and l alike. Names on the root: Amorite ŠIQL-AN-U, ŠIQL-AN-UM, ŠIQL-IM (Gelb 1980, nos. 5881–5883; glossary ŠQL 'to weigh'); Akkadian Šaqilia (ORACC P514274) and Šiqila (ORACC Q003427, Q006330).

entries.meaning: queen, princess (feminine of šarru)

cognates.Akkadian: šarratu 'queen'
cognates.Amorite: šarra beside šarratum 'queen' (Gelb 1980, glossary); ʿAštar-šarra, EŠ₄-DAR-ŠAR-RA (no. 1693); Mari women's names DN-šarra(t) 'DN is the queen' (Nakata 1995, 249); śartu 'queen', qallt, beside śarru 'king' (Buck 2019, 332)

entries.note: SAMW a 1, a Samothrace nodule: JA-SA SA-RA TE 10 ¹⁄₁₆. šarra 'queen', the feminine of SA-RU šarru 'king', -a against -u: Amorite šarra beside šarratum 'queen' (Gelb 1980, glossary), ʿAštar-šarra (no. 1693); Heb. śārā 'woman of rank, princess' (HALOT 1354), the name Sarah (Gen 17:15). Philistine seren (Heb. sərānîm, HALOT 770; Ug. srn, DULAT 759) is Minoan šarrān, šarr with the afformative -ān, as KI-RE-TA-NA Kretan. The same word is written SA-RA₂ on 20 HT tablets. Rival: JA-SA-SA-RA as one word across a line break, as IO Za 12 writes JA-SA / SA-RA-ME and IO Za 16 JA-SA-SA-RA / ME. HT 62 .1 [·-·]-SA-RA is broken before (GORILA I 117), the end of a longer word, so it stays out of the attestations. See SA-RO.
entries.source: di Mino; Gelb 1980; Nakata 1995; Buck 2019; HALOT; DULAT; GORILA I

entries.meaning: queen/princess; by metonymy the queen's or royal establishment (recipient/institutional heading)

cognates.Akkadian: šarratu (construct šarrat-) 'queen'
cognates.Amorite: šarra 'queen' (Gelb 1980, glossary); Nanni-šarra(t), a woman of Zimri-Lim's palace at Mari, written both ᵈna-an-ni-šar-ra and na-an-ni-šar-ra-at (Ziegler 1999, 278)
cognates.Linear A: SA-RU /šarru/ 'king/prince' and SA-RA /šarra/ 'queen/princess', the same title family

entries.note: Twenty Haghia Triada accounting tablets; on HT 125a ]SA-RA₂ stands at a broken edge. HT 105 sets KA-PA and SA-RA₂ in parallel before VIR 234 and 235; HT 100 and HT 94a put SA-RA₂ after a closed KU-RO and before a new commodity; HT 97b has SA-RA₂ alone, a docket or recipient label. Montecchi takes it as a sender, recipient or name and excludes a transactional sense (Montecchi 2008, 321). šarra 'queen, princess', the queen's establishment as recipient: Akk. šarratu 'queen' (CAD Š/2 72), Heb. śārâ 'woman of rank, princess' (HALOT 1354), Amorite šarra without -t, as the Mari name Nanni-šarra beside Nanni-šarrat (Ziegler 1999, 278; see SA-RA). RA₂ writes the geminate, as Linear B ra₂ writes rra, lla beside plain ra (Judson 2020, 74). Rivals: Šar-ra, a man's name at Alalakh (Niedorf 2008, 490); šeʾārā 'remainder' (√š-ʾ-r), where HT 30 and HT 34 write the deficit KI-RO; 'personnel', the 100 of HT 94a (Schrijver 2014, 26–29); 'rations' (Pope 1958, 16), against HT 105 SA-RA₂ VIR 235.
entries.source: di Mino; Montecchi 2008; CAD Š/2; HALOT; Gelb 1980; Ziegler 1999; Judson 2020; Niedorf 2008; Schrijver 2014; Pope 1958

entries.meaning: king; the king's account (heading and recipient)

cognates.Akkadian: šarrum 'king'

entries.note: HT 9a SA-RO · TE · VIN · heads a wine list, the slot RA-*164-TI holds on HT 17 and HT 19, where SA-RO 10 and SA-RO 5½ stand under VIN; HT 42+59 has SA-RO OLE+KI 8, OLE+U 2. GORILA V 295 reads the second sign as A 315 = Linear B RO₂ (Schrijver 2014, 10 n. 9), its foot traced on HT 17.2 and 19.2, one wine series (Montecchi 2010, 23), plain RO on HT 9a.1 and 42+59. Linear B ro₂ writes /rro, llo/ and alternates with ro (Judson 2020, 74), as RA₂ writes the geminate of SA-RA₂ šarra: šarr 'king', the O vowel dead as in KU-RO kull (Rendsburg 2026, 203 n. 4). SA-RO (4 tablets) and SA-RA₂ (20) never share a tablet. Schrijver takes sa-ro₂ for a variant of sa-ra₂ (2014, 10 n. 9).
entries.source: di Mino; GORILA V; Schrijver 2014; Montecchi 2010; Judson 2020; Rendsburg 2026

entries.meaning: king, prince (administrative title/category)

cognates.Akkadian: šarru 'king'
cognates.Hebrew: sǝrānīm 'city-princes' (KB 727); śar 'prince, chief' belongs with Akkadian šarru

entries.note: HT 86a and 86b (A-KA-RU · KU-NI-SU GRA+K+L 20, SA-RU 20, DI-DE-RU 20, QA-RA₂-WA 10), HT 95a (DA-DU-MA-TA · GRA, SA-RU 20 among DA-ME, MI-NU-TE, KU-NI-SU, DI-DE-RU and QE-RA₂-U) and HT 95b (A-DU · SA-RU 10, the same list): an entry in grain lists. HT 123+124a SA-RU OLIV 16, *308 4, beside KI-TA-I, PU-VIN and DA-TU; HT 94b SA-RU 1, one of five entries totalled KU-RO 5. šarru 'king', Akk. šarru (CAD Š/2 76), Heb. śar 'official, prince' (HALOT 1350): a title or category. Rivals: Ug. srn 'prince' (DULAT 759) and Heb. sərānîm, the governors of the five Philistine cities (HALOT 770); śaʿru 'barley' (Woudhuizen 2016, 226; Heb. śəʿōrâ, Ug. šʿrm, Old Aramaic šʿrh), ʿ unwritten, a grain kind beside QE-RA₂-U 'parched grain', which fits the four grain lists but not the olive and roster entries. See SA-RA.

entries.meaning: tribute, gift—logographic abbreviation of šay(u); administrative category marker for goods designated as tribute/gift offerings

cognates.Hebrew: šay (שַׁי) tribute, gift, present. Ps 68:30—tribute brought to the Temple; Ps 76:12—tribute brought to the Awesome One; Isa 18:7—tribute brought to YHWH Ṣebaʾôt. √š-y biconsonantal root
cognates.Akkadian: šūtu / šâtu gift, present—functional parallel

entries.note: One sign in three uses, the pair of TE terûmā. In entries of the form SI · n, ten times at HT, KH, PH and GO, it marks part of a quantity as tribute: HT 106 MI-NU-TE · CYP · 6 · SI · 5½ · SI · 1 · DA · 8 · SI · 3, sub-quantities within a CYP reckoning; on HT 30, SI · 4 opens a summary of several commodities. Alone, it stamps 92 HT nodules, one of the single-sign nodule categories: *301 231, KU 152, KA 150, SI 92, RO 91, ZE 46, TE 27, I 25. In ligatures it appears as SI+SE (3 tablets), QI+SI (ZA 9), SI+ME and SI-CYP (HT 130), 'tribute-cypress', on the model of VIN+TE 'wine-offering'. Heb. šay (שַׁי) 'tribute' is brought to a temple or a divine authority at all three of its attestations (Isa 18:7; Ps 68:30; 76:12). SI šay, the owed or diplomatic gift, stands beside TE terûmā, the free donation to the sanctuary.

entries.meaning: the account/record (phonetic complement + logogram)

cognates.Ugaritic: spr (II) 'tablet, register, list, inventory; record of tribute' (DULAT 756)

entries.note: HT 34 DA-JU-TE · SI-*516 ·, the heading, before SA-RA₂ · MI+JA+KA. SI is a phonetic complement giving the s- onset of the logogram *516, its proposed value SIPRU, as PA₃ gives the b- of BUṬNU in PA₃-*188. Ug. spr /sipru/, pl. sprm /siparūma/ 'document' (Huehnergard 2012, 42), BH sēper. One attestation.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Arranger'

cognates.Akkadian: sadāru 'to array, to set in a row' (CAD S 11)

entries.note: HT 17: SI-DA-RE 5 after SA-RO 10 under RA-*164-TI · TE · VIN 38. HT 122a: SI-DA-RE 1 in a roster of men, KU-RO 31. √s-d-r 'to set in order' (Akk. sadāru, Heb. sēder); SI-DA-RO (GO 2r) and JA-SI-DA-RA[ (PH 7a) are on the same signs. RE writes the -i of names in -I, as Amorite KAKKAR-I (Gelb 1980, no. 3957); SI-DA-RO has -u. Rival: √s-t-r 'to hide', Heb. Sitrī (Exod 6:22). Two attestations. See *324-DI-RA.

entries.meaning: personal name, Ugaritic Šadiya (šdy II), 'field'

cognates.Ugaritic: šdy (II) PN, syllabic ši-DI-ia, PRU 6 78 (RS 19.41):4, 16, and ša-TI-ya, PRU 3 40 (RS 15.173) rev. 2 (DULAT 799)
cognates.Akkadian: Šadīya, a personal name at Kiš (de Boer 2014, 401)

entries.note: A personal name in the damaged HT 126a list, immediately followed by 1. Ugaritic alphabetic śdy is attested as a PN in šmbʿl bn śdy (BAH 214, 7, o 14), and syllabic {m}ša-di-ia occurs at Ugarit in RS 15.0173, r. 2′. Ugarit also writes it ši-DI-ia (PRU 6 78:4, 16), SI-DI-JA sign for sign, and DULAT files both spellings under šdy (II) (DULAT 799). Kiš has ša-di-ia as a name too (de Boer 2014, 401). Sanmartín files the Ugarit names ša-du-ya, ša-dì-ia under Sadaw/y 'open field, field, steppe' (GlOS 2, 272–273). Rivals: 2514 'mountain', on the same lemma; a Hurrian element šad- (Kinlaw 1967, 201–202).
entries.source: GORILA I 217; ORACC aemw/ugarit P521356.17.3 (BAH 214, 7, o 14); P503354.14.2 (RS 15.0173, r. 2′); de Boer 2014; GlOS 2; Kinlaw 1967

entries.meaning: which goes out (disbursement marker)—relative particle šī + 3ms imperfect √y-ṣ-ʾ "to go out"

cognates.Hebrew: אֲשֶׁר־יֵצֵא ʾašer-yēṣē "that which goes out" (2 Kgs 12:13, Temple expenditure)
cognates.Akkadian: ṣītu "expenditure, disbursement"; wāṣītu "outgoing goods" (OB/MB palace archives)
cognates.Phoenician: š- relative particle (< PS *ḏū)—diagnostic Canaanite feature

entries.note: A suffix on pithos labels: A-NA-NU-SI-JA-SE (HT Zb 159), KI-TA-NA-SI-JA-SE (PE Zb 3). Two morphemes, a relative clause: šī, the Phoenician-type relative (cf. MLK Š-PʿL), with yāṣē, the 3ms imperfect of √y-ṣ-ʾ with the third aleph lost (*yiṣʾaʾu > yāṣē), marking goods as issued. Hebrew Temple accounts use the same construction, אשר-יצא (2 Kgs 12:13), relative with imperfect √y-ṣ-ʾ, for expenditure, and Akkadian ṣītu is the term for disbursements against ēribu 'income'. With SI the relative š(ī), Minoan sides with Canaanite š- against Ugaritic and Aramaic d-. Bare yāṣē stands in JA-PA-RA-JA-SE yapʾara yāṣē (SY Za 9, a Syme libation vessel), the libation as 'that which goes out'; see JA-SE.

entries.meaning: office of the steward or prefect (√s-k-n); rival sukkā 'booth' (√s-k-k)

cognates.Hebrew: šākan "to dwell" (HALOT 1496); šĕkīnā "Shekhinah"; OR sukkā (סֻכָּה) "booth, tabernacle" (√s-k-k "to cover"); Sukkot (סֻכּוֹת) festival of booths
cognates.Akkadian: šakānu "to place, set, establish" (CAD Š1 115); šaknu "governor"

entries.note: Six identical nodules from Portico 11/Room 13 at Haghia Triada (HT Wa 1014–1018, 1028): sealings of an institution, the office of a steward or prefect. √s-k-n (š-k-n), the title family of Ug. skn 'prefect, governor; manager, administrator' (DULAT 746), the Amarna gloss sú-ki-na (DULAT 746) and SI-KI-NE Sikinet. Rival: √s-k-k 'to cover', Heb. sukkā 'booth'. Weak point: SI-KA writes neither the n of the title nor a suffix. IO Za 6 I-NA-TA-I-ZU-DI-SI-KA ends in a homograph, šiqā 'she who gives drink' (√š-q-y).

entries.meaning: stewardess or female administrator; compare masculine prefect/commissioner

Amarna.meaning: commissioner, one who provides (glossing Akk. rābišu)
Amarna.moran_page: Intro p. xxvi n.70; EA 287 n.22
Amarna.note: Moran: West Semitic *sōkinu (Hebrew sōkēn), 'one who provides.' Durand proposes 'resident.' These administrative title readings are the primary comparison.

cognates.Hebrew: sōkenet (סֹכֶנֶת), Qal participle fs, of Abishag (1 Kgs 1:2, 4)

entries.note: HT 116a: SI-KI-NE GRA 12, then *304 12, in a list of grain and oil issues, after *OLIV+TU 2 and before QA-NU-MA GRA 20. Sikinet /šikinēt/ follows SI-KI-NE syllable for syllable, with the feminine final /t/ unwritten. Ugaritic šknt /sākinat-/ 'female administrator, stewardess' (Tropper 2000, 180, KTU 4.135:2; škn 4.36:3), and Hebrew has the same feminine participle, sōkenet, of Abishag (1 Kgs 1:2, 4); Akk. šakintu, oblique šakinte, 'woman manager' (CAD Š/1 165). The masculine is Ugaritic skn /sākinu/ 'prefect', syllabic sā-ki-ni (Huehnergard 2012, 156), and Amarna Canaanite sū-ki-ni /sōkini/, a prefect or commissioner. Rival: the masculine title 'prefect, commissioner'. Weak point: one attestation. See *47-KU-NA.
entries.source: di Mino; Tropper 2000; Huehnergard 2012; Lipiński 1997; CAD Š/1

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Hired' (√ś-k-r 'to hire'); rival šēkār 'strong drink'

cognates.Hebrew: śākîr 'hired labourer' (HALOT 1327); śākār 'wages, reward' (HALOT 1331); šēkār 'intoxicating drink, beer' (HALOT 1501), the rival
cognates.Amorite: Sa-ki-rum, Mari (Huffmon 1965, 54), under škr 'hire, reward, favor' (Huffmon 1965, 245)

entries.note: HT 8a: JE-DI · OLE+KI 10, then PA₃-KA-RA-TI 1½, PA 3½, TE-*301 2, QA-*310-I ¾, SI-KI-RA ¼, KI-RE-TA-NA ½; a recipient of KI-oil beside Tēnā 'Fig', the smith and the Cretan. √ś-k-r 'to hire' (Ug. /š-k-r/ I, DULAT 804; Heb. śākār 'wages', HALOT 1330): at Mari Sa-ki-rum and the woman's name Sa-ki-ra, under *škr 'hire, reward, favor' (Huffmon, APNM 245–46), Sa-ki-rum compared to Hebrew śākîr 'hired; hireling' (APNM 145); Gelb, AS 21, no. 5400 ŠAKIR-U (SA-KI-RU). Rival: Hebrew שֵׁכָר šēkār 'strong drink' (HALOT 1501; Lev 10:9), √š-k-r 'to become intoxicated' (Ug. /š-k-r/ II, DULAT 804). A-SI-KI-RA (KH 20) stands in the entry slot before CYP+E, parallel to ]DU-RE-ZA. One witness.

entries.meaning: name, renown, progeny (common noun in construct state; also attested as personal name Šima = Shem)

cognates.Akkadian: šumu "name, offspring, progeny" (CAD Š/III 281); Amorite PN element: Sumu-abum "Progeny of the Father" (founder of 1st Dynasty of Babylon, c. 1894 BCE), Sumu-la-El "Progeny of God"

entries.note: PH Zb 4 (Phaistos, a clay vessel): SI-MA 𐄁 I-JA-TE. Either the common noun šima 'name of', in construct with I-JA-TE, šima ʾiyyate 'name of the island', or the personal name Šima, Shem, 'Name, Renown, Progeny', a person named on a commodity vessel, as DI-NA-U 𐄁 VIN on KN Zb 27. šumu- is the most productive element of Old Babylonian Amorite names (Sumu-abum, Sumu-la-El, Šumu-ditāna in Hammurabi's genealogy), and Amorite has the bare ŠU-MU-UM Šumum (Gelb 1980, no. 5941). Rival: the name Šimaʿ 'hear!', Ebla si-ma, three witnesses (Pagan 1998, row 4222). No case is assigned, since nothing here selects one (Fischer 2002, §140). One attestation. See JA-SU-MA-TU.

entries.meaning: pourings, libation portions (wine administration term)
entries.cognates: Akkadian šapāku 'to pour, heap up'; Hebrew šāpak (שָׁפַךְ) 'to pour out, shed'; Ugaritic špk 'to spill, shed' (DULAT 823)
entries.note: ZA 4a *28B-NU-MA-RE 13, SI-PI-KI 5; ZA 5b *28B-NU-MA-RE 20, SI-PI-KI 1½, then MA-KA-I-TA 3 (Makīt, a recipient); ZA 15a *28B-NU-MA-RE 6, SI-PI-KI 2½: beside JI-NU-MA-RE 'wine-stewards' on all three Zakros wine tablets, with commodity quantities. šipkī 'pourings, libation portions', √š-p-k 'pour out': Heb. šāpak 'pour out', Ug. špk 'spill', Akk. šapāku 'heap up; pour, serve lavishly' (HALOT 1629). Rival: the attested noun šipku, Mari SÍG ši-ip-ku 'in bulk, loose' and šipku 'cereal(s)' (GlOS 2, 257–258; CAD Š/3 71). Three attestations. See JI-NU-MA-RE.

entries.meaning: sacred song, hymnody (abstract in -ūt of √š-y-r "sing")

cognates.Akkadian: non-cognate semantic and morphological controls in -ūtu: kalûtu "the lament-singer's craft/repertoire," zammārūtu "music," and Old Babylonian nārūtu "musicianship"

entries.note: šīrūt 'sacred song', an abstract in -ūt from √š-y-r 'sing', 'sacred' from its ritual distribution: 7 tokens on stone vessels at five peak sanctuaries (Iouktas, Kophinas, Syme, Troullos, Vrysinas), fragmentary on IO Za 14, IO Za 15 and TL Za 1; PK Za 11 breaks after SI-RU-[. Ugaritic syllabic ši-i-ru /šīru/ 'song' gives the root and the long ī in the Bronze Age (Huehnergard 2012, 158). The plural šīrōt 'songs' (Amos 8:3) would be SI-RA-TE from *šīrāt or SI-RO-TE from šīrōt; Linear A keeps O and U apart (Steele 2024, 17), and the stone has RU wherever the sign survives (IO Za 2, KO Za 1, SY Za 3, VRY Za 1). TE writes final t with a support vowel, as in genitive position on AP Za 2 and PH Zb 4. Rival: širrūt 'cultic service' (√š-r-t), MHeb. šêrût, JArm. šêrûtā 'service, worship' (HALOT 1661), the Levites who stand 'to minister to him' (lĕšārĕtô, Deut 10:8) and the singers who 'ministered … with song' (1 Chr 6:17), Ph. mšrt 'service' (KAI 60.7–8; Krahmalkov 2000, s.v. MŠRT); Ugaritic šrd 'to serve' is 'more likely' Š of √yrd (Huehnergard 2012, 157). Weak point: after I-PI-NA-MA a genitive šīrūti is expected (Fischer 2002, §292).
entries.source: di Mino; Huehnergard 2012; Steele 2024; HALOT; Krahmalkov 2000; Fischer 2002

entries.meaning: vessel (pot)

cognates.Egyptian: group writing ṯi₂-pa-ra sipl 'large drinking bowl, crater', ra for l (GlOS 2, 203, after Hoch, SWET 364, no. 541)

entries.note: HT 31, the vessel tablet, written with the *402-VS vessel sign among QA-PA₃, SU-PU and KA-RO-PA₃; Ventris and Chadwick also take it for a vessel. Gordon read su-pa-ra as Heb. sēpel (ספל) 'bowl' (Gordon 1966 §115), with PA for p and RA for l. PA₃ writes ba, so the spelling is s-b-r: √s-p-l with p voiced to b between u and a, and RA for l. In Gordon's HT 31 set, four of the five vessel names are Semitic (§115). Weak point: PA₃ = ba is a proposed value; Gordon's p gives √s-p-l directly. One attestation.

entries.meaning: bowl, basin (the vessel named on HT31)

cognates.Old Syrian: Mari sà-ap-pu sapp 'a type of bowl' (GlOS 2, 203)

entries.note: On HT 31, the vessel tablet, the word is written into a vessel sign: *415-VS-SU-PU 10, beside *416-VS-KA-RO-PA₃ 10 (the jar, Akkadian karpu) and *402-VS-QA-PA₃ 10. sapu 'bowl, basin': Heb. sap (HALOT 762), Ug. and Ph. sp 'bowl' (DULAT 753), Mari sà-ap-pu (GlOS 2, 203); a bowl, which also keeps HT 31's two vessels distinct. See SU-PU₂-*188.

entries.meaning: bowl of terebinth (pistachio) nuts (commodity measured in bowl-units)
entries.note: HT 8b .1 SU-PU₂-*188 1, heading the list, before PA₃-*188 2 and QA-*310-I 1⅜ (Haghia Triada, Villa Magazine). SU-PU₂ sapu 'bowl, basin' (see SU-PU) with the commodity *188 buṭnu 'terebinth' (CAD B 358): Heb. boṭnîm 'pistachio nuts' (Gen 43:11; HALOT 121), Ug. bṭm 'pistachio' (DULAT 249); one bowl of terebinth nuts. SU-PU₂ alone on HT 63, under the personnel sign *305, is the name Ṣubʾu, a homograph; here it is bound to *188, as PA₃ is in PA₃-*188. See *188 and PA₃-*188.
entries.source: di Mino; CAD B; HALOT; DULAT

entries.meaning: may you (f.) be favorable toward us (N-stem of √r-ṣ-y + indicative -u + analogical 2fs subject clitic -tī + 1cp object -n)

cognates.Hebrew: rāṣāh (רָצָה) 'to be pleased with, accept favorably' (Lev 1:4, Ps 19:15, Mal 1:8, Ezek 20:40–41, 43:27); rāṣōn (רָצוֹן) 'favor, acceptance, goodwill' (Prov 11:1, Ps 5:13); √r-ṣ-y 'to accept, be pleased'
cognates.Akkadian: râṣu 'to be content, acquiesce' (CAD R 186)
cognates.Arabic: raḍiya (رضي) 'to be pleased, satisfied, accept'; riḍā 'acceptance, divine pleasure'

entries.note: IO Za 2 .2, in the frame TA-NA-[X]-U-TI-NU shared with IO Za 6 (X = I-*301) and IO Za 11 (]U-TI-NU). TA- is the 2fs prefix, -NA- the N-stem n- unassimilated before r, where Hebrew assimilates it, תֵּרָצֶה tērāṣeh 'it shall be accepted' (Lipiński 1997, §41.16), RA-TE √r-ṣ-y 'be acceptable', the Hebrew Niphal of Lev 1:4, U the indicative -u of yaqtulu before the subject pronoun (Ugaritic ʾargmk /ʾargumu-kī/, KTU 1.3 III 21), with the modal 'may' sense (Huehnergard 2012, 55–56), and -u 'remains attached directly to the verbal base, and pronominal object suffixes follow it' (Bjøru and Pat-El 2021, 56). TI is the archaic 2fs nominative subject clitic, the clitics drawn from the nominative pronouns and usable on other bases (Pat-El 2025, 330, 332), extended to a finite host, NU the 1cp object 'us' (PS *-na, Ugaritic -n/-nā, Eblaite accusative -nu in i-ne-sa-nu, ARET XVI 16, Kogan and Krebernik 2021, 754). Cf. Enūma eliš I 119–120 ul taremmināsi 'you (f.) do not love us', Josh 2:18 hôradtēnû and Ugaritic tšqy-n (KTU 1.19 IV 53). Byblos marks person twice in the same way, ta-šap-pár-ta 'why were you sent?' (EA 102:10), and PS Za 2 writes TA-NA-I-*301-TI (di Mino, Ya Diktu 14). TE writes *ṣ́ after r with the T-series, as A-RA-TU ʾarṣ́- (#768) does. One attestation.

entries.meaning: may [it] be drunk for you (f.)—N-stem 3fs imperfective of √š-t-y 'to drink' + 2fs pronominal suffix -kī

cognates.Akkadian: šatû 'to drink'

entries.note: PR Za 1, a Prassa stone vessel (LM IA), position 1, the verb slot of the formula, before SE-TO-I-JA, a place name or epithet, and A-SA-SA-RA-ME, the formula word, with RA drawn reversed. tanašutē-kī 'may [the offering] be drunk for you (f.)', the vessel addressing the Goddess: TA-NA the prefix ta- with the N-stem na-, here 3fs with the offering as subject, where TA-NA-RA-TE-U-TI-NU (√r-ṣ-y) has the same ta- as 2fs, the t- prefix serving both persons; SU and TE the first two root consonants of √š-t-y, š (the sibilants merged) and t; KE the 2fs suffix -kī; the weak third radical y unwritten, as in III-weak verbs. Both verbs have the N-stem shape with the root after TA-NA. One attestation.

entries.meaning: the goddess TNT (Tinnit), feminine of √t-n-n 'sea-dragon'
entries.note: Four Haghia Triada lists: HT 7a TA-NA-TI 1, among the men under QE-TI · VIR+[?]; HT 10b TA-NA-TI 9¼, the last entry; HT 49a ]TA-NA-TI 1, in a list with KU-PA₃-NU and TU-SU-PU₂; HT 98a TA-NA-TI ¾, among fractional issues with RO-KE and KA-RI-*310-I. Tanāti, the goddess TNT with the a-vowels against Punic Tinnit: the feminine of √t-n-n, Heb. tannîn, Tannin 'sea-monster, sea-dragon', Ug. tnn (HALOT 1764). Rival: ʿAnat with the feminine prefix t-, *t(a)-ʿanât > *teʿnât > *tennât (Hvidberg-Hansen 1979, 140, who takes the prefix as Libyco-Berber). TA-NA-TE is the Zakros form. See TA-NA-TE.

entries.meaning: may you (f.) be gracious, favourable

cognates.Amorite: NʿM 'be pleasant': naʿimum, niʿimatum (Gelb AS 21, 26)

entries.note: KN Za 10: ]TA-NU-MU-TI · before JA-SA-SA-RA-MA-NA (GORILA IV 8–9). ta-nʿum-u-tī 'may you (f.) be gracious', a G u-class prefix form of √n-ʿ-m: Arabic naʿuma/yanʿumu has the u-vowel, Sabaic n²m 'be favourable, prosper' the closest sense (Beeston et al. 1982, 90), and Hebrew nāʿamt (Song 7:7) the 2fs in the same sense. The ʿ is unwritten. Byblos marks person twice in the same way, ta-šap-pár-ta (EA 102:10), and PS Za 2 writes TA-NA-I-*301-TI (di Mino, Ya Diktu 14). Weak point: the break before TA is of indeterminate extent. Rival: Thomas's plural-agreement reading, with -ti a third-person plural subject marker (Thomas 2020, 12–14). One attestation. See TA-NA-MA-JE.
entries.source: di Mino; GORILA IV, 8–9; Beeston et al. 1982, 90, s.v. N²M; Fischer 2002, §162f; Harding 1971, 139; Thomas 2020

entries.meaning: chant a dirge!

cognates.Hebrew: Piʿel √t-n-y ‘recount, recite’ (Judg 5:11; 11:40), including a proposed association with repetition in antiphonal performance (HALOT, 1759–60)
cognates.Northwest Semitic: Hebrew qînâ ‘funeral song, dirge’; Syriac qintā ‘hymn, lament’ (HALOT, 1097)

entries.note: PL Zf 1, a silver pin from a funerary context: … TA-NU-NI-KI-NA · NI-NU-NI …. tannî qînâ 'chant a dirge!': tannî, the 2fs Piʿel imperative of √t-n-y 'recount, recite' (Judg 5:11; HALOT 1759), and qînâ 'funeral song, dirge' (HALOT 1097). TA-NU-NI keeps the doubled middle radical with a dead vowel in NU; KI-NA writes qînâ without the vowel length or the final h. The same Piʿel is the women's yearly rite for Jephthah's daughter, lətannôt (Judg 11:40; HALOT 1759). The votive texts join words without a divider, as U-NA-KA-NA-SI wannā kanāsī and JA-PA-RA-JA-SE yapʾara yāṣē (SY Za 9). Weak point: one attestation. See TI-NU-JA.

entries.meaning: gatekeepers (of the sanctuary); rival Akkadian tārû 'child-minder'

cognates.Ugaritic: ṯġr (II) 'gatekeeper', pl. ṯġrm, in personnel and ration lists (KTU 4.126:22; 4.141 III 2; 4.128:11)
cognates.Akkadian: tārû/tāriu 'child-minder, male nursemaid or fosterer' (rival)

entries.note: HT 89 TA-RA 5, last of five classes under A-SA-RA₂ · *307 (dubur 'sanctuary'), KU-RO 87. /ṯa(ġ)ra/ from *ṯaġr- 'gate', ṯ written in the T-series before a and ġ unwritten: Ug. ṯġr 'gatekeeper', a personnel class with grain rations (DULAT 888); the gatekeepers of the house of God beside MA-I-MI's water-drawers (Ezra 7:24). Cf. TA 4, last entry before KU-RO on HT 94a (entries 111 against KU-RO 110), and ]TA 4 before ]KU-RO 129 on HT 109, broken on the left. Rival: Akkadian tārû 'male nursemaid' (CAD T 250), which predicts TA-RU. One witness.
entries.source: di Mino; DULAT; Uchitel 2006; SED II; CAD T

entries.meaning: personal name; rival tati 'father' (Luwian tati-)
entries.note: An entry in two lists of quantities: HT 26a TA-TI 21, before MI-KI-SE-NA 15 and U-NU-*21F 5; HT 97a TA-TI 2, under VIR+KA 82 beside PA-I-TO and KA-NU-TI. Ugarit has the man's name Tati, DUMU-[MEŠ {m}ta]-⸢ti⸣ 'the sons of Tati' (RS 15.0109 + RS 16.0296 o 24; ORACC aemw/ugarit P503325), its first sign restored. Rival: CL Luwian tati- 'father' (Melchert 1993, 209). Two attestations.

entries.meaning: proposed Semitic lexical name of the PALM/TREE sign
entries.note: *49 (AB049), PALM/TREE by its pictorial form, four tokens at three sites: TO-*49-RE (PE 2), DA-U-*49 (HT 120), U-*49 whole (ZA 10b) and ]U-*49 after a left break (HT 126a). tamir, PS *tamr- 'date palm': Heb. tāmār (HALOT 1756), with Ug. syllabic [ta]-ma-ru (HALOT 1756), Arb. tamr 'dates, the fruit of the palm-tree' (Lane 317). TO-*49-RE gives t-m-r with *49 in its proposed value mi, and DA-U-*49 reads Dawmi. Weak point: *49 = mi is a proposed value; Linear B writes *49 beside ordinary MI in tu-*49-mi. See TO-MI-RE.

entries.meaning: contribution, offering (terûmā), a transaction marker

cognates.Ugaritic: trmt 'offering' (KTU 1.43:3; 1.6 VI:44; Copenhagen Ugaritic Corpus lexicon)
cognates.Akkadian: cf. tāmartu 'gift, present (to temple or king)'

entries.note: TE stands with VIN in the heading of every HT wine tablet and with the large barley entries of HT 40, 52 and 133 (Montecchi 2010, 17, 19). It marks commodity-number entries on 54 documents, and 25 HT nodules carry it alone (HT Wa 1122–1146). terûmā 'contribution, offering' (HALOT 1788), Ug. trmt 'offering', trmt lbš w ktn 'an offering: a garment and a tunic' (KTU 1.43:3; DULAT 866); TE abbreviates it, and VIN+TE is a wine-offering. Weak point: KU stands beside the full KU-RO kull, where no TE-RU-MA stands beside TE. See RU-MA.

entries.meaning: Fig (personal name); a recipient in allocation lists

cognates.Akkadian: tittu (tiʾittu), pl. tinātu 'fig'; Old Assyrian 'Month of Figs' (CAD T 435)

entries.note: A recipient on both tablets: HT 8a TE-*301 2 in the OLE+KI list between PA 3½ and QA-*310-I ¾ (QA-*310-I receives again on HT 8b); HT 98a TE-*301 ¾ between DI-RE-DI-NA and RO-KE. Tēnā 'Fig': TE-*301 writes the shape of Hebrew təʾēnāh 'fig' with the ʾ lost, as in Judaic Aramaic tēnəṯā (HALOT 1675). A fruit-tree name as a personal name, as Hebrew Tamar 'date palm' (HALOT 1756) and Ugaritic tmr (DULAT 859). Weak point: *301 = na is a proposed value, and no other fig-name is attested. Two attestations. See TI.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Merciful (god)'; rival tayyār 'trader'

cognates.Akkadian: tajjāru 'merciful; turning back', from târu, in names: aA Aššur-tayyār, aB Ilum-, Marduk-, Sîn-tayyār, Tayyār-ilu, hypocoristic Tayyarītum (CAD T 60; AHw 1303–1304)
cognates.Ugarit: ti-ya-ru₃ Tiyaru, a man's name (RS 14.0016 r 3, ORACC aemw/ugarit)
cognates.Hebrew: hattārîm 'traders', beside rōkəlîm (1 Kgs 10:15 = 2 Chr 9:14; HALOT 1708)

entries.note: HT 117a (Haghia Triada, Casa Room 9, LM IB): one of ten entries counted 1 each, KU-RO 10, under the heading MA-KA-RI-TE 'merchants', alongside KU-RA-MU Kurmu 'Vineyard', KU-PA₃-NU Kubānu and NA-DA-RE Nadr 'Vow'. Ugarit has the man's name Tiyaru, ti-ya-ru₃ (RS 14.0016 r 3); Linear B has the man's name te-ja-ro (KN V 479). Akkadian names give the sense: tajjāru 'merciful (god)', from târu 'turn, relent', in Aššur-tayyār, Sîn-tayyār and Tayyār-ilu (AHw 1304; CAD T 60), of which Teyar is the short form; tajārtu is the god's 'forgiveness', lit. 'return' (CAD T 59). Rival: tayyār 'trader', √t-w-r 'travel about': Heb. hattārîm 'traders' (1 Kgs 10:15; HALOT 1708), Ug. /t-r/ 'to scour, travel through' (DULAT 862–863), on the qattāl pattern of Heb. ṣayyād 'hunter' (√ṣ-w-d). One attestation.
entries.source: di Mino; AHw 1304; CAD T 59–60; ORACC aemw/ugarit; HALOT 1708; DULAT 862

entries.meaning: Tinit (goddess, = Phoenician Tanit)

cognates.Phoenician: tnt 'Tanit' (Sarepta, KAI 285, 7th c. BCE: dedication to Tanit-Astarte)
cognates.Punic: tnt 'Tinnit' (Carthage stelae: lrbt ltnt pn bʿl 'to the Lady Tinnit, face of Baal')
cognates.Punic in Greek letters: Θινιθ-Φανεβαλ, Θεννειθ-Φενηβαλ 'Tinnit-Phanebal' (Krahmalkov 2000, 495); Θινιθ-Φανεβαλ on the El-Hofra stele EH 1.1/5 (ibid., 126)

entries.note: HT 27a: TI-NI-TA directly before *307 DUBUR 'sanctuary', the goddess with her sanctuary, as Linear B Potnia Daboritu. The variant TA-NA-TI is commoner, four attestations (HT 7a, HT 10b, HT 49a, HT 98a). Punic in Greek letters writes Θινιθ, i–i, on the El-Hofra stele EH 1 (Krahmalkov 2000, 126), beside Θεννειθ (ibid., 495), against the conventional 'Tanit': the vowels of TI-NI-TA, a millennium later. Rival: a Berber origin for Tanit, on the t…t feminine of Tamazight names, against which an LM I attestation a millennium before Carthage stands. See TI-NI-TA *307.

entries.meaning: Tinit of the Sanctuary (Goddess + Sanctuary pattern)

cognates.Punic in Greek letters: Θινιθ 'Tinnit' on the El-Hofra stele EH 1.1/5 (Krahmalkov 2000, 126, 495)

entries.note: HT 27a: TI-NI-TA *307 'Tinit of the Sanctuary', the goddess's name with the sanctuary logogram, kept whole as the attested epithet. Linear B Potnia da-pu₂-ri-to-jo and Hebrew Baʿalat ha-Dəḇîr carry the same title. For *307, see VIR+*307.

entries.meaning: date palm, its produce

cognates.Hebrew: tōmer 'palm', tōmer Dəbôrâ, Judg 4:5 (HALOT 1757); tāmār 'date palm' (HALOT 1756)

entries.note: PE 2: TO-*49-RE 1, the last entry of a Petras commodity list, after QA-QA-DA ½ and TO-ME ⅓. *49 is read PALM/TREE as a logogram; at the proposed syllabic value mi, TO-MI-RE gives t-m-r, tōmir, palm or date-palm produce: Proto-Semitic *tam(V)r-, Heb. tāmār 'date palm' (HALOT 1756), Ugaritic tmrm, read 'dates' by Pardee (DULAT 859), Arb. tamr. TO writes the ō of Heb. tōmer 'palm' (Judg 4:5). Final RE writes the coda /r/. Weak point: *49 = mi is a proposed value, and TO-MI-RE is one of its two syllabic witnesses, with DA-U-MI. One attestation. See TO-MA-RO.

entries.meaning: the pure ones (adjective, masculine plural -īna), a grain and oil recipient

cognates.Hebrew: ṭohŏrâ 'cleanness, purification', dəmê ṭohŏrâ 'blood of purification', Lev 12:4 (HALOT 370); ṭōhar 'purity' (HALOT 370)

entries.note: HT 129: KI-RE-TA₂ Kret receives grain, fat and figs; TU-*21F-RI-NA, in the same slot, grain 40½ and three oils (OLE+DI 1, OLE+KI 6, OLE[). ṭuhārīna 'the pure ones', the plural of the adjective √ṭ-h-r 'pure': Ug. ṭhr /ṭuhūru/ < *ṭahūru (DULAT 875; Huehnergard 2012, 42), plural in bht ṭhrm iqnim 'a palace of the purest lapis' (KTU 1.4 V 19; DULAT 90–91); Heb. ṭāhôr (HALOT 369); Ar. al-mutaṭahhirīna 'those who purify themselves' (Q 2:222). TU writes ṭu, the u of Ug. /ṭuhūru/. -NA is the plural *-īna, which the external endings carried first on adjectives (Huehnergard 2019, 59), as on the grain recipient DI-RI-NA. Akkadian counts pure men, 7 LÚ.MEŠ KÙ.MEŠ (CAD E 104). Rival: ṭuhārī-nā 'our purification', Heb. ṭōhar 'purifying' (Lv 12:4, 6; HALOT 370), with the flour and oil of Lev 14:10, 21. Weak point: one attestation. See OLE+TU.

entries.meaning: my wholeness, my completeness (noun *tumm- + 1cs -ī)

cognates.Hebrew: tōm 'integrity, completeness'; bətummî 'in my integrity', Ps 26:1 (HALOT 1743)

entries.note: Two damaged witnesses give the group in full. PK Za 8 (GORILA IV 24–26) secures the start with a divider before TU, but ME is partial and I survives only as the tops of three prongs at the broken corner, with no divider before JA-SA[ on the next face; Younger reads only TU as sure (Younger, Linear A Texts, PK Za 8). PK Za 14 (GORILA IV 40) secures the end, ]-TU-ME-I · JA-SA-SA-[, but breaks before TU. Hebrew תֻּמִּי tummī 'my wholeness, integrity' (Ps 7:9; 26:1) has the same nominal shape. On both vessels √t-m-m stands before a √y-š-r word (JA-SA[, JA-SA-SA-[), as Job 1:1 tām wə-yāšār and Ps 25:21 tōm wāyōšer pair them (di Mino, Ya Diktu), which supports 'my wholeness, [in righteousness]' with the two roots kept apart. Rival: a D-stem imperative 'be made whole', though a regular factitive imperative keeps more of the stem. Two attestations.
entries.source: di Mino; Younger, Linear A Texts

entries.meaning: judge (title)
entries.note: POR Zf 2 (Poros Herakleiou): a single word stamped on a bronze object, an authority token or judicial seal. ṯāpiṭu 'judge': Ug. ṯpṭ, Yamm's epithet ṯpṭ nhr 'Judge River'; Heb. šōpēṭ 'judge' (√š-p-ṭ, ṯ > š); Arb. ṣabiṭ. TU writes ṯ in the T-series, as KA-TA-RE writes it with TA (di Mino, Ya Diktu 16–17 n. 27); TA writes ṭ. One attestation.

alternative_readings.note: sacred precinct / place of judgment (root ṯ-p-ṭ (same root)). Cognates: Heb. תֹּפֶת tōpet (2 Kgs 23:10, Jer 7:31–32); Punic tpt (Carthaginian sacred precinct for votive deposits) tōpet may itself derive from √ṯ-p-ṭ: 'place of judgment' where the deity accepts/rejects the offering. If so, ṯāpiṭu and tōpet are cognate derivatives of the same root, and the two readings collapse: 'judge' (title) → 'place of judgment' (sacred precinct). Both senses fit a metal votive object at a harbor sanctuary.

entries.phonological_notes: Skeleton tpt requires T→ṯ (interdental), P→p (trivial), T→ṭ (emphatic). TU writes /ṯā/ because ZU=/ṯu/ is vowel-locked to /u/. PI = /pi/. TA = /ṭu/ with dead vowel.

entries.meaning: Shield, Protector (invoked in formula position two); the name Tursha

cognates.Aramaic: תְּרִיסָא tᵉrîsā 'shield', rendering Hebrew māgēn (Tg. Ps 3:4) and ṣinnāh (Tg. Ps 5:13) (Jastrow 1698)
cognates.Egyptian: twršꜣ Tursha, a Sea People, under Merneptah and at Medinet Habu (di Mino, Ya Diktu)
