entries.note: KO Za 1, formula position two, before DU-*314-RE · I-DA-A dubur ʾIda 'the sanctuary of Ida'. √t-r-s 'to shield, protect' (Ar. turs; Lane 302); the shield-bearing Kouretes of Ida, and the Sea People Tursha, named from the same root (di Mino, Ya Diktu). Rival: Mari has Tursa as a place or ethnic name (FM V, 281). One attestation.

entries.meaning: Teshub (Hurrian storm god theophoric PN)

cognates.Hurrian: Teššub/Tešub 'storm god'—supreme deity of Hurrian pantheon (Laroche 1980, 263; Hittite Tarhunt)
cognates.Ugaritic: tṯb, the Hurrian storm god in Ugaritic texts (DULAT 870)

entries.note: HT 49a, a personnel register: TU-SU-PU₂ 1, beside KU-PA₃-NU, TA-NA-TI and eight other names. Hurrian Tešub, the storm god, as a theophoric name: TU-SU-PU₂ writes t-s-b, with PU₂ for b. Faience and cylinder seals show Hurrian contact. Weak point: one attestation.

entries.meaning: and (conjunction)

cognates.Hebrew: wə- (וְ) 'and'; û- (וּ) before b, m, p and shewa (Gesenius §104e)
cognates.Akkadian: u 'and' (Gordon 1966 §163)

entries.note: GORILA has U after a number on ARKH 4b (RE 10 U̥[, .2; GORILA III 15) and HT 56a (]11 ½ U[, .2; GORILA I 109), and U[ on HT 126a and U̥[ on HT 47a (GORILA I 91). u 'and', with the allomorph wa- in WA-DU-NI-MI 'and (to) the lord(s)' (HT 6b, HT 85b; see DU-NI-MI) and prefixed u- in U-DI-RI-KI. Gordon's only citation, Brice I,14 (*ya-ta-no-x u ya-[*), is in GORILA the U inside the formula verb JA-TA-I-*301-U-JA (AP Za 1). Weak point: every standalone U breaks after the sign, so each can open a lost word, and Linear A accounts do not otherwise join entries with a conjunction. See WBQY.

entries.meaning: mother; rivals Akk. ummu 'capital', u- 'and' + PALM/TREE

cognates.Akkadian: ummu 'mother; initial investment, capital' (CAD U/W 120)

entries.note: ZA 10b .3 U-*49 6, in a list of entries with numbers. *49 writes mi, as in DA-U-*49 Dawmi and TO-*49-RE tamir; U-MI ʾummi 'mother', or Akk. ummu 'initial investment, capital' (CAD U/W 120), an account term. Rival: u- 'and' + *49 PALM/TREE, though *49 never stands alone. HT 126a ]U-*49 1 is broken before U. One witness. See U-MI-NA-SI and A-RE-TU-MI.

entries.meaning: My mother is chief/exalted (sentence name)
entries.cognates: Ugaritic ʾum "mother", našaʾa "to lift, raise"; Hebrew nāśīʾ (Gen 23:6 nəśîʾ ʾĕlōhīm); Amorite mother-element in Ummum-ka-abī (Gelb AS 21 nos. 6246–7, FN) and Našiʾ name element (NIQM-I·LA·NAŠIʾ, no. 5051); ʾummī + predicate in ʾUmmī-ʾilī, UM-MI-I₂-LI₂ (no. 6231), a woman's name, as are all of Gelb's ʾUMM-I names; Ebla na-si-um, Amorite ia-aḫ-wi-na-si (GlOS 2, 106); = *301-SI nāśī (PROBABLE)
entries.note: HT 117a and HT 28b, in the header both times, outside the count: on HT 117a (MA-KA-RI-TE KI-RO U-MI-NA-SI) the roster's ten entries of 1 sum to KU-RO 10 without it, the responsible party, not a counted worker; on HT 28b it stands in the header pair with A-SI-JA-KA before the commodity block. Ummī-naśiʾ 'My mother is chief', a sentence name: ʾummī 'my mother', the geminate mm written with one sign, with naśiʾ 'chief, exalted one' (√n-ś-ʾ 'lift'; see *301-SI). U- is radical: bare MI-NA-SI and DI-MI occur nowhere in the corpus, and the tablet's other U- words are radical too, U-SU ʾUšu, mainland Tyre, and U-DI-MI ʾUdmī, the man of Udum, origin labels known from Amarna. Amorite women's names carry the mother element (Ummum-ka-abī 'the mother is like my father'). Rival: u-Minasī 'and Minasī', MI-NA-SI sign for sign the Neo-Assyrian Mi-na-si-i (Manasseh), √m-n-n with mnn > mnš, beside MI-NA-NE; it needs the conjunction, the dissimilation and an eight-century reach, and the Ugaritic mnn > mnš pair is in neither the Copenhagen Ugaritic Corpus nor DULAT, where the tribute word is mnḥ (KTU 3.8:21, 3.10:1; mnḥy 'offering', KTU 1.2 I 38). See DA-NA-SI, U-*49.

entries.meaning: So, behold my gathering! (conjunction + presentative + G verbal noun kanāsī + 1cs -ī)

cognates.Hebrew: kānas (כָּנַס) 'to gather, assemble' (Esth 4:16, Ezek 22:21, Neh 12:44); knesset (כְּנֶסֶת) 'assembly, gathering'; √k-n-s 'to gather'
cognates.Akkadian: kamāsu A 'to gather, store' (CAD K 114–117); earlier form of Hebrew kns via m~n interchange (Greenfield 2001, 840–846)
cognates.Aramaic: knaš (כנש) 'to gather, assemble'; kiništu (NB/LB loan) 'priestly college' (AHw 480a; Greenfield 2001)
cognates.Arabic: kanasa (كنس) 'to sweep, collect'; kanīsah (كنيسة) 'synagogue, church' (< Aramaic knš)

entries.note: U-NA is wannā 'and behold', Ugaritic wn from *wa-hanna/u, the Hebrew wə-hinnē (Lipiński 1997, §27.25); the alphabetic spelling leaves the vowels open, and winnā is the rival. KA-NA-SI is kanāsī, the G verbal noun of √k-n-s 'gather' with the 1cs suffix -ī, 'my gathering', agreeing with the 1cs A- of formula position one. SI writes s and the hushed š alike, so KA-NA-SI also reads kanāšī, with the š of Aramaic knaš 'gather' and knāš 'gathering'. The group is intact on KO Za 1, PK Za 8, SY Za 2 and TL Za 1, restored or partial on IO Za 2 and IO Za 9. Rivals: Syriac knšy 'gather!' (Peshitta Jer 10:17); kanāšī 'my submission' (√k-n-š, Akk. kanāšu 'bow down'; Amorite ka-na-šum, ka-ni-šum, Ebla gi-ne-su-um, GlOS 1, 313), the sense of Arabic ʾislām 'submission' (Q 3:19). See U-NA-RU-KA-NA-SI.

entries.meaning: and behold, may my gathering [take place] (proposed precative lū)

cognates.Hebrew: kānas (כָּנַס) 'to gather, assemble' (Esth 4:16, Ezek 22:21, Neh 12:44); knesset (כְּנֶסֶת) 'assembly, gathering'; √k-n-s 'to gather'
cognates.Akkadian: kamāsu A 'to gather, store' (CAD K 114–117); earlier form of Hebrew kns via m~n interchange (Greenfield 2001, 840–846); lū 'may, indeed'—the precative/asseverative particle written by -RU- (akk_hg_0642)
cognates.Aramaic: knaš (כנש) 'to gather, assemble'; kiništu (NB/LB loan) 'priestly college' (AHw 480a; Greenfield 2001)
cognates.Arabic: kanasa (كنس) 'to sweep, collect'; kanīsah (كنيسة) 'synagogue, church' (< Aramaic knš)

entries.note: PK Za 12 writes U-NA-RU-KA-[?]-JA-SI, JA legible (GORILA IV 38). The lost sign is restored as NA from the formula, and NI fits the trace equally (Soldani 2012, 221–222 n. 129). NA-JA recurs in I-NA-JA-PA-QA on PK Za 11, a Palaikastro spelling, and PK Za 11 preserves U-NA-RU-KA-NA-TI whole. U-NA wannā 'and behold', RU lū 'may', KA-NA-SI kanāsī 'my gathering'. Akkadian lū introduces a positive injunction in a verbless clause (Huehnergard 1997, §22.2). Duhoux and Thomas take -RU- for a morphological variant within the group, Thomas an infix (Duhoux 1992, 69–70; Thomas 2020, 12–13). Cf. IO Za 16, which ends U-NA-RU-KA[. Rival: Soldani's KA-NI-JA- beside KA-NI-JA-MI (CR Zf 1), with SI an ending. Hebrew has the same sequence, hēn lū yəhî 'behold, may it be' (Gen 30:34). Weak point: the sign after KA is restored. One attestation. See U-NA-KA-NA-SI for the rival √k-n-š.

entries.meaning: the burning one (f.); name or epithet

cognates.Hebrew: yqd 'to burn' (HALOT 430); yōqedet 'burning' (f. ptc., Isa 65:5); môqēd 'hearth, burning' (HALOT 560)

entries.note: PL Zf 1, a silver pin from beside Platanos Tholos A: ]TA · WI-TE-JA-MU · U-QE-TI · JA-SA-SA-RA-ME (GORILA IV 161). Feminine participle of √w-q-d 'to burn': U writes w-, as in U-NA-KA-NA-SI wannā; QE the qe of Heb. yōqedet; the d before t unwritten; TI the feminine -t. Initial w- where Hebrew and Aramaic have y-. Rival: U- + QE-TI, the element of HT 7a, HT 58 and PO Zc 1. Weak point: one attestation.

entries.meaning: light of the Levite (compound PN)
entries.note: HT 25a, a personnel roster: U-RE-WI 1, on the same roster as DU-RU-WI. ʾūr-lēwī 'light of the Levite': U writes ʾūr 'light, flame' (√ʾ-w-r) and RE-WI lēwī, the type of Hebrew ʾŪriyyāh (HALOT 25). DU-RU-WI ends in the same -WI on the same tablet, an ethnonymic element. Rival: lāwī, the Ebla name la-wi 'one who encircles' (Pagan 1998, row 3460). One attestation.

entries.meaning: sanctuary personnel

cognates.Egyptian: group writing d-bi₄-r dabīr 'naos, inner sanctuary' (GlOS 1, 140, after Hoch, SWET 376, no. 561)

entries.note: VIR with *307 dubur 'sanctuary' (see DU-PU₂-RE): sanctuary personnel, at Khania alone. KH 9 opens A-SI-SU-PO-A · VIR+*307, before NI and CYP entries; KH 14 VIR+*307 2 follows NI ¼ among CYP entries; KH 19 *306-VIR+*307 13 heads OLE+TA ⅓. Heb. dəbîr 'rear room, holy of holies' (HALOT 208), Egyptian group writing d-bi₄-r dabīr 'naos, inner sanctuary' (GlOS 1, 140).

entries.meaning: a counted class of men, VIR qualified by *313

cognates.Akkadian: raqqu (rāqu) "oil presser, perfume maker" (CAD R 173)
cognates.Ugaritic: rqḥ (I) "perfumer, druggist" (DULAT 734); Ebla /rāqihum/, ra-gi-um (VE 892, apud DULAT 734)

entries.note: HT 89, HT 94a, HT 100, HT 127b and KH 7a: VIR marks a human referent, and the counts make VIR+*313 a class of men: on HT 89 VIR+*313a 13 stands in the total 23+22+24+13+5, KU-RO 87, and on HT 100 VIR+*313a 16 is counted in KU-RO 97. Three palaeographic variants stand in comparable lists: VIR+*313a (A570) on HT 89 and HT 100, VIR+*313b (A571) on HT 94a and KH 7a, VIR+*313c (A572) on HT 127b. No phonetic complement fixes *313. Rival: *rāqiḥū 'perfumers', √r-q-ḥ: Ug. rqḥ 'perfumer' (DULAT 734), Akk. raqqu 'oil presser, perfume maker' (CAD R 173), Heb. rōqēaḥ 'ointment-mixer' (HALOT 1290), which rests on co-occurrence with aromatics. CYP and the other aromatics are not confined to these tablets, and on HT 89 CYP follows the personnel total, in a separate section.

entries.meaning: kāribū, intercessory priests (VIR with the KA complement)

cognates.Akkadian: kāribu 'worshipper'; deity in adoration (CAD K 216); karābu 'prayer, blessing' (CAD K 192)
cognates.Amorite: KRB 'bless, pray': jakrub, kirb(ān)um (Gelb AS 21, 23)

entries.note: HT 97a VIR+KA 82, HT 100 VIR+KA 58, HT 88 A-DU VIR+KA 20, HT 28a VIR+KA-VIN 6, and VIR+KA alone on five Khania roundels, KH Wc 2029–2032 and 2106. VIR marks personnel, and KA is a written complement: a personnel class. KA writes the initial of Akk. kāribu 'one who prays', designating a priest (CAD K 216): the kāribū. Rival: Akk. kallû 'official, messenger' (CAD K 83). Weak point: no witness spells the word out, and KA is also the initial of the rival kallû. Nine attestations.

entries.meaning: Beloved of the Deep (title or name)

cognates.Arabic: widd 'love' (Lane 2931); names of wdd + a god: wddʾl, wddʿm (Harding 1971, 637)
cognates.Ugaritic: thm 'ocean', thmt 'Primordial Ocean' (DULAT 851); ydd il ġzr 'beloved of El, the hero' (DULAT 943)
cognates.Akkadian: tâmtu, tiāmtu 'sea'; Tiāmat (CAD T 150)

entries.note: PL Zf 1, a silver pin from beside Platanos Tholos A: ]TA · WI-TE-JA-MU · U-QE-TI · JA-SA-SA-RA-ME (GORILA IV 161). WI = wid(d)-, as in WI-DI-NA Widdinā, dd unwritten before t; TE-JA-MU = ti(h)āmu, h unwritten, JA the glide. Construct 'beloved of the Deep', the title type of Ug. ydd il. Sign dispute: GORILA reads WI and MU, both doubtful; a second reading of the facsimile takes the fourth sign as RU, which gives no reading. -MU the nominative the Amorite construct names keep, as SU-MU-A-BU-UM beside SU-MU-A-BI-IM (Gelb 1980, nos. 5606, 5608). One attestation.

entries.meaning: this (f.sg. demonstrative)

cognates.Hebrew: zō(ʾ)t 'this' (f.sg.), from an earlier interdental demonstrative base; closest lexical parallel (Huehnergard 2023, 46)
cognates.Phoenician: ʾGN n.f. 'bowl'; FK D 35 hʾgn hz 'this bowl,' with a postposed demonstrative (Krahmalkov 2000, 31)
cognates.Ugaritic/Arabic: dāti/ḏāti is an inflected genitive relative/possessive form with a phonemic final /i/; it is retained only as the rejected rival analysis

entries.sigla_note: SigLA reads AB74 (ZE) against GORILA AB17 (ZA) at KNZc7 position 4. The /zāt/ proposal depends on GORILA's ZA reading; ZE-TI would require a different vocalization or analysis.
entries.note: Fills the gap Gordon (1966 §156) marked between A-KA-NU and DU-RA-RE. ZA-TI writes zāt (older *zāʾt), TI giving final t with a support vowel; Hebrew zō(ʾ)t, from West Semitic *ðv̄- (Huehnergard 2023, 46), is the closest parallel. Phoenician ʾGN is feminine, and FK D 35 hʾgn hz 'this bowl' sets the demonstrative after its noun (Krahmalkov 2000, 31): A-KA-NU ZA-TI 'this bowl'. Rivals: ḏāti 'of', whose Ugaritic dāti and Arabic ḏāti keep a genitive i and need an agreement frame absent here; a name, 'bowl of Zati': Ebla za-ti (Pagan 1998, row 5052; ARET 15 30). Weak points: a hapax; GORILA reads ZA where SigLA reads ZE; A-ZU-RA on the same cup leaves its final t unwritten. See TA-TE-I-KE-ZA-RE.
entries.source: Gordon 1966 §156; Krahmalkov 2000, 31; Huehnergard 2023, 46; Pagan 1998; di Mino

entries.meaning: breast (√ṯ-d-y, PS *ṯad-); at IOZa6 first member of ZU-DI SI-KA (ṯudī-šiqā)

cognates.MSA: Mehri ṯódi, Harsusi ṯōdi, Soqotri tódi "breast, bosom"

entries.note: IO Za 6 I-NA-TA-I-ZU-DI-SI-KA: ZU-DI is the first member of the compound epithet ZU-DI SI-KA ṯudī-šiqā 'Breast-Who-Gives-Drink', after I-NA-TA-I ʿInatī 'my Anat'; its -ī is the construct vowel binding it to SI-KA. ṯudī 'breast': Ug. ṯd (DULAT 886), Arab. ṯady-, Mehri ṯódi, Harsusi ṯōdi (SED I, no. 280). Ugarit has the nursing at Athirat's breast, ynqm b ảp zd ảṯrt 'who suck at the nipples of Athirat' (KTU 1.23:24), zd an allomorph of ṯd (DULAT 983). ZU-DI-RA occurs on HT Wc 3011–3012. See ZU-DU.

entries.meaning: breast (woman's)
entries.note: HT 51b ]ZU-DU ⅝, after ]KU-ME-TA 12[; HT 99b ZU-DU 1, after SI+SE FIC 6 and DA-SI-*118 2, before RU-MA-TA 1: a counted entry, in a fraction on HT 51b. ṯudu 'breast', a biconsonantal noun: Ug. ṯd 'breast, bosom', also 'breast (of meat)' (DULAT 886), Heb. šad 'breast' (HALOT 1416), Ar. ṯady-. Two attestations. See ZU-DI.

entries.meaning: Bull- (personal name)
entries.note: KN Zb 52, a clay vessel: ZU-RI-NI-MA alone. √ṯ-w-r 'bull' (semitic_roots 269), ZU writing the ū of Ebla šu-ra /ṯūr/ (GlOS 2, 330) and Akk. šūru, with -īn and mimation -MA. Cf. I-ZU-RI-NI-TA (PH 6), with feminine -TA. One attestation.

entries.meaning: conjunction u- "and" + dirik "way, path"—Hebrew derek דֶּרֶךְ, Akkadian darāku "to tread"; cross-ref DA-RE-KU (ZA18a, same √d-r-k skeleton, different vowel class)

cognates.Akkadian: darāku "to tread, follow"

entries.note: PH 7a .2 U-DI-RI-KI[, broken after KI (GORILA I 295). Amorite and Ebla names on √d-r-k mean 'successor': darikum (Gelb 1980, nos. 1404, 1481–82), Dark-i-Ma (no. 1497), Ebla dar-gi (GlOS 1, 150); the sense 'way' rests on Hebrew derek. DA-RE-KU (ZA 18a)is an independent √d-r-k token at Zakros.

entries.meaning: head, top, capital (Akkadian qaqqadu(m))

cognates.Akkadian: qaqqadu 'head; top; original amount, principal' (CAD Q 100, 108–109)

entries.note: PE 2, among fractional entries: A-RI-PA ¼, QA-QA-DA ½, TO-ME ⅓. QA-QA-DA writes qaqqada, the geminate unmarked, as QA-QA-RU qaqqaru. Akk. qaqqadu 'head; original amount, principal' (CAD Q 100, 109). Rival: a personal name, as on the neighbouring entries: Qaqqadum (Old Babylonian, ORACC rimanum), Amorite qa-aq-qa-da-an, Ebla ga-ga-da-nu (GlOS 1, 340). One attestation.

entries.meaning: all, totality, everything (administrative category: miscellaneous/general allocation; section subtotal)

cognates.Akkadian: kalu/kallu 'all, totality, everything'

entries.note: HT 127b: KU-RO *307 156, KU 72, VIR+*313c 24, KI+MU 15, *301 11 and the erased KI+MU 14, KU-RO 292 (GORILA I 219): KU is one section of the total. On HT 131a KU 353 is the largest number, a subtotal; on HT 45b KU ¼ stands three times. KU alone marks 151 HT nodules (HT Wa 1471–1622), the second commonest after *301, and stands on tablets at five sites. HT 42+59 has KU-[ ]OLE[, a broken longer word. kull 'all, section', beside KU-RO kull-rōʿu 'grand total': Ug. kl /kullu/ 'each, every, all, entire' and kll /kalīlu/ 'entirety, everything' (Huehnergard 2012, 37), BH kōl, kālīl.

entries.meaning: palm-measure, bowl (unit of dry/liquid measure; administrative commodity category)

cognates.Akkadian: kappu 'palm of hand, bowl, pan; a small unit of measure'
cognates.Hebrew: kap (כַּף) 'palm, hollow of hand, bowl, pan, spoon'

entries.note: HT 11b: *86 KA 40, KA 30, KA 50, RU-ZU-NA KA 30, SA-QE-RI · KA 30, KU-RO 180: the sum is exact, and KA is the unit counted out to named recipients in 30s to 50s; on GO 2r KA ⅛ is a fraction of it. kapp 'bowl, palm-measure': Akk. kappu B 'bowl', and at Mari barley and linseed measured ina kappi maḫīrim 'in the k. of the market' (ARMT 13 100:7; CAD K 188). It stands alone on 149 HT nodules (HT Wa 1322–1470), the third commonest after *301 and KU, and appears on tablets at HT, KH, Milos and Gournia. On HT 85b and HT 140 KA is an entry of its own: KA 1 stands among KI-RE-TA₂ 1, PA 1 and DI 1 under KI-KI-RA-JA (HT 85b); KA 1 and ]KA 1 alternate with OLE+U as KA-PA ½ does on the same tablet, so KA there abbreviates KA-PA (HT 140; Montecchi 2010, 15). Rival: kaspu 'silver', which the abbreviation to one syllable weakens.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'he shone forth' (causative of w-p-ʿ 'be brilliant')

cognates.Hebrew: הוֹפִיעַ hôpîaʿ "shone forth" (hiphil; Deut 33:2, Ps 50:2; HALOT 424)
cognates.Amorite: *wpʿ 'be brilliant', apart from *ypʿ 'raise up': Ya-a-pa-aḫ-ᵈIM, Ya-pí-iḫ-ᵈIM (Huffmon 1965, 212); yapiʕ 'radiant' in names (GlOS 2, 375)
cognates.Ugaritic: /y-p-ʿ/ "to go up, rise"; PN ypʿ, syll. ia-pa-ú; ypʿbʿl, ypʿmlk (DULAT 958–959)
cognates.Egyptian: group writing y-w-pꜢ-ʕ, a name with the w-glide (GlOS 2, 374, after Schneider, APÄQ 53)

entries.note: KN Zf 31 · A-WA-PI ·, undotted, between dividers (GORILA IV 155), among the man's names. Causative with ʾa-, final ʿ unwritten. The w is the root's: Huffmon separates *wpʿ 'be brilliant' from *ypʿ 'raise up' (1965, 212), and Heb. hôpîaʿ, the theophany verb (Deut 33:2; Ps 50:2; 80:2), keeps it in ô < aw. The bare verb as a name, as Ug. ypʿ, syllabic ia-pa-ú (DULAT 958), and Amorite Ya-a-pa-aḫ. Cf. JA-WA-[?] on PE Zb 7, its third sign unread, for the prefix form. Rival: ʿawp 'bird' (Heb. ʿôp), which would need *306 for ʿa. See JA-PA.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'who stands: He is fire'

cognates.Amorite: QWM 'to stand'; GA-MI-DINGIR Qawmī-ʾIl (Gelb 1980, no. 1743)
cognates.Eblaitic: šū-X 'he is X': šū-ʾabu 'he is father', šū-nūrī 'he is my light' (Pagan 1998, rows 4265–4285)

entries.note: KN Zf 31, a silver pin, first line, between DA-DU-MI-NE and A-WA-PI; whole and undotted (GORILA IV 155). QA-MI qāmī 'who stands', the opener of Qawmī-ʾIl. *47 = so writes šū, as in *47-NU-RA-JA Šū-nūraya (HT 115a); so for šū is a vowel mismatch only. NA-RA nār 'fire' against NU-RA nūr 'light' on HT 115a, the Arabic pair. Standing, fire and shining forth are the theophany's: yāqûm ʾĕlōhîm 'God arises' (Ps 68:2); ʾĕlōhîm hôpîaʿ … ʾēš lə-pānāyw tōʾkēl 'God shone forth … fire devours before him' (Ps 50:2–3), and A-WA-PI 'he shone forth' follows. The same pin writes SU in TE-SU-DE-SE-KE-I. Rival: *47 = mo, manāra 'lampstand' (Ug. mnrt, DULAT 558). One attestation. See *47-KU-NA.
entries.source: di Mino; Gelb 1980; Pagan 1998; Kogan 2011; DULAT

entries.meaning: reeds (qanūma); heading on KH 88, grain entry on HT 116a

cognates.Akkadian: qanû 'reed; arrow; measuring rod' (CAD Q 85)

entries.note: KH 88 heads its list with QA-NU-MA; on HT 116a QA-NU-MA GRA 20 is the last of six grain recipients under U-TA-RO · TE, with KU-PA-JA Kubbaya and SI-KI-NE Sikinet. qanūma 'reeds' < *qanawūma, as Huehnergard reconstructs Ugaritic qnm, with Eblaite qā-nu-wu, qā-nu-um (Huehnergard 2008, 291), the closest vocalic parallel. Weak point: on HT 116a reeds stand in a recipient's slot. Rival: √q-n-y 'acquire, possess', a heading for acquisitions. See QA-NE and KA-NA.

entries.meaning: verbal ending: indicative -u + 2fs -tī + -n(u) 'us'

cognates.Arabic: qatal-ti-nā 'you (f.) killed us', 2fs subject before 1cp object (Fischer 2002, §§207, 268, 270)
cognates.Akkadian: attī … ul taremmīnâši 'you do not love us', Enūma eliš I 119–120 (Haubold et al. 2025, 32–33)
cognates.Ugaritic: indicative -u before a suffix, ʾargmk /ʾargumu-kī/ 'I will say to you (fs)', KTU 1.3 III 21; 1cp object -n, -nā (Huehnergard 2012, 33–34, 74)
cognates.Amarna Canaanite: Byblos ta-šap-pár-ta 'why were you sent?', the person marked twice, by prefix ta- and suffix -ta, EA 102:10 (Baranowski 2014, 120; Rainey 1996, 2:345); yâtinu 'us', EA 74:26; ittinu 'with us', EA 81:50 (Rainey 1996, 1:68, 91)

entries.note: Ending of the petition verb: TA-NA-RA-TE-U-TI-NU (IO Za 2), TA-NA-I-*301-U-TI-NU (IO Za 6), ]U-TI-NU · I-NA-I-DA-[ (IO Za 11, broken before U). Davis, Thomas and Monti isolate it (Monti 2022, 111–112). U = indicative -u, TI = 2fs -tī, which fixes the ta- prefix as 2fs, as in PS Za 2 TA-NA-I-*301-TI 'may you (f.) answer', NU = -n(u) 'us' (di Mino, Ya Diktu; cf. Eblaite accusative -nu, Kogan and Krebernik 2021, 754). Thomas takes -u-, -ti- and -nu as three suffixes, not one morpheme (Thomas 2020, 16). Rival: -NU the precative particle (cf. Heb. nāʾ, Ps 119:108). Three attestations.
entries.source: di Mino; Monti 2022; Kogan and Krebernik 2021; Thomas 2020

entries.meaning: Piṭrī, personal name, 'my release'

cognates.Ugaritic: pṭry, Semitic personal name (DULAT 677); /piṭru/ 'loosening, release', pí-iṭ-r[ù] (GlOS 2, 142)
cognates.Amorite: PTR 'solve, redeem'; Annu-puṭri, Ištar-puṭri; Paṭriya (Gelb 1980, no. 1056)
cognates.Akkadian: paṭāru 'to release, loosen' (CAD P 297)

entries.note: PK Za 11, once: PI-TE-RI A-KO-A-NE, in the subject or dedicant slot (Davis 2013, 42–43; Thomas 2020, 8–10). Piṭrī 'my release', a personal name in apposition to A-KO-A-NE 'the priest', on the qitl base of Ugaritic /piṭru/ 'loosening, release' (GlOS 2, 142): Ugaritic PN pṭry (DULAT 677), Amorite PTR 'solve, redeem' in Annu-puṭri and Ištar-puṭri (Gelb 1980, 339; Nakata 1995, 244). Rivals: the common noun piṭrī 'my release'; a 2fs imperative 'release!'; the goddess Pidray (pdry, syllabic pi-id-ra-yu), with TE writing d; Gordon's pi-te za 'this engraved monument' (1966, §124), Phoenician ptḥ 'inscription' with z 'this' after it, as pthy z (KAI 10.3–5, 14), which reads the third sign, a loop on a long stroke, as ZA where GORILA dots RI, with no divider before it.
entries.source: di Mino; Davis 2013; Thomas 2020; GlOS 2; DULAT; Gelb 1980; Nakata 1995; Gordon 1966

entries.meaning: the priest (proposed title after PI-TE-RI)
entries.note: PK Za 11 .2 […]-RE · PI-TE-RI · A-KO-A-NE ·, the one witness; damaged A-[…]-NE stands in the same slot on PK Za 12. A title in apposition: PI-TE-RI A-KO-A-NE 'Pitrī, the priest', ha-kōhan with the Canaanite article ha-. Ug. khn 'priest' (DULAT 428), Heb. kōhēn (HALOT 461–462), Phoenician khn (Krahmalkov 2000, 224). The second A writes the a that h keeps in Heb. kōhănîm, JArm. kāhănā (HALOT 461) and Arb. kihānat 'divination' (Lane 3004). Name and title stand as in Heb. ʾahărōn ha-kkōhēn 'Aaron the priest' (Exod 31:10). Rivals: a second personal name, the second of two dedicants (Davis 2013, 42; Thomas 2020, 8, 10); Akk. and Nuzi Aḫūni 'our brother' and Arb. ʾaḫawāni 'two brothers', which fit the signs poorly. Weak point: one attestation.

entries.reading: wannā lū kanasti / winnā lū kanasti
entries.meaning: so, behold, may you gather!

cognates.Hebrew: כְּנֶסֶת kəneset 'assembly' (later Hebrew); כָּנַסְתִּי qānastī 'I gathered' (Eccl 2:8)
cognates.Akkadian: kamāsu A 'to gather, store' (CAD K 114–117); earlier form via m~n interchange (Greenfield 2001)

entries.note: PK Za 11, after A-SA-SA-RA-ME and before I-PI-NA-MI-NA: U-NA /wannā/ or /winnā/ 'so, behold' + RU /lū/ 'may' + KA-NA-TI /kanasti/, 2fs suffix form of √k-n-s 'gather': 'so, behold, may you gather!' (di Mino, Ya Diktu). The coda /s/ is unwritten, per the Linear B rule that drops syllable-final s before a stop (Ventris and Chadwick 1956, 45; pa-ka-na /phasgana/). Hebrew has the same opening sequence: הֵן לוּ יְהִי hēn lū yəhî 'behold, may it be' (Gen 30:34). Cf. KA-NA-SI /kanāsī/ 'my gathering'. Rivals: a K-N-S-T feminine collective /kanast/, 'may there be a gathering', with lū introducing a verbless injunction as in Akkadian (Huehnergard 1997, §§22.2, 29.3; cf. later Hebrew kəneset 'assembly'); /kānastī/ 'I gathered', paralleled by Biblical Hebrew כָּנַסְתִּי (Eccl 2:8), a 1cs verb; √k-n-š, see U-NA-KA-NA-SI. One attestation.

entries.meaning: you (f.) gathered (2fs suffix form; after lū 'may you gather'); rival K-N-S-T feminine collective 'assembly'

cognates.Hebrew: כְּנֶסֶת kəneset 'assembly' (later Hebrew); כָּנַסְתִּי qānastī 'I gathered' (Eccl 2:8)
cognates.Aramaic: kənaš 'to assemble' (Dan 3:2); Syriac knuštā 'congregation, synagogue' (Peshitta, Acts 6:9)
cognates.Linear B: pa-ka-na /phasgana/ and PA-I-TO /Phaistos/ illustrate non-writing of /s/ before a stop

entries.note: PK Za 11, in U-NA-RU-KA-NA-TI. kanasti 'you (f.) gathered', the 2fs suffix form of √k-n-s, with the s unwritten before t, as Linear B omits s before a stop (pa-ka-na phasgana) and PA-I-TO writes Phaistos (Ventris and Chadwick 1956, 45, 80); after RU lū it reads 'may you gather!' (di Mino, Ya Diktu). Rivals: a feminine collective kanast 'assembly', with final I a support vowel, as later Hebrew kəneset and Aramaic and Syriac knuštā; TI as -tī, qānastī 'I gathered' (Eccl 2:8); √k-n-š, see U-NA-KA-NA-SI. One attestation.

entries.meaning: Behold, he opens (his eyes)!—theophanic epiphany closure
entries.note: PK Za 11 closes with I-NA-JA-PA-QA, after I-PI-NA-MI-NA SI-RU-[?] ·, the last words of the damaged prayer; JA-PA-QA stands alone on PK Za 12. I-NA hinna 'behold!' and JA-PA-QA yapqaḥ, 3ms yaqtul of √p-q-ḥ 'open (the eyes)'. Hebrew hinnēh/hēn and Ugaritic hn 'behold!' (DULAT 337) give the presentative, and Isa 42:7 lipqōaḥ ʿênayim 'to open eyes' the usage. One attestation. See JA-PA-QA, I-NA.

entries.meaning: he opens (the eyes)

cognates.Hebrew: פָּקַח pāqaḥ "to open (eyes)" (Isa 42:7 lipqōaḥ ʿēnayim ʿiwwərōt "to open blind eyes")
cognates.Eblaite: ib-ga-il yipqaḥ-ʾIl 'ʾIl opened', a name (Pagan 1998, row 2878)

entries.note: PK Za 12, the complete final group, and PK Za 11, after I-NA. yapqaḥ, 3ms yaqtul of √p-q-ḥ 'open (the eyes)': Heb. pāqaḥ (HALOT 959), Aram. pqḥ, PS *paqaḥ-, the final laryngeal unwritten. Rival: √p-q-d, which needs a final d. JA- requires a masculine subject: in Tropper's prefix paradigm the 3rd feminine takes t- in singular, plural and dual, and y- stands only in masculine cells (Tropper 2000, 432, §73.222), with gender agreement kept when the verb stands first (886). Hebrew leaves a preceding verb in the uninflected 3ms only before subjects 'denoting animals or things' (GKC §145 o, p. 465). Weak point: the damaged context has lost the subject. Two attestations. See I-NA-JA-PA-QA.

entries.meaning: behold! (presentative particle)
entries.note: PK Za 11 I-NA-JA-PA-QA, the close of the prayer, and AP Za 2 I-NA-JA-RE-TA[: hinna 'behold!', the bare counterpart of U-NA u=hinna, written as one word with what it presents. Heb. hēn, hinnē 'behold' (HALOT 251–252), Ug. hn 'behold!; here' (DULAT 337). Rival: Akk. ina 'in, when', in suitable contexts. Two attestations. See I-NA-JA-PA-QA and I-NA-JA-RE-TA.

entries.meaning: O Diktaean (f.), the feminine nisbe of Dikte

cognates.Ugaritic: dqt 'female head of small cattle for sacrifice', a ewe or she-goat (Gordon UT §19.695, cited by Astour 1966, 283 n. 74); DN dqt, KTU 1.102:8 (Astour 1966, 283–84; DULAT 276)

entries.note: PK Za 11, A-DI-KI-TE-TE-[DU-PU₂]-RE: the Palaikastro form of JA-DI-KI-TU (Diktu, Dikte), whose cognates it shares. TE-TE is the feminine nisbe -īt, ʾa-Diqqitīt 'the Diktaean', E for i: JA-DI-KI-TU ~ JA-DI-KI-TE-TE as *312-TA ~ *312-TE-TE (Davis 2026, 45), the base T kept as in SU-KI-RI-TE-I-JA beside SU-KI-RI-TA; Heb. ʾašdôdît, yĕhûdît (Neh 13:24); LB di-ka-ta-jo Diktaios (KN Fp 1). Every TE-TE form is one sign group with dubur (PK Za 8, PK Za 11, PK Za 15), Diqqitīt dubur 'the Diktaean of the sanctuary'. PK Za 12 a: A-DI-KI-TẸ-[TE], TE damaged, no divider, the surface after it lost (GORILA IV 36–38). Rival: Davis parses A- as a prepositional prefix, 'to, for the Diktaian' (Davis 2026, in Salgarella and Petrakis eds., The Wor(l)ds of Linear A, 43–60). Weak point: E writes i twice, and no held Semitic form of the name carries the nisbe.

entries.meaning: (Man) of the throne-house, crown dependant (title); rival Hurrian PN Pidi-kešḫi

cognates.Akkadian: bīt kussî, É.GIŠ.GU.ZA, '1. royal property (real estate), 2. royal service' (CAD K 593); PN and PN ša GIŠ.GU.ZA 'belonging to the crown' (Alalakh 7:26; CAD K 592)
cognates.Hurrian: kešḫi 'siège, trône', ki-iš-hi = Akk. kussû (Laroche 1980, 143–44), rival

entries.note: HT 87 PI-TA-KE-SI 1, first of six one-unit entries under MA-KA-RI-TE in a roster of men. bīt-kissi, construct + genitive, as Akk. bīt kussî 'royal property, royal service' (CAD K 593): '(man) of the throne-house', as the šūt GIŠ.GU.ZA 'those of the throne' of an Old Akkadian roster of men (CAD K 592). The house itself heads HT 21 as PI-TA-KA-SE. Rival: Hurrian Pidi-kešḫi, kešḫi 'throne' (Laroche 1980, 143–44) with pidi/u- unglossed (1980, 200).

entries.meaning: Dikise, personal name, Hurrian tagiše 'beauty'

cognates.Hurrian: tagi 'beautiful'; tagiše/tegiše 'beautiful' or 'beauty', written t/da-a-ki-ši and ta-(a)-ki-(e)-še (Laroche, Glossaire hourrite, pp. 249–50)
cognates.Amarna: Tagi (EA 264–66), mayor of Gintikirmil—Hurrian name, same root

entries.note: HT 87 and HT 117b, two lists headed *21F-TU-NE, each count DI-KI-SE 1: on HT 87 between JA-RE-MI 1 and QE-SU-PU 1, on HT 117b after KU-RE-JU 1. Hurrian tagi 'beautiful' and the theme tagiše/tegiše 'beautiful, beauty', written t/da-a-ki-ši and ta-(a)-ki-(e)-še (Laroche 1980, 249–50), under stop and sibilant neutralization; Tagi is a Hurrian personal name in EA 264–66. DI writes the e of tegiše by the Hurrian e/i convention (Laroche 1980, 23). Weak point: no name Tegiše is attested; the held name is Tagi.

entries.meaning: group of daughters (Hurrian collective)

cognates.Hurrian: šāl=ardi 'group of daughters' (Wilhelm, "Hurrian," 103); šalardi 'qualité de fille', ša-la-ar-di, Mari 5, 11; RS h. 5, 12 (Laroche 1980, 213); šal(a)=arde 'Tochterschaft' (Wegner 2000, 51; Richter 2012, 344)

entries.note: HT 27a .5 ]SA-RA-DI 5, broken directly before SA (GORILA I 49), a counted row in the personnel tally under TI-NI-TA · *307 (KU-RO 335). Hurrian šāl(a)=ardi, šāla 'daughter' with the collective -ardi, the thematic vowel lost before it: šāl=ardi 'group of daughters' (Wilhelm, "Hurrian," 103); ša-la-ar-di at Mari and Ugarit (Laroche 1980, 213); šal(a)=arde 'Tochterschaft' (Wegner 2000, 51). ša-la-ar-di gives SA-RA-DI sign for sign: coda r unwritten, RA for /la/. Laroche and Wegner gloss an abstract, 'qualité de fille,' 'Tochterschaft'; Wilhelm's collective fits a counted row. The break allows a longer compound, as Mari sindišalardi 'Siebentochterschaft' (Richter 2012, 388). One witness.
entries.source: di Mino; Wilhelm, Hurrian; Laroche 1980; Wegner 2000; Richter 2012

entries.meaning: Iruja (personal name; Hurrian hypocoristic of Irup-tešup)

cognates.Nuzi: Iruja (I-ru-ia, E-ru-ú-ia, I-ru-ú-ia), hypocoristic of Irup-tešup (Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943, s.v. IRUJA; 220)

entries.note: HT 7a .2 I-RU-JA 3, all three signs whole and undotted, the first entry under .1 QE-TI · VIR+[?], before DU-JA 4 (GORILA I 15). Nuzi Iruja, I-ru-ia, var. E-ru-ú-ia, I-ru-ú-ia: the son of Ziqaya bears both Iruja and Irup-tešup, and the element list gives iruja as the 'Hypocoristic for Irup-tešup' (Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943, s.v. IRUJA, IRUP-TEŠUP; 220). The element ir- is Hurrian; Speiser's gloss 'aid' is uncertain (ibid., 220). I-ru-ia gives I-RU-JA sign for sign. One attestation.
entries.source: di Mino; Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943

entries.meaning: Ipšaja (personal name; Hurrian hypocoristic)

cognates.Nuzi: Ipšaja (Ip-ša-a-a, Ip-šá-a-a), probably hypocoristic of Ipša-halu (Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943, 220)

entries.note: KH 10 .3 I-PA-SA-JẠ · QA-*118, JA dotted on both copies, before A-KI-PI-E-TE GRA 90 (GORILA III 37). Nuzi Ipšaja, Ip-ša-a-a, Ip-šá-a-a, "Probably hypocoristic for Ipša-halu" (Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943, 220); the element ipš- is Hurrian (ibid., 220). The coda p takes a dead A: Ip-ša-a-a gives I-PA-SA-JA. JA is dotted and there is one witness.
entries.source: di Mino; Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943

entries.meaning: sorcerer, diviner (occupational title or PN)

cognates.Akkadian: kaššāpu/qaššāpu 'sorcerer, practitioner of witchcraft' (Maqlû passim); kašāpu 'to bewitch' (CAD K 282)
cognates.Hebrew: mǝkaššēp 'sorcerer' (Exod 22:17, 7:11); mǝkaššēfīm = palace cult specialists (Exod 7:11); qōšēp (Deut 18:10)
cognates.Amarna: Not attested as Canaanite gloss; but cf. EA 35:26 kaššāpu in Akkadian matrix
cognates.Hurrian: kaššapte 'magie', a transcription of Akkadian kaššaptu (Laroche 1980, 138)

entries.note: HT 87, a register of cult personnel: an occupational title in the name slot with an allocation of 1, among Hurrian names (PI-TA-KE-SI, DI-KI-SE) and NWS ones (JA-RE-MI). √k-š-p / √q-š-p 'practise sorcery': Akk. kaššāpu/qaššāpu 'sorcerer', a qattāl agent noun; Heb. məkaššēp (Deut 18:10), fem. məkaššēpāh (Exod 22:17). Š is written S and the geminate šš single. QE writes q, its primary value, which sets the word apart from √k-s-p 'silver' (kaspu), spelled with KA. Exod 7:11 names the məkaššəpîm beside the ḥăkāmîm and ḥarṭummîm, palace specialists of the kind HT 87 lists. One attestation.

entries.meaning: burnt offering

cognates.Akkadian: elû 'to go up'

entries.note: ZA 7a, a tablet: U-JU 5 · A-RA-TU 4 · A-RE-TU-MI[, a counted list. Heb. ʿōlâ 'burnt offering' (Lev 1:3), from √ʿ-l-h 'go up' (semitic_roots 2707); Neo-Punic ʿlt 'whole burnt offering' (KAI 159.7/8; Krahmalkov 2000, 374); the -t unwritten, as in *21F-*118 ḥiṭṭa. DU-JU[ (ZA 22, a tablet, beside OVISf) is a candidate from the same root.

entries.meaning: fine flour, semolina

cognates.Egyptian: group writing ṯu-ru₂-ta 'fine flour' (GlOS 2, 198, after Hoch, SWET 369f., no. 550)

entries.note: KN 22a, a lame (a short thin tablet): SU-JU-TA 20 / KA-JE. sulta 'fine flour', JU writing lu, su-lu-ta, the skeleton s-l-t: Heb. sōlet 'finely milled flour' (HALOT 759), the flour of the offering (Lev 2:1; Exod 29:2). One attestation.

entries.meaning: Uta, personal name heading the fig (NI) entry on HT 103; rival the town Uda
entries.note: HT 103 .1 U-TA₂ · NI 40, the opening group, before the divider and the fig entry; DA-KU-SE-NE, *188, DA-KU-NA and KI-RA follow. The heading slot fits an entity, institution, recipient or place named over the figs. Uta is a Neo-Assyrian personal name, ᵐu₂-ta-a (SAA 6 277). Rival: Uda, an Anatolian town near Firaktin, named at Ugarit (dIŠKUR ᵘʳᵘU-da, RS 17.338+; RGTC 12/2, 304), Hittite Uta. One attestation.

entries.meaning: additional, surplus, or excess (administrative heading)

cognates.Akkadian: watrum 'additional, in excess'; watartum 'excess, surplus' (Huehnergard 1997, §10.1)

entries.note: HT 116a: U-TA-RO · TE ·, the heading over six entries of grain, oil, olives and *304 (KU-PA-JA, PU-RA₂, SI+SE, PI-*34-TE, SI-KI-NE, QA-NU-MA). watru 'surplus', U writing wa and RO a dead vowel: Akk. watru 'in excess, additional' (CAD A/2 499), watartu 'excess, surplus' (CAD A/2 485; Huehnergard 1997, §10.1). Rival: Heb. √ʿ-t-r 'entreat' (Gen 25:21; Judg 13:8), an agent noun *ʿattār 'supplicant', unattested. One attestation. See TE-RI.
entries.source: di Mino; CAD A/2; Huehnergard 1997; GlOS 2

entries.meaning: the salt-works (Ug. ṣṣ, WSem. ṣēṣūma 'salt marsh'), an establishment drawing grain, oil and figs; rival Šipšu, the Sun-deity

cognates.Ugaritic: ṣṣ 'salt-works', ṣṣ PN 'salt-works of PN' (KTU 4.340; 4.344; DULAT 781)
cognates.Akkadian: ṣēṣūma pl. 'salt marsh', a WSem. word at Ras Shamra: ṣí-ṣú-ma, ṣi-e-ṣi-ma for A.ŠÀ MUN.MEŠ 'fields of salt' (CAD Ṣ 150)

entries.note: HT 116a: SI+SE GRA 16, OLE+KI 1, OLE+MI 6, OLIV 3, a recipient among KU-PA-JA, PU-RA₂, PI-*34-TE, SI-KI-NE and QA-NU-MA. HT 42+59: ]-TA · SI+SE · TE · OLE+KI 8, OLE+U 7, beside SA-RO. HT 99b: SI+SE FIC 6, AB30 read as the fig logogram (SigLA). Read in sign order, ṣi-ṣe: Ug. ṣṣ 'salt-works', listed by owner (KTU 4.340; DULAT 781), the WSem. ṣēṣūma 'salt marsh' of Ras Shamra, spelled ṣi-e-ṣi-ma (CAD Ṣ 150). SI writes ṣ as in SI-DA-TE ṣēdat. The salt-works draws rations beside QA-NU-MA qanūma 'reeds'. Rivals: Šipšu, the Sun-deity, Ebla sí-piš (Lipiński 1997, 113, 118; #1407), with the coda p unwritten; a syllabic še, as in SI+SE-RA+KA (HT Wa 1021). Three attestations.
entries.source: di Mino; CAD Ṣ; DULAT; HALOT; Lipiński 1997

entries.meaning: levy, gift—fiscal category on a commodity nodule

cognates.Akkadian: širku B 'gift; (a tax)', at Ugarit with the tithe and toll of a town (RS 16.276:10; CAD Š/3 111); širiktu, also šeriktu, 'grant, gift' (CAD Š/3 103); šarāku A 'to dedicate, to give' (CAD Š/2 40)

entries.note: HT Wa 1021, a nodule: *188-DU · ¾ · SI+SE-RA+KA, a commodity, a fraction and a word. With SI+SE as še, SI+SE-RA+KA writes šeraka: Akk. širku 'gift; a tax', levied at Ugarit with a town's tithe and toll (CAD Š/3 111), and širiktu, also šeriktu, 'grant, gift' (CAD Š/3 103), of šarāku 'to dedicate, to give'. RA+KA read in sign order, as MI+*301 minā. Weak point: SI+SE for še. Rival: a personal name, the official of the sealing. One attestation.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Her Ka endures' (Egyptian)

cognates.Egyptian: ḏd 'enduring' + kꜣ⸗s 'her ka', the type of ꜥꜣ-kꜣ⸗s 'her ka is great' (Ranke I, 58.14) and wꜣḏ-kꜣ.w⸗s (PNM v6)

entries.note: ZA Zb 3 VIN 32 / DI-DI-KA-SE A-SA-MU-NE A-SE, the dedicator of wine to Eshmun. Egyptian ḏd-kꜣ⸗s 'her ka endures', the name type of ꜥꜣ-kꜣ⸗s 'her ka is great' (Ranke I, 58.14) and wꜣḏ-kꜣ.w⸗s 'her ka is flourishing' (PNM v6, personal_names_id 142608414); DI-DI writes ḏd, SE ⸗s. Rival: Semitic DI-DI + KA-SE kissē 'throne', KA-SE as in PI-TA-KA-SE bīt-kissē (HT 21), DI-DI as in DI-DI-ZA-KE (HT 1). One attestation.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'The ka of Re endures, the reliable one' (Egyptian)

cognates.Egyptian: ḏd-kꜣ-rꜥ, a man's name (Ranke I, 412.17); mtj 'the reliable one' (TLA lemma 853566)

entries.note: ZA 11a .1 DI-DI-KO-RA-ME⌊ ⌋TA₂ · *516 ·, the holder of an account of grain, wine and olives; the destroyed space before TA₂ could have held a divider (GORILA III 173), and SigLA reads one word. Egyptian ḏd-kꜣ-rꜥ 'the ka of Re endures' (Ranke I, 412.17) with mtj 'the reliable one' (TLA lemma 853566): DI-DI writes ḏd as in DI-DI-KA-SE, KO kꜣ as in KO-SA-I-TI, ME-TA₂ mtj on TA₂'s value t. A locally made scarab from Sidon names an MB IIB lord Ḏdkꜣrꜥ, 'beloved of Seth, lord of Iꜣy' (Mourad 2014, I, 319; II, 149). Rival: DI-DI-KO · RA-ME-TA₂, Egyptian rmṯ 'people, personnel' (TLA lemma 450402), which leaves DI-DI-KO unread. One attestation. See DU-DA-MA.

entries.meaning: the Kinsman who comes forth (El epithet); rival 'Strong One'

cognates.Amorite: ʿammum 'paternal uncle' (Gelb AS 21, 15); Yawṣiʾ-ʾIl 'El has come forth' (Gelb AS 21, no. 3574)

entries.note: CR(?) Zf 1, a gold pin: A-MA-WA-SI · KA-NI-JA-MI · I-JA · QA-KI-SE-NU-TI · A-TA-DE. A-MA-WA-SI opens the text beside KA-NI-JA-MI 'Creator of the Sea': ʿAmma-wāṣiʾ 'the Kinsman who comes forth', A-MA ʿamma 'kinsman' (as A-MA, A-MA-JA ʿAmmaya) with WA-SI wāṣi(ʾ), active participle of √w-ṣ-ʾ 'go out, appear', the final ʾ unwritten. Every sign is read. The type is A-MI-DA-U ʿAmmī-dāʿ's, and Amorite sets the same verb on El: Yawṣiʾ-ʾIl 'El has come forth' (Gelb AS 21, no. 3574). Rivals: ʾammāṣ 'Strong One', √ʾ-m-ṣ (semitic_roots 3778), Heb. ʾammîṣ, said of YHWH (Job 9:4, 19; HALOT 63), Ug. ảmṣ (DULAT 71), which leaves -WA- unread; the dedicant's name. One attestation.

entries.meaning: Creator of the Sea (El epithet)

cognates.Ugaritic: qnyt ʾilm 'Creatress of the Gods' (KTU 1.4 III 26)—standard epithet of Athirat/Asherah
cognates.Hebrew: קֹנֵה שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ qōnēh šāmayim wāʾāreṣ (Gen 14:19)—epithet of El ʿElyon; also קֹנֵה qōnēh alone as divine title
cognates.Phoenician: ʾl qn ʾrṣ 'El Creator of the Earth' (KAI 26 III 18, Karatepe bilingual)
cognates.Amarna: EA 266:16—Canaanite vassal invokes qny in theophoric context
cognates.Amorite: qanij(ān)um 'to create' (QNJ; Gelb 1980, glossary p. 29); names KA-NI-IA-NU qaniyānu (no. 3980), fem. QA-NI-A-TUM (no. 5196); jammum 'sea' in IA-AM-MU-U₂ (no. 2946)

entries.note: CR Zf 1, a gold pin of unknown findspot: A-MA-WA-SI · KA-NI-JA-MI. qāniy-yammi 'Creator of the Sea': the masculine construct participle qāniy (Amorite qanijum) with the genitive yammi 'of the Sea'; KA writes q. √q-n-y is a Bronze Age divine epithet: Ugaritic qnyt ʾilm of Athirat (KTU 1.4 III 26); the Hittite divine name Elkunirša, ʾil qōnē ʾarṣ 'El, creator of the earth' (HALOT 1112), whose wife is Ašertu, Athirat (Olyan 1988, 41–42); Karatepe ʾl qn ʾrṣ (KAI 26 A III 18); Gen 14:19. El's Ugaritic creation epithet is bny bnwt (KTU 1.4 II 11). Rival: -MI as mimation.

entries.meaning: I make ready (1cs prefix form)

cognates.Hebrew: ʿātîd "ready, prepared"; Piel ʿattᵊdāh "make it ready" (Prov 24:27)

entries.note: CR Zf 1, the gold pin, divider-bounded, the last group after QA-KI-SE-NU-TI. ʾaʿtid(u) 'I make ready', 1cs prefix form of √ʿ-t-d 'be ready, prepare' (HALOT 901), the ʿ dropped: a-ta-de sign for sign. A suffix-form 1cs needs -t- (Heb. ʿātadtî). GORILA V's AB45 variant table gives the final DE. Cf. AU-TA-DE (KO(?) Zf 2), inside an undivided sequence. One attestation.

entries.meaning: the fibula, the pin; rivals ʾAdara 'the Strong One' (epithet), ʾaddart- 'mantle'

cognates.Ugaritic: adr (IV) 'fibula', pl. adrm, pldm b adrm 'garments with fibulae', KTU 4.4:5, beside Akk. edēru 'to hug, embrace' (DULAT 22; GlOS 1, 10); adr 'mighty'; adrt 'of good quality' (DULAT 22)
cognates.Eblaite: a-da-ra ʾadara 'the strong one', a name (Pagan 1998, row 558); ʔadar 'strong' (GlOS 1, 10)

entries.note: KN Zf 31, a silver pin, first word of the second line (GORILA IV 155), before TI-DI-TE-QA-TI 'fix it, you have fastened it'. ʾadra 'the fibula', Ug. adr (IV), pl. adrm, pldm b adrm 'garments with fibulae' (KTU 4.4:5; DULAT 22): the pin names itself at the head of the line that speaks of it. Rivals: ʾAdara 'the Strong One', an epithet after DA-DU-MI-NE, QA-MI-*47-NA-RA and A-WA-PI on the first line, sign for sign the Ebla name a-da-ra (Pagan 1998, row 558), ʾadar 'strong' (GlOS 1, 10), cf. Heb. ʾaddīr 'mighty' (Ps 8:2, 93:4); ʾaddart- 'mantle', Heb. ʾadderet (Gen 25:25; Josh 7:21, beside silver and gold; 1 Kgs 19:13), final -t unwritten. Spelling: ʾ dropped, single DA. See DI-DE-RU, A-DA-RO and DI-RE-DI-NA.

entries.meaning: Addar, 'Mighty' (personal name)

cognates.Hebrew: ʾAddār (אַדָּר), son of Bela (1 Chr 8:3; HALOT 17); place names ʾAddārâ (Josh 15:3), Ḥăṣar-ʾAddār (Num 34:4)
cognates.Ebla: ʾa₅-da-ru₁₂ ʾadaru 'strong' (Pagan 1998, row 130); a-da-ra 'the strong one' (row 558)

entries.note: Recipient slot on ARKH 5, parallel to A-DU-NI-TA-NA: A-DA-RO GRA 40[+, the entry wrapping past the broken edge to *131B 6 at the start of .3 (GORILA III 16–17). Final -O is a dead vowel; GORILA dots RO, and the .3 logogram is written over an erasure. Cf. A-DA-RA (KN Zf 31). Rival: Akk. adru 'threshing floor' (CAD A/1 129), against which one entry carries both grain and must (cf. Num 18:27). One attestation. See DI-DE-RU.

entries.meaning: Ḫadki gives drink (personal name; Ḫadki, a Mari-area name of Adad, + šiqā 'who gives drink'); rival 'Ḫadki is (my) dwelling'

cognates.Amorite: ḫadk-, theophorous element, perhaps identical with Adgi, a local (Mari area) name of Adad: Ḫa-ad-ku-um, Mu-tu-ḫa-ad-ki-im (Huffmon 1965, 190–191); Mu-tu-ḫa-ad-ki-im, var. Mu-tu-ḫa-ad-ki (ARM IV 80.10′), Mu-tu-ad-ki-im (ARM II 122.7) (Huffmon 1965, 53)

entries.note: KH 5 .1 A-DA-KI-SI-KA · A-RA-U-DA ·, the heading over WI-SA-SA-NE CYP+E 2, VINb+WI 2 (GORILA III 25): the party, then its city, Arwad. A-DA-KI Ḫadki, the theophoric element ḥadk- of Mari names, which Huffmon, after Albright, sets beside Adgi, a Mari-area name of Adad (Huffmon 1965, 190–191); turūmnā-ḫadki 'Ḫadki shall exalt us' (ARM 16.1; Buck 2018, 351); ḫ unwritten as Mari Mu-tu-ad-ki-im writes it beside Mu-tu-ḫa-ad-ki (ARM II 122.7, IV 80.10′; Huffmon 1965, 53); DA for d. SI-KA šiqā 'who gives drink', √š-q-y, as SI-KA on IO Za 6, the i-noun of Ebla /šiḳītum/ 'irrigation' (Kogan 2025, 8–9; semitic_roots 1389): the storm god who waters. Rival: šikā (√š-k-n), the HT nodule word, 'Ḫadki is (my) dwelling'. Weak point: Ḫadki is attested only in Mari texts. One attestation.

entries.meaning: 'fix it, you have fastened it' (of the pin); rival Tidiʿ-Teqaʿt, personal name 'Teqaʿt knows', after one of the Kotharat

cognates.Arabic: watada, imperfect yatidu, imperative tid, verbal noun tida, 'fixed a wooden pin or peg' (Lane 2916–17); watid 'peg' (Lane 2917)
cognates.Hebrew: yātēd 'peg', for the loom, Judg 16:14, and driven, Judg 4:21; Isa 22:23 (HALOT 451); tāqaʿ 'to drive in, fasten', of Samson's braids fastened with the pin, Judg 16:13–14; 'blow (a horn), clap', Ps 47:2 (HALOT 1785); kôšārôt, Ps 68:7 bakkôšārôt 'with songs of joy' (HALOT 467)
cognates.Ugaritic: tqʿt /Tāqiʿatu/, participle of tqʿ, 'she who applauds', one of the kṯrt (DULAT 862; GlOS 2, 295), named in their roll, KTU 1.24:49; kṯrt, female singers (HALOT 467) who also preside over childbirth (DULAT 468), sung in KTU 1.24:40–41 ašr ilht kṯrt bnt hll snnt 'I sing of the goddesses, the Kotharat, daughters of Hilal, the Swallows'; the Kotharat in a name: bnkṯrt 'son of the Kotharat', PN (DULAT 226; Gröndahl PTU 152)
cognates.Eblaite: ti-da tidaʿ 'she knows', a name (Pagan 1998, row 4469)

entries.note: KN Zf 31, a silver pin from a Mavro Spelio tomb, second row: A-DA-RA · TI-DI-TE-QA-TI · TA-SA-ZA, intact and undotted (GORILA IV 154–155). The pin speaks of itself. TI-DI tidī 'fix it!', 2fs imperative of √w-t-d 'to fix a peg', w dropped as in Arabic tid, tida (Lane 2916–17) and Heb. šēb from yāšab. TE-QA-TI teqaʿti 'you (f.) have fastened', -ti 2fs, of √t-q-ʿ, the verb of the pin driven into Samson's braids (Judg 16:13–14; HALOT 1785); e by Akkadian-type coloring from ʿ. Heb. yātēd 'peg' pairs with tāqaʿ (Judg 4:21; Isa 22:23; HALOT 451). Rival: Tidiʿ-Teqaʿt 'Teqaʿt knows', a sentence name: tidiʿ 3fs of √y-d-ʿ, the Ebla name ti-da tidaʿ (Pagan 1998, row 4469), i by coloring as in tīde 'you know' (Huehnergard 1997, §26.1); Teqaʿt, tqʿt 'she who applauds' (DULAT 862), one of the Kotharat, songstresses akin to the Muses (KTU 1.24:40–50). ʿ unwritten in both readings. One attestation. See A-DA-RA, TA-TE-I-KE-ZA-RE and A-MI-DA-U.
entries.source: di Mino; Lane; HALOT 451, 467, 1785; Pagan 1998; DULAT; KTU 1.24; GlOS 2; Huehnergard 1997

entries.meaning: with which one curls (the hair)

cognates.Akkadian: kezēru 'to curl the hair', i-ke-ez-zi-ru in EA 14 ii 56, silver spatulas 'with which one curls hair' among gifts from Egypt (CAD K 316); kezertu 'woman with curled hair' (CAD K 314)
cognates.Ugaritic: d, f. and pl. dt 'which, who', the relative (DULAT 252)

entries.note: KN Zf 31, a silver pin from a Mavro Spelio tomb, end of the second row: TI-DI-TE-QA-TI · TA-SA-ZA · TA-TE-I-KẸ-ZA-RE, KE dotted in GORILA IV 154–155, undotted in Younger. TA-TE ṯāt 'which', the feminine relative, ṯ in the T-series as in KA-TA-RE; Ug. d, dt (DULAT 252). I-KE-ZA-RE ʾikezzer 'one curls', present of kezēru 'to curl the hair' (CAD K 316), the verb of EA 14 ii 56, silver spatulas 'with which one curls hair' (i-ke-ez-zi-ru). The root is Akkadian only. I- is the Akkadian-type 3cs prefix, or 1cs ʾi- 'I curl'. ZA has a where Akkadian has i. One attestation. See TI-DI-TE-QA-TI, A-DA-RA and ZA-TI.
entries.source: di Mino; CAD K; DULAT; Younger

entries.meaning: she remembers

cognates.Ugaritic: /ḫ-s-s/ 'to remember', G prefix tḫss: w tḫss aṯrt ndrh 'and Athirat remembered his vow'; ḫss, Ḫasis, second name of the craftsman god Kothar (DULAT 405)
cognates.Akkadian: ḫasāsu 'to think of' (CAD Ḫ 122ff., apud DULAT 405)
cognates.Eblaite: ḫasīsu written ḫa-zi-zu-um, ḫa-zi-zú (VE 389, apud DULAT 405)

entries.note: KN Zf 31, a silver pin from a Mavro Spelio tomb, second line, between TI-DI-TE-QA-TI 'fix it, you have fastened it' and TA-TE-I-KE-ZA-RE 'with which one curls (the hair)', intact and undotted (GORILA IV 155). ta-, 3fs prefix, of √ḫ-s-s 'to remember', the Ugaritic prefix form tḫss (DULAT 405). ḫ closes the first syllable and is unwritten, as the ʿ of teqaʿti. ZA writes the root's second s as z, as Ebla writes ḫasīsu ḫa-zi-zu-um (VE 389). No final -ī, so 3fs, or 2ms 'you remember'. The root gives Ḫasis, the second name of Kothar. Rival: tašʿazz 'you make (it) firm', Š of √ʿ-z-z (DULAT 194), which needs SA as ša and a Š stem Ugaritic does not attest. One attestation. See TI-DI-TE-QA-TI and TA-TE-I-KE-ZA-RE.

entries.meaning: she serves; give (him) drink!

cognates.Ugaritic: /s-ʔ-d/ 'to support, comfort', tsảd; /š-q-y/ G 'to offer drink', qḥn w tšqyn yn, KTU 1.19 IV 53 (DULAT 740, 827)
cognates.Hebrew: sʿd 'to sustain', of serving guests bread: wə-saʿădû libbəkem, Gen 18:5; səʿād libbəkā pat-leḥem, Judg 19:5

entries.note: KN Zf 31, a silver pin from a Mavro Spelio tomb, last word of the first line, before A-DA-RA; legible, dividers both sides (GORILA IV 155). TE-SU-DE tesʾad 'she serves', 3fs G prefix of √s-ʾ-d. No sign of its own writes the ʾ: the U of SU stands in its place, where Ugaritic writes ʾ only with a vowel-bearing aleph, ả in tsảd (Huehnergard 2012, 21). SE-KE-I šeqī 'give drink!', 2fs G imperative of √š-q-y; KE writes q as in RO-KE, final I the 2fs -ī as in TI-DI tidī. Ugaritic pairs the verbs when Kothar-wa-Ḫasis brings the bow: Danel orders šlḥm ššqy ỉlm, sảd kbd hmt 'feed and give drink to the god, serve and honor him' (KTU 1.17 V 19–20), and Danatiya serves (V 29–30). Ugaritic gives drink with Š ššqy. One attestation. See TA-SA-ZA, TA-NA-SU-TE-KE and SI-KA (IO Za 6).

entries.meaning: my Creatress (divine epithet)

cognates.Akkadian: banû "to create" (semantic parallel)

entries.note: ZA Zb 34, a Zakros clay vessel: ]PU₂-RE-JẠ · KỌ-MỤ · RỤ-DI[ (GORILA IV 115); PU₂ is damaged at the fracture, the word whole. burē(t)yā 'my Creatress', addressed by the feminine imperative RU-DI: Heb. bārāʾ 'to create' (Gen 1:1), Arb. baraʾa 'to create (God)' (HALOT 153); PU₂ writes bu, as in DU-PU₂-RE dubur, the final ʾ unwritten, and -JA is the 1cs suffix -yā 'my'. The feminine -t is unwritten before -yā, as in A-TA-NA-JE 'my ʾAtanat' beside A-TA-NA-TE; it is omissible in West Semitic names of the second millennium (Astour 1966, 315). PK Za 16 ]TO-SA · PỤ₂-RE-JẠ ]vest.[ (GORILA IV 42) is a second witness, the word whole, traces following after a damaged stretch. Rivals: PU₂-RE + -JA; √p-r-y 'fruit', *puriyya. See A-PA-RA-NE.

entries.meaning: cella, inner sanctuary

cognates.Akkadian: kummu "cella, inner room of a temple"
cognates.Ugaritic: kbm, a (closed) cult installation (DULAT 423), filed with kummu under √k-m-m (GlOS 1, 308)

entries.note: ZA Zb 34, a Zakros clay vessel: ]PU₂-RE-JẠ · KỌ-MỤ · RỤ-DI[ (GORILA IV 115). kummu 'cella': Akkadian kummu 'cella, private room (of a temple)' (CAD K 533); cf. DU-PU₂-RE dubur 'sanctuary'. KO writes ku, as RO writes ru in SA-RO beside SA-RU šarru. Rival: √q-w-m 'arise', qūmū (imperative plural). One attestation.

entries.meaning: Roam! (f. imperative)

cognates.Hebrew: רוּד rûd "to roam about freely" (HALOT 1194); רָדָה rādâ "to rule, have dominion" (HALOT 1190)
cognates.Arabic: rāda (rwd) "to go back and forth, roam, search" (HALOT 1194)
cognates.Akkadian: redû "to accompany, lead, drive"

entries.note: ZA Zb 34 ]PU₂-RE-JA · KO-MU · RU-DI[ (GORILA IV 115) holds the word, more signs perhaps following it. HT 141 .2 ]RU-DỊ-[ (GORILA I 239) breaks after DI, the word possibly whole. rūdī 'roam!', the feminine imperative of √r-w-d (semitic_roots K0360), addressed to PU₂-RE-JA 'my Creatress', with KO-MU the accusative of place: Heb. rûd 'roam about freely' (Jer 2:31), 'Judah still goes about with God' (Hos 12:1); Arb. rāda 'go back and forth' (HALOT 1194). Rival: 'Rule!', √r-d-y, Heb. rādâ (Gen 1:26, Ps 72:8), whose imperative rədēh has no u (HALOT 1190). Two attestations.

entries.meaning: She-of-the-Lion (feminine gentilic—priestess/cult title; cf. I-ZU-RI-NI-TA She-of-the-Bull)

cognates.Hebrew: ari lion (Gen 49:9 gur aryeh Yehudah; Num 23:24; Judg 14:8)

entries.note: HT 25a and ZA 8, at two sites. ʾarīnīt 'She-of-the-Lion', the feminine gentilic -nīt on NWS ari 'lion', as I-ZU-RI-NI-TA i-ṯawrinīt 'She-of-the-Bull' takes the same -NI-TA on an animal root; bull and lion are the two central sacred animals of Minoan iconography. Both tablets enter A-RI-NI-TA with 1 in a list of personal names (HT 25a with DI-NA-U, U-RE-WI and I-KI-RA; ZA 8 with KU-TU-KO-RE and DA-I-PI-TA), so -īt here names one woman, where it also forms relational adjectives, abstracts and collectives (Fischer 2002, §§64, 116). Weak point: the lists set no title apart from a name.

entries.meaning: farmer, tenant farmer (occupational title)

cognates.Akkadian: ikkaru 'plowman, farmer, farm bailiff' (CAD I/J 49)
cognates.Hebrew: ʾikkār 'farmer, agricultural worker', bōšû ʾikkārîm 'the farmers were ashamed' (Jer 14:4; HALOT 47)

entries.note: HT 25a .5, a personnel list: I-KI-RA 1, whole as written; the lower-left margin before it is lost (GORILA I 44–45). ikkara 'farmer': Akkadian ikkaru 'plowman, farmer' (CAD I/J 49), Hebrew ʾikkār (Isa 61:5; Jer 14:4; HALOT 47). I-KA ʾikkār (HT 91, HT 102) leaves the final r unwritten; here r is written with a following vowel. Rival: a personal name. One attestation. See A-KI-RO.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Šum knew'

cognates.Amorite: JI-JDAʿ+ŚUM, I-DA-SU-UM (Gelb 1980, no. 2430); JADAʿ names, IA-DA-AḪ-…, IA-DA-DINGIR (Gelb 1980, nos. 3168–3178); Mari ia-da-am-mu, ia-da-aḫ-DINGIR (GlOS 2, 342)

entries.note: KH 74: ]-SỊ · JA-DA-SU, then ]SỊ-*805-MI, both broken before. Yadaʿ-Šum 'Šum knew', the Amorite JI-JDAʿ+ŚUM, I-DA-SU-UM (Gelb 1980, no. 2430), with JADAʿ (nos. 3168–3178) and Sum, the divine 'Name' (GlOS 2, 249–250; semitic_roots 621); ʿ and mimation unwritten. Ug. ydʿ (DULAT 942), Heb. Yədaʿyāh. Rival: yadaʿšu 'he knew him', the verb with -šu, as Akk. Ilšu-ibbīšu 'his god named him' (de Boer 2014, 305). One attestation. See A-MI-DA-U.
entries.source: di Mino; Gelb 1980; DULAT; GlOS 2; de Boer 2014

entries.meaning: personal name (f.), 'she who judges'

cognates.Ugaritic: dnty, wife of Danel (KTU 1.17 V 16; DULAT 274); dn 'judgment' (DULAT 273)

entries.note: ARKH 6: DA-NA-TU · KU heads the tablet, TE-RI on the next line. Feminine participle dānat- + -u, √d-y-n 'to judge'; cf. Ug. dnty, Danel's wife (KTU 1.17 V 16), Heb. Dînāh, and DI-NA-U. Da-na-tum is a man's seal name, son of Sîn-taʾar, servant of Rīm-Sîn (RIME 4.02.14.2009). Weak point: -t may make an abstract 'judgment' as well as a feminine; the Babylonian Da-na-tum is a man. Rival: dannatu 'hardship; fortress' (CAD D 87), a heading. One attestation. See DI-NA-RO.

entries.meaning: Qātilu (personal name), 'killer'; rival Hurrian Katiya 'He/She said'

cognates.Hurrian: Katiya, ka-ti-ia, kad=i=ya 'He/She said', Mari (Monti 2017, 255); Nuzi Kataja, Qa-ta-a-a (NPN 224)

entries.note: ZA 14: QA-TI-JU 8, a name among recipients (ME-KI-DI 1, PU-NI-KA-*363 3, KU-PI 1, TU-MI-TI-ZA-SE 45). JU writes lu: qa-ti-lu, the qātil participle of *ḳtl 'kill', a name in Safaitic qtl and Arabic Qātila (Harding 1971, 476). Rival: Hurrian Katiya 'He/She said' (Mari ka-ti-ia; Monti 2017, 255), with JU for yu, on the stem of QA-TI-DA-TE Kati-tati. One witness.

entries.meaning: Tanāt, a variant of Tinit, the goddess TNT, feminine of √t-n-n 'sea-dragon'; rival a form of A-TA-NA-TE ʾAtanat

cognates.Punic: TNT (Tanit, Tinnit); in Greek letters Θινιθ, Θεννειθ (Krahmalkov 2000, 495)
cognates.Greek: θύννος "tunny" (BDB: Phoenician loanword from same root)

entries.note: ZA 10a TA-NA-TE 2 heads a list of single entries, with A-TA-NA-TE 1 the fourth. Tanāt, as the signs write it, a variant of Tinit, the goddess TNT, on √t-n-n: Ugaritic tnn 'dragon' (DULAT 860). TA writes the t, or the ṯ of ṯ-n-n, as scribes wrote ṯ in the T-series (di Mino, Ya Diktu 16–17 n. 27). TI-NI-TA writes Tinit with i, TA-NA-TI and TA-NA-TE with a. Cf. Linear B ta-na-to (KN De 1618). Rival: a form of A-TA-NA-TE ʾAtanat (√y-t-n), as Ya Diktu 45 relates it. See TA-NA-TI.
related_forms: Θηναί (Thenai, Cretan toponym near Amnisos)—Greek rendering with ṯ→θ

entries.meaning: ʾAtanat, 'She-who-gives'—feminine of √y-t-n 'to give' with I-y > ʾ; the etymon of Athena (di Mino, Ya Diktu 20)

cognates.Linear B: a-ta-na-po-ti-ni-ja (KN V 52)—divine offering list alongside e-nu-wa-ri-jo, pa-ja-wo-ne, po-se-da-o-ne
cognates.Ugaritic: √ytn 'to give; to set, place' (Huehnergard 2012); ytnt 'she gave' (GlOS 2, 78)
cognates.Phoenician: BʿLYTN Baʿal Yaton 'Baʿal has given'; YTNT, a woman's name 'she gave' (Benz 1972, 328; Krahmalkov 2000, 220)
cognates.Hurrian: a-da-na, Atana, a personal name at Kaneš (Monti 2017, 451), the rival

entries.note: ZA 10a: A-TA-NA-TE 1, fourth in a list headed by TA-NA-TE 2. ʾAtanat 'She-who-gives' (di Mino, Ya Diktu 20): feminine *yātanat of √y-t-n 'to give' with y > ʾ, final E a dead vowel after t; Phoenician keeps the y- in BʿLYTN Baʿal-yatōn 'Baʿal has given'. Greek takes the weakened form: Mycenaean a-ta-na-po-ti-ni-ja (KN V 52), Doric Ἀθάνα, Ionic Ἀθήνη, Pre-Greek for Beekes (2010); Athena wins Athens by giving the olive. The A-/∅ alternation with TA-NA-TE on ZA 10a recurs in A-PA-RA-NE/PA-RA-NE, A-MI-TA/MI-TA and A-DU/DU. Rivals: a form of TA-NA-TE Tanāt (√t-n-n, Tinnit), which heads the ZA 10a list; Hurrian Atana (Monti 2017, 451). See A-TA-NA-JE.
entries.source: di Mino; Monti 2017; Benz 1972; Krahmalkov 2000; GlOS 2

entries.meaning: Beloved of Minos (compound theophoric name)

cognates.Akkadian: dādu 'darling' (CAD D 20)
cognates.Ugaritic: dd 'love, loved one' (DULAT 262); ydd 'loved' (DULAT 943); lydd il 'to the beloved of El' (KTU 1.4 VII 46)
cognates.Hebrew: dōd 'beloved' (HALOT 215); Yədîdyāh 'beloved of Yah' (2 Sam 12:25; HALOT 390)
cognates.Hurrian: tad- 'to love', tadi-/tadu- in names (Laroche GLH 248); Tadu-Ḫepa (TLHdig KBo 27.93+)

entries.note: KN Zf 31, a silver dress pin from a Mavro Spelio tomb: DA-DỤ-MI-NE between ]SỊ-ZẠ-NE-*310 and QA-MI-*47-NA-RA, DU dotted (GORILA IV 155). A compound of two roots: DA-DU 'beloved' + MI-NE, Minos (√m-n-n 'to allot, portion'). 'Beloved of DN' is a name type: Heb. Yədîdyāh (2 Sam 12:25), Ug. ydd il (KTU 1.4 VII 46). The type dādu + DN: Ebla da-du-ʾIl 'beloved is ʾIl' (Pagan 1998, row 1402), Mari da-du-ma-lik, da-du-me-er (GlOS 1, 152). Hurrian builds the type on tad- 'to love'; DA writes /da/ and /ta/. MI-NE is the Ebla name mi-ne (ARET 3 134, 4 15, 12 668, 15 20) and the element of ù-na-mi-ne. Rivals: Sanmartín's meny '(the) love; DN', √m-n-w/y 'to love', entered with a query (GlOS 2, 45); a Hurrian tadu- name. One attestation. See TA-DI, I-DA-DA, DA-DU-*301 and PI-MI-NA-TE.
entries.source: di Mino; Pagan 1998; GlOS 1; GlOS 2; EbDA

entries.meaning: Mari (place name; Linear B ma-ri); rival Mari on the Euphrates

cognates.Linear B: ma-ri, a place in the Knossos sheep tablets, KN Dl 947.B (si-da-jo / ma-ri), 948.B (pa-za-ti / ma-ri); ethnic ma-ri-jo, KN X 1581 (DMic I 425–426)

entries.note: HT 128a .4 MA-RI, both signs whole, after GRA+KU 4 at the end of the face; face b opens with GRA+KU 6 and no word before it, MA-RI's entry carried over (GORILA I 221). A barley list by recipient. Rival: Mari on the Euphrates, whose eighteenth-century archive records Caphtorian weapons, textiles and shoes (Cline 2014, 19); Ugarit still names ʿṯtrt Mrh, ʿAṯtart of Mari (KTU 1.100:78; RGTC 12/2, 186). One attestation.
entries.source: di Mino; DMic I; Cline 2014; RGTC 12/2

entries.meaning: the Lady (divine title; personal-name element)

cognates.Sabaic: mrʾt 'woman, girl; lady, divine or human' (Biella 1982, 283)
cognates.Akkadian: mārtu (marʾatu, merʾatu) 'daughter, girl, woman' (CAD M/1 300)
cognates.Amorite: MA-RA-TUM maʾratum, MA-RI-TUM maʾritum, names (Gelb 1980, nos. 4536, 4541)

entries.note: Second element of HT 90 SI-RU-MA-RI-TA₂, written as one word (GORILA I 143): Ṣill-marʾita 'Shade of the Lady', the Amorite pattern of Ṣill-Haddu (Gelb 1980, no. 6482) and Ṣill-ʿAnat, with a goddess (no. 4716). Feminine of marʾ- 'lord': Sabaic mrʾt 'woman, girl; lady, divine or human' (Biella 1982, 283), Akkadian mārtu (marʾatu, merʾatu) (CAD M/1 300), Aramaic mārtā 'lady' (the name Martha), Arabic marʾat-. The glottal stop is unwritten, and TA₂ gives final -ta as in KI-RE-TA₂. See MA-RE.

entries.meaning: bull, cattle (logographic abbreviation of ṯawr; administrative commodity category for bovine livestock/products)

cognates.Ugaritic: ṯr 'bull' (KTU 1.10 iii:35, 1.12 i:30); epithet of El: ṯr ʾil 'Bull El'
cognates.Akkadian: šūru 'bull' (CAD Š/3 370)

entries.note: Two complete witnesses: HT 49a .8 TU 4 (GORILA I 93) and KH 91 .3 TU ¹⁄₁₆ (V 45). The fraction on KH 91 marks a measured commodity, not a person. Every other TU is broken or dotted: HT 55a ]TU 1[ (I 107), HT 79+83 ]TU-[·] 3 (I 127), HT 98a ]TU 1 (I 161), HT 126b ]TU 6 (I 217), KH 2 TU-[ (III 23), KH 51 TU[ (III 75), KH 57 ]TU[ (III 79), ZA 12b ]TỤ[ (III 177), PH(?) 31b TU-[ (I 319). TU is the first syllable of ṯawr 'bull', √ṯ-w-r, writing ṯu as ZU does: Ug. ṯwr /ṯōru/ < *ṯawru 'bull' (Huehnergard 2012, 42), BH šōr 'bull, ox', with ṯ > š. See I-ZU-RI-NI-TA.

entries.meaning: figs—commodity ideogram (FIC)

cognates.Linear B: NI ideogram = figs, anchored by the phonetic descriptor su-za on KN F 841 (V&C 1956: σῦκον 'fig'); the Fs ration series HORD+NI+OLE(+VIN) directly continues the LA GRA+NI+OLE+VIN lists (KN Fs 2/4/8/17, PY Fn 187, PY Fg 253)

entries.note: Figs. Linear B writes su-za, σῦκον, beside the same ideogram on KN F 841. The Linear A commodity signs OLE, VIN, GRA, VIR and OLIV keep their sense in Linear B. NI is the onset of *nikuleon. NI takes the small food-measure fractions ½ ⅓ ¼ ⅕ ⅙ ⅒ ¹⁄₁₆ ¹⁄₂₄ in 20 entries (HT 30 NI 7⅙; HT 94a NI 3¹⁄₁₆; KH 8 NI ½, erased), as Linear B measures figs in fractions on the Fs tablets. The sign draws a fig leaf or plant, AB 30, descended from CH 024. 66 documents carry it (HT 35, KH 22, KN 3, PH 2, ZA 2, CR 1, Tel Haror 1). It stands alone 76 times, 66% of them before a numeral, most often beside VIN (12), CYP (8) and GRA (4).
entries.source: di Mino; Neumann 1957, 157–58; Montecchi 2024, 178; Salgarella et al. 2025, 38–39; V&C 1956 s.v. su-za

entries.meaning: fruit (commodity)

cognates.Hebrew: nîḇ, ketiv nôḇ 'fruit': nîḇ śᵉpātayim 'fruit of the lips', Is 57:19 (HALOT 696)

entries.note: KN Wc 26, a roundel (CMS X 120): RU-JA Ruya on face a, NI-PI on face b, intact and undotted (GORILA II 85); Younger enters face b in the logogram column. The thing received against the receiver. nīb 'fruit': Heb. nîb 'fruit' (Isa 57:19; HALOT 696); NI writes nī, PI the b. Rival: NI, the fig sign, with PI written beside it. Weak point: the Knossos findspot is queried (Søyen Collection, formerly Erlenmeyer; Ferrara, Montecchi and Valério 2022, 103–104). One attestation.

entries.meaning: pig (livestock commodity)

cognates.Akkadian: šaḫû 'pig', Sum. lw., wr. ŠAḪ (CAD Š/1 102; AHw 1133)
cognates.Ugaritic: polyglot list [ŠA]Ḫ = še-ḫu-ú = ú-ḫi = ḫu-zi-rù: Akk. šaḫû beside local ḫuzīr (GlOS 1, 277)

entries.note: A logogram, the first syllable of šaḫū 'pig'; the pictographic ancestor of AB 58 is a pig or boar (CH 035; Ferrara 2022). Seven standalone occurrences at three sites (KH 4, HT 2, ZA 1), most followed by numerals; HT 115a's fraction (2 ¹⁄₅) marks a measured commodity, meat by weight, not a head count. On KH 11 it stands with VIN, NI, SI and CYP. Akk. šaḫû, a Sumerian loanword: the ḫ is unwritten and šaū contracts to šū. Linear B parted the pig logogram (*85 SUS₂) from the syllabogram B 58, so AB 58 served both in Linear A. Rival: NWS ḫuzīr (PS 2170 *ḫV(n)zīr-), Mari names ḫu-zi-ra-nu-um, ḫu-zi-ra-tum 'sow' (GlOS 1, 277).
entries.source: di Mino; Ferrara 2022; GlOS 1; CAD; AHw

entries.meaning: honey, fruit syrup—commodity abbreviation of *dibšu; rival dblt 'fig cake'. In personnel lists a separate single-sign abbreviation

cognates.Akkadian: dišpu 'honey' (CAD D 161–63); delivered with oil, EA 55:12
cognates.Hebrew: דְּבַשׁ dǝbaš 'honey'; Deut 32:13–14 beside חֶמְאַת בָּקָר (cf. DI and E on HT12)
cognates.Ugaritic (rival): dblt 'dried fig, fig cake' (DULAT 261), in commodity lists by the quarter (KTU 4.751:10; 4.60:5) beside nbt 'honey' (DULAT 610; 4.14, 4.751); Hebrew dǝbēlâ

entries.note: Two uses, all at Haghia Triada (GORILA I 7, 37, 61, 121, 123, 133, 159, 181, 209). Commodity: HT 20 .3 QE-KU-RE · DI ½ (logographic, a divisible product: Montecchi 2008, 318); HT 32 SU-RE 108, DI 65 and OLE+NE RE 104, DI 53 (each after a larger figure, as a sub-entry); OLE+DI 12× on HT 12, 14, 28a, 28b, 50b, 90, 116a, 129, also OLE+QE+DI (HT 121), DI+QE (HT 101); HT 111a DI 14[ before NI. Personnel or recipient, whole numbers in name lists, a single-sign abbreviation like PA, KA, JU, KI (Montecchi 2008, 318): HT 97a .4 DI 4 under VIR+KA; HT 122b .4 DI 2 within KU-RO 65; HT 66 DI 2 after VIR; HT 85b DI 1; HT 3 DI 2; HT 69 DI 8. dibšu applies to the commodity only; rival Ug. dblt 'fig cake'. MA-DI beside DI on 4 tablets. Broken: HT 122a ]-DI, HT 128a DỊ[, HT 62+73 DI[, HT 3 .5 DỊ[, HT 69 .3 ]DI 12[. One consonant, /d/; all witnesses at HT.
entries.source: GORILA I; CAD D 161–63; DULAT 261, 610; Montecchi 2008, 318

entries.meaning: the craftsman, artisan (title)
entries.note: HT 118 A-RI-SU 4, with KI 1 owed, in a pig account among MA-DI, QA-QA-RU (Qaqqaru) and RI-RU-MA, KU-RO 30. ḥārišu 'the craftsman', the qātil participle: Ugaritic ḥrš 'craftsman, manual worker; artisan, builder' (DULAT 366); Ugarit's polyglot list ḫa-ra-šu 'craftsman, builder' (GlOS 1, 251); Amorite ḥariš-, *ḥāriṯ- 'artificer, worker', from *ḥrṯ 'engrave, cut', in the Mari name Ḫa-ri-ša-an (Huffmon 1965, 205). A title in a recipient list, as QA-*310-I qaynī 'the smith' takes KI-oil on HT 8a. Rivals: a personal name ʾarīšu on √ʾ-r-š 'to request': Amorite ʾARUŚ-U (A-RU-SU; Gelb 1980, no. 511), glossary ʾariśum; A-RE-SA-NA (THE Zb 2) is read on that root. Akkadian eršu B (Neo-Assyrian aršu) 'drilled, plowed and sown', substantivally 'drilled field' (CAD E 314), a sense the recipient slot does not fit. One attestation.
entries.source: di Mino; DULAT; GlOS 1; Huffmon 1965; Gelb 1980; CAD E

entries.meaning: twin—birth-circumstance personal name from √t-ʾ-m

cognates.Amorite: TU-MA-NU-UM tuʾmānum (Gelb 1980, no. 6114), TA-MI (no. 6028), fem. tu-a-ma-tum, 'twin' (GlOS 2, 290)

entries.note: HT 94b, under KI-RO: TU-MA 1 opens a list of five persons, 1 each, with PA-TA-NE, DE-DI, KE-KI-RU and SA-RU, totalled KU-RO 5. tuʾma 'twin', a birth-circumstance name, the medial ʾ unwritten: Heb. tôʾămîm 'twins' (Gen 25:24; 38:27), Akk. tū(ʾ)mu (HALOT 1694). The Amorite name TU-MA-NU-UM, Gelb's TUʾM-AN-UM, is built on the same word (Gelb 1980, no. 6114). One attestation.

entries.meaning: young bull, young animal

cognates.Akkadian: mūru 'young animal; young bull; foal' (eBL mūru I; CAD M2 229–30)

entries.note: HT 3 MU-RU 1 and HT 46a MU-RU 1, the latter before KU-RO 43½: whole units, as *23M counts whole animals. MU-RU spells mūru sign for sign, the proposed value of the *23M logogram: Akk. mūru 'foal; calf' (CAD M/2 229–230). Rival: √m-r-ʾ 'fatling', Ug. mrỉ (DULAT 563). Two attestations.
entries.source: di Mino; GlOS 2; CAD M/2; DULAT

alternative_readings.note: 'lord, master' (Ug. mrʾ, Aram. mārē; Amorite MRʾ, Gelb AS 21 §0.7); needs MU for ma. NWS *marʾ- 'lord, master' (Ugaritic mrʾ, Aramaic mārē). MU=/mu/ for /m/, RU=/ru/ for /rʾ/ (guttural ʾ drops). On HT3 with qty 1 on personnel roster. Alternative: opaque PN. || Third attestation HT46a; Amorite MRʾ (Gelb AS 21 §0.7). Ug mrủ is 'fattened, fatling' (DULAT 563) and, as mrủ (III), an official (DULAT 564; Akk. murʔu); 'lord' is Aramaic mārē.

entries.meaning: beer, strong drink—logographic abbreviation of *śakaru/*šikaru; commodity logogram, compounded with VIN

cognates.Akkadian: šikaru 'beer; fermented alcoholic beverage' (CAD Š/2 420)

entries.note: HT 56a: SA 11½ under the heading *188 (buṭnu). Compound forms: VIN+SA (HT 131b), SA-VIN (HT 114b SA-VIN 9, ZA 15a), a compounded beverage 'wine-beer' (cf. the yayin/šēkār doublet, Num 6:3, Isa 5:11). Akk. šikaru 'beer (made from grain), fermented alcoholic beverage' (CAD Š/2 420), Heb. šēkār 'intoxicating drink' (HALOT 1501), Arab. sakar. On HT 27b SA n pairs with RE m (SA 1 RE 14, SA 4 RE 70[, SA 4 RE ]40), a transaction notation, with no reading there.

entries.meaning: herb, aromatic plant (commodity term in allocation lists)

cognates.Akkadian: šammu(m) "herb, plant, drug, aromatic"—ubiquitous in administrative/pharmaceutical texts

entries.note: HT 10a: the first entry under KU-NI-SU 'emmer', quantity 4, on an allocation tablet. samm- 'plant, herb', PS *samm- (semitic_roots 2409): Ug. smm 'perfume' (DULAT 751), Akk. šammu(m) 'plant, herb', the geminate mm written single. Rival: a place name, on the quantity 35 of HT 6b. Weak point: no commodity logogram stands with SA-MA on its four tablets.

entries.meaning: measure unit (dry/liquid capacity ≈ 1.2 liters)—metrological logographic abbreviation

cognates.Akkadian: qû B 'measuring vessel; a measure of capacity', gen. qê (CAD Q 288)
cognates.Hebrew: קַב qab 'qab-measure' (HALOT 1060; 2 Kgs 6:25 רֹבַע הַקַּב 'a quarter of a qab')

entries.note: HT Wc 3014, a roundel: side a KU-MI-NA, side b QE · CAP (GORILA II 76), QE before the caprid logogram. QE writes qê, the genitive of Akk. qû in measure phrases, šá 2 qe-e 'of 2 q.' (Hh. X 261ff.; CAD Q 288–289); Heb. qab (2 Kgs 6:25). THE Zg 16 (Akrotiri faience triton, Doumas, PAE 2019, fig. 9) opens QE · at the broken left edge. Every tablet QE is broken or dotted (HT 27a, 37, 55b, 111b, 146; KH 50). Weak point: a measure before CAP, not before the cumin of side a. Rival: QE an adjunct or abbreviation qualifying CAP. One complete attestation.

entries.meaning: light, fire (divine epithet or votive label on clay vessels)

cognates.Akkadian: nūru "light, fire" (CAD N/II)

entries.note: IN Zb 1 and KAM Zb 1, the sole word on two clay vessels, from Kamilari and an unknown site, with no sentence context. nūr- 'light, fire', √n-w-r: Ug. nwr /nāra/, /yanūr-/ 'to be bright, shine' (Huehnergard 2012, 50), BH nēr 'lamp'. On a votive vessel nūru 'Light' addresses a god, as in the epithets of Shamash. Rival: a name on nūr, as Mari nu-ur-me-er, Emar nu-ri-ᵈda-gan, Ugarit nu-ri-ia-nu (GlOS 2, 114). Two attestations. See *301-U-RA.

entries.meaning: garment, textile

cognates.Hebrew: sût (סוּת) 'garment' (Gen 49:11; HALOT 749); šît (שִׁית) 'clothing, garment' (Ps 73:6, Prov 7:10; HALOT 1486)

entries.note: ZA 20, an allocation list: SI-TU 6, after SI-TE-TU šetātu 'woven' 1; HT Wa 1019, a nodule sealed with the name PA-TA-NE. sūt 'garment': Heb. sût, sûtōh 'his garment' beside lᵉbûšô (Gen 49:11), Ph. swt (HALOT 749).

entries.meaning: suckling (lamb or kid)

cognates.Ugaritic: llủ, llỉ, llả, pl. llỉm 'suckling (lamb or kid)', // ỉmr: k llỉ b ṯbrn qnh 'like a suckling in the opening of his oesophagus', KTU 1.4 VIII 19 (DULAT 494)
cognates.Akkadian: lalû B (laliʾu, lalaʾu) 'kid', OB on, in Nuzi and MB lists of sheep and goats (CAD L 51–52)

entries.note: HT Wc 3012, a roundel: ZU-DI-RA on face a, RE-RO on face b, both whole and undotted (GORILA II 75). The thing received, one suckling, against the receiver ṯudira. lalʾu 'suckling': Ug. llu 'suckling (lamb or kid)' (DULAT 494), Akk. lalû 'kid' (CAD L 51). RE writes la as in RE-ZA ʾaraz, RO the -lu as in KU-RO kull, the ʾ unwritten. One attestation. Cf. ZU-DI-RA.

entries.meaning: cedar (wood, resin or oil; commodity); rival Luwian aruza, a measure

cognates.Hieroglyphic Luwian: aruza, a measure equated with Urartian liš, rival

entries.note: KH 86 ]RE-ZA CYP, before the aromatic cyperus, broken before, with no numeral of its own; HT 88 RE-ZA 6 before NI KI-KI-NA 7; HT 13 RE-ZA 5½, first entry of the VIN · TE list. ʾarz 'cedar', the aromatic wood, resin and oil, beside cyperus at Khania as cedar beside juniper in Hebrew (1 Kgs 5:22); RE writes the ra of *ʾaraz-, as Ugarit ar-zi-ma |ʔarzīma| < *|ʔarazīma| (GlOS 1, 43), ZA the z. Weak points: initial ʾa- unwritten; KH 20 ]DU-RE-ZA · CYP+E ½ fills the same slot before cyperus, so KH 86 ]RE-ZA can end DU-RE-ZA. Rival: Hieroglyphic Luwian aruza, a measure, attested later.

entries.meaning: butter, ghee (ḥemʾat), a quantified commodity

cognates.Akkadian: ḫimētu (palace ration lists, Ur III–NB)
cognates.Eblaite: ḫi-ma-ad ḥimʾat 'butter, curd', a commodity in the administrative texts (ARET 13; GlOS 1, 272)

entries.note: E stands before a numeral in eight of nine occurrences, at HT and KN: HT 12 E 30, HT 23a E 17, HT 23b E 7, HT 35 E 5, HT 91 E 5 and E 3, KN 1a E 240, KN 1b E 105. ḥemʾat 'butter, ghee', E its first vowel: Heb. ḥemʾâ 'sour milk, cream' (HALOT 325), Ug. ḫmảt 'butter, curd' (DULAT 390), Akk. ḫimētu 'ghee' (CAD Ḫ 189). Weak point: no phonetic complement confirms it. ZA 4a has ]E[, broken on both sides.
entries.source: di Mino; HALOT; DULAT; CAD Ḫ

entries.meaning: figs (logographic abbreviation of TI-NI)

cognates.Akkadian: tittu / tiʔittu / tīnātu

entries.note: A sign of two functions: the syllabogram ti (AB 04), and, standalone with quantities, the fig logogram, the abbreviation of TI-NI. Eleven standalone occurrences at six sites, most followed by numerals, with quantities from ¼ to 100. Pan-Semitic *tiʔin- 'fig', one of the seven species of Deut 8:8. Weak points: NI is the confirmed fig logogram, and TI never shares a tablet with it: TI stands alone at Malia, Palaikastro and Pyrgos, NI alone at Khania and Knossos; on HT 119, TI 7 stands among names inside a personnel total (KU-RO 160 with VIR 68). See TE-*301.

entries.meaning: myrrh (murru), compound logogram

cognates.Akkadian: murru "myrrh, bitter resin" (CAD M/2 222; OB medical/ritual texts, c. 2000–1600 BCE)
cognates.Egyptian: mꜣrw "myrrh" (attested from 2400 BCE, imported from Punt)

entries.note: A ligature of three signs, on eight tablets at two sites (HT 5, KH 3), always in sequences of oils and aromatics beside *308 šamnu, OLE+NE, OLE+RI, OLE+TA, CYP and VIN, in the small fractions of aromatics (⅙, ⅓, ½). murru 'myrrh', from pan-Semitic √m-r-r 'bitter'; three signs for a two-consonant root make the compound ideographic, not phonetic. Exod 30:23 mōr-dərōr heads the anointing-oil recipe, the place MI+JA+RU takes in the Linear A aromatic lists, and the Uluburun wreck (c. 1300 BCE) carried aromatic resins between the Levant and the Aegean. ME-MI-JA-RU on ZA Zg 35 is a prefixed form. See MA-RI-RE-I.

entries.meaning: dagān 'grain, cereal'
entries.note: A commodity logogram, grain: 60 standalone and 52 in compounds, on 47 tablets at 5 sites; Linear B uses it too. dagān 'grain': Heb. דָּגָן, Ug. dgn, Ph. dgn. In GRA+DA (HT 133) DA is the phonetic complement for the da- of dagān, and DA-KA on five HT Wa nodules writes daga(n). Four times it stands with A-DU, the Storm God, an agricultural and cultic setting. See DA-KU-NA.

entries.meaning: wayn 'wine'
entries.note: A commodity logogram, wine: 52 standalone at 10 sites, the widest distribution of any commodity. On HT 89 it follows KU-RO in a separate commodity section, the numeral 6 damaged. wayn 'wine': Heb. yayin, Ug. yn, Gk. οἶνος < *woinos. VIN+WA (twice, HT 27b) takes WA as the complement for the wa- of *wayn-; Canaanite is y-initial (Ug. yn; Amarna ye-ni, EA 84:44; Aphek ye-nu; GlOS 2, 366), so the complement writes the form before the shift. VIN, GRA and SA on HT 27b make the set of wine, grain and beer. Gordon's ya-ne 'wine' (1966, §123) is KN Zb 4, whose corrected reading is JA-SI (see JA-SI). Geʿez wayn 'wine; vine, grapes' and Sabaic wyn 'vineyard' keep the w- (K0457). Weak point: in Linear A the *wayn- etymology rests on the VIN+WA complement alone, the commodity function on everything else. See JI-NU-MA-RE.

entries.meaning: šamnu 'oil, olive oil'

cognates.Akkadian: šamnu 'oil, fat, cream' (CAD Š/1 321)

entries.note: A commodity logogram, oil: 21 standalone occurrences; Linear B uses it too. šamnu 'oil, olive oil': Heb. šemen, Ug. šmn, Akk. šamnu, the root of *308, the pressed-oil derivative, of which OLE is the base. Its compounds are the richest of any commodity, eighteen types: OLE+KI standard, OLE+MI anointing, OLE+DI honey-infused, OLE+TA fine grade, OLE+NE libation, OLE+RI aromatic.

entries.meaning: zayt 'olive (fruit)'
entries.note: Commodity ideogram for the olive fruit, apart from OLE šamnu 'oil', a logogram Linear B shares. OLIV and OLE stand on the same tablets with separate quantities (HT 50a, HT 101, HT 116a), fruit beside product. HT 123+124a gives OLIV 31 beside *308, pressed oil, 8¼, a record of olive processing; on HT W 231a OLIV alone labels a sealed commodity; OLIV+TU is a subtype, three times. zayt 'olive': Heb. zayit 'olive tree, olive' (HALOT 268–269), Ug. zt 'olive; olive tree; olive grove' (DULAT 984), Arb. zayt 'olive oil', zaytūn 'olive' (Lane 1274). OLIV stands alone 25 times on 18 documents from Haghia Triada, Arkhanes, Tylissos and Zakros.

entries.meaning: olive product qualified by TU (cf. OLE+TU ṭuhūru 'purified')
entries.note: Three Haghia Triada commodity lists: HT 50a *OLIV+TU ⅜ after OLIV 3, HT 101 *OLIV+TU 1 after OLIV 1¼, HT 116a *OLIV+TU 2 after OLE+MI 1. The OLIV host places it in the olive-product family, and TU distinguishes it from plain OLIV: a TU-qualified olive product. Cf. OLE+TU ṭuhūru 'purified', the same adjunct on the oil host. Three attestations.

entries.meaning: barr- 'wheat, threshed grain'
entries.note: Single-sign commodity logogram: PA writes the ba- of barr- 'wheat, threshed grain', Hebrew bār (Gen 41:35–49; HALOT 153). Standalone commodity (16×, 5 sites) in bulk quantities, 64 and 40 on ZA 12a/b, clustering with TI (figs). After GRA, PA is the measure parīsu (GRA+PA); *304+PA 3×. On HT 8a PA takes KI-oil 3½ in a list of recipients, an abbreviation there. Rival: parīsu standing alone. One sign, no phonetic complement.

entries.meaning: physician, healer

cognates.Akkadian: asû 'physician' (GlOS 1, 47)

entries.note: HT 81 A-SE · MI+JA+RU · ≈⅙, HT 93a A-SE · I GRA+PA 26¾, HT 132 A-SE · A319 5: A-SE opens an entry, then a divider and a commodity; ZA Zb 3, a clay vessel, writes VIN 32 over DI-DI-KA-SE A-SA-MU-NE A-SE. Four attestations at two sites, on tablets and a vessel. ʾāsē 'physician', a culture word from Sum. azu: Akk. asû, Aram. ʔsy(ʔ), Arb. ʔāsin, and the Euphrates name ì-lí-a-si-ia 'my god is my physician' (GlOS 1, 47); Official Aramaic, Nabataean and Palmyrene ʾsy 'physician' (DNWSI 88). Hebrew Asa is read 'physician' by Stamm (HALOT 73). Each entry is an allocation to the physician: myrrh, a drug, on HT 81; grain on HT 93a, as QA-QA-RU receives the same grain; on ZA Zb 3 the title follows Eshmun, the healing god, as A-KO-A-NE follows PI-TE-RI. Rival: ʾaššē 'fire offering', Heb. ʾiššeh (HALOT 93). Weak point: the West Semitic forms are Aramaic and Arabic; the Bronze Age witnesses are names, ì-lí-a-si-ia (GlOS 1, 47) and Asīya (A-SE-JA). See I-SI.

entries.meaning: Il-Mīšar, god of justice—theophoric compound: ʾil 'god' + Mīšaru (justice god, maqtal pattern of √y-š-r). Personnel category on sanctuary allocation tablet.

cognates.Akkadian: Mīšaru (d-Mīšaru)—god of justice, son of Adad and Šala, spouse of Išartu (An = Anum III). maqtal nominal of ešēru "to be straight/just" (CAD E 352). Attested: OB theophoric names, Mari, Seleucid Uruk god-lists.
cognates.Ugaritic: mšr—"justice, equity" (DULAT 586); KTU 1.16 vi: mšr as divine attribute
cognates.Hebrew: mêšārîm (מֵישָׁרִים) "equity, uprightness" (Ps 9:9, 58:2, 75:3); same maqtal pattern as Akkadian Mīšaru
cognates.Phoenician: Misor (Μισωρ)—Philo of Byblos via Eusebius PE 1.10.13: father of Taautus/Thoth; paired with Sydyk (√ṣ-d-q)

entries.note: HT 27a .3 I-MI-SA-RA 43[, line-initial at an intact edge, on a personnel allocation tablet headed by TI-NI-TA *307 (Tinit of the Sanctuary); the numeral meets a break, so 43 or more. I ʾi(l), MI mī, SA ša, RA r.
