CAD M/2 118 lists ᵈMi-šá-ru ᵈIl-mi-šá-ru (KAV 42 i 34) and the god of justice as DINGIR-lum mi-š[a-ri] (KUB 4 47 r. 8); I-MI-SA-RA writes Il-Mīšar with the coda l unwritten, as Linear B leaves a syllable-final l unwritten (ka-ko = khal-kos; Ventris and Chadwick 1956, 45). ʾil 'god' heads Amorite names written I-lī- (I-lī-ṣa-du-uq, I-lī-ma-lik; Huffmon 1965, 165); išar, the Akkadian form of √yšr, serves Amorite names as a theophorous element or divine name (I-šar-li-im; Huffmon 1965, 216), and Me-ša-rum is an Amorite name (Gelb 1980, no. 4661). With Tinit at its head in the place of Išartu, HT 27a holds both members of the Akkadian justice dyad. Rival: ʾī-Mīšar, with the interrogative ʾī 'where is' of liturgy and names: Ug. ỉy (DULAT 130) in the cultic cry ỉy ảlỉyn bʿl (KTU 1.6 IV 28–29; Pope 1977, 589); Heb. ʾÎ-kāḇôd (1 Sam 4:21; HALOT 38, s.v. III אִי); Amorite Ḥa-ya-ab-AN 'where is the father, O god' (Huffmon 1965, 128 n. 18). Weak points: one attestation, though √y-š-r runs through the libation formula (JA-SA-SA-RA-ME, 7 inscriptions); the right end of .2 is broken, and the scribe runs KI-*310 across .4–.5, so I can close a word lost there; MI-SA-RA alone then writes Mīšar (ᵈMi-šar, BRM 4 25:45; CAD M/2 118). See JA-SA-SA-RA-ME.
entries.source: di Mino; DULAT; HALOT; CAD M/2; Huffmon 1965; Gelb 1980; Ventris and Chadwick 1956; Pope 1977
related_forms: TI-NI-TA (Tinitu/Tanit, CONFIRMED — heading deity on same tablet)

entries.meaning: ruqqû-ru 'aromatic preparation (with phonetic complement RU confirming /ru-/ onset)'

cognates.Akkadian: ruqqû 'to prepare perfume'; ruqqû adj. 'perfumed (oil)' (CAD R 420)

entries.note: *401 with the rider RU, which gives the ru- onset of its proposed value RUQQÛ: Akk. ruqqû 'perfumed (oil)' and ruqqû 'to prepare perfume' (CAD R 420). Six Khania documents, KH 12 twice, KH 63, KH 83, KH 84, KH 85 and KH 91, and KN Zg 57a, the ivory sceptre ring from Knossos. Counted in fractions (¹⁄₁₆ on KH 85 and KH 91), it stands with CYP, MI+JA+RU (myrrh), *308 (šamnu) and OLE+TA (fine oil): an aromatic. KH 91 writes *401+RU beside *401+RA, two compounds on one tablet. Cf. *401+*304 (RUQQÛ+PIDRU, 'aromatic fat'). See *401.

entries.meaning: shade, protection (personal-name element)

cognates.Amorite: ṣill- 'shade, protection' (Huffmon, APNM 257); Ṣillī-Baʿli, Ṣill-Haddu

entries.note: Name on the HT 55a KI-RO list (SI-RU 1) and first element of HT 90 SI-RU-MA-RI-TA₂ (GORILA I 107, 143). Amorite ṣill- 'shade, protection' (Huffmon 1965, 257): Ṣillī-Baʿli (Huffmon 1965, 58), Ṣill-Haddu, Ṣillān (Gelb 1980, nos. 6482–6483); Heb. ṣēl 'shade' (HALOT 1024), the name Ṣillāh (Gen 4:19; HALOT 1025); Ug. ẓl /ẓillu/ 'shade, shadow' (Huehnergard 2012, 161). ẓill-, written with SI and one RU for the geminate. Two attestations.

entries.meaning: waitress, serving-girl (title)

cognates.Hurrian: Hurro-Hittite šiduri 'girl'; Akk. šiduri 'young woman', the source of Ug. ṯdr (Watson 2018, 336)

entries.note: A recipient in the HT 9a/9b wine lists under SA-RO · TE · VIN (2½, 2) and on HT 122a (1), one roster in three copies, among names and titles. *324 = ṮA, the sign SigLA reads A364 at Zakros. ṮA-DI-RA = ṯadira, Ug. ṯdr 'waitress, girl' (DULAT 886–887), a Hurrian loan (Watson 2018, 336), on a wine issue.

entries.meaning: Star (place name, as Mari Kabkab)

cognates.Eblaite: ᵈMUL = gag-gáb 'star', also a DN; names ga-kab, ga-ba-ga-bù (GlOS 1, 297)
cognates.Mari: Kabkab, ka-ab-ka-ab, a place name (M.7630:4; FM II 338; MTT I/1, s.v. KABKAB)

entries.note: HT 16 KA-KU-PA ·, the heading over DI-NA-U ⅛, WA ⅓, *188+KU ⅜ and SA-PO ZE 1⁄16; on the roundels HT Wc 3015 KA-KU-PA with CYP and HT Wc 3016 with *304+PA and CYP+D, a party receiving cyperus. kawkab 'star', the Semitic word as a place name, as Mari's town Kabkab (MTT I/1, s.v. Kabkab): Hebrew kôkāb (HALOT 463), Akkadian kakkabu, Arabic kawkab. Three attestations, all Haghia Triada.
entries.source: di Mino; HALOT; MTT I/1; GlOS 1; FM II

entries.meaning: the Charioteer (PN, √d-h-r 'dash, gallop'; *21F = ha)

cognates.Hebrew: dāhar 'to dash, gallop' (of a horse), Nah 3:2; dahărâ 'galloping', Judg 5:22 (HALOT 214)
cognates.Egyptian: twhr '(foreign) warrior' (AED lemma 173060; Wb 5, 322.10–14), a loan of Canaanite dhr, 'charioteer' (HALOT 214)

entries.note: KH 92 .1 A-DA-*21F-RI · KU-NI-TE 10[, a personal name at the head of an allocation list. ha-dāhari 'the Charioteer': Hebrew dāhar 'to dash, gallop' of a horse (Nah 3:2), dahărâ 'galloping' (Judg 5:22; HALOT 214). Egypt borrowed the word for the chariot warrior, twhr (AED lemma 173060). Albright's Canaanite source of Eg. tuhira 'charioteer' is *dōhar < *dāhar (HALOT 214), the a that *21F writes. Rival: Arabic dahr 'time, fate, epoch', which has no cognate of that sense in Hebrew, Ugaritic or Akkadian. A- is the article on the title, as in Heb. Hallôḥēš (Neh 3:12) and Hassōperet (Ezra 2:55). Weak point: no Semitic name from the root is attested. One attestation.

entries.meaning: compounded perfume, ointment (vessel label)

cognates.Eblaite: GIŠ.NAGA = rí-ga-tum 'spiced, oily ointment'; Ì.RÁ.RA = ra-gi-um 'oil-perfumer' (GlOS 2, 165)
cognates.Akkadian: raqqû in bīt raqqî 'perfume makers' bureau' (CAD R 174)

entries.note: SY Za 11, the sole word on a stone vessel from the Syme sanctuary: · RO-QA. Heb. rōqaḥ 'compounded perfume' (Exod 30:25, 35), final ḥ unwritten; a label for the vessel's contents. Rival: rōqēaḥ 'perfumer' (Ug. rqḥ, DULAT 734), the maker or owner. One attestation. See *401, OLE+RI, VIN+RA and RO-KE.

entries.meaning: myrrh (the bitter resin)
entries.cognates: Akk. murru, Ug. mr, Heb. mōr (Exod 30:23), Ar. murr
entries.note: HT 6b: MA-RI-RE-I 3, after RA-TI-SE 1 and before DU-DA-MA 66, on an aromatic allocation tablet whose face also counts SA-MA 'herb' 35. marīrēy 'the bitter stuff', myrrh: a qaṭīl adjective of √m-r-r with the nisbe -ēy, as Heb. mōr 'myrrh' and mar 'bitter', with Mandaic and Ethiopic marīr (HALOT 630). Song 4:14 lists mōr beside qāneh and karkōm 'saffron'. One attestation. See MI+JA+RU.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'our Beloved'

cognates.Amorite: JADID 'dear', IA-DI-DA, IA-DI-DU-UM (Gelb 1980, nos. 3183–3192)
cognates.Arabic: wadda (وَدَّ) 'to love', inf. n. wudd, widd, wadd; widād 'love' (Lane 2931); names wdn, wdnt (Harding 1971, 639), wdd, wddʾl (637); Wadd, a god (Faris 1952, 9)

entries.note: HT 28b: WI-DI-NA OLE+DI 3, VIN 3¼, after PU-RA₂ and JA-*21F, each with its own entry. widd 'love', the i-form of √w-d-d (Lane 2931), + -i- and the 1cp -nā, as PA₃-NI-NA banīna 'our builder' and Amorite I-LU-NA 'our god' (Gelb 1980, no. 2555); dd unwritten. Initial w- where Amorite (JADID, Gelb 1980, nos. 3183–3192), Ugaritic (ydd) and Hebrew (yādîd) have y-. Rival: Wadd, a god (Faris 1952, 9; Q 71:23), which needs WI for wa. Cf. WA-DI-NI (HT Wc 3007). One attestation. See WI-TE-JA-MU.

entries.meaning: Inatos (place name on the south coast; Linear B wi-na-to)

cognates.Linear B: wi-na-to, a place, KN As 604.2, 604.3, after a man's name with VIR 1 (DMic II 432: *Ϝίνατος, Ἴνατος)

entries.note: KH 5 .3 WI-NA-DU · *301̣-NA ·, the head of the second section, over KU-PA-ZU CYP 3 and figs 2, as A-DA-KI-SI-KA · A-RA-U-DA · heads the first; intact, no dots (GORILA III 25). An entity slot in a transfer (Hogan, in Salgarella and Petrakis, The Wor(l)ds of Linear A, 81). Linear B wi-na-to, a place on KN As 604.2–3 in the slot of ra-su-to and pu-so: *Ϝίνατος, Ἴνατος on the south coast, modern Tsoúdsouro (DMic II 432). DU for the t of -to, stops unmarked for voice. Younger rejects the identification, Inatos lying too far for Khania to have controlled it, and notes dedications in its Eileithyia cave from the Neopalatial period on (Younger, Linear A Texts); A-RA-U-DA, Arwad, stands on the same tablet. Rival: wi + Nadūb, the Amorite name NA-DU-BU-UM (Gelb 1980, no. 4956), with WI a conjunction and b unwritten. Place before party, as in A-RA-JU-U-DE-ZA, Ḥudaṯu of ʾArāyu (HT 122b); the first head runs party then origin, A-DA-KI-SI-KA of Arwad. One attestation.

entries.meaning: Calf of the Wild Cow (personal name, compound; wild 'young one' + rēmtu 'wild cow')

cognates.Arabic: walad, wuld, wild, wald, each sing. and pl., masc. and fem., 'a child, son, daughter, youngling, or young one … of any kind' (Lane 2966); al-wild, bi-l-kasr, ka-l-walad lughatan 'wild, with i, is a dialect form of walad' (Lisān al-ʿArab III 467)
cognates.Akkadian: ildu (wildu, weldu, mildu) 'offspring, progeny': wi-il-di-ša 'her offspring' (CT 8 25a:16, OB); wi-li-id bilim 'the progeny of the cattle' (YOS 10 35:31, OB); per hundred ewes 66⅔ mi-il-du (PBS 2/1 145:6f., NB); construct wilid bītim 'house-born slave' (VAS 16 4:25, OB) (CAD I/J 71). rīmtu 'wild cow', fem. of rī/ēmu; in personal names fRīmtum (OB, MB), Ištar-rīmti-ilī, Aja-rīmti-ilāti, and as a cow's name (CAD R 358–359)
cognates.Ugaritic: rủm 'wild bull': k ỉbr l bʕl yld w rủm l rkb ʕrpt 'because to Baal a bull has been born, a wild bull to the Charioteer of the clouds' (KTU 1.10 III 36; DULAT 712)

entries.note: ZA 9 .6 WI-RA-RE-MI-TE *21F 1, the last entry, a recipient of one ewe after [·]-MA-JU *21F 2; intact, RE a Y with the stem through it (GORILA III 167). Construct by juxtaposition: WI-RA wild 'young one', as Akkadian wilid in wilid bītim, RA for l and the final d unwritten; RE-MI-TE rēmti 'wild cow', RE for the rē- of rēmu. A name of the type of fRīmat-Ninsun, the wild-cow mother of Gilgameš (CAD R 359). TE writes the genitive -ti, as TA-NA-TE beside TA-NA-TI Tanāti; RA writes l, as in SU-PA₃-RA subāra. One attestation.
entries.source: di Mino; Lane; Lisān al-ʿArab; CAD I/J; CAD R; DULAT

entries.meaning: Yāh, divine name; deity receiving offerings alongside Baal on HT28b

cognates.Hebrew: יָהּ Yāh (Ex 15:2 ʿozzī wə-zimrāt Yāh; Ps 68:5 bə-Yāh šemō; Ex 17:16 kēs Yāh)
cognates.Ugaritic: yw, a name of the god Yam: šm bny yw 'the name of my son is yw' (KTU 1.1 IV 14; DULAT 980)
cognates.Egyptian: tꜣ šꜣsw yhwꜣ 'land of the Shasu of YHW' (Soleb, Amenhotep III c. 1390 BCE; Amarah West, Ramesses II)

entries.note: Written JA-*21F, with *21F = HA (h, ḫ). HT 28b: the recipient of VIN 6, between PU-RA₂ (Baal, NI 6) and WI-DI-NA (OLE+DI 3, VIN 3¼), as in the Ugaritic offering lists (KTU 1.39, 1.41). HT 28a: heads its own commodity list after A-SI-JA-KA. Yāh, the short form of the divine name (HALOT 393). Rivals: the Egyptian moon god Iah, jꜥḥ (Ilin-Tomich 2025); the Amorite verbal names Yahwiy-ʾIl, Yahwiy-Haddu (Gelb 1980, nos. 2871, 3593). DULAT 980 keeps Ugaritic yw apart from Hebrew yh. Weak point: Hebrew yh is first attested in the Iron Age, on jar handles from Jericho and Samaria and the Lachish altar (HALOT 393). Two attestations.
entries.source: di Mino; HALOT; Gelb 1980; DULAT; Ilin-Tomich 2025

entries.meaning: Cat (personal name)

cognates.Akkadian: šurānu 'cat'; Šu-ra-nu, a personal name (CAD Š/3 339)
cognates.Ugaritic: snr, syll. si-na-ri, si-na-ru, a personal name (Kinlaw 1967, 101), read 'cat' (GlOS 2, 201)
cognates.Amorite: Šurān-at-um, a woman's name (Gelb 1980, no. 5952)

entries.note: ZA 11b .1–.2 E-TO-RI-[?] *516 / SA-*301-RI · GRA+PA 1 / I OLIV 1. šannāri 'Cat', with *301 = na: SA-NA-RI, s-n-r, as Arabic sinnawr 'the cat' (Lane 1445), where Akk. šurānu has r before n; the geminate nn unwritten. Ugarit has the name: si-na-ri, sí-na-a-r[i] (Kinlaw 1967, 101), read 'cat' (GlOS 2, 201). Rival: a name from a town, as DULAT derives Ugaritic snr from Sināru (DULAT 753). Weak point: *301 = na is a proposed value. One attestation.
entries.source: di Mino; Kinlaw 1967; GlOS 2; Gelb 1980; DULAT

entries.meaning: young bull, head of cattle (live livestock logogram; MU-onset abbreviation of *mūru)

cognates.Akkadian: mūru 'foal; calf' (CAD M/2 229); mīru A 'young bull' (CAD M/2 109)

entries.note: HT 30, HT 114a and HT 121 set it after VIN in whole numbers (1, 3, 3); KH 87 *23M 1, GO Wc 1b *23M 5, and the roundel KH Wc 2069 bears it alone. TU, which counts cattle products in fractions, never shares a tablet with it. mūru 'young bull, head of cattle', MU writing its ū: Akk. mūru 'foal (donkey or horse); calf', from Old Akkadian on (CAD M/2 229–30; eBL mūru I 'young animal; young bull; foal'). Middle Assyrian ledgers write it with the ox determinative, {gu₄}mu-ru{nita₂} 'young bull' (MARV 2 6), and count it by head: 67 mu-ru ša MU '67 calves, yearlings' (KAJ 289:11); the calf sense runs on into Neo-Assyrian, so the Cretan form needs no early split of foal and calf. Ug. mrủ 'fattened, fatling' (DULAT 563); Heb. מְרִיא mǝrīʾ 'fatted steer' (1 Kgs 1:9; Amos 5:22). Rival: *ʾalpu 'cattle' (2113), with the sign a picture, not an abbreviation. See MU-RU.

entries.meaning: attendant, courtier (recipient)

cognates.Akkadian: tīru A (tēru), te-i-rum 'courtier, attendant (a member of the palace or temple staff)' (CAD T 429)

entries.note: HT 91 TE-RI · OLE+MI ≈¹⁄₆, E 3, a second allocation after I-KA's closes with E 5; ARKH 6 DA-NA-TU · KU / TE-RI; PH(?) 31b TE-RI *21M[ 1, among names that each receive a ram. tēri 'attendant, courtier', Akk. tīru A (tēru), 'a member of the palace or temple staff', written te-i-rum (CAD T 429): an Old Akkadian survey totals '27 court attendants', and the tīr bīti draws rations (CT 45 85:6, OB). TE writes the ē of tēru. Weak point: tīru is Akkadian, with no West Semitic cognate. Three attestations.

entries.meaning: box, basket (standardized container for measured commodity allocations)

cognates.Akkadian: quppu 'box'; qappatu 'basket'

entries.note: ZA 11a and ZA 11b each have KU-PA · GRA+PA, with 1 and 3: a container named before measured grain; HT 110a has KU-PA 1 after CYP+E 20, and KH 29 KU-PA before 2. quppa 'box, basket': Akk. quppu A '(a wicker basket or wooden chest)' (CAD Q 307), KU writing qu, since Linear A has no QU sign; the accusative *quppa(m) gives KU-PA. The small quantities (1–3) count single containers. See QE-PI-TA and KA-PA.

entries.meaning: principal, primary, capital (quality/grade marker on sealed goods and commodity allocations)

cognates.Akkadian: rūštu 'fine quality of oil', written Ì.SAG (CAD R 430); rēštû 'first, firstborn' (CAD R 274)
cognates.Hebrew: rōʾš 'head; first, best'; bəśāmîm rōʾš 'the finest spices', Exod 30:23 (HALOT 1164)

entries.note: ZA 1b ]RO GRA 47 and KH 100 RO VIN[, before the commodity: 'principal grain', 'principal wine'; HT 110b RO 20 under GRA; PH Wc 39 JA-DI RO, on a roundel. RO stands alone on 90 HT Wa nodules, HT Wb 2001 and 2002, and ZA Wa 36, marking the sealed goods as of the first grade. rōʾš 'head; first, best': Heb. rōʾš, bəśāmîm rōʾš 'balsam of top quality' (Exod 30:23; HALOT 1166), Ug. riš 'head; top; first-fruits' (DULAT 713), Akk. rēšu 'head; top; beginning' (CAD R 277), Arb. raʾs, Aram. rēš. See RI-SU-MA.

entries.meaning: seed-grain (agricultural category marker for planting stock allocations)

cognates.Akkadian: zēru 'seed, acreage, semen, descendants' (CAD Z 89)
cognates.Amorite: ḎRʿ 'sow, seed': jaḏraʿ, ḏarʿum (Gelb AS 21, 18)

entries.note: HT 16, under KA-KU-PA: SA-PO ZE ¹⁄₁₆, the smallest quantity on the tablet. ZE alone marks 40 HT nodules (HT Wa 1282–1321) and six Khania nodules (KH Wa 1005–1010), a seed-grain category beside GRA. zēru 'seed': Akk. zēru 'seed (of cereals and of other plants), acreage' (CAD Z 89), Heb. zeraʿ 'seed' (HALOT 282), Ph. zrʿ, Aram. zəraʿ. Ebla has ðerʕ 'seed' with the same e (zi-ir-ḫu; GlOS 1, 167). Weak point: ZE stands alone, and only its context ties it to seed. See *305-RU.
entries.source: di Mino; CAD Z; HALOT; DULAT; Krahmalkov 2000; Gelb 1980

entries.meaning: turn away! (2mp imperative—disease expulsion command)

cognates.Hebrew: sōbbû 'turn!', 2mp imperative, Saul's command to the runners, 1 Sam 22:17; sbb 'go around' (HALOT 738)

entries.note: London Medical Papyrus BM 10059, Keftiu Spell #33 against the samānu disease: Egyptian group-writing s3bw. √s-b-b 'to turn, go around': Heb. sābab (HALOT 738), 2mp imperative sōbbū, סֹבּוּ צִיּוֹן sōbbū Ṣiyyôn 'go around Zion' (Ps 48:13). Group-writing s3 is plain /s/: the same scribe renders Semitic ṣ as Egyptian ḏ in the next word, yaṣʾā (y3yd33), and the geminate -bb- goes unwritten. The pair sabbū yaṣʾā 'Turn away! Go out!' is an expulsion command, as Udug-hul utukku lemnu ṣi ana nisâti 'evil spirit, go far away!' (CT 16 29:92f.; CAD N/2 184). The D54 determinative sits in the phonogram ḏi of word 2 (Kyriakidis 2002, n. 16). One attestation. See Y3-Y-D33.
entries.source: di Mino; HALOT; Kyriakidis 2002; CAD N/2

entries.meaning: go out! (3ms volitive yaqtula—disease expulsion command)

cognates.Akkadian: aṣû, waṣû 'to go out, leave' (CAD A/2 356)
cognates.Amorite: JṢʾ 'go out': jīṣiʾ, jāṣiʾ (Gelb AS 21, 22)

entries.note: Egyptian group-writing: y3yd33 [element 6b, Det: D54 'to go']. Proto-Semitic *wṣʾ becomes NWS *yaṣʾa by the diagnostic shift of *w to y: Akk. waṣû (CAD W 319), which keeps *w-; Ug. yṣʾ (DLU 946); Heb. yāṣāʾ (HALOT 427). Egyptian d renders Semitic ṣ, and 33 (double aleph) renders final ʾ with a short a; group-writing never marks length. Steiner reads √y-ṣ-ʾ yaṣʾā 'go out!' in this spell (Steiner 1992). The volitive is the yaqtula modal prefix form in -a of Amarna Canaanite (Moran 1960), cognate with the Arabic subjunctive and ancestral to the Heb. cohortative ʾeṣʾā. Rival: perfect yaṣaʾa 'it has gone out', Ugaritic yṣả, syllabic i-ṣa-ʔa (GlOS 2, 361). Keftiu Spell #33 (samānu disease), LMP BM 10059. See JA-SE and SI-TE.

entries.meaning: strangling-demon (feminine personification of disease)
entries.note: Keftiu Spell 33 (London Medical Papyrus, BM 10059), element 7, in Egyptian group-writing with the determinative A2 'to speak, think'. Steiner reads *ḥanqatu 'she who strangles', a disease demon: √ḥ-n-q, Akk. ḫanāqu (CAD Ḫ 75), Heb. ḥānaq (Nah 2:13), Syr. ḥnaq, Ar. ḫanaqa, with Egyptian h for ḥ as usual. The samānu disease swells and constricts, and a strangling demon fits it. The m' before k writes the velar nasal [ŋ], as Akkadian writes /n/ as m before a velar, ku-um-ka for /kunkū/ (Steiner 1992, 198 and n. 61). Weak point: N and M' both stand before K3, where Steiner reads one nasal, ḥ-m-k-tu.

entries.meaning: my Healer (deity invocation—divine title of Rapʾu)

cognates.Ugaritic: rpỉy, a personal name; rpủ 'healer', DN, in ỉlrpỉ, ʿmrpỉ, mlkrpỉ (GlOS 2, 170)
cognates.Egyptian: r-pꜢ-y, a Semitic name (GlOS 2, 168, after Schneider, APÄQ no. 319)

entries.note: Keftiu Spell 33 (London Medical Papyrus, BM 10059), element 8, in Egyptian group-writing; the determinative A40, the seated god, marks a deity. Steiner reads r-p-y rpʾy 'my Healer': √r-p-ʾ 'to heal' with the 1cs -ī. Ug. rpʾu, the divine title in rpʾu mlk ʿlm 'the Healer, eternal king' (KTU 1.108:1) and the rpʾim, Rephaim (KTU 1.20–22); Heb. rāpāʾ (rōpʾekā, Exod 15:26; Ps 103:3); the Phoenician month mrpʾ (KAI 37:3). Rival: Akulov's Erupa-j, joined to Greek Europa through Hattic *lup 'bull', on the same consonants. See A-RE-PI-RE-NA and A-RI-PA.

entries.meaning: I cry out! / my invocation (ritual speech act)

cognates.Ugaritic: pʿr 'open the mouth; shout, proclaim', ypʿr, tpʿr (GlOS 2, 121)

entries.note: Egyptian group-writing p33wry, with the A2 determinative 'to speak, think'. √p-ʿ-r 'open wide (the mouth)' with the 1cs -ī: Heb. pāʿar (Isa 5:14 ūpāʿărāh pīhā 'and she has opened wide her mouth', of Sheol; Ps 119:131 pī pāʿartī 'I opened wide my mouth'), Ug. pʿr 'open the mouth; shout, proclaim' (GlOS 2, 121), Ar. faġara, with the regular ġ for ʿ. The form is *paʿūr-ī, a qatūl verbal noun with the possessive; the A2 determinative suits a speech act. It follows rpʾy 'my Healer' (Steiner 1992, 198–199): rpʾī paʿūrī Mayyā, 'My Healer, I cry out to Mayyā'. Rival: √p-ʾ-r 'glorify' (Isa 60:7). Keftiu Spell #33, LMP BM 10059.

entries.meaning: Mayyā—deified Water (deity name)

cognates.Akkadian: mû 'water; liquid' (CAD M/2 149)

entries.note: Keftiu Spell 33 (London Medical Papyrus, BM 10059), element 10, m'y3 in Egyptian group-writing, with the determinative A40, the seated god. Mayyā, Water deified: √m-y-y, PS *maʔ-, *may- 'water', masculine in every branch (Akk. mû, Heb. mayim m. pl., Ug. my, Ar. māʾ m.), with the NWS feminine -ā (cf. malkā, ʾilat), the feminine Water, a water goddess. Arabic مَيَّة Mayya, a woman's name 'water' from pre-Islamic poetry on (Dhū l-Rumma, d. 735), is geminated mayy- with feminine -a(t); Ugaritic forms goddesses' names from nouns with -ā, -at, as ʿAṯirat and ʿAnat from √ʿ-n-y, the pattern of a *Mayyat-; and the primordial water is a goddess in Tiʾāmat (Akk.), Tĕhôm (Heb.) and Namma (Sum.), all feminine. The male A40 is the Egyptian scribes' default for a foreign god, the -ā of the source carrying the gender. Paired with rpʾī 'Healer', cure with purification, the spell is said over liquid, fermented drink and urine, the media of a water god. Rival: Akulov's 'Maja', joined to Greek Μαῖα, the Pleiad. See MI-JA and MA-I-MI.

entries.meaning: who cries out, the one who implores (relative clause: √š-w-ʿ + determinative-relative dē)

cognates.Hebrew: šwʿ 'call for help', təšawwaʿ wəyōʾmar hinnēnî 'you will cry for help, and he will say: Here I am' (Isa 58:9; HALOT 1443)

entries.note: ZA Zg 35 (label): ]A-MI-JA-RU · SE-WA-AU-DE. √š-w-ʿ 'cry for help' (Heb. šiwwaʿ, Isa 58:9; šawʿâ) + -DE dē, the relative of A-TA-I-*301-DE-KA (di Mino, Ya Diktu): 'the one who cries out'. Weak point: AU is /aw/, one w more than the root. Rival: a second personal name, as on a label. See DU.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'the True One' (kīnu 'true, reliable')

cognates.Eblaite: gi-num kīnum 'reliable', a name (Pagan 1998, row 2059); names gi-na, gi-núm (GlOS 1, 332)
cognates.Amorite: kīnum 'firm' (Gelb 1980, glossary); names ki-nu-um-a-da-al, la-ki-nu (GlOS 1, 332)
cognates.Akkadian: kīnu 'true, reliable, just' (CAD K 391–394); kânu 'to be firm, true'; PN element in Nabû-kīn-apli, Marduk-kīn-šumi
cognates.Hebrew: kūn (כּוּן) 'to be established, firm'; nākōn (נָכוֹן) 'right, true'

entries.note: ARKH 3a: KI-NU heads a commodity allocation section. Kīnu 'the True One', kīn- in Eblaite, Amorite and Akkadian alike, both a name element and the quality adjective 'true, standard': the heading admits 'Kīnu: grain 13' and 'standard grade: grain 13', as KA-NE qanē on the same tablet has two senses. A second attestation, with a quantity in a list or heading an OLE section, would decide between them. Standalone KI is an administrative sign of open value. One attestation. See OLE+KI.

entries.meaning: must, new wine (unfermented or partially fermented grape juice) — commodity logogram

cognates.Hebrew: tīrōš (תִּירוֹשׁ) 'must, new wine' (HALOT 1727; Deut 7:13, 11:14, 12:17; Hos 2:10; Joel 2:19)

entries.note: A wine-class logogram of the AB131 family, beside VIN 'wine' (wayn) and *131C 'vinegar': ARKH 2 KU-RA *131B 5 under the heading SI-DA-TE, ARKH 3a *131B 2 after OLIV 3⅕, ARKH 5 *131B 6 after A-DA-RO GRA 40, ZA 10b DU-RE-ZA-SE *131B 5. tirōšu 'must, new wine', Heb. tîrôš (HALOT 1727). The triad dāgān-tîrôš-yiṣhār (Deut 7:13) matches ARKH 3a's GRA, OLIV and *131B. On ZA 10b DU-RE-ZA-SE turēṯa-se 'for the must' stands before its own logogram. Rival: SigLA codes the ARKH 3a, ARKH 5 and ZA 10b tokens VINb, a variant of VIN, and reads ARKH 2 KU-RA-*131B as one word. Four attestations, at Arkhanes and Zakros.

entries.meaning: sixth, the sixth section

cognates.Akkadian: šeššu

entries.note: HT 123+124b, after *312 1¾: TI-DA-TA ·, then PI-SA 4, the group followed by a divider with no numeral. Ugaritic ṯdṯ 'sixth' (DULAT 887), which keeps the d that the cardinal ṯṯ assimilates (Huehnergard 2012, 51), with T writing the interdental. TI writes the i of the NWS ordinal, Heb. šiššî, fem. šiššît, which is also the fraction 'a sixth': šiššît hāʾêpâ 'a sixth of an ephah' (Ezek 45:13; HALOT 1666). Rival: the cardinal ṯidṯat- 'six', Ug. f. ṯṯt (DULAT 922). Weak point: one attestation. Cf. TI-TI-MA.

entries.meaning: sixty (numeral)

cognates.Akkadian: šuššum

entries.note: PH Wc 40, a roundel: TI-TI-MA NA. Ug. ṯṯm 'sixty', nom. /ṯiṯṯūma/ (Huehnergard 2012, 50), consonant for consonant, the geminate ṯṯ spelled with the doubled sign TI-TI. The second TI writes the ī of the oblique, ṯṯm ksp 'sixty (shekels of) silver' (CAT 2.26:20–21; Huehnergard 2012, 49), the form Heb. šiššîm keeps. NA is the sign counted, as in NA 2 (HT 64), NA 2½ (HT 154c), NA 8 (ARKH 1b) and the roundel KN Wc 42 NA O; it stands where RO stands on PH Wc 39 JA-DI RO. Weak point: the Phaistos roundels write counts as numerals (PH Wc 41 VIN 1½), and no other spells one out. One attestation. Cf. TI-DA-TA, ṯidṯīt- 'sixth', from the same root.

entries.meaning: door, doorway

cognates.Akkadian: daltu

entries.note: HT 34 .1 DA-JU-TE · SI-*516 ·, the header of a grain tablet with E · GRA 200 and KI-RO 30. With JU at the proposed value lu, DA-JU-TE writes d-l-t: Ugaritic dlt /daltu/ 'door' (Huehnergard 2012, 41), BH dēlet, Akk. daltu. A header in first position names a location or distribution point: the door, doorway. One attestation.

entries.meaning: jar, jug (liquid container)

cognates.Ugaritic: kd "jar; measure of capacity for liquids" (DULAT 424); syll. DUG ka-du-ma 'jars' (GlOS 1, 301)
cognates.Akkadian: kandu "a container of earthenware or silver, mainly for wine", NB, West Semitic word (CAD K 148)
cognates.Greek: κάδος 'jug, pitcher', Lat. cadus, borrowed from Semitic kd, chiefly for wine (Rendsburg 2026, 213)

entries.note: ZA 15b: KA-DI · VIN 3, then KU-RO VIN 78. ZA 4a: KA-DI 3, the last entry of the list, after E-*82 50. Ug. kd 'jar; liquid measure' (DULAT 424), Heb. kad (Gen 24:14), Akk. kandu, a wine container, a West Semitic word (CAD K 148). KA-DI writes kadd-, the geminate unmarked. Rival on ZA 4a: a personal name among the list's entries. Two attestations, both Zakros.

entries.meaning: reed, cane; rival lapis lazuli

cognates.Ugaritic: qn 'cane; arrow'; lapis lazuli is ỉqnủ, var. qnỉm (KTU 2.73:7) (GlOS 1, 19, 348)
cognates.Hebrew: qāneh קָנֶה "reed, cane, measuring rod" (Exod 30:23, Ezek 40:3)
cognates.Akkadian: qanû "reed, cane"

entries.note: KH 47: QA-NE 6 in a commodity context, which favours a commodity over a name; Khania is a western Cretan port with strong trade, and either imported lapis or local cane suits its accounts. Ug. qn has two senses: 'reed, cane', √q-n-y, qanē, BH qāneh קָנֶה 'reed, measuring rod', the source of 'cane' and 'canon'; and 'lapis lazuli', a sense of Ugaritic alone. KA-NA, at the head of the HT 23a aromatics ledger and on HT 123+124b, is the same word with K for q, so the word stands at two sites, and the aromatics ledger favours the cane there over the stone.

entries.meaning: fruit
entries.note: Logogram *322 on the Khania roundels KH Wc 2026, 2027 and 2098, alone, with no numeral: a commodity, read as fruit, Heb. pərî 'fruit' (HALOT 967). The roundel sign faintly resembles Linear B *158 (Schoep 2002, 91). HT 11a *322-RI is another sign (GORILA I 23; III 124, 141). Weak point: a logogram has no spelling, so nothing in the script carries pir-. Three attestations.

entries.meaning: a party receiving grain (name or place)

cognates.Akkadian: kaddu "lid, cover"

entries.note: HT 40: NU-DU-*331 · TE · GRA 207 / KI-DA-TA · GRA 134 / KU-RO; KI-DA-TA holds the slot of NU-DU-*331, a party, with its own GRA entry. HT 27a .4 KI-DA-[, broken after DA, where GORILA prefers KI-DA-TẸ[ (GORILA I 49), is a damaged second witness. Rival: kaddat 'jar' (Ug. kd, a jar and a measure for liquids, ca. 22 l, DULAT 424), which leaves KI for ka unexplained and does not fit a grain entry.

entries.meaning: kunāšu 'emmer wheat' (logographic abbreviation)
entries.note: GRA with the KU adjunct, 7 tokens on three Haghia Triada tablets: HT 61 MI-TI · GRA+KU 6, HT 128a WA-TU-MA-RE GRA+KU 12 and twice more, beside GRA+PA as a distinct grain subtype, and HT 128b. KU, the onset of kunāšu 'emmer' (CAD K 536), written in full as KU-NI-SU, Nuzi ku-ni-šu. The Ugarit polyglot gives Akkadian ku-na]-šu beside Hurrian ut-te and Ugaritic ku-sú-mu (GlOS 1, 323). See KU-NI-SU.

entries.meaning: pressed oil (ʿuṣār)

cognates.Arabic: ʿaṣara 'he pressed it so as to force out its juice, honey, oil' (Lane 2061); ʿuṣārat, coll. ʿuṣār, 'expressed juice' (Lane 2062)
cognates.Aramaic: Syriac ʿṣar 'tread, press out; crush' (Payne Smith 423); JArm. maʿṣartā 'press' (Tg. Ps.-J. Num 18:27)

entries.note: OLE with the adjunct U, 22 tokens on 13 documents from Haghia Triada and Tylissos (TY 3a): a distinct oil subtype. ʿuṣār 'pressed (oil)', √ʿ-ṣ-r: Arb. ʿaṣara 'he pressed it so as to force out its juice, sirup, honey, oil' (Lane 2061), and ʿuṣārat, coll. ʿuṣār, 'expressed juice… of things having oil or sirup or honey' (Lane 2062), the u that U writes; Syr. ʿṣar 'tread, press out' (Payne Smith 423); JArm. maʿṣartā 'press' (Tg. Ps.-J. Num 18:27). The ʿ goes unwritten, as in E. Weak point: the noun ʿuṣār is Arabic.

entries.meaning: ṭuhūru 'purified/ritually clean oil'

cognates.Ugaritic: ṭhr 'pure'; syll. ṭu-ú-ru = Akk. ellu 'pure', h unwritten (GlOS 2, 307)

entries.note: HT 23a: five entries at the same fraction under KA-NA (*308, OLE+NE, OLE+TU, OLE+RI, MI+JA+RU); also HT 28a and TY 3a (OLE+TU 1). The OLE ideogram with the TU adjunct, TU the initial of ṭuhūru 'purified': Ug. ṭhr /ṭuhūru/ 'pure' (Huehnergard 2012, 45), Heb. ṭāhôr; Linear A writes √ṭ-h-r in TU-*21F-RI-NA ṭuhārīna (HT 129). Cf. *OLIV+TU (HT 50a, HT 101, HT 116a). Three attestations.

entries.meaning: kor (dry measure); rival 'ram'

cognates.Akkadian: kurru A 'a measure of capacity' (CAD K 564)
cognates.Hebrew: kōr 'kor, dry or liquid measure', šəlōšîm kōr sōlet 'thirty kor of fine flour' (1 Kgs 5:2; HALOT 496); kar 'ram' (HALOT 496), the rival

entries.note: HT 23a .5 · KO-RU 1, the last entry of side a after SI+ME 10, in a list of commodities with quantities (GORILA I 41). Akkadian kurru A 'a measure of capacity' (CAD K 564), Hebrew kōr (HALOT 496; 1 Kgs 5:2). Rival: Hebrew kar 'ram' (HALOT 496; Isa 16:1). One witness.

entries.meaning: mixed wine (wine-section heading); rival 'must'

cognates.Ugaritic: msk 'mixture, mixed wine, mixed drink', paired with yn 'wine' (DULAT 575)
cognates.Hebrew: mesek 'spiced drink', wəyayin ḥāmar mālēʾ mesek 'and the wine foams, full of mixture' (Ps 75:9; HALOT 605)

entries.note: ZA 15a .3 ME VIN, two separate signs after I-TI-NI-SA 10, no numeral: it heads the second section of the wine list, as SA VIN heads the first (GORILA III 182–183). ME as the onset of Ugaritic msk 'mixture, mixed wine' (DULAT 575; KTU 1.19 IV 61, // yn), Hebrew mesek (HALOT 605; Ps 75:9). VIN takes single-sign qualifiers elsewhere (VIN+RA, VIN+KA, VIN+TE, VIN+WA). Rival: mrṯ 'must' (DULAT 571–572). One witness.

entries.meaning: spiced wine (Hebrew yayin hāreqaḥ); rival raḥṣu 'washed wine'

cognates.Hebrew: yayin hāreqaḥ 'spiced wine', Song 8:2 (HALOT 409); reqaḥ 'spice mixture' (HALOT 1290)
cognates.Akkadian: ruqqû adj. 'perfumed (oil)' (CAD R 420)

entries.note: VIN with the adjunct RA: KE Zb 5, ZA 15b, ZA 6b and the doubtful seal CR Zg 3. Beside plain VIN on ZA 15b (KU-RO VIN 78, VIN+RA 17) it is a distinct wine category, and ZA 6b sets VIN+RA 40 against VIN+KA 10. RA writes the ra- of raqḥ 'spiced', Hebrew yayin hāreqaḥ 'spiced wine' (Song 8:2; HALOT 409): the wine of the r-q-ḥ series with OLE+RI riqqu 'perfumed oil', *401 ruqqû and RO-QA rōqaḥ. Rival: raḥṣu 'washed, filtered' (√r-ḥ-ṣ; Ug. rḥṣ, Heb. rāḥaṣ). Four attestations.

entries.meaning: priest(s) (personnel category, ligatured onset abbreviation)
entries.note: HT 127b KI+MU 15, after VIR+*313c 24 and before *301 11, with an erased KI+MU 14, KU-RO 292, and HT 26b KI+MU 12, after KA-U-ZU-NI 4: a category label on personnel registers. A two-sign onset abbreviation of kumru 'priest' (√k-m-r): Akk. kumru 'a priest' (CAD K 534), Old Syrian kamr, kumr 'a priest' (GlOS 1, 309), Emar ka-ma-ri 'priests' (Pentiuc 2001, 95), Heb. kōmer (HALOT 482). Weak point: the one fuller spelling, HT 96a ]KU-MA-RO, is broken before KU. Two attestations.
entries.source: di Mino; Pentiuc 2001; GlOS 1; CAD K; HALOT

entries.meaning: May he cover you (f. pl.)! (3ms G imperfect yaksī + 2fp object suffix -kin; NU writes the final nasal, as in -U-TI-NU)

cognates.Hebrew: kāsā (כָּסָה) 'to cover' (Jonah 3:6 wayekas śaq—same root with ashes in penitential context)
cognates.Amorite: Yaksiy-ʾIl, with the prefix form yaksiy (Gelb 1980, nos. 22, 2918); Mari ia-ak-sí-ia (GlOS 1, 325)
cognates.Akkadian: kasû 'to bind, cover'

entries.note: ARKH Zf 9, a bronze votive object from Arkhanes: JA-KI-SI-KI-NU · MI-DA-RU-RA ·, the first of two words. yaksīkin 'May he cover you (women)!': ya-, the 3ms prefix, the G-stem imperfect *yaksī of √k-s-y 'to cover', a III-weak root, and -kin, the 2fp object suffix, NU writing the final nasal. 'Cover' takes a second object, the covering, MI-DA-RU-RA. Jonah 3:6 וַיְכַ֣ס שַׂ֔ק וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב עַל־הָאֵֽפֶר 'he covered himself with sackcloth and sat in the ashes' joins √k-s-y and ashes in penitence before God, and Jonah 3:8 וְיִתְכַּסּ֣וּ שַׂקִּ֗ים 'let them cover themselves with sackcloth' has the Hithpael (tD) of the same root. One attestation. See MI-DA-RU-RA and MI-KI-SE-NA.

entries.meaning: dust, ashes, dry earth (second accusative after √k-s-y 'cover')

cognates.Emar: ma-da-ri 'field', the etymon of Syriac mdr 'soil, dust' (Pentiuc 2001, 117; GlOS 2, 30)

entries.note: ARKH Zf 9 (Arkhanes, a bronze votive object), word 2 of JA-KI-SI-KI-NU <> MI-DA-RU-RA; RILA rereads GORILA's MI-DA-MA-RA₂, sign 3 as RU (AB 26) and sign 4 as RA (AB 27). midrara 'dust, ashes', the second accusative after JA-KI-SI-KI-NU *yaksīkīnū 'May he cover you!': 'May he cover you with dust and ashes!' 'Cover, clothe' takes two accusatives, person and covering (Fischer 2002, §374a: albasanī ṯiyābahu 'He clothed me in his garments'), so the -a has its governor; the final RA writes either that accusative -a on a root-final r, *midr-a, or the geminate rr of an intensive *midrar-. Ashes and dust serve penance and purification, both fit for a votive bronze: sitting in ashes (Jonah 3:6), the red heifer's ashes (Num 19:17), dust on the head in mourning (Job 2:12), ashes in lament (2 Sam 13:19), rolling in ashes, בָּאֵפֶר יִתְפַּלָּשׁוּ (Ezek 27:30), sackcloth and ashes, וַיִּלְבַּשׁ שַׂק וָאֵפֶר (Esth 4:1), Abraham's עָפָר וָאֵפֶר 'dust and ashes' (Gen 18:27), and פְּאֵר תַּחַת אֵפֶר 'beauty instead of ashes' (Isa 61:3). One attestation.

entries.meaning: My Giver / My Athena—1cs possessive on divine epithet (√y-t-n 'to give' + -ya 'my')

cognates.Linear B: a-ta-na-po-ti-ni-ja, KN V 52.1, beside e-na-wa-ri-jo, pa-ja-wo-ne, po-se-da[-o-ne] (DMic I, s.v.)—Athena Potnia
cognates.Ugaritic: ytn 'give'; names ytn Yatanu, mlkytn Milki-Yatanu (Kinlaw 1967, 135, 81), bʿltn (GlOS 2, 78); 1cs possessive -y: ʾaby 'my father,' ʾumy 'my mother' (Huehnergard 2012)

entries.note: THE Zb 6, a clay vessel from Thera, its one word: A-TA-NA ʾAtanat 'She-who-gives', the etymon of Athena (see A-TA-NA-TE), + -ya 'my', the 1cs suffix of PU₂-RE-JA burē(t)yā 'my Creatress'. The stem stands at two sites: A-TA-NA-TE (ZA 10a; ZA 9 A-TA-NA-[TE], GORILA III 166–167) and A-TA-NA-JE (Thera). At Knossos Athena heads KN V 52.1 among the gods, a-ta-na-po-ti-ni-ja beside Enyalios, Paiawon and Poseidon. At Ugarit the god is the one who gives, Milki-Yatanu 'Milku has given' (mlkytn, son of a priest of Baal; Kinlaw 1967, 81), and the verb stands alone as a name, Yatanu (ytn); Alalakh has nādin 'giver' as a name. √y-t-n is the Ugaritic and Phoenician form. One attestation.
entries.source: di Mino; DMic I; Kinlaw 1967; GlOS 2

entries.meaning: sesame (seed-spice commodity)

cognates.Akkadian: šamaššammū (šamšamū) 'the principal oleiferous plant and its seed' (CAD Š/1 301)
cognates.Linear B: sa-sa-ma (MY Ge 602, Mycenae spice series)

entries.note: HT 23a, a ledger of cyperus, oils and wine: SA-SA-ME ¹⁄₁₆, after *21F-RI-TU-QA ¹⁄₁₆. The second SA is dotted, and GORILA I 41 records SA [units] ME as a less satisfactory reading. šašam- 'sesame', the reduplicated š-š-m: Akk. šamaššammū (CAD Š/1 301), Ug. ššmn 'sesame' with the afformative -n (DULAT 834), Linear B sa-sa-ma σάσαμα on the Mycenae Ge tablets of aromatic plants, beside ku-mi-no 'cumin' (DMic II 284), as KU-MI-NA stands in Linear A. Rival: flax and its seed, CAD's sense of šamaššammū, 'the principal oleiferous plant, probably flax' (CAD Š/1 301). One attestation.
entries.source: di Mino; GORILA I; CAD Š/1; DULAT; DMic II

entries.meaning: aromatic reed, sweet cane (commodity; spelling variant of QA-NE)

cognates.Eblaite: GIŠ.GI = ga-nu-um 'reed', q in the G-series (GlOS 1, 348)
cognates.Hebrew: qāneh קָנֶה 'reed, cane' — qəneh-bośem 'aromatic cane' Exod 30:23, anointing-oil ingredient
cognates.Akkadian: qanû 'reed'
cognates.Linear B: cf. ko-no (σχοῖνος 'aromatic rush') — semantic parallel in Mycenaean spice accounting

entries.note: HT 23a: KA-NA heads an aromatics ledger (CYP, oil subtypes, VIN and SA-SA-ME 'sesame'), the ground for Heb. qāneh 'reed' and qəneh-bośem 'sweet cane'. A spelling of QA-NE (KH 47), with KA for q (Gordon 1966, §§4, 76). On HT 123+124b the central lacuna follows it, and the tablet shows the word recurring in the accounts without fixing the product. Rival: lapis lazuli, a homograph (Ugaritic ỉqnủ, var. qnỉm, from Akk. uqnû).

entries.meaning: the best of beer (compound; ṭūb 'the best of' + dida 'beer extract')

cognates.Hebrew: ṭûb 'the best things of a place, country or person' (Gen 45:18, 20, 23) (HALOT 372)
cognates.Amorite: di-du-um // Akk. billatum, a beer of the second kind, KAŠ.Ú.SA, read dida (George and Krebernik 2022, 120)
cognates.Akkadian: billatu, KAŠ.Ú.SA, a dry mixture for beer, perhaps the sweetwort; KAŠ.Ú.SA SIG₅ 'fine b.', among spices, condiments and fruit for the royal banquet (Iraq 14 43:122); bil-lat SIG₅-tim (CAD B 226–228)

entries.note: HT 123+124b .3–4 TU-PA-DI-DA J+L2, whole and undotted, on a face written over an erasure, after *188-DU 10 and before KA-NẠ[ (GORILA I 213). ṭūb 'the best of' in construct, PA for b, before dida, the beer extract of KAŠ.Ú.SA: fine billatu, KAŠ.Ú.SA SIG₅, as in Akkadian (CAD B 226, 228). A product among the *188 and KA-NA entries, measured in fractions. One attestation. Cf. KA-NA.
entries.source: di Mino; HALOT; George and Krebernik 2022; CAD B

entries.meaning: the stall, storehouse

cognates.Akkadian: abūsu 'storehouse', pl. abūsātu, ubsātu (CAD A/1 92); bēl abūsi 'overseer of the storehouse', Ras Shamra (CAD A/1 93)

entries.note: HT 10a U-*325-ZA 4 and U-*325-ZA 14, two issues; HT 85a U-*325-ZA 6 among the men under A-DU, beside DA-RI-DA and DA-RE, the pattern of a standing unit. With *325 read bu, and PS *s = [ts] taking the Z-series, ʾubūs(a) 'the stall, storehouse': Akk. abūsu 'storehouse', plural abūsātu and ubsātu (CAD A/1 92); the U-/A- onset against A-*325-ZA (PE 2) matches ubsātu beside abūsātu. At Ras Shamra a bēl abūsi 'overseer of the storehouse' receives goods (RS 17.382+:45; CAD A/1 93). Rival: *325 = /ḫu/, ʾuḫuzza(t) 'holding' (Heb. ʾăḥuzzâ, HALOT 32), with ZA for PS *ḏ. Two attestations. See A-*325-ZA.
entries.source: di Mino; CAD A/1; HALOT; GlOS 1

entries.meaning: the stall, storehouse
entries.cognates: see U-*325-ZA
entries.note: PE 2, a list in fractions: RU-PI ⅓, SA-*305-MI 1⅛, A-*325-ZA ¼, A-RI-PA ¼, QA-QA-DA ½, TO-ME ⅓, TO-*49-RE 1. ʾabūs(a) 'the stall, storehouse', Akk. abūsu 'storehouse', pl. abūsātu and ubsātu (CAD A/1 92), with *325 read bu: A-*325-ZA spells ʾabūs- sign for sign, the PS *s, pronounced [ts], taking the Z-series. A variant of U-*325-ZA, as Akk. abūsātu beside ubsātu. One attestation. See U-*325-ZA.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'palm'

cognates.Amorite: TAMAR-U /ta-ma-ru/, a one-element personal name; also ŠUM-U*TAMAR and ŠUM-U*TAMAR-U (Gelb 1980, nos. 6027, 5716, 5715)
cognates.Hebrew: tōmer תֹּמֶר masculine palm (Judges 4:5, the Palm of Deborah) / tāmār תָּמָר feminine name
cognates.Ugaritic: syllabic /tamaru/ 'date palm' proposed for Ug. 5 137 (Huehnergard 2008, nos. 175, TMR); tmr, a personal name (GlOS 2, 298)
cognates.Mari: qí-iš-ti-ᵈta-ma-ru Qišti-Tamaru, with the DN Tamaru (GlOS 2, 298)

entries.note: In the bronze-bowl scriptio continua A-RA-KO-KU-QA-WA-SA-TO-MA-RO-AU-TA-DE-PO-NI-ZA. A palm name of the Bronze Age type: Amorite Tamar-u (Gelb 1980, no. 6027), Ugaritic tmr 'date palm' (GlOS 2, 298), Hebrew Tāmār (Gen 38; 2 Sam 13). TO writes the ō of Hebrew tōmer 'palm' (Judg 4:5); final O is the support vowel of coda r. Weak point: GORILA prints no divider in the sixteen signs, and no sequence beside TO-MA-RO recurs as a word elsewhere, so the word boundary rests on the parse. One attestation. See TO-MI-RE.

entries.meaning: linen (material adjectival base in jar labels)

cognates.Akkadian: kitûm/kitinnû 'linen'
cognates.Greek: χιτών via LB ki-to, from Ug. ktn (Rendsburg 2026, 214); here fully vocalized

entries.note: PE Zb 3, a pithos label: KI-TA-NA-SI-JA-SE, kitāna šī-yāṣē pidr-qê 'linen which goes out, a qê-measure of fat'. SI-JA-SE šī-yāṣē, the relative with the 3ms imperfect of √y-ṣ-ʾ 'to go out', marks goods for issue, as in A-NA-NU-SI-JA-SE (HT Zb 159) on another stem. Linear B ki-to, χιτών, comes from the same ktn. KI-TA-NI-TE kitānit 'linen robe, linen cloth' (PK Zb 21) is its -t derivative.

entries.meaning: linen robe, linen cloth

cognates.Akkadian: kitītu, var. kitintu "linen robe" (eBL kitītu I); kitû "flax, linen"

entries.note: PK Zb 21, a pithos incised before firing (Building 7, MM IIIB–LM IA). A -t derivative of KI-TA-NA (PE Zb 3 KI-TA-NA-SI-JA-SE; KH 60 RA-KI-TA-NA-SI); the reading, and the recurrence of KI-TA-N-, follow Davis (Kadmos 47, 2008, 1–2, apud Younger, Linear A Texts, Other Texts: Palaikastro). Unshifted ā: the pre-Canaanite form of Heb. kuttōnet, kətōnet 'tunic' (HALOT 505). As a jar label, the stored linen goods. Rival: ME-WI-TA-NI-TE, cf. HT Wc 3004a–3005a (Driessen 1991, apud Younger).
entries.source: di Mino; Younger, Linear A Texts; HALOT

entries.meaning: flask, vial (small libation/oil vessel)

cognates.Hebrew: pak פַּךְ 'flask, vial' — pak ha-šemen, the anointing-oil flask (1 Sam 10:1; 2 Kgs 9:1-3)
cognates.Ugaritic: bk rb 'a large vessel' (KTU 1.3 I 12), in the passage that pairs ks // krpn

entries.note: Two spellings of one vessel word. PU-KO stands alone on the HT 31 vessel inventory directly before *410-VS, the only vessel on the tablet without a name ligatured to its sign. PA-KU (KN Zc 6, an inked cup, written as one unit after DA-KI-TI) is a segment of continuous writing on a dedicatory object, where an oil-vial word fits: Hebrew pak 'flask' (HALOT 926), the vessel of royal anointing (1 Sam 10:1; 2 Kgs 9:1–3). PU-KO pukku keeps the older vowel that Hebrew pak lost after the labial; -KO writes final -ku, as -RO does in KU-RO. Ugaritic bk rb 'a large vessel' (KTU 1.3 I 12) stands in the same passage as krpn, the counterpart of HT 31's KA-RO-PA₃. Rival: bk is commonly compared with Greek βῖκος, and Smith and Pitard (2009, 108) call it 'apparently an Indo-European Kulturwort'.
entries.source: di Mino; HALOT; Smith and Pitard 2009

entries.meaning: share(s), portion

cognates.Hebrew: bad 'part, portion'; bad bəbad 'in equal portions' (Ex 30:34; HALOT 108)

entries.note: KH 88, a list headed QA-NU-MA · *21F-*118 ḥiṭṭa 'wheat', with NI figs 10 before PU-DE 8. buddē 'share(s)', PS *bud- 'distribute, share out' (semitic_roots 519): Arab. budd, budda 'a lot, share, portion' (Lane 161), the u after the labial as PU writes it; Heb. bad 'part, portion', bad bəbad 'in equal portions' (Ex 30:34; HALOT 108). DE writes plain d. A share follows the wheat and figs. One attestation.

entries.meaning: the (wine-)vat, a pressing unit (allocation heading); rival 'madder'

cognates.Hebrew: pûrâ (פּוּרָה) 'wine-press' (BDB 807), 'tub, trough' (HALOT 920); pûrâ dāraktî lᵉbaddî 'I have trodden the vat alone' (Isa 63:3), // gat (Isa 63:2); Hag 2:16

entries.note: More exactly PU-*131A. PU as the onset of pûrâ, VIN as its classifier, as ME VIN mesek. HT 123+124a: PU-*131A · OLIV 31½, *308 8¾, KI-RO, the second of four parties beside KI-TA-I gittī 'of the press', SA-RU and DA-TU; each returns pressed oil at about a quarter of its olives, so the parties are pressing units, and gat and pûrâ are the pair of Isa 63:2–3. HT 14: PU-VIN · TE · GRA 30, two oils, *304, OLIV, beside A-PU₂-NA-DU; PU is written over an erased sign (GORILA I 29). Rival: Ug. pwt 'madder' (DULAT 678), Heb. PN Puwwāh (Gen 46:13), with VIN for wa as VIN+WA on HT 27b.

entries.meaning: garlic (logographic abbreviation)

cognates.Akkadian: šūmū 'garlic' (CAD Š/3 298)
cognates.Hebrew: šûmîm 'garlic', among the foods of Egypt, Num 11:5 (HALOT 1443)

entries.note: KH 91, a ration list: GRA 1, VIN[, *316 1 13/20, ZU[ ]≈ ⅙, TU ¹⁄₁₆, NI[, *401+RU ¹⁄₁₆, *401+RA[. ZU writes ṯu and abbreviates ṯūm 'garlic': Arab. ṯūm, Heb. šûmîm 'garlic' (Num 11:5; HALOT 1443), Akk. šumû (CAD Š/3 298). In the personnel lists HT 63, HT 66 and HT 97a ZU is a single-sign abbreviation beside DI, JU and KI (Montecchi 2008, 318). Weak point: GORILA marks a break after ZU on KH 91, where SigLA sets the fraction straight after it.
entries.source: di Mino; HALOT; CAD Š/3; Lane

entries.meaning: cyperus, aromatic sedge (commodity logogram)

cognates.Akkadian: suādu 'an aromatic plant, Cyperus esculentus', also suʾādu, sumādu (CAD S 338)

entries.note: Cyperus commodity logogram, its principal distribution at Khania: 35 plain and 28 in the fraction ligatures CYP+D and CYP+E. The sign continues as the Linear B CYPERUS ideogram, associated with ku-pa-ro. On HT 89 it opens the commodity section after the total, at 2 + A732. At Khania it keeps company with aromatics: myrrh (MI+JA+RU), *401+RU and fine oil (OLE+TA).

entries.meaning: tripod cauldron (vessel logogram)
entries.note: A hemispherical bowl on three legs with side handles, the same on all 15 Khania roundels (KH Wc 2008–2024, 2079), each a sealed receipt bearing this sign alone: a bronze-vessel receipt series of the harbour town. Cf. LB *201 TRIPOD, ti-ri-po-de (PY Ta 641).

entries.meaning: Healer of Jubilation (Eshmun epithet)

cognates.Ugaritic: rpu 'healer', divine ancestor and eponymous god (DULAT 731); rnn 'to shout', åp ån årnn ql 'then let me myself shout' (KTU 1.82:6; DULAT 731)
cognates.Amorite: rāpiʾ 'healer', a DN (Gelb 1980, §0.7); RA-BI-U₂-UM, RA-BI-A-TUM (nos. 5243, 5237)
cognates.Hebrew: rōpʾekā (רֹפְאֶךָ) 'your healer', kî ʾănî YHWH rōpʾekā 'for I am YHWH your healer' (Exod 15:26); wattirpāʾēnî 'and you healed me' (Ps 30:3); rinnâ 'joyful cry' (Ps 30:6)

entries.note: ZA Zb 3 .2 A-TA-I-*301-DE-KA · A-RE-PI-RE-NA · TI-TI-KU, a healer's title on the pithos that offers wine to A-SA-MU-NE Eshmun, the healing god. Vocative ʾa-, the east-Cretan form of yā, as A-DI-KI-TE-TE (di Mino, Ya Diktu, 20), then rāpiʾ 'healer' (√r-p-ʾ) and rinnā 'joyful cry' (√r-n-n), participle and genitive in one word as KA-NI-JA-MI qāniy-yammi. It names the god whom -DE-KA addresses, as rōpʾekā 'your healer' names YHWH (Exod 15:26); Ps 30:3 and 30:6 join the two roots. RE-PI is written over an erased PI, and damage crosses PI (GORILA IV 113). Rival: Gordon (1975, 153) reads MA for PI: re-ma-re-na, Aramaic mārēnā 'our lord'. One witness. See A-RI-PA, RP-33-Y, RU-PI and RA-NA-TU-SU.
entries.source: di Mino; Gelb 1980; DULAT; GORILA IV; Gordon 1975

entries.meaning: the tied, sealed (packet)
entries.note: HT 23a, K-fraction entry between E 17 and sesame in an aromatics ledger; RI dotted (GORILA I 41). RI-TU-QA from √r-t-q 'to tie, bind': Ug. rtq (DULAT 737); Heb. ruttəqû (Nah 3:10), rətuqôt (Isa 40:19); Ar. ratq (Q 21:30). *21F the article ha-, as Punic writes the article h- or ʾ- (Krahmalkov 2000, 154). Weak point: the only article written *21F; no bare RI-TU-QA. One attestation.

entries.meaning: outpouring, pouring-out—(header) disbursed; (libation) may it be poured
entries.cognates: Ug. √n-t-k "pour out" (KTU 1.14 I 28-30); Heb. נָתַךְ nātak—nifal nittak (Exod 9:33, 2 Chr 34:25), Hiphil hittīkū "they disbursed" (2 Kgs 22:9), Hiphil hitaktī (Ezek 22:20-22); Akk. natāku "drip"
entries.note: HT 35 and ZA Zb 3. On HT 35 it heads a list in which every commodity pours, cyperus, myrrh, three grades of oil, butter and wine, all in fractional liquid measures, the pouring counterpart of the headers for given, received and counted. On ZA Zb 3 it closes the wine-libation formula (wine 32, ʾaššē fire-offering, the √n-w-y formula word, the epithet of Eshmun), as a libation should close. √n-t-k 'to pour out, forth', the tt the assimilated nun, written with the doubled TI: Ug. tntkn udmʿth km ṯqlm arṣh 'his tears pour out like shekels to the ground' (KTU 1.14 I 28–30); Heb. nifal nittak of rain (Exod 9:33), wrath (2 Chr 34:25) and molten metal (Ezek 22:20–22); Akk. natāku 'drip', with tabāku 'pour out' the standard verb of disbursement. 2 Kgs 22:9 הִתִּיכוּ hittīkū, Hiphil 3cp with the nun assimilated, 'your servants have disbursed the silver found in the house', has the disbursement sense on a financial report and the same tt. Either the noun tittuk(u) 'outpouring' or the G imperfect tittōk 'may it be poured'; both fit both slots. Rival: a toponym on ZA Zb 3, 'from Tittiku'. See I-TI-TI-KU-NI.

entries.meaning: which have been poured out—disbursed (derived-stem header); rival a heading name

cognates.Ugaritic: ntk to pour out, forth (base form TI-TI-KU)
cognates.Hebrew: hittiku they disbursed (2 Kgs 22:9, n-t-k Hiphil 3cp); paragogic nun: Job 19:2 (energic -nn- + 1cs -i)

entries.note: HT 96a: I-TI-TI-KU-NI · A-PA-RA-NE · A-*123-TE ·, the heading of a grain list (SI-MI-TA GRA 5, RU-SA 4, PI-TA-RA 1). (y)ittatkūni 'which have been poured out', disbursed: I- the relative or the 3ms yi-, TI-TI-KU the Nt stem of √n-t-k 'pour out', the n assimilated in the geminate tt, and -NI the energic -n(n), as Ugaritic yqtln /yaqtulan(na)/ (Huehnergard 2012, 57). The base TI-TI-KU heads HT 35. Rivals: -NI the 1cs object or dative suffix, as Amarna -ni on verbs, often through the ventive -anni (Rainey 1996, I:72–74, II:264); a heading name. Hebrew uses the Hiphil of silver, 'to melt down, or to throw away (money)' (2 Kgs 22:9; HALOT 733). Weak point: no text uses n-t-k of grain or figs, which HT 96a issues. One attestation.

entries.meaning: gift

cognates.Hebrew: mattat 'gift' < *mattant (1 Kgs 13:7; Prov 25:14; Eccl 3:13; 5:18; Ezek 46:5, 11; HALOT 656)
cognates.Amorite: MATAN-I, MA-AT-TA-NI (Gelb 1980, no. 4445); Tuttul ma-ta-an 'Gift' (Buck 2018, 342)

entries.note: HT Zd 155 and HT Zd 157, each time right before A319 with no divider before MA; the cut rests on the ending the two graffiti share (Duhoux 1978, §29 A6). Heb. mattat 'gift' < *mattant, Ph. mtt (HALOT 656). MA-TI-TI writes the i-grade *mattint- > mattitt-, the final TI a dead vowel. WI-JA-SU on HT Zd 157 and NA-MA Naʿma on HT Zd 155 name the recipient. The rival √š-m-ṭ 'release' parse needs TI-TI to write a geminate. See NA-TU-*301-NE.
entries.source: di Mino; Pagan 1998; Gelb 1980; Buck 2018; GlOS 2

entries.meaning: Naʿma 'Grace' (personal name)

cognates.Eblaite: na-ma, PN (ARET 15 25 r. ii 12); na-ma-da-mu naʿma-Damu 'grace of Damu' (Pagan 1998, row 3812); PNN na-a-ma, na-ma-(DN) (DULAT 605)
cognates.Hebrew: Naʿămāh, PN (Gen 4:22; 1 Kgs 14:21, 31; 2 Chr 12:13); a town of Judah (Josh 15:41)
cognates.Amorite: NAʿM-AN-U, NA-AḪ-MA-NU (Gelb 1980, no. 4890); NAʿM-I, NA-AḪ-MI (no. 4893)

entries.note: HT Zd 155 A-JU · NA-MA-MA-TI-TI-A319 (GORILA IV 130–131): NA-MA stands before MA-TI-TI-A319 where WI-JA-SU stands on HT Zd 157, the name of the party to the gift. Naʿma, √n-ʿ-m 'grace', the ʿ unwritten as in TA-NA-MA-JE and DU-NE-MI. Ebla writes the same name na-ma (ARET 15 25 r. ii 12), short for names such as na-ma-da-mu naʿma-Damu 'grace of Damu' (Pagan 1998, row 3812); Hebrew has Naʿămāh (Gen 4:22; 1 Kgs 14:21). Weak point: the stucco is worn at the first MA, and GORILA's second transcription dots the second. Rival: nʿm 'good, of fine quality', as Ugaritic qn nʿm 'cane of good quality' (KTU 4.247:29; DULAT 605), but a Semitic attributive follows its noun, and NA-MA precedes MA-TI-TI. One attestation. Cf. TA-NA-MA-JE, DU-NE-MI.
entries.source: di Mino; DULAT; Pagan 1998; Kinlaw 1967; Gelb 1980

entries.meaning: Protector of the olive trees (personal name; matiʿ 'protector' + zayt 'olive tree'); rival Hurrian mat-

cognates.Amorite: MTʿ 'to protect': jamattiʿ, mataʿa, matiʿum (Gelb 1980, 25); names MATI+ʾIL, MA-TI-DINGIR; MATI+ʾAHL-I, MA-TI-IA-LI; MATI+TIWR-UM, MA-TI-TI-RUM (Gelb 1980, nos. 4568, 4570, 4573)
cognates.Hebrew: zayit 'olive tree, olive' (HALOT 268); Zêtān, a man of Benjamin, 'who has dealings with olive trees' (1 Chr 7:10; HALOT 269)

entries.note: PK 1 .7 MA-TI-ZA-I-TE 1, whole and undotted, in a roster of names each counted 1, in the closing MA- group with MA-TE-TI and MA-KA-I-TA (GORILA I 281). MA-TI matiʿ 'protector', the ʿ unwritten, spelt MA-TI- as in the Amorite names Matiʿ-ʾIl, Matiʿ-ʾAhli and Matiʿ-Tiwrum (Gelb 1980, nos. 4568, 4570, 4573); ZA-I-TE zayt 'olive tree', I the glide y, the noun that writes the OLIV logogram. Matiʿ with a noun, as Matiʿ-ʾAhli. Rival: Hurrian mat- (NPN 233–234: Matip-tešup, Mat-teja), which leaves ZA-I unread. Ugaritic tmtʕ stands under |m-t-ʕ| 'to take away; to help, rescue', with mātiʕ 'helper, saviour' in ma-ti-DINGIR (GlOS 2, 58). Weak point: no Matiʿ-zayt name is attested. One attestation. Cf. MA-KA-I-TA.

entries.meaning: My kinsman knows (sentence name)

cognates.Eblaite: ʿamm-ī-ʾIl 'ʾIl is my uncle'; yādaʿ-ʾabu 'father knows' (Pagan 1998, rows 718, 538)
cognates.Amorite: noun-ī + dāʿ: Śamī-dāʿum, Śamšī-dāʿī; Yadaʿ-ʿammu (Gelb 1980, nos. 5450, 6272, 3172)

entries.note: ZA 10a: among personal names, quantity 1. A sentence name, ʿammī 'my kinsman', a divine epithet, with dāʿ (√y-d-ʿ 'know'): ʿAmmī-dāʿ 'My kinsman knows'. ʿammī- opens ʿAmmîšaddāy (Num 1:12) and ʿAmmînādāb (Exod 6:23); -dāʿ closes ʾĂbîdāʿ and ʾEldāʿā (Gen 25:4) and ʾElyādāʿ (2 Sam 5:16). The abī-/aḫī-/ʿammī- rotation on one base (Abinadab, Ahinadab 1 Kgs 4:14, Amminadab) sets ʿAmmī-dāʿ beside the attested ʾĂbîdāʿ. Initial ʿa- is written A. Howard tabulates the ʿAmmī + verb sentence name (ʿAmmi-yepuʿ, kings of Talhayum, at Mari, Terqa and Šeḥna), with ʾIli-yepaʿ at Alalah rotating the first element (Howard 2023, appendix). A-MI-DA-O (PH(?) 31b.5) is broken at the start, ]A-MI-DA-O (GORILA I 319). Rival: a Hurrian name (cf. MI-TA). Cf. JA-DA-SU (Yadaʿ-Šum), from the same verb. One attestation. See *306+MI.

entries.meaning: the Height (toponym of the Ramah/Ramoth type)

cognates.Hebrew: rāmâ 'height, high place' (HALOT 1240), and the town hārāmâ, Judg 4:5
cognates.Amorite: RWM 'be high': rāmum, rāmatum (Gelb AS 21, 29–30)

entries.note: Bare RU-MA-TA at HT 29 (2) and HT 99b (1, in the SI+SE FIC list); RU-MA-TA-SE on ZA 20 (3) beside DU-RE-ZA-SE: bare at home, -SE abroad. Every attestation carries a quantity: a recipient entry. rūmatā, √r-w-m 'to be high', *rūmat-, a feminine noun of place: Hebrew toponyms רוּמָה Rûmâ (2 Kgs 23:36, the u-vowel form), אֲרוּמָה ʾĂrûmâ (Judg 9:41), רָמַת Rāmat (Josh 13:26), הָרָמָתָה hā-Rāmātâ (1 Sam 1:19), רָאמֹת Rāʾmōt (Josh 20:8); Ug. rm 'to go up'. Final -A is the written vowel. Rival: *rumanth-, the Aegean name of LB o-ru-ma-to *Orumanthos (PY Cn 3.6; ethnic o-ru-ma-si-ja-jo, PY An 519.12; DMic II 50–51), cf. Ἐρύμανθος, a mountain, with the nasal before a stop that Linear A leaves unwritten. See RU-MA.

entries.meaning: man of Ušu (mainland Tyre)—origin-labeled worker

cognates.Akkadian: {uru}U₂-su₂ Usu, Amarna, EA 148:11, 148 r. 30, 149 r. 49, 150 r. 18 (ORACC aemw/amarna)
cognates.Hebrew: Ḥōsâ, a town of Asher by Tyre, wəšāb haggəbûl ḥōsâ 'and the border turned to Hosah' (Josh 19:29; HALOT 337, which sets Akkadian Uzu, Ušu beside it)

entries.note: HT 117a: a counted roster item, quantity 1 within KU-RO 10. Amarna Ušu (EA 148, 149, 150), the mainland twin of Tyre, with š written s. The reverse labels personnel by origin (DI-KI-SE 'the Diktaian', HT 117b), and U-DI-MI (ʾUdmī) stands seven lines below: Levantine workers on a Haghia Triada roster, each entered under his town. One attestation.

entries.meaning: the Udumite—man of Udum (Kirta's city), 'red (land)'

cognates.Ugaritic: udm, a town, Kirta's city (DULAT 18); udmy 'Udumite' (DULAT 19)

entries.note: HT 117a: U-DI-MI 1, the seventh of the ten men in KU-RO 10, on the list with U-SU ʾUšu (mainland Tyre); the reverse labels men by origin (DI-KI-SE, HT 117b). ʾUdmī 'the Udumite': Udum, Kirta's city, Ugaritic udm rbt 'Udum the great' (KTU 1.14 III 30), Amarna ᵘʳᵘú-du-mu (EA 256:24) (DULAT 18–19). DI writes the d of the -dm- cluster with the vowel of MI, as KI writes the k of -kr- in SU-KI-RI-TA Sukrita; Ugaritic udm, udmy. udm is *ʾudum-, the form of Hebrew ʾēdōm (UVST 275 n. 39), Edom, '? orig. the area distinguished by red soil' (HALOT 12); HALOT 16 reads Adami-nekeb as 'red (place) at the pass', with a queried Ugaritic udm. One attestation. See U-SU.

entries.meaning: flax, linseed—field-crop commodity

cognates.Akkadian: kitû 'flax, linen'

entries.note: KH 10, a Khania grain ledger (GRA 10 … A-KI-PI-E-TE GRA 90): flax beside grain, as in Ugaritic field-crop records. Ug. qṭ (I) 'flax', n. m. (DULAT 708), four times in KTU: the hippiatric prescriptions 1.71, 1.72 and 1.85 (št bln qṭ, linseed ground with mixed fodder) and 4.166:4, ḫmš mỉṣpt qṭ 'five m. of flax' in an administrative list; ḥwt qṭ (2.36:17) is a place name, qṭ (II). The Wanderwort *kito- 'flax, linen': Akk. kitû, Aram. kittānā, Sum. gada, Gk. χιτών, the Ugaritic branch with q for k. *118 at ṭa gives the emphatic the root requires. Rival: Aram. qaṭṭ- 'cucumber' (semitic_roots K0325: Syr. qaṭṭūṯā, Akk. qiššû), with ṭ for *118. Weak points: ṭa for *118 is a proposed value whose corpus test fails; QA-*118 has no number of its own, after I-PA-SA-JA ·, and the GRA 90 below belongs to A-KI-PI-E-TE.

entries.meaning: She-of-the-Bull (feminine personal/divine name)
entries.cognates: Ug. ṯr/ṯrn "bull" (KTU deity epithet, PN element); Heb. שׁוֹר šōr "ox" (< *ṯawr with interdental→sibilant); Ar. ṯawr "bull"; Ebla šu-ra, šu-ru₁₂, su-rí-a, 'bull' names (Pagan 1998, rows 4404, 4410, 4294); Euphratian šu-ra-nu, ab-du-šu-ri-im (GlOS 2, 330)
entries.note: PH 6: I-NA-WA · A-RI / I-ZU-RI-NI-TA / A-RI / I-DA-PA₃-I-SA-RI, the name governed by A-RI harrī 'mountain of'. Feminine counterpart of ZU-RI-NI-MA (KN Zb 52, masculine with mimation). I- is a prosthetic vowel (cf. I-DA-MA-TE beside DA-MA-TE); ZU-RI-NI writes the base ṯawrīn-, the bull word with relational -īn, ZU read ṯu, a proposed value: Ug. ṯr 'bull' (DULAT 916), Old Syrian ṯuwr 'bull; DN' (GlOS 2, 330). -TA is the feminine -t where the masculine has -MA. -TA is the diptote genitive of a feminine proper name after A-RI, as Ug. ḥāmiyātu ʾugarita 'the walls of Ugarit' (Huehnergard 2012, 40; Tropper 2000, §54.112) and Arb. names in -at of more than three consonants (Fischer 2002, §153). Weak point: ZU = ṯu is a proposed value. One attestation.
entries.source: di Mino; Pagan 1998; GlOS 2; Huehnergard 2012; Tropper 2000; Fischer 2002

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Eternal'; rival Arabic Dārim

cognates.Amorite: dārum 'eternity, eternal', on DWR (Gelb 1980, §0.7)
cognates.Eblaite: da-ri₂ dārī 'eternal', fem. da₅-ri₂-da dārīta; ʾila-Dārum 'Dārum is god' (Pagan 1998, rows 1471, 1507, 1591; GlOS 1, 153)
cognates.Akkadian: Old Babylonian da-ru-um 'lasting' (CAD D 117)

entries.note: HT 7b .2 DA-RU-*329 2, after *21F-TU-NE 1, both over an erasure (GORILA I 15); face a lists Iruja, Tuya and Tetu. *329 read mo: Montecchi queries A 329 = Linear B *15 mo (Montecchi 2024, 173). DA-RU- recurs in DA-RU-NE-TE (HT 98b). Rival Arabic Dārim, Safaitic drm (Harding 1971, 239). One attestation.
entries.source: di Mino; Montecchi 2024; Gelb 1980; Pagan 1998; GlOS 1; CAD D; Harding 1971

entries.meaning: Anat is everlasting (theophoric personal name); rivals Dūr-ʿAnat 'Wall of Anat', and Egyptian Neith as the second element

cognates.Amorite: dāru 'generation; lasting' (40); Šumī-dāru 'my name is lasting' (Buck 2018, 349); ʿAnat second in ʿAmmī-ʿAnat, Mut-ʿAnat, ʿAbd-ʿAnat, written ḪA-NA-AT (Gelb 1980, nos. 2132, 4857, 1844); Tuttul ʿabdu-ʿanata (Buck 2018, 320)
cognates.Akkadian: dārû 'everlasting' (CAD D 115); dūru 'wall, fortress' (CAD D 196)
cognates.Egyptian: n.t 'Neith' as the second element of personal names: sꜣ-n.t, wsr-n.t, rdj-n.t, ḥtp-n.t (PNM v6)

entries.note: HT 98b .2 DA-RU-NE-TE 1/10, after ]VIN ¾ (GORILA I 161); face a lists TA-NA-TI ¾. DA-RU dāru 'lasting' (#40), as DA-RU-*329 Dārum and Amorite Šumī-dāru 'my name is lasting' (Buck 2018, 349); -NE-TE ʿAnat (#2771), as Šum-Anati and Abdi-Anati at Ugarit (Kinlaw 1967, 111, 7). Anat is NA-TA in I-NA-TA-I and NA-TI on face a: the lost ʿa- and the e of -NE-TE are unexplained. Rivals: Dūr-ʿAnat 'Wall of Anat', as Ili-dūri 'my god is my wall' (de Boer 2014, 351) and the town Dūr-Addu (MTT I/1, s.v. Dūr-Addu); Egyptian Neith (n.t), as sꜣ-n.t 'son of Neith', wsr-n.t 'Neith is powerful' (Ilin-Tomich 2025, s.v. n.t). One attestation.
entries.source: di Mino; Gelb 1980; Buck 2018; Kinlaw 1967; de Boer 2014; MTT I/1; Ilin-Tomich 2025

entries.meaning: Weapon of Anat (theophoric personal name); rival Egyptian Neith as the second element

cognates.Akkadian: kakku 'weapon, arms' (CAD K 52); Kakka, DN
cognates.Amorite: kakkum, fem. kakka 'weapon'; Kakka, DN (Gelb 1980); names KAKK-U KA-AK-KU, KAKK-AH KA-AK-KÁ (nos. 3913, 3904); ʿAnat names, see DA-RU-NE-TE
cognates.Egyptian: mhr.j ꜥnṯj 'warrior of Anat', of the king (ORAEC 113, 564, 922); n.t 'Neith' in sꜣ-n.t, wsr-n.t (PNM v6)

entries.note: ZA 10b KA-KU-NE-TE ½, in a must (*131B) list of recipients, after the Egyptian PA-JA-RE Payare 1. KA-KU kakku 'weapon', also the god Kakka (Gelb 1980, 22), as in Amorite Kakka-liʾdi (no. 3907), ᶠKakka-lidi (ARM 26/1, 597) and Iddin-Kakka (Podany 2002, 11); -NE-TE ʿAnat (2771), as Šum-Anati and Abdi-Anati at Ugarit (Kinlaw 1967, 111, 7). Anat is the warrior: 'ʿAnat the divine, she the victorious, a woman acting as a warrior' (P. Chester Beatty VII vs. 1, 5–8; Gardiner 1935, I, 62); the king is mhr.j ꜥnṯj 'warrior of Anat' (ORAEC 113, 564, 922). Face a writes TA-NA-TE and A-TA-NA-TE: the lost ʿa- and the e of -NE-TE are unexplained. Rival: Egyptian Neith (n.t), as sꜣ-n.t, wsr-n.t (Ilin-Tomich 2025, s.v.). See I-NA-TA-I.
entries.source: di Mino; Gelb 1980; ARM 26/1; Podany 2002; Kinlaw 1967; Gardiner 1935; ORAEC; Ilin-Tomich 2025

entries.meaning: the wool (substrate commodity noun with Semitic mimation)

cognates.Greek: μαλλός (mallos) 'flock of wool' < Minoan /maru/ (Salgarella 2022; Nosch & Weilhartner 2026)
cognates.Linear A: A559 = MA+RU composite wool logogram (*146 Raison-Pope)

entries.note: HT 24a, under the heading KU-PA₃-RI-JA · KI-MA+RU-[, writes the word with the wool ligature MA+RU (A 559) followed by ME (GORILA I 43): .2 MA+RU-ME 10, .3 MA+RU-MẸ 6, .4 PA-SA-RI-JA · MA+RU-MẸ[, broken after ME. The ligature is the wool logogram AB MA+RU (Nosch and Weilhartner 2026, 122–123, 131), the Minoan wool word maru that Greek keeps as μαλλός, Cretan μάλλυκες in Hesychius (Salgarella, Mix and Match, n. 8); -ME adds mimation, the spelling convention of JA-SA-SA-RA-ME yaššaram. The two complete entries carry quantities (10, 6) under two section headings, a wool distribution. Mimation doublet of syllabic MA-RU (HT 117a).
entries.source: di Mino; GORILA I; Nosch and Weilhartner 2026; Salgarella 2022

entries.meaning: healer (active participle of √r-p-ʾ), a counted entry

cognates.Amorite: rāpiʾu 'healer' (Buck 2019, 331)

entries.note: PE 2 .2 RU-PI, then a damaged mark and ⅓, before SA-*305-MI 1⅛. rōpiʾ 'healer', the active participle of √r-p-ʾ (semitic_roots K0355), U for ō as in *47-KU-NA sōkina, the final ʾ unwritten. A-RI-PA ʾaripāʾ, of the same root, stands on the tablet. Weak point: the damaged mark after PI may be a lost sign. One attestation. See A-RI-PA and A-RE-PI-RE-NA.

entries.meaning: terrace, terraced field (a counted entry); rival the place Šdmy

cognates.Ugaritic: šdmt 'terrace' (KTU 1.23:10; DULAT 799); Šdmy, a town of Ugarit (KTU 4.244:13)
cognates.Hebrew: šᵊdēmâ 'terrace, field', pl. šadmôt (Deut 32:32; Isa 16:8; 2 Kgs 23:4; HALOT 1422–1423)

entries.note: PE 2 .2 SA-*305-MI 1⅛, after RU-PI ⅓, in a list of entries with fractions. šadmi 'terrace': Ug. šdmt, yšql šdmth km gpn 'they threw it on the terrace like a vine-stock' (KTU 1.23:10; DULAT 799), Heb. šᵊdēmâ, pl. šadmôt, the terraced vineyards of Deut 32:32 and Isa 16:8 (HALOT 1422–1423); *305 da. Rival: the town Šdmy on the border with Alalakh, krm PN b šdmy 'the vineyard of PN at Šdmy' (KTU 4.244:13; RGTC 12/2, 255). The first sign is SA (AB31), a fork with no crossbar. One attestation.

entries.meaning: Kikkina, recipient or named administrative entity

cognates.Amorite: KIKKIN-I (KI-IK-KI-NI), KIKKIN-U (KI-IK-KI-NU), KIKKIN-UM (KI-IK-KI-NUM), with KI-KI-NU-UM and KI-IK-KI-NI-IM variants
cognates.Ugaritic: kkn, personal name of uncertain etymology; distinct kknt 'pot/vessel' has final -t
cognates.Eblaite: Gi-gi-na, a singer (nar) from Mari (Prosopography of Ebla, list nar)

entries.note: HT 88 .3 NI · KI-KI-NA 7: after the fig logogram NI and before the quantity, a recipient, group or other named entity, 'figs: Kikkina, 7'. Amorite has the close name KIKKIN, written KI-IK-KI-NI, KI-IK-KI-NU and KI-IK-KI-NUM (Gelb 1980, nos. 4036–4038). Ugaritic kkn is a personal name of unknown etymology (DULAT 429). One attestation.
entries.source: di Mino; Gelb 1980, AS 21 nos. 4036–4038; Prosopography of Ebla; de Boer 2014

entries.meaning: box, chest, basket (container or unit)

cognates.Akkadian: quppatu 'box, basket'; quppu A 'wicker basket or wooden chest' (CAD Q 307); qappatu (qabbatu) '(a basket made of palm leaves)' (CAD Q 91)

entries.note: HT 6a, after DA-QE-RA: QE-PI-TA 22¾, counted in quarters, a container or unit. Ug. qpt 'box, chest, basket' (DULAT 696); Akk. quppatu, quppu (CAD Q 307). QE writes the vowel of Akk. qappatu beside quppatu (CAD Q 91, 307) and Mehri ḳeffēt (semitic_roots 301). Weak point: one attestation. See KU-PA.

entries.meaning: waitress, girl (Ug. ṯdr, a Hurro-Hittite loan from šiduri); rival the name Šituri

cognates.Akkadian: šiduri 'young woman' (CAD Š/2 408)

entries.note: HT Wc 3011 ZU-DI-RA and HT Wc 3012 ZU-DI-RA RE-RO, two roundels of the Haghia Triada series. ṯudira 'waitress, girl': Ugaritic ṯdr, a Hurro-Hittite loan from šiduri 'young woman' (Laroche 1980, 229; CAD Š/2 408), reaching Crete through Hurrian or Ugaritic. Rival: the Hurrian woman's name Šituri 'Girl', ši-du-ri at Mari and ši-tu-ri at Ašnakkum (Monti 2017, 296, 373). Weak point: DULAT marks the gloss '(?)', and Ugarit has two witnesses, one in a Hurrian text (DULAT 886–887). Two attestations.
entries.source: di Mino; DULAT; Laroche 1980; CAD Š/2; Monti 2017

entries.meaning: Most Righteous (PN)

cognates.Amorite: ṢDQ 'be just': ṣadaqa, jaṣduq (Gelb AS 21, 34); PN ṢADAQ-AH, written ZA-DA-GA (Gelb AS 21 no. 6350)

entries.note: MA Wc <5>, a Mallia roundel: A-SA-DA-KẠ with a dotted unit stroke on face a, GRA+E 4 on face b, a grain context (GORILA II 88); SA is drawn damaged. ʾaṣdaqa 'Most Righteous', the ʾaqtal elative of √ṣ-d-q: SA writes the coda ṣ with a dead vowel, as A-SA-MU-NE ʾAšmūn, and KA q, the emphatics unmarked; -A is the oblique of the diptote elative (Fischer 2002, §§125a, 153a), as in I-ZU-RI-NI-TA. ʾṢDQ is a name in Lihyanite and Sabaic (Harding 1971, 51) and in Qatabanic (Aylward 2) and Ḥaḍramitic (Raybūn-Kafas/Naʿmān 123) texts (DASI). Amorite names carry the root: Ṣa-du-qum and Am-mi-ṣa-du-qá (Huffmon 1965, 256–257), ʿAMM-I+ṢADUQ-A (Gelb 1980, no. 753). Cf. Zadok (2 Sam 8:17), Zedekiah (2 Kgs 24:17), Melchizedek (Gen 14:18). Weak point: ʾṢDQ is a first-millennium Arabian name, and no Amorite, Ugaritic or Hebrew name has the elative. Rival: ha-ṣadaqa 'the Righteous', the article ha- as in A-SI-KI-RA. Rival: Hurrian aštaga 'woman', the diminutive in -(a)ga of ašte 'woman' (Wilhelm, "Hurrian," 103; Laroche 1980, 61–62), written aš-ta-ka (Meskene) and aš-da-a-ga-bi (KUB XXIX 8 IV 23): coda š with a dead A, as A-SA-MU-NE, accounts for every sign. One attestation.
entries.source: di Mino; Fischer 2002; Harding 1971; GORILA II

entries.meaning: and the bahaq-rash (wa- + pan-Semitic skin-disease noun—rubric disease name)

cognates.Hebrew: bōhaq 'white spot on skin', bōhaq hûʾ pāraḥ bāʿôr 'it is a bōhaq that has broken out on the skin' (Lev 13:39; HALOT 112)

entries.note: Egyptian group-writing, rubric element 4 (Akulov 2023, 3): wbqy with the disease determinative. Kyriakidis reads the final sign as l, w-b-ql (Kyriakidis 2002, 213), and finds that 'the combination wbq may suggest a Semitic language' (214); Steiner transcribes w-b-ḳi and leaves it unread (Steiner 1992, 198). wa- 'and' + b(u)haq-ī, SED #135 *bahaḳ- '(kind of) skin disease': Heb. bōhaq 'tetter' (Lev 13:39), Arab. bahaq, and Mandaic baqiata 'decay, gangrene' without the h. A skin disease named beside samāwnā (Akk. sāmānu 'the red one') in a skin-disease papyrus. Rivals: Arabic √w-b-q 'perish' (Q 18:52; 42:34); Akulov's Eg. wbnw 'wound', with q for n unexplained. Weak points: the unwritten medial h; the disputed final sign. See U.
entries.source: di Mino; Akulov 2023; Kyriakidis 2002; Steiner 1992; SED; HALOT

entries.meaning: the śĕʾēt-mark (skin-disease term—rubric disease name)

cognates.Hebrew: śəʾēt II 'spot, blemish on the skin', ʾādām kî yihyeh bəʿôr bəśārô śəʾēt 'a man, when there is on the skin of his flesh a śəʾēt' (Lev 13:2; HALOT 1301)

entries.note: LMP Spell 33, rubric element 5 (Akulov 2023, 3): s-ꜣ-t, the final loaf the Egyptian word t(i) 'bread' used for its sound (Kyriakidis 2002, 213 n. 15), a many-consonant sign read as a whole Egyptian word (Helck 1989, 123). s-ꜣ-t writes ś-ʾ-t: Heb. שְׂאֵת śĕʾēt, a skin-disease term (Lev 13:2, 10, 19, 28, 43; 14:56), 'swelling' for the rabbis, from nāśāʾ 'lift' (Sipra, b. Šebu. 6b), 'mark' in the Targums, 'discoloration' for Milgrom (Milgrom 1991, 773). With WBQY the rubric names the disease in the vocabulary of Lev 13, śĕʾēt (13:2) and bōhaq (13:39). Rival: Akulov's 'spread through grain and soil', which takes the loaf and land signs as determinatives (Akulov 2023, 3–4). Steiner leaves s-ꜣ-t unread (Steiner 1992, 198). See DA-NA-SI.
entries.source: di Mino; Akulov 2023; Kyriakidis 2002; Helck 1989; Milgrom 1991; Steiner 1992

entries.meaning: the dwelling, abode (sanctuary as divine habitation)

cognates.Amorite: nawûm 'steppe; encampment (man and beast)' (Huffmon, APNM 237)
cognates.Hebrew: nāweh (נָוֶה) 'habitation, pasture-land; temple, shrine' (Exod 15:13 אֶל־נְוֵה קׇדְשֶׁךָ)
cognates.Akkadian: nawûm 'pasture, steppe'

entries.note: PH 6 (MM IIB), the heading, set off by the divider: I-NA-WA · A-RI / I-ZU-RI-NI-TA / A-RI / I-DA-PA₃-I-SA-RI. ʾi-nawā 'the dwelling', the nominal core of the libation formula, spelled with plain NA: A-TA-I-*301-WA-JA ʾata-i-nawa-ya 'I make myself a dwelling', eleven times at five peak sanctuaries, conjugates this noun, and *301-WA nawā (IO Za 4) writes it with *301 = na, the sign whose value derives from this root; PH 6 predates that convention. √n-w-y: Heb. nāweh 'grazing place; settlement' (HALOT 678–679), Amorite nawûm 'steppe; encampment' (Huffmon 1965, 237). ʾi- is the prosthetic vowel, as in I-ZU-RI-NI-TA and I-DA-MA-TE against DA-MA-TE. One attestation.

entries.meaning: mountain of (construct state before divine names)

cognates.Hebrew: har (הַר) 'mountain' (< *harr-); construct har- as in har Sinai, har Tsiyyon
cognates.Eblaite: hārrum 'mountain'; hārru-Šum 'a mountain is Šum', names (Pagan 1998, rows 46, 1002)

entries.note: PH 6 .1 I-NA-WA · A-RI and .3 A-RI. harrī 'mountain of', the construct before a divine name, genitive -ī (nawā harrī DN 'dwelling of the mountain of DN'): Hebrew har (HALOT 254), Ugaritic hr 'mountain' (DULAT 341), the Amarna gloss ḫa-ar-ri on ḪUR.SAG (EA 74:20), Emar harru (Pentiuc 2001, 57); h unwritten, as in A-KI-DA-RO. Rivals: ʿalē 'upon, for' and ʾarī 'lion'; the A-RA/A-RI/A-RU triple of a, i and u argues an inflected noun against a frozen preposition, and the house dative is la- (RE/RA). Rival parse: harr-ī 'my mountain', 1cs suffix, an Ebla name (Pagan 1998, row 789). HT 141 .1 A-RI-[ runs into the break after RI (GORILA I 239), and PH 28a A-RI-JA-[ breaks after JA.
entries.source: di Mino; HALOT; DULAT; Pentiuc 2001; Pagan 1998; GlOS 1

entries.meaning: Ida, in righteousness (toponym + prepositional phrase written as one word)

cognates.Akkadian: išaru 'straight, just'; mīšaru 'justice, equity' (CAD M/II 116)

entries.note: PH 6, an MM II tablet: I-DA-PA₃-I-SA-RI closes it, after I-NA-WA · A-RI and I-ZU-RI-NI-TA / A-RI. I-DA ʾIdā, Mount Ida, + PA₃-I-SA-RI bi-ʾišarī 'in righteousness': the b= proclitic spelled with PA₃ = /ba/ (dead vowel), medial I carrying the ʾ of ʾišar-, and genitive -ī after the preposition, as la-piṭrī (PK Za 11). Same √y-š-r as the formula's yaššaram (JA-SA-SA-RA-ME): PH 6 writes the idea with b= and the genitive where the LM I vessels use the adverbial accusative with mimation. One attestation. See I-DA, PA₃ and I-SA-RI.

entries.meaning: uprightness, righteousness (genitive after the b= proclitic)

cognates.Akkadian: išaru 'straight, just'; mīšaru 'justice, equity' (CAD M/II 116)
cognates.Eblaite: i-sa-rí 'just, favourable' in running text; i-sar Yiśar, a name and DN (GlOS 2, 377; Pagan 1998, row 2604)

entries.note: PH 6: only within I-DA-PA₃-I-SA-RI, after the b= proclitic. The medial I writes the ʾ of ʾišar-, and the final -ī is the genitive a preposition governs (cf. la-piṭrī, PK Za 11). √y-š-r, the root of the formula's yaššaram (JA-SA-SA-RA-ME); the nominal shape is Akk. išaru 'straight, just, fair' (CAD I/J 224). See I-DA-PA₃-I-SA-RI.

entries.meaning: in, with, by (proclitic b-); rival on HT 103 bād(i) 'in the charge of'

cognates.Phoenician: b 'in, from'; bd ‘in the charge of’

entries.note: PH 6 I-DA-PA₃-I-SA-RI ʾIdā bi-ʾišarī: PA₃, a proposed ba, writes the proclitic b- 'in, with, by' with a dead vowel, as a CV syllabary must, after PS and Ugaritic bi=. On HT 9b PA₃ stands between dividers before WA-JA-PI, a transaction sign like TE in the HT 9a heading. Rival on HT 103, PA₃-DA-KU-SE-NE[ ]6½ with a possible divider after PA₃ (GORILA I 171), and Ugaritic often sets a divider after a one-syllable proclitic, b. bnk (CAT 1.6:I:46; Tropper 2000, §21.412a): bād(i) 'in the charge of' (< *bi-yadi), as Kition no. 84 bd with a personal name and counted workmen (Krahmalkov 2000, 97) and CAT 4.145:9–10 bd rb ḥršm 'in the custody of the chief of the craftsmen' (Huehnergard 2012, 76, 94). Cf. Linear B pa-ro with a personal name, 'in the charge of' (Killen 2024, 103). Weak point: HT 103 wants bd 'in the charge of', and no Semitic text shortens bd to b. Two attestations. See PA₃-E.
entries.root_meaning: in, with, by (PS proclitic preposition bi=)

entries.meaning: Fattened (personal name), the bare stem of the Amorite MARUʾ- names; rival Maru 'Wool'

cognates.Amorite: MARUʾ+JAT-UM, MARUʾ+LI+ʾEL, MAʾR-U+ZAʾT-U-HU, all written MA-RU- (Gelb 1980, nos. 4542, 4543, 4545); Tuttul dādu-marʾum 'my beloved is fat' (Buck 2018, 327)
cognates.Linear A: rival MA+RU (A559), the wool logogram, and MA+RU-ME (HT 24a)

entries.note: HT 117a, the fourth of ten men at 1 each under MA-KA-RI-TE · KI-RO · U-MI-NA-SI (KU-RO 10), between KU-RA-MU Kurmu and KU-PA₃-NU Kubānu. Amorite names open with MA-RU on MRʾ: MARUʾ+JAT-UM MA-RU-IA-TUM, MARUʾ+LI+ʾEL MA-RU-LI-EL, MAʾR-U+ZAʾT-U-HU MA-RU-ZA-TU-U₂ (Gelb 1980, nos. 4542, 4543, 4545), beside MAʾR-A+ʾEL MA-RA-EL and MAʾR-AT-UM MA-RA-TUM (nos. 4531, 4536); Gelb lists MRʾ? as a verb. MA-RU is the stem alone, the glottal stop unwritten. Ugaritic mrủ 'fatling' (DULAT 563): an animal name, as TE-JA-RE Tayru 'Bull' on the same list. Rival: Maru 'Wool', the wool word of the ligature MA+RU (A559) and MA+RU-ME (HT 24a), source of Greek μαλλός; Linear B ma-ro-ne, a man at Knossos (KN Fh 347). One witness.
entries.source: di Mino; Gelb 1980; DULAT; Buck 2018; GlOS 2

entries.meaning: Kulelu (personal name; cf. Middle Assyrian Kulilu)

cognates.Middle Assyrian: Kulilu, written {m}ki-li-lu, T 98-038 obv. 4', Dunni-Aššur/Tell Sabi Abyad (ORACC P532066)
cognates.Amorite: KU-LA-IL-E and KI+L-I+IL (secondary k-l-l name-family comparisons; Gelb, AS 21 nos. 4114, 4065–66)
cognates.Akkadian: kalû 'all, entirety'; kilīlu 'circlet, wreath'

entries.note: The HT 117b roster, headed *21F-TU-NE, fixes the personal-name slot, KU-RE-JU 1 before DI-KI-SE 1; on HT 39 KU-RE-JU takes 8. With R/L neutralization and JU = lu, the spelling writes Kulelu. The strongest external formal parallel is the Middle Assyrian personal name Kulilu, written {m}ki-li-lu at Dunni-Aššur (Tell Sabi Abyad), T 98-038 obv. 4' (ORACC tcma/tsa1, P532066). The later personal name Kullulu is written {1}ku-lu-lu in SAA 6 22 rev. 9'. Amorite KU-LA-IL-E belongs to the same k-l-l family (Gelb 1980, no. 4114). Rival: kᵉlûlâ 'betrothal, being a bride' (Jer 2:2; HALOT 478), as the pair of *21F-TU-NE 'bridegroom' on HT 117b; the quantity 8 on HT 39 and DI-KI-SE, a name in the same layout, favour a name. Both readings take JU = lu.

entries.meaning: Dūmatī (personal name—'the Enduring One', √dwm hypocoristic)

cognates.Amorite: Dūmat-An (DU-MA-TA-AN), Gelb 1980, no. 1581—u-vocalized dūmat- name element
cognates.Hebrew: דּוּמָה Dūmāh, Ishmaelite eponym (Gen 25:14); cf. Dūmat al-Jandal
cognates.Arabian: dmt / dwmt / dymt / dwmn name cluster under dm 'enduring' (Harding 1971, 242)
cognates.Sabaic: dwm 'lasting, permanent'; dwmm 'forever' (Beeston et al. 1982, 36; Biella 1982, 81)

entries.note: HT 19 and HT 17, under the same heading RA-*164-TI · TE · VIN, name the third entry after SA-RO: DU-ME-DI 43½ on HT 19, SI-DA-RE 5 on HT 17. Dūmatī, of the dūmat- name family 'enduring': Amorite Dūmat-An (DU-MA-TA-AN, Gelb 1980, no. 1581), Hebrew Dūmāh, the Ishmaelite eponym (Gen 25:14), Arabian dmt, dwmt, dymt and dwmn under dm 'enduring' (Harding 1971, 242), Sabaic dwm 'lasting' (Beeston et al. 1982, 36; Biella 1982, 81). ME's vowel is dead, DI writes tī after the nasal, and -ī is hypocoristic as in QA-*310-I qaynī. Rival: Dimti 'the Tower-estate', Ug. dmt 'tower' and the toponym dmt (DULAT 272), Akk. dimtum 'tower; fortified area, settlement; district' (Huehnergard 2011, 492), with the by-forms dintu and dindu (CAD D 144), which make DI regular. See DA-U-MI.
entries.source: di Mino; Gelb 1980; Harding 1971; Beeston et al. 1982; Biella 1982; DULAT; Huehnergard 2011; CAD D

entries.meaning: ʿAttiru, personal name, the nisbe 'man of ʿAṯtar'; rival ʿatīru 'entreated'

cognates.Akkadian: Ištar (i-vocalism of the same DN)
cognates.Amorite: Aštar divine element (Gelb AS 21; cuneiform š for /ṯ/); assimilated Attar in [A]t-ta-ri-ša-du-u[q] (Huffmon 1965, 173)
cognates.Sabaic: ʿṯtr, chief deity of the South Arabian pantheon

entries.note: ZA 4a, a Zakros tablet: a roster slot of 4 units, directly before the personal name JA-PA. ʿAṯtar with ṯt assimilated to tt, as in Amorite [A]t-ta-ri-ša-du-u[q] (Huffmon 1965, 173: "perhaps an assimilated form representing *Attar"); the geminate is unwritten and ʿayin rides the plain vowel sign. Canaanite merged ṯ with š only after the Bronze Age. The i has precedent in the family's Akk. Ištar (CAD I/J 271; semitic_roots 2770), where Ebla keeps aš-dar, or marks the nisbe ʿAttirī, which the roster slot favors. Rival: ʿatīru 'entreated' (√ʿ-t-r; Gen 25:21 wayyēʿāter; HALOT 905), which fits a-ti-ru as written.
entries.source: di Mino; Huffmon 1965; CAD I/J; HALOT

entries.meaning: with, at (comitative preposition); on IO Za 12 ʾittī 'with me'

cognates.Akkadian: itti 'with' (< *ʔin-t- + n-assimilation)

entries.note: HT 25b WI-TE-RO 𐄁 I-TI VIR 28 / VIR 24 / KU-RO 52: I-TI stands before the first of two personnel entries, 28 and 24 making the 52, as Akkadian ledgers write itti 'with, including' before an included subgroup.
