IO Za 12 ]𐄁 ]𐄁 JA-SA-SA-RA-ME 𐄁 I-TI[, set off from the formula word by a divider and broken after: bare ʾitt- 'with', its complement lost, or ʾittī 'with me' (Heb. ʾittī), a predication of the ʿimmānû-ʾēl type. PS *ʾin-t- 'with, at, via', the extended form of *ʾin (Huehnergard 2019, §3.6): *ʾinti > ʾitti, the assimilated n and the geminate unwritten, the glottal onset on the bare vowel sign. Ugaritic prefers ʿm 'with'; ʾitt- stands with Akkadian and Canaanite, a Proto-Semitic retention. Rival on HT 25b: a personal name, in the name–VIR–number layout of the rosters.

entries.meaning: may you (f.) answer us (N-stem of √ʿ-n-y in the TA-NA-[X]-U-TI-NU frame: 2fs prefix + indicative -u + subject clitic -tī + 1cp object -n)
entries.cognates: Hebrew עָנָה (ʿānāh) 'answer'; Ugaritic ʿny 'answer'; Amarna Canaanite ʿ-n-y forms; Eblaite i-na-a yiʿnay, na-ni naʿni, the ʿ unwritten, Amorite ia-aḫ-nu-ú yaʿnū (GlOS 1, 84)
entries.note: IO Za 6, position 1: TA-NA-I-*301-U-TI-NU · I-NA-TA-I-ZU-DI-SI-KA · JA-SA-SA-RA-ME ·. tan-ʿinā-u-tī-n(u) 'may you (f.) answer us': TA the 2fs prefix, NA the N-stem, I-*301 the root ʿ-n-y with *301 = na, U the indicative -u, TI the 2fs subject clitic -tī, NU the 1cp object -n. The verb addresses and puns on the theonym that follows, I-NA-TA-I ʿInatī 'my Anat'. The frame is that of TA-NA-RA-TE-U-TI-NU (IO Za 2, √r-ṣ-y), with the root slot changed. Ugaritic tʿnyn /taʿniyūna/ (KTU 1.23:12) supports the root and a t-…-n profile, not the segmentation. The family: TA-NA-I-*301-TI on PS Za 2, where GORILA reads the last sign as an uncertain TI and Ferrara, Montecchi and Valério (2022, 87) as E, 'may you (f.) answer' with TI, 'may she or you answer' with E; A-TA-I-*301-DE-KA on ZA Zb 3, 'who answered for you'. One attestation of this form, three of the family. See I-NA-TA-I.

entries.meaning: in, at (preposition)
entries.cognates: Hebrew בְּ- (bə-); Ugaritic b-; Amarna Canaanite bi-; Phoenician b-
entries.note: PK Za 8 ]NU · PA₃-E · JA-DI-KI-TE-TE-*307-PU₂-RE · TU-ME-I: PA₃-E stands between dividers before the vocative of Dikte (GORILA IV 24–27). bē 'in, at': PA₃, the proposed value /ba~be/, + E, the b- preposition, Ugaritic b 'in, at' (DULAT 196), Hebrew bə-, Amarna bi-. The divider after it is Ugaritic practice with a one-syllable proclitic, b. bnk (CAT 1.6:I:46), l. mlkt (CAT 2.12:1; Tropper 2000, §21.412a). Weak point: one attestation. See JA-DI-KI-TU.

entries.meaning: personal name Ḥanānu 'gracious'; rival ʿAnānu 'cloud'
entries.cognates: Amorite A-NA-NU-UM-DINGIR, read ḤANAN-UM+ʾIL (Gelb 1980, Add. 476a), and Ḥanan-a, Ḥanan-at-um, Ḥanan-im (Gelb, AS 21, nos. 475–478); Ugarit Ḫananu (Kinlaw 1967, 55); biblical PN חָנָן (Ḥānān, Neh 10:27; HALOT 335); rival: Hebrew עָנָן (ʿānān) 'cloud', biblical PN עָנָן (ʿĀnān, Neh 10:27; HALOT 858)
entries.note: Owner/recipient name on a painted pithos, base of A-NA-NU-SI-JA-SE (HT Zb 159). -SI-JA-SE is the vessel-label adjectival formation shared with KI-TA-NA-SI-JA-SE (PE Zb 3). Gelb 1980 reads the same spelling, A-NA-NU-UM-DINGIR, as ḤANAN-UM+ʾIL (Add. 476a), beside the Amorite Ḥanan- names (nos. 475–478); Ugarit has Ḫananu, Kinlaw's spelling (Kinlaw 1967, 55). Cuneiform does not tell ḥ from ʿ. Rival: ʿAnānu 'cloud', and Neh 10:27 names ʿĀnān beside Ḥānān. See A-NA-NE.

entries.meaning: In the charge of Našūka ('the Bitten one')—custody formula + personal name on a sealed receipt

cognates.Ugaritic: bd 'in the hand, charge of' (< bi-yadi) (Huehnergard 2012, glossary); nṯk (I) 'biter' (DULAT 643)
cognates.Akkadian: ina qāt 'in the charge of' (functional parallel); našāku 'to bite' (CAD N/2 53)

entries.note: HT Wc 3010, a roundel: *333-DI-NA-SU-KA alone. With *333 = bi, bīdi 'in the charge of': Ug. bd 'into the hands of, (intended) for', from b (y)d (DULAT 211), the custody preposition of administrative receipts. Našūka 'the Bitten one', qatūl of √n-š-k 'bite', as Hebrew nāšak of the snake (Gen 49:17; HALOT 729); cf. the serpent names Naḥash (1 Sam 11:1) and Naḥshon. Pair of HT Wc 3009 *333-DI-SU-KA: the same frame, another name. -KA the diptote genitive -a of a proper name, as Ugaritic ugrt /ʾugarita/ (Huehnergard 2012, 40). Weak point: *333 = bi rests on its three words. Rival: the whole group a personal name. One attestation. See PA₃.

entries.meaning: In the charge of Sūka—custody formula + personal name on a sealed receipt

cognates.Ugaritic: bd 'in the hand, charge of' (< bi-yadi) (Huehnergard 2012, glossary)

entries.note: HT Wc 3009, a roundel: *333-DI-SU-KA *188. With *333 = bi, bīdi 'in the charge of' (Ug. bd, DULAT 211) + Sūka, a name without a secure etymology. Pair of HT Wc 3010 *333-DI-NA-SU-KA. Weak point: *333 = bi rests on its three words. Rivals: the whole group a personal name; *333 as ZU (AB 79) after Facchetti, ZU-DI-SU-KA beside ZU-DI-SI-KA of IO Za 6 (Schoep 2002, 50), where the HT Wc 3009 sign has the form of *333 on HT Wc 3010. One attestation. See PA₃.

entries.meaning: Balsam, perfume—aromatic personal name (cf. Basemath) on a metal ornament
entries.note: MO Zf 1, a metal ornament from Mokhlos, the word alone. With *333 = bi, *333-SA-MU writes biśāmu 'balsam', before the Canaanite shift of ā (Heb. bōśem 'balsam tree; perfume', HALOT 163); a name of the aromatic class, cf. Basemath (Gen 26:34). Weak point: *333 = bi rests on its three words. Rival: a label for the object, or a non-Semitic name. One attestation.

entries.meaning: may that which goes out glorify—volitive yaqtula √p-ʾ-r + √y-ṣ-ʾ participle/imperfect (the outpoured libation as subject)
entries.cognates: Hebrew פָּאַר (pāʾar) "glorify, beautify" (Isa 60:7, 13; hitpaʿel Isa 60:21, 61:3), פְּאֵר (pəʾēr) "diadem, headdress", תִּפְאֶרֶת (tipʾart) "beauty, splendor"; Akkadian apāru "to cap, crown" (CAD A/2 166–67; āpirat agê bēlūti of Ištar, STC 2 75:7); Hebrew יָצָא/יֹצֵא (yāṣāʾ/yōṣē) "go out"; Akkadian (w)aṣû "go out", ṣītu "outflow, disbursement"
entries.note: SY Za 9, Syme, HM 5585, found 1987 (Muhly and Olivier 2008, 212–13, transcription only): two words, JA-PA-RA and JA-SE. JA-PA-RA yapʾara, the 3 m. sg. ya- prefix with √p-ʾ-r 'glorify, adorn', the ʾ unwritten as in JA-PA-QA yapqaḥ (PK Za 11, PK Za 12), final -A the volitive yaqtula of prayer. JA-SE yāṣē, the yāṣē of SI-JA-SE šī-yāṣē 'which goes out' (HT Zb 159, PE Zb 3), the disbursement marker there, the outpoured libation here: 'may that which goes out glorify (her)', verb first. Hebrew puts the root in the sanctuary: לְפָאֵר מְקוֹם מִקְדָּשִׁי 'to beautify the place of my sanctuary' (Isa 60:13), the hitpaʿel in Isa 60:21 and 61:3, and Ben Sira 50:20 (MS B) ובשם ייי התפאר 'and in the name of YYY he gloried'. The root also gives pəʾēr 'diadem' and tipʾart 'splendor'. Rivals: Ugaritic pʿr 'proclaim (a name)' (ypʿr šmthm, KTU 1.2 IV 11, 18), the same spelling once ʿ drops, attested only with šm 'name' as object; PS *wpr 'pilgrimage', a noun with no denominal verb and an initial w to lose. Weak point: one attestation of √p-ʾ-r; the support is yāṣē at two sites and the ya- prefix.
entries.root_meaning: to glorify, beautify, adorn + to go out

entries.meaning: may he/it glorify, adorn (3ms volitive yaqtula √p-ʾ-r; guttural ʾ unwritten)
entries.cognates: Hebrew פָּאַר (pāʾar) "glorify, beautify", פְּאֵר (pəʾēr) "diadem" (Exod 39:28; Isa 61:3), תִּפְאֶרֶת (tipʾart) "beauty, splendor"; Akkadian apāru "to cap, crown"—metathesis sibling (BDB s.v. פְּאֵר compares Assyrian ipru, ēpartu; inner-Hebrew doublet אֲפֵר ʾăpēr "headband", 1 Kgs 20:38, 41)
entries.note: SY Za 9: only within JA-PA-RA-JA-SE. yapʾara, 3ms volitive yaqtula of √p-ʾ-r 'glorify, adorn', the guttural ʾ unwritten, as in JA-PA-QA yapqaḥ (PK Za 11, PK Za 12): the same ya- prefix before a p-initial root with the guttural dropped. One attestation. See JA-PA-RA-JA-SE.
entries.root_meaning: to glorify, beautify, adorn; nominal: diadem, headdress

entries.meaning: that which goes out, it goes out (3ms imperfect/participle √y-ṣ-ʾ with ʾaleph-III loss)
entries.cognates: Hebrew יָצָא (yāṣāʾ) "go out", participle יֹצֵא (yōṣē); Ugaritic √yṣʾ "go out, appear"; Akkadian (w)aṣû "go out", ṣītu "expenditure, outflow"; Amorite names with the 3ms imperfect: ʾAWIJ+JA-JṢIʾ (A-WI-IA-ZI), JI-JṢIʾ+ʾAŠAR (I-ṢI-A-ŠAR) (Gelb 1980, nos. 561, 2602); Euphratian ia-zi-e, Alalakh ia-ṣí, Ugarit syll. i-ṣa-ʔa (GlOS 2, 361)
entries.note: SY Za 9, inside JA-PA-RA-JA-SE yapʾara yāṣē on a Syme libation vessel: yāṣē 'that which goes out', the 3ms imperfect of √y-ṣ-ʾ with the third aleph lost, the libation poured out of the vessel. The same two signs close SI-JA-SE šī-yāṣē 'which goes out', the disbursement marker on the pithos labels HT Zb 159 and PE Zb 3, counted under that entry. Cf. Hebrew אֲשֶׁר־יֵצֵא 'whatever goes out', of Temple expenditure (2 Kgs 12:13). One attestation.

entries.meaning: 'The Requested One'—votive birth-name from √ʾ-r-š "to request, desire" + hypocoristic -ān; the child asked of the goddess, the name a receipt

cognates.Amorite: ʾARIŚ-AN, ḪA-RI-ŠA-AN (Gelb AS 21 §6 Index of Names no. 2190), A-ru-si-AN (Huffmon APNM p. 22)
cognates.Ugaritic: ʾrš 'to request, wish, demand, claim' (CUC); irš 'demand' (DULAT)
cognates.Akkadian: erēšu 'to request'—the Erišti-DN class ('Requested-of-DN', e.g. Erišti-Aya) among the commonest OB female names
cognates.Safaitic: ʾrš ×12 + ʾršt ×11 + ʾršn—the exact shape ʾAriš-ān (Harding 1971 p. 37)
cognates.Hebrew: ʾărešet 'request' (Ps 21:3, hapax); naming-motif parallel Šāʾûl 'Asked-For' and Hannah's Samuel etymology (1 Sam 1:20)

entries.note: THE Zb 2, an Akrotiri clay vessel, the sole word: the owner's or dedicant's slot. ʾAriš-ān 'The Requested One', a votive birth-name from √ʾ-r-š 'to request, desire' with the hypocoristic -ān: the Amorite name ʾARIŚ-AN, ḪA-RI-ŠA-AN (Gelb 1980, no. 2190), -NA writing its closing n; Ug. /ʾ-r-š/ 'to request, wish, demand' (DULAT 104), Heb. ʾărešet 'desire' (Ps 21:3; HALOT 92), pre-Islamic Arabian ʾršn (Harding 1971, 37). RE writes ri, as KI-RE-TA₂ beside KI-RI-TA₂. One attestation.

entries.meaning: O Beloved!—vocative of the reduplicative divine epithet (with i- prosthesis)

cognates.Amorite: dad- 'favorite' (Huffmon 1965, 181); dādum 'beloved' (Gelb 1980); Alalakh DAWD-A, DA-DA (Gelb 1980, no. 1413)
cognates.Eblaite: da-da dādā 'the beloved', a name (Pagan 1998, row 1396)

entries.note: CR Zg 4: I-DA-DA, with A-RO-TE on line 2. Cf. Ugaritic dd 'love', by metonymy 'loved one' (DULAT 262), ydd 'loved' (DULAT 943); Amorite dad- 'favorite' (Huffmon 1965, 181). I- is the prosthetic vowel of I-DA-MA-TE beside DA-MA-TE. Rival: a personal name. See TA-DI and DU-DA-MA.
entries.source: di Mino; DULAT; Huffmon 1965; Pagan 1998; Gelb 1980; ARM 26/1; Kinlaw 1967

entries.meaning: Salvation—votive exclamation/dedication term

cognates.Amorite: ia-še-ia, ia-ši-iḫ-ìl; Alalakh zu-ia-še-ia; the noun in iš-ḫa, iš-a-ti (GlOS 2, 379); jišʿum 'help' (Gelb 1980, glossary)

entries.note: KN Zb 4 ]-JU · JA-SI · SI[ and PE Zc 4 A-JA · JA-SI. yašīʿ 'salvation', √y-š-ʿ 'to help, save' (semitic_roots 3332): Heb. yēšaʿ 'help, salvation' (HALOT 449), Amorite yiṯʿu 'salvation' (Buck 2019, 335). SI writes the ṯ as cuneiform writes it in the Amorite names, ia-aš-ḫa (GlOS 2, 379). On KN Zb 4 inside the votive frame JU · JA-SI · SI, l(u) 'for' + yašīʿ + šay 'tribute'; on PE Zc 4 after A-JA: 'Living One!—Salvation!'; JA-SI-E on the lamp KE Zb 4 is its vocative, 'O Salvation!'. Rivals: yāṯiʿ 'saviour', Amorite yāṯiʿa (Buck 2019, 335), and the verb 'he saves', Heb. hôšîaʿ (HALOT 448). Gordon's ya-ne 'wine' (Gordon 1966 §123, his text II,3) is this KN Zb 4 group; its second sign reads SI (Packard 1974, 260; GORILA IV).
entries.source: di Mino; HALOT; Buck 2019; GlOS 2; Gordon 1966; Packard 1974; GORILA IV

entries.meaning: O Salvation—vocative/petitionary extension of yašīʿ
entries.cognates: see JA-SI
entries.note: KE Zb 4, a lamp from Kea: a one-word dedication. √y-š-ʿ 'save', as in JA-SI ('Salvation', KN Zb 4) and PE Zc 4 ('he saves'): one root at three sites. Š is written S and the final ʿ is unwritten. The vocative JA- is JA-DI-KI-TU's (IO Za 2). Amorite ia-še-ia carries the hypocoristic -iya on the same stem (GlOS 2, 379). Weak point: the -E extension, vocative or petitionary, against bare JA-SI. One attestation.

entries.meaning: the Tylissian (f.): provenance label on a jar

cognates.Hebrew: ha-kkĕnaʿănît 'the Canaanite (woman)' (Gen 46:10; Exod 6:15; 1 Chr 2:3), ha-mmôʾābît (2 Chr 24:26): article + feminine gentilic -ît
cognates.Ugaritic: ḫtyt GN f. 'Hittite', hmš ddm l ḫtyt 'five cauldronsful for the Hittite (people?)', KTU 4.269:3 (DULAT 409); kd (I) n. f. 'jar' (DULAT 424)
cognates.Amorite: GUBL-AJIT-UM, Gu-ub-la-ji-tum 'the Byblian (woman)' (Gelb 1980, no. 1795)
cognates.Linear B: tu-ri-so Tylissos (KN Ce 59, Da, Db, Dd, Dh); ethnic tu-ri-si-jo (KN E 668, Og 833), fem. tu-ri-si-ja (KN Lc 533)

entries.note: KN Zb 5, a clay vessel (MM IIIB), the single word A-TU-RI-SI-TI ·. Pre-Greek Turis- (LB tu-ri-so, Tylissos) with the NWS article ha- (h dropped to A, as A-KI-DA-RO) and the feminine gentilic -īt, as KA-NA-NI-TI kanaʿanītī. The feminine agrees with the jar (Ug. kd n. f. 'jar', DULAT 424; KA-DI kadd): a provenance label of the SU-KI-RI-TE-I-JA genre. Linear B writes the same feminine ethnic with Greek -ia, tu-ri-si-ja (KN Lc 533.8; DMic II 378, s.v. tu-ri-si-jo). A Semitic formation on a pre-Greek stem.
entries.source: di Mino; Gelb 1980; DULAT; DMic II; Beekes 2014

entries.meaning: personal name, 'hidden one'
entries.note: HT 117a: TU-JU-MA 1 in the roster under MA-KA-RI-TE, 'merchants'. √ʿ-l-m 'to be hidden' (HALOT 834), ʿ unwritten, JU writing lu. Rival: √t-l-m, Heb. telem 'furrow' (HALOT 1740). One attestation.

entries.meaning: fire offering(s)
entries.cognates: see A-SE
entries.note: KH 9 MI / I-SI · CYP+D ½ 2, with cyperus; PYR Wc 4, a roundel, TI (figs) · I-SI. Hebrew ʾiššeh 'offering by fire' (HALOT 93), the rival of A-SE ʾāsē 'physician'; the two spellings share no site (A-SE: HT, ZA; I-SI: KH, PYR). Frankincense alone is an ʾiššeh (Lev 24:7), as cyperus is on KH 9. Weak point: one consonant. Two attestations. See A-SE.

entries.meaning: pasture, meadow (estate heading)

cognates.Hebrew: כַּר kar 'pasture, meadow' (Isa 30:23 kar nirḥāb; Ps 65:14); also 'lamb, ram' (Deut 32:14; Amos 6:4)

entries.note: HT 97a opens KA-RU · *307+*307 · VIR+KA 82, then *327 33, KA-NU-TI 25, PA-I-TO 6: the heading slot of HT 85a A-DU · *307+*307 · VIR+[?], 'pasture-sanctuary: men'. HT 75 KA-RU[, broken after RU (GORILA I 125). karru 'pasture', Heb. kar 'pasture' (Isa 30:23; HALOT 496), the geminate written single. Rivals: Akkadian kāru 'quay, harbour, trading station' (CAD K 231), an East Semitic word, for the harbour at Kommos; and a divine name, as A-DU heads HT 85a.

entries.meaning: He of Grace (personal name; ḏū 'he of' + naʿm 'grace, pleasantness')

cognates.Amorite: NAʿM-I, NA-AḪ-MI, genitive, Mari (Gelb no. 4893); NA-AḪ-ME-ᵈDA-GAN (no. 4892); NA-MI-ᵈDA-GAN, Alalakh (no. 4999) (Gelb AS 21, 627–628)

entries.note: HT 127a .2 DU-NE-MI 1̣[, all three signs whole and undotted at the head of the line, after .1 vest.[, where GORILA's tabular copy sets ] before the word; one man, beside *304+PA-DA-*47-KU 1 (GORILA I 219). DU ḏū 'he of', as in DU-ZU-WA and DU-MA-I-NA; NE-MI naʿmi, the genitive after ḏū, the ʿ unwritten and its a coloured e, as Amorite NA-AḪ-MI, NA-AḪ-ME-ᵈDA-GAN and NA-MI-ᵈDA-GAN (Gelb 1980, nos. 4893, 4892, 4999). Sabaic has ḏ-Nʿmn 'he of Nʿmn' as a by-name (Ja 331; CIH 117). Weak point: no Bronze Age ḏū name on nʿm. One attestation. Cf. TA-NA-MA-JE.

entries.meaning: (to) the lord / lords—recipient entry; written only as WA-DU-NI-MI 'and (to) the lord(s)'

cognates.Amorite: ʾadun- in PNs: ʾADUN-UM A-DU-NU-UM (Gelb AS 21 no. 199); LA+ʾADON-IM LA-DU-NIM, genitive (no. 4246, Mari); A-du-na-dIM (Huffmon APNM p. 20). Huffmon p. 159: the names favour Albright's *ʾadun- 'lord' over Gelb's *ʾadān-
cognates.Amarna: Aduna, ruler of Irqata (EA 75:25; EA 140:10); Moran 1992: 380 'WS hypo. "father" or "lord"'
cognates.Ugaritic: ʾadn /ʔadānu/ 'father, lord'; PN A-du-ni-dU (PRU III 15.42 ii 20′, via Huffmon p. 159)
cognates.Hebrew: אָדוֹן ʾādôn, pl. אֲדֹנִים ʾădōnîm (< *ʾadān- by the Canaanite shift)

entries.note: HT 6b WA-DU-NI-MI 3 + fractions, first line of the verso; HT 85b WA-DU-NI-MI 1, ninth of eleven entries of one unit each, the others names or places (Scribe 9). WA- is wa- 'and', allomorph of U; list entries otherwise carry no conjunction. The initial ʾa- is absorbed after the particle, as in Amorite LA-DU-NIM la-ʾadun-im (Gelb 1980, no. 4246). -NI-MI is the genitive singular -im or the plural -īm, which the script does not distinguish. With no DO sign, ʾadun- and ʾadōn- both write DU. HT 127a DU-NE-MI, whole at the head of its line, is a separate name, ḏū-naʿmi. Two attestations. Cf. A-DU-NI-TA-NA (ARKH 5), ʾadun-nittan 'the lord gave'. See DU-NE-MI.

entries.meaning: personal name: 'my kinsman / my (paternal) uncle'

cognates.Amorite: ʿAMM-IJA AM-MI-IA (Gelb AS 21 no. 735), Tuttul am-mi-ia 'My paternal ancestor' (Buck 2018, 323); ʿAMM-I+HADD-U AM-MI-A-DU, AM-MI-AD-DU (nos. 726–727); ʿAMM-I+DANN-U AM-MI-DA-NU (no. 728); ḥamm- 'paternal uncle' (Huffmon APNM 196)

entries.note: HT 115b *306+MI 1, a recipient after *306-TU-JA 1 and A-I 1. Ligature ʿA+MI: ʿAmmī, the geminate unwritten, the -ī of 'my'; a hypocoristic of the ʿAmmī-DN names, cf. Amorite ʿAMM-IJA (Gelb AS 21 no. 735). One attestation. See A-MA, A-MI-DA-U and A-MA-JA.

entries.meaning: steppe-dweller, (man) of the encampment—qualifier after a personal name

cognates.Amorite: NW *naw(u)-, *nawiy- 'steppe; encampment (man and beast)'; Mari nawûm, feminine (Huffmon APNM p. 237); BU-NU-NA-WI-E (Gelb 1980, no. 1342)
cognates.Akkadian (Ugarit, Alalakh): LÚ na-mu-ú 'steppe-dweller' (Ugarit), ERÍN.MEŠ na-me-e (Alalakh IV), personnel terms (GlOS 2, 116)
cognates.Hebrew: נָוֶה nāweh 'pasture, abode'; construct נְוֵה nᵊwēh, as נְוֵה רֹעִים 'abode of shepherds' (Jer 33:12)
cognates.Akkadian: nawû / namû 'pasturage; flocks; steppe' (ORACC CAMS/GKAB)

entries.note: HT 115b TI-NU-JA · NU-WI · GRA ½; HT 115a RI-TA-MA / NU-WI 2, under a GRA+BOSm heading, one scribe (Scribe 8). Two men carry it, so it names a class, as LÚ na-mu-ú 'steppe-dweller' at Ugarit (GlOS 2, 116). On HT 115a the copie tabulaire joins RỊ-TẠ-MẠ-NU-WI, and GORILA's note on .2 allows the divider (GORILA I 189). NU-WI writes the G participle nōwē 'migrant', Safaitic nwy 'migrating' (KRS 1949; Al-Jallad 2026, 107), with the ō of the Canaanite shift, as su₂-ki-na sōkinu 'prefect' (EA 362). Weak point: only Safaitic attests the participle. Rivals: a patronymic '(son of) Nuwī', Arabian PN nwy (Harding 1971, 604), which needs the two men to be brothers; Egyptian nw 'hunter; scout' (Wb 2, 218.19–21), as nw n tꜣ ḫꜣs.t 'hunter of the desert' (pKoller, pAnastasi; ORAEC 313, 360). See *301 and I-NA-WA.
entries.source: di Mino; GORILA I; Gelb 1980; GlOS 2; Harding 1971; Al-Jallad 2026; Wb 2; ORAEC

entries.meaning: Rimši; a personnel group named with the Amorite element rimši (Ugaritic DN rmš)

cognates.Amorite: Gelb AS 21 root RMS (unglossed): Rimši-ʾIl RI-IM-ŠI-DINGIR (no. 5285) and Rimši-ʾIli RI-IM-ŠI-I₃-LI₂ (no. 5286), Mari; feminine ʾAnnu-rimši AN-NU-RI-IM-ŠI (no. 831, Mari) and Kakka-rimši KA-AK-KA-RI-IM-ŠI (no. 3912); same root Ramaši RA-MA-SI (FN), Ramišum RA-MI-SUM

entries.note: HT 119 RI-MI-SI 13, a group in a personnel list. /rimši/ matches the Amorite element in Rimši-ʾIl, Rimši-ʾIli, ʾAnnu-rimši, Kakka-rimši (Gelb 1980, nos. 5285–5286, 831, 3912); Gelb leaves RMŠ unglossed, Sanmartín reads rimš 'moving, setting in motion', with Ebla ra-maš (GlOS 2, 167). Ugaritic rmš is a divine name receiving a ram (š l rmš) in KTU 1.46:13, 1.109:7, 1.130:21 (DULAT 730). One attestation.

entries.meaning: personal name, Amorite type (quwy- 'wait for, hope'); rival 'be strong'

cognates.Amorite: Gelb AS 21 root QWJ (unglossed): Quwyum KU-IA-UM (no. 4109), KU-WU-UM (no. 4188); -at- form Kuyatum KU-IA-TUM (no. 4108); theophorics Quwi-Dagan KU-U₂-D-DA-GAN (no. 4145), Quwi-Haddu KU-U₂-D-IM (no. 4146, Mari), Quwi-Yaraḫ KU-WE-RA-AH (no. 4187), KU-UM-D-U (no. 4162, Ugarit MRS XVI 9:7)
cognates.Hebrew: קָוָה qāwāh 'wait for, hope' (HALOT 1082); קַוֵּה אֶל־יְהוָה 'wait for YHWH' (Ps 27:14)
cognates.Akkadian: quʾʾû 'to wait' (CAD Q 328)

entries.note: HT 119 KO-JA 10, after RI-MI-SI 13, in a personnel list (Scribe 9). Qōya, a hypocoristic on qōy-, quy- with -a, the Amorite -ya type, from qwy 'wait for, hope': Amorite Quwi-Haddu, imperative and divine name (Gelb 1980, no. 4146); Heb. qāwāh 'wait for, hope' (HALOT 1082), as qawwēh ʾel-YHWH 'wait for YHWH' (Ps 27:14); Akk. quʾʾû 'to wait' (CAD Q 328). Cuneiform has no o, so Gelb's KU- spellings fit qō as well as qu; KO writes qō from *qaw- with aw > ō, or qu, as RO writes ru in SA-RO beside SA-RU šarru. Rival: 'be strong', Arab. qawiya (Lane 2997). Weak point: two signs, one witness. See JA-KU and JA-KU-TI.
entries.source: di Mino; Gelb 1980; HALOT; CAD Q; Lane

entries.meaning: Kiriš, the god of the Amorite names, as oil recipient; rivals Hurrian Kiriš and a personal name

cognates.Amorite: Gelb AS 21 glossary 'Kiriš, Kirišu, DN' (root KRS); ʾAwij-Kiriš A-WI-KI-RI-IŠ (no. 563; ARM XIV 106:18) and Iluna-Kiriš (no. 2556; ARM XIII 8:19 = LAPO 16 no. 104), Mari, Zimri-Lim era. Kiri(š) in 2 women's and 5 men's name types (Nakata 1995, Orient 30–31, charts pp. 251–252); seal of Iluna-Kiriš, servant of Zimri-Lim (Topçuoğlu 2016 no. 251 = Otto 2000 fig. 435)
cognates.Linear B: qe-ra-si-ja (KN Fp 1+31, 5, 6, 13, 14, 48; fem. dat., oil offerings beside pa-si-te-o-i), masc. qe-ra-si-jo (KN Fp 16.2): comparandum, not identity (KI/QE, RI/RA)
cognates.Hurrian: Gelb 1944 (Hurrians and Subarians, 113) parses Ur III Pudum-kiriš as Hurrian kir + -š; Karana ki-ri-šu Kirišu, in Monti's Hurrian list (Monti 2017, 390)

entries.note: TY 3b (Tylissos, LM IB): KI-RI-SI OLE+MI 6 heads side b of an oil-distribution tablet whose other recipients are PI-KU-ZU, ZA-*321, A-DU, A-DA and KO-A-DU-WA. SI writes the final š. Kiriš, Kirišu, a god of the Amorite names (Gelb 1980, 23): ʾIlunā-kirišu 'Kiriš is our god' at Tuttul (Buck 2018, 338; Gelb 1980, no. 2556) and A-WI-KI-RI-IŠ at Mari (ARM 14 106:18; Gelb 1980, no. 563). Rival: Hurrian, where Awi-kiriš reads 'Kiriš, save him!' and Putum-kiriš 'Kiriš begot him' (Monti 2017, 115, 111), and kiriš stands beside Kirip-atal and Nuzi Kirip-tilla (Gelb 1944, 113). Rival: a personal name. Cf. Linear B qe-ra-si-ja, an oil recipient at Knossos, with ra where KI-RI has ri. Weak point: the god is known only from names. One attestation.
entries.source: di Mino; Gelb 1980; Buck 2018; Monti 2017; Gelb 1944

entries.meaning: the Eastern (place), a central Cretan toponym; rivals the epithet 'she of the East' and a pre-Greek toponym Setoiya

cognates.Akkadian: ṣītum / ṣīt šamšim 'sunrise, east' (Huehnergard 1997, glossary); ṣītān 'at sunrise' (ORACC CAMS/GKAB); Ebla balri ṣīt šamši 'on the east bank' (EDA I, P0477)
cognates.Hebrew: ṣēʾt (צֵאת) 'going out', kə-ṣēʾt ha-šemeš (Judg 5:31); gentilic of 'east': haq-Qadmōnî (Gen 15:19), hay-yām haq-qadmônî 'the eastern sea' (Ezek 47:18)

entries.note: PR Za 1, formula slot 2, the site-specific slot (cf. TU-RU-SA at Kophinas, O-SU-QA-RE at Tylissos, I-DA-MI at Syme): 'at Ṣētiya', the place. Linear B writes the same spelling, se-to-i-ja, a Knossos toponym on 17 tablets (As 40+5093, As 1516, Dc 5687+, Lc 525, Le 654, Mc 4464+, Sd 4407+ and others; DMic II 288). √y-ṣ-ʾ (K0448): ṣēt 'the East' with the gentilic -iya of SU-KI-RI-TE-I-JA; SE writes the ē of Hebrew ṣēʾt (Judg 5:31), SI-TE Ṣīt the ī. East with a gentilic names a people in haq-Qadmōnî 'the Kadmonites' (Gen 15:19) and a sea in hay-yām haq-qadmônî 'the eastern sea' (Ezek 47:18). Rivals: an epithet 'she of the East'; a pre-Greek toponym Setoiya.

entries.meaning: personal name: 'Sîn has gathered in / laid up (the child)'—verb + DN sentence name

cognates.Akkadian: kamāsu A 'to gather in', D kummusu (CAD K 114); moon-god Suen/Sîn, OB {d}suen, su₂-en, zu-en.
cognates.Amorite: Gelb AS 21 glossary KMS "to hide"; nouns kamisum, kumisum, kumsum; names KAMIS-UM (nos. 1745, 3971, 3972), JA-KMIS-I Yakmisi (no. 2910), KUMS-AJA (no. 4163). Sîn in Amorite names is a Mesopotamian borrowing: cult at Mari, treaty in his temple at Ḥarran, Ḥa-an-na-EN.ZU (Huffmon 1965, 35, 273).
cognates.Hebrew: kāmus "laid up" // ḥātûm "sealed" (Deut 32:34; HALOT 481); sense parallel Ṣəpanyāh "Yah has treasured" (√ṣ-p-n).

entries.note: PK 1 .3–4, a one-each roster sorted by first sign; SI on the right edge, I-NA at the left margin (GORILA I 280–281; SigLA side b). Ukammis-Sîn 'Sîn has laid up': O the u- of the D preterite, KA-MI kamm-, ZA the final s, SI-I-NA Sîn (Suen > Sîn). Akkadian kamāsu A 'to gather, to bring in' (CAD K 114), Hebrew kāmus 'stored up' (Deut 32:34; HALOT 481); Amorite names on KMS: JA-KMIS-I, KAMIS-UM, KUMIS-AN (Gelb 1980, 23; nos. 2910, 3971, 4116). Sibling frame U-KA-RE-A-SE-SI-NA (PE 1). O writes u, as RO writes ru in SA-RO beside SA-RU šarru; PE 1 U-KA- writes the same u-. Sîn as in the Mari names Erîb-Sîn and Narâm-Sîn (ARM 26/1, 595; FM I, 155). One attestation.
entries.source: di Mino; CAD K; HALOT; Gelb 1980; ARM 26/1; FM I

entries.meaning: I weep (G prefix form, 1cs); rival ʾabakki (G present)

cognates.Hebrew: G 1cs ʾebkeh 'I weep' (Isa 16:9; Jer 48:32); wāʾebkeh 'and I wept' beside prayer (Neh 1:4); D-stem bikkâ 'bewail': məbakkôt ʾet-hattammûz, women bewailing Tammuz (Ezek 8:14)
cognates.Akkadian: bakû 'weep' (ORACC CAMS; 3cs preterite ibki, so 1cs abki); a-bak-ki = G present 1cs abakki (ORACC P273162, P338383)
cognates.Ugaritic: bky 'weeping, lament'; G prefix ỉbky, ảky, tbky, ybky (DULAT 217f.)
cognates.Eblaite: da-ba-ga tabkay, G prefix; ib-gi yibkī, a name (GlOS 1, 115)
cognates.Geʿez: bäkäyä 'flere, plorare, lamentari' (Dillmann 1865, no. 4035), imperfect of the yəqättəl type

entries.note: KN Zb 40 .1 A-PA-KI, then U-NA-A, incised on a pithoid jar from the Unexplored Mansion, Knossos, in an LM II destruction deposit, the jar typologically LM I and the inscription LM IB (Popham 1976, 102–106, apud Owens 1998–99, 148), with a domestic shrine and a goddess figurine on the upper floor (Owens 1998–99, 148). A writes the 1cs ʾa- (as in ʾata-inawaya), PA b with a dead vowel, KI kī: ʾabkī, the G prefix form, Heb. ʾebkeh 'I weep' (Isa 16:9; Jer 48:32). A- marks the G, since a D 1cs takes ʾu- (Ar. ʾu-, Fischer 2002, §211b; Akk. ubakka). Rivals: the G present ʾabakki, which fills every vowel, Akk. a-bak-ki (ORACC P273162, P338383), Geʿez bäkäyä 'flere, lamentari' (Dillmann 1865, no. 4035) with the yəqättəl imperfect (Gragg 1997, Table 13.3), a present East and South Semitic keep and Central Semitic lost, and ʾa-pak- 'jug, bottle', Heb. pak, a small flask (HALOT 926), a poor fit for a pithoid jar, with Ug. bk 'beaker' (DULAT 216). Weak point: a lament on a household storage jar rests on the shrine context. One attestation.
entries.source: di Mino; GlOS 1; Owens 1998–99; HALOT; DULAT

entries.meaning: and here, hither

cognates.Ugaritic: hnh 'hither?' (reading uncertain; possibly hn + terminative -h), beside hnn 'here' (Tropper §81.11a-b)

entries.note: KN Zb 40 .2, under A-PA-KI. U-NA- as in U-NA-KA-NA-SI and U-NA-RU-KA-NA-TI, w- + hn (di Mino, Ya Diktu); final A = -ā(h), as Hebrew hēnnâ 'here, hither' (Gen 45:8), Ugaritic hnh 'hither?' (Tropper §81.11a). Rival: hunāha without the conjunction. See U-NA.

entries.meaning: of the (olive-)press, press-estate (nisbe -ī on gitt- 'press; farmstead, estate')

cognates.Ugaritic: gt /gittu/ 'wine or olive press; farmstead, estate' (DULAT 307)
cognates.Hebrew: gat (גַּת) 'winepress'; gittî 'Gittite, of Gath' (2 Sam 6:10), pl. gittîm (2 Sam 15:18), the same nisbe

entries.note: KI for /gi/, TA for /tt/, -I for the nisbe -ī. HT 123+124a, two joining palimpsest fragments (GORILA I 210–211): KI-TA-I · OLIV 31, *308 8¼, KI-RO 1, the first of four parties in an olive and pressed-oil account beside PU-*131A, SA-RU (šarru) and DA-TU; KU-RO OLIV 93½. A press-estate fits as a party beside a royal establishment: Ug. gt 'press; farmstead, estate' (DULAT 307). Rival: a personal or institutional name. One attestation; HT 29 has [?]-KI-TA, a name. See *312-TA.

entries.meaning: provisions (cf. Heb. ṣêdâ, travelling provision)

cognates.Akkadian: ṣidītu 'viaticum, travel provisions' (CAD Ṣ 172)

entries.note: ARKH 2 .1, intact: SI-DA-TE heads the tablet without a numeral over a must list, KU-RA *131B 5, then A-SI-DA-TO-I 12, ZU-*301-SE-DE-*21F-*118 6, A-SU-PU-WA 4, RU-MI[ (GORILA III 7). Heb. ṣêdâ 'food for a journey' (Gen 42:25; Josh 1:11; HALOT 1021), Ug. ṣd 'hunt, game' (DULAT 767). SI writes the i of Akk. ṣidītu 'viaticum, travel provisions' (CAD Ṣ 172), Heb. ṣêdâ the contracted ē; TE the feminine -t. Rival: a personal name or party heading, as on HT 20 and HT 16; cf. SI-DA-RE (HT 17, HT 122a). One attestation. See SE-*305 and MA-SI-DU.
entries.source: di Mino; HALOT; DULAT; CAD Ṣ

entries.meaning: Arwad (island city of the Phoenician coast), an entity in a transfer
entries.note: KH 5: A-DA-KI-SI-KA · A-RA-U-DA · over WI-SA-SA-NE CYP+E 2, VINb+WI 2, then WI-NA-DU · *301-NA ·, KU-PA-ZU CYP 3. Hogan reads the tablet as one transfer of CYP+E and VINb+WI to several entities, A-RA-U-DA among them (Hogan, in Salgarella and Petrakis, The Wor(l)ds of Linear A, 81): an entity slot, which a place fills. RA-U writes /raw/, as A-I writes /ay/: all four consonants ʾ-r-w-d stand in order, and SigLA reads U (AB10), not AU. Late Bronze Ugarit writes the gentilic {iri}a-ru-a-di-yu (RS 19.0042) with the same u for w. Rival: the personal name ʾArōd (Num 26:17). One attestation.

entries.meaning: personal name (cf. Hebrew ʿAttay)
entries.note: A recipient on three tablets: the HT 9a/9b wine roster (10, 8), the same roster on HT 122a (1[, with PA-DE and *324-DI-RA), and the HT 119 personnel count (2, before *327-JU 8 and KU-RO 160). *306 at the proposed value ʿa, and TU writes -tu with the geminate unwritten: ʿAttu, cf. Heb. ʿAttay (1 Chr 2:35), the short form of ʿĂtāyāh (Neh 11:4), Palm. f. ʿty, Greek Αθθαια, which writes the geminate (HALOT 903), and Pun. ʿTʾ (Benz 1972, 388). The name slot is secure. ʿĂtāyāh 'Yahweh has shown himself as surpassing', from Arb. ʿatā (Noth, apud HALOT 903), whose usual sense is 'to be insolent, unruly' (HALOT 903; Lane 1951). Weak point: *306 = ʿa is a proposed value. *306-TU-JA (HT 115b) is the same name with hypocoristic -ya. See *306-TU-JA.

entries.meaning: personal name, hypocoristic of *306-TU in -ya
entries.note: HT 115b *306-TU-JA 1, whole and undotted, between KU-RU-MA · I ½ and A-Ị-[··] 1̣, on a palimpsest (GORILA I 191); *306+MI stands on the same face. *306-TU (HT 9a, 9b, 119, 122a) with hypocoristic -ya, cf. Heb. ʿAttay (1 Chr 2:35); the -ya of Amorite ʿAMM-IJA (Gelb 1980, no. 735), as *306+MI ʿAmmī on the same face. Weak point: -ya is also Hurrian and Akkadian. Rival: a Hurrian name in -ya. One attestation.

entries.meaning: personal name, Amorite type (yaqtul of QWJ)

cognates.Amorite: JA-QWUJ-U, written ia-ku-ú (Gelb 1980, no. 3314); JA-QWUJ-UM, ia-ku-ú-um and ia-ku-um (nos. 3315, 3317); JA-QWUJ-JA, ia-ku-ia (nos. 3300–3301)

entries.note: MA 2b: ]-RE-TI 4, ]TI 1, JA-KU 2, TI[, a roster of small whole numbers on a three-sided bar (DU-RA 5 on face a). JA-KU matches Amorite ia-ku-ú (Gelb 1980, no. 3314) sign for sign: final *-y is lost in both, and /qu/ is written KU. Same root as KO-JA. JA-KU-TI (KN 1a) carries the same base. Rival: JA-KWUN-U, ia-ku-nu (Gelb 1980, no. 3309), with final n unwritten. Two signs, one attestation.

entries.meaning: personal name, Amorite type: base JA-KU with -TI

cognates.Amorite: JA-QWUJ-U, written ia-ku-ú (Gelb 1980, no. 3314)

entries.note: KN 1a: JA-KU-TI E 240; the verso has JA-DU-RA-TI E 105 in the same layout (SigLA reads AB38, E, on both faces), so both are names. Base JA-KU (MA 2b), Amorite ia-ku-ú (Gelb 1980, no. 3314). -TI is the -at-i of Amorite hypocoristics, JIŠʿ-AT-I, IŠ-A-TI and JIŠʿ-AT-IJA, IŠ-ḪA-TI-IA (Gelb 1980, nos. 3764, 3787), as on JA-DU-RA-TI. One attestation.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Weapon' (Amorite Kakku)

cognates.Amorite: KAKK-U, written ka-ak-ku, a woman's name (Gelb 1980, no. 3913); KAKK-A+ compounds (nos. 3905–3912); kakkum, fem. kakka 'weapon', and the god Kakka (Gelb 1980, glossary)

entries.note: HT 62 .2 (GORILA I 117): ][·]-NA GRA 15¼ KA-KU 7[, a recipient after a grain entry; the 7 is Pugliese Carratelli's reading, four strokes now. Matches Amorite KAKK-U, ka-ak-ku (Gelb 1980, no. 3913), with the geminate unwritten. The same element stands first in KA-KU-NE-TE (ZA 10b). Rival: kakkum 'weapon' as a commodity, which the recipient slot does not favour. One attestation.

entries.meaning: personal or clan name, 'Flea'

cognates.Hebrew: Parʿōš (פַּרְעֹשׁ), a clan, 'the sons of Parʿōš' (Ezra 2:3; HALOT 971); parʿōš 'flea' (1 Sam 24:15)
cognates.Amorite: purʿušum 'flea'; PURʿUŠ-AN-U, PU-UR-ḪU-ŠA-NU, Mari (Gelb 1980, no. 5184)

entries.note: HT 20 (GORILA I 37): PA-RO-SU · heads six fraction entries (KU-MA-JU ¼, QE-KU-RE · DI ½, *21M ⅛, SA-RE-JU ⅛, WA ¼, *188+KU ½). The same scribe's HT 16 has the same layout under KA-KU-PA ·, a party, so the heading names the recipient. Parʿōš 'flea', the clan of Ezra 2:3 (HALOT 971); RO writes rʿō with ʿ lost. Rival: parsu 'portion, dry measure' (Ug. prs, DULAT 671), which leaves RO unexplained. HT 104 .3–4 PA-DA-SU-TI 29 is a candidate for PA-RO-SU-TI, this name with -TI, in a list of X-TI entries (GORILA I 171; Schoep 2002, 47). One attestation.
entries.source: di Mino; HALOT; DULAT; GORILA I; Schoep 2002

entries.meaning: personal name, 'with me (is God)', hypocoristic in -aya (cf. Hebrew ʾIttay)

cognates.Hebrew: ʾIttay (אִתַּי), Ittai the Gittite (2 Sam 15:19; HALOT 102); Ittai son of Ribai (2 Sam 23:29)
cognates.Old Babylonian: it-ta-ia Ittāya, a woman at Kiš (de Boer 2014, 402)
cognates.Linear B: i-ta-ja, a woman (KN Ap 769.2); o-pi i-ta-ja[ (KN Od 537.3)

entries.note: HT 28a: I-TA-JA OLE+DI 10, the last recipient of the A-SI-JA-KA list, after A-RU-DA-RA GRA 5. Gemination unwritten; -aya written JA. Hebrew ʾIttay, the short form of ʾItīʾēl 'With me is God', Akk. Ili-ittia (HALOT 102, 44): Ittai the Gittite, who marches with the Cherethites and Pelethites (2 Sam 15:18–19), and Ittai the Benjaminite (2 Sam 23:29). Rival: Noth's 'El exists' (HALOT 44). Linear B i-ta-ja is a woman's name at Knossos (KN Ap 769.2): the name outlives Linear A on Crete, which fixes the name but not its language. Two consonants, one attestation.

entries.meaning: (men) of the Kikkar, 'round district' (gentilic heading of a head-count roster)

cognates.Hebrew: kikkār (כִּכָּר) 'round district' (Gen 13:12; Neh 12:28); ʾanšê hakkikkār 'the men of the Kikkar' (Neh 3:22); also 'round loaf' (1 Sam 2:36)

entries.note: HT 85b: KI-KI-RA-JA · heads the face over eleven entries of one unit each (KI-RE-TA₂ 1, QE-KA 1 … WA-DU-NI-MI 1, MA-DI 1, QA-*310-I 1). HT 85a is headed A-DU · *307+*307 · VIR+[?], so the tablet counts men, and a group label fits the heading. -JA writes the gentilic -āya: the men of the Kikkar, kikkār 'territory around a place', as the Kikkar of the Jordan (Gen 13:10; HALOT 473). KI-KI-RA writes kikkər-, the stem before an ending, as construct kikkəráyim 'two talents' (2 Kgs 5:23). Rivals: kikkār 'round loaf' (1 Sam 2:36; HALOT 473), one to each man; a personal name heading the roster. KE-KI-RU (HT 94b) is on the same root. One attestation.

entries.meaning: large vessel (vessel label)

cognates.Akkadian: kirru A (DUG.KIR) 'a large vessel of earthenware, metal or stone', from Old Akkadian on (CAD K 408–410)
cognates.Hebrew: kiyyôr (כִּיֹּר) 'pot, basin, laver' (1 Sam 2:14; Exod 30:18), rival

entries.note: MI Zb 1, incised on the base of a clay vase (Copenhagen NM 6960): KI-RU, two signs, nothing else (GORILA IV 91). Akk. kirru A, a large vessel of earthenware, metal or stone for water, beer, oil, wine, honey or perfume, from Old Akkadian on; perfume kirrātu among Tušratta's gifts (EA 22 iii 36) (CAD K 408–410). KI-RU writes kirru, the geminate unmarked. Rival: Heb. kiyyôr 'basin, laver' (Exod 30:18), Akk. kiūru 'metal cauldron', a Neo-Assyrian foreign word (CAD K 476), which needs an unwritten y; or an owner's mark. One attestation.

entries.meaning: personal name (Hurrian); cf. Linear B ta-ta-ro, Mari ᶠTatara

cognates.Hurrian: Tatara, ta-da-ra, a woman at Mari, Hurrian with a query (Monti 2017, 302)
cognates.Akkadian: (f) Tadara, ta-da-ra, a musician at Mari (FM IV, 284)
cognates.Linear B: ta-ta-ro, a man on the Knossos roster KN As(1) 607, also KN Pp 498, PY Eb 874, Eo 224, Ep 301

entries.note: PK 1 .2 TA₂-TA-RE 1, a single-unit entry in a column of names, TA₂ distinct from TA (GORILA I 281). Linear B ta-ta-ro is a man on the Knossos roster KN As(1) 607.2 (VIR 1), also KN Pp 498, Xd 8605 and PY Eb 874, Ep 301.6, Eo 224.7. Final -RE answers Linear B -ro as in A-RA-NA-RE / a-ra-na-ro (KN As 1516), PA-JA-RE / pa-ja-ro (KN As 1519) and NA-DA-RE / no-da-ro (KN As 609), all on the same roster series. Mari ᶠTatara, ta-da-ra, a woman, Hurrian with a query (Sasson 1974, 370; ARM XVI/1, 201; Monti 2017, 302); TA₂-TI-TE Tati-te, Hurrian, two lines below. One attestation.

entries.meaning: Beloved (personal name, √d-w-d + -ma); rival the Aegean name of the Keftiu board and Linear B di-du-me

cognates.Hebrew: dûdāʾîm 'mandrakes, love-apples' (Gen 30:14; Song 7:14), the u-ā form of √d-w-d
cognates.Amorite: DAWD-U*MA, DA-DU-MA (Gelb 1980, no. 1433); DAWD-A (no. 1413)
cognates.Egyptian: {d-j}-d-ȝ-d-ȝ-m{a}, an 'Aegean' beneficiary of a wine account, BM EA 5647 v. I 3a (Dautais & Gabolde 2025, 14–15); Schneider reads it Semitic *Mudādum 'Beloved' (apud Dautais & Gabolde 2025, 14)
cognates.Linear B: di-du-me (KN L 588), di-du-mo (KN X 5751, MY Oe 129) (Dautais & Gabolde 2025, Table 1)

entries.note: HT 6b .4 DU-DA-MA 66, the largest entry in a list of names, on a face written over an erasure; DU-DA-MA itself shows no undertext (GORILA I 13). dū-dā-ma, the vowels of Heb. dûdāʾîm 'love-apples', √d-w-d 'beloved', + -ma as in the Amorite name DA-DU-MA, Dawdu-ma (Gelb 1980, no. 1433). One attestation. See TA-DI.

entries.meaning: Qaṣṣāru 'Fuller' (personal name); compare Linear B ka-sa-ro; rival Kaṣṣāru 'donkey driver'

cognates.Eblaite: ga-za-ru₁₂, a personal name, read /qaṣṣāru/ 'fuller' or /kaṣṣāru/ 'donkey driver' (Pagan 1998, rows 1979–1980)
cognates.Arabic: qaṣṣār 'one who beats and washes and whitens clothes' (Lane 2535); qaṣṣara 'he beat, washed, and whitened the cloth' (Lane 2534)
cognates.Syriac: qāṣrā 'fuller' (HALOT 819, s.v. ʿên rōgēl 'spring of the fuller')
cognates.Linear B: ka-sa-ro, a man at Knossos, KN C(2) 912, Dv 1450

entries.note: HT 10b .3 KA-SA-RU 6, a personnel entry on a face written over an erasure; the three signs are clear (GORILA I 21). Ebla ga-za-ru₁₂, read /qaṣṣāru/ 'fuller' or /kaṣṣāru/ 'donkey driver' (Pagan 1998, rows 1979–1980), sign for sign with its vowels; Sanmartín files ga-za-ru₁₂ under q-ṣ-r 'to be short' (GlOS 1, 355). Linear B ka-sa-ro is a man's name at Knossos (KN C(2) 912.8, Dv 1450), with no Greek interpretation; final -RU against Linear B -ro, as I-TA-NU against u-ta-no. Ugarit has DUMU ka-ša₂-ri (ORACC P503760). Rivals: Kaṣṣāru 'donkey driver'; Amorite Kašerum (Gelb 1980, no. 4000), √kṯr (3548), which needs S for ṯ, against KA-TA-RE. One attestation.

entries.meaning: provisions (list heading); rival a personal name, cf. Linear B ma-si-dwo
entries.note: HT 43 .1 MA-SI-DU ·, all three signs whole, heading the tablet before PA-*342-I · I GRA+PA 5̣[ (GORILA I 83). maṣīdu 'provisions': Ug. mṣd '(feast of) game' (DULAT 578), Heb. ṣêdâ 'provisions' (HALOT 1021); SI writes ṣi. Rival: a personal name, cf. Linear B ma-si-dwo, a man at Knossos (KN Fh 360.b; DMic I s.v.), with -Cu for Linear B -Co (Woudhuizen 2016, 218). One attestation. See SE-*305 and SI-DA-TE.

entries.meaning: dignitary, prince (title of a recipient); rival a personal name

cognates.Amorite: razinum (Gelb 1980, glossary); RAZIN-IM, RA-ZI-NI-IM (no. 5268)

entries.note: HT 11b .4 RU-ZU-NA KA 30, whole and undotted (GORILA I 23), the fourth of five KA entries that KU-RO 180 totals, before SA-QE-RI · KA 30. Heb. rōzēn 'dignitary, prince' (HALOT 1210); Ar. razuna 'was weighty, grave' (Lane 1079) fixes the PS *z, which ZU writes beside ṯ. Woudhuizen (2016, 223–224) reads the same word. Rival: a personal name. One attestation.

entries.meaning: personal name; compare Egyptian rw-sȝ, one of the 'names of Crete' on BM EA 5647; rival Egyptian Rs 'he who is awake'

cognates.Egyptian: rw-sȝ, the seventh of the 'names of Crete' on the writing board BM EA 5647, r. I 7 (Dautais and Gabolde 2025, 14–15); rs '(he) who is awake', late 12th–18th Dynasty (PNM v6, personal_names_id 142607501; Ranke I, 226.18; II, 303.1)

entries.note: HT 96a .3 RU-SA 4, whole and undotted, after SI-MI-TA GRA 5 and before *323-*317 1, with no logogram of its own (GORILA I 157). Rusa: the writing board BM EA 5647 heads seven 'names of Crete' (jr.t rn.w n[y.w] kftjw), and the seventh, rw-sȝ (r. I 7), is ru-sa sign for sign (Dautais and Gabolde 2025, 9, 14–15, table 2). Rivals: Greek Lysis, Linear B ru-si, as the editors take rw-sȝ; a short Egyptian name, rw-zA (Louvre E 5608), as Schneider takes it (ibid., 14 nn. 87–88); Egyptian Rs '(he) who is awake' (Ranke I, 226.18; II, 303.1), 59 attestations, late 12th to 18th Dynasty (Ilin-Tomich 2025), which Vercoutter reads on the board, Rs (Ru-sa), 'vraisemblablement égyptien' (Vercoutter 1956, 45, 48). Linear B has ru-si at Knossos (KN Ak 634) and ru-si-qe on KN L 588.1, the tablet with di-du-me on .3, which the board's {d-j}-d-ȝ-d-ȝ-m and DU-DA-MA match (DMic II s.v. ru-si). Two signs; one attestation.
entries.source: di Mino; GORILA I; Dautais and Gabolde 2025; Vercoutter 1956; Ranke; Ilin-Tomich 2025; DMic II

entries.meaning: personal name, 'enduring'; compare Linear B a-ti-ka

cognates.Eblaite: a-ti-gu ʿatīq 'old', AL₆.GÍD = a-ti-gu-um (GlOS 1, 93); a-ti-ga, a name (EbDA, ARET 20 0014)

entries.note: ZA Wc 2, a Zakros roundel: .1 A-TI-KA-A, .2 DỤ-KO-⟦MI⟧, the signs of .1 evenly spaced; GORILA divides A-TI-KA · A-DU-KO-⟦MI⟧ (GORILA II 98). Perna and Anastasiadou, after autopsy, read the last sign as the numeral 2, matching the two seal impressions on the rim (CMS II,7 no. 25; Anastasiadou 2026, 37–39). Ugaritic ʿtq 'durable', syllabic at-qá (DULAT 189); Safaitic personal name ʿtq (Harding 1971, 405). Linear B a-ti-ka is a man at Knossos (KN V 831.4; DMic I 119). One attestation. See *306-TI-KA-A-RE.
entries.source: di Mino; DULAT; Harding 1971; DMic I 119; CMS II,7; Anastasiadou 2026, 37–39, in Salgarella & Petrakis (eds.) 2026; GlOS 1; EbDA

entries.meaning: bundle, bag (commodity or container)

cognates.Ugaritic: mṣrr(t) 'a piece of fabric or a garment' (DULAT 581); 'bundle, parcel' (GlOS 2, 224)

entries.note: HT 30 .3 SA-RA-RA ½: three separate signs, both RA of the plain form (RA₂ in SA-RA₂ on .1), on a tablet written over an erasure, between QA2+[?]+PU ⅕ and *23M 1 (GORILA I 57). The tablet lists commodities with fractions and no names. Heb. I צְרוֹר 'little pack, bag', for money (Gen 42:35) and myrrh (Song 1:13), JArm. Syr. ṣərārā 'bundle, bag', Arab. ṣurrat 'purse' (HALOT 1054). Rival: a personal name (Heb. Šārār, 2 Sam 23:33), against the slot. One attestation.

entries.meaning: personal name, as Ugaritic Kušinu (kṯn)

cognates.Ugaritic: kṯn (I) PN, syllabic ku-ši-nu (RS 15.09 B I 7; Kinlaw 1967, 76), ki-še-na (RS 16.131; Kinlaw 1967, 73), ki-ši-na (DULAT s.v. kṯn (I))
cognates.Hebrew: Kûšān (כּוּשָׁן) (Hab 3:7), Kûšan Rišʿātayim (Judg 3:8), compared with Ugaritic kṯn (II) (Dijkstra, apud DULAT)

entries.note: HT 13 KU-ZU-NI 18, in the KA-U-DE-TA wine list beside TE-TU (Ugaritic tt); HT 85a KU-ZU-NI 5, in a roster counted in men; both tablets also list DA-SI-*118 and TE-KE/TE-KI. ZU writes ṯ as in ZU-DI ṯudī and A-ZU-RA ʾAṯirat: KU-ZU-NI spells Ugaritic kṯn, syllabic ku-ši-nu (RS 15.09 B I 7; Kinlaw 1967, 76), ki-še-na, ki-ši-na, etym. unc. (DULAT s.v. kṯn (I)). Cf. kṯn (II), compared with Hebrew Kûšān (Hab 3:7; Judg 3:8; Dijkstra, apud DULAT s.v. kṯn (II)). Rival: Ug. ktn 'tunic' (DULAT 464), which has t, not ṯ.

entries.meaning: in flasks (preposition bi- + kuṯ 'flask, jar'; heading of an oil section)

cognates.Ugaritic: kṯ 'a measure and a container ("flask, bottle, jar")': kṯm ššmn 'two flasks(?) of (cream of) sesame', KTU 4.60:8; kṯ ẓrw kṯ nbt 'a flask(?) of balsam (and) a flask(?) of honey', KTU 1.148:22; ʕšr kṯt, KTU 6.12:2 (DULAT 466)
cognates.Akkadian: kišu B '(a metal bowl)': 1 ki-iš kaspi, between bīt šamni 'oil lamp' and ḫubunnu, EA 14 i 37 (CAD K 463)

entries.note: TY 3b .2–.4 PI-KU-ZU OLE+KI 4, OLE+MI 11, OLE+NE 2, the ruled section after KI-RI-SI OLE+MI 6 (GORILA I 329); KU and ZU drawn whole on the worn surface of the facsimile. PI the proclitic bi- 'in', as PA₃-E bē; KU-ZU kuṯ, ZU for ṯ as in KU-ZU-NI Kuṯinu: three oils counted in kṯ-flasks, the Ugaritic flask for sesame, balsam and cumin (DULAT 466). Weak points: PI for the proclitic bi- has no second witness; the vowel of kṯ is unknown. One attestation.

entries.meaning: personal name; Egyptian pꜣ.jj, the first element of PA-JA-RE

cognates.Egyptian: pꜣ.jj, a name borne by men and women, late 12th–18th Dynasty before Amenhotep IV (PNM v6, personal_names_id 142610149; Ranke I, 129.4)

entries.note: HT 41a .4 MI-DA-NI · PA-JA 2 and two fraction signs, both signs whole and undotted, the last line of the face (GORILA I 79). Egyptian Pꜣjj is a common name, borne under Thutmose III and Amenhotep II among others (PNM v6, s.v. pꜣjj); PA-JA-RE (HT 8b, 29, 88, ZA 10b) reads Pꜣjj-Rꜥ with the same JA. Egyptian two-consonant names are many, so the match rests on the identity with PA-JA-RE. Rival: a Semitic hypocoristic. Two signs; one attestation.
entries.source: Ilin-Tomich 2025 (PNM v6), s.v. pꜣjj; di Mino

entries.meaning: personal name 'redeemer' (p-d-y); recipient of wine

cognates.Ugaritic: pdy (II), a name, syll. pa-di/dì-ya, etym. unc. (DULAT 653); pādiy 'redeemer, ransomer' (GlOS 2, 123)

entries.note: HT 9a SA-RO · TE · VIN · PA-DE · 5¾, the first entry of the wine roster; HT 9b PẠ-DẸ 3, both signs dotted (GORILA I 18–19); HT 122a PA-DE 1. HT 122a recopies the HT 9 roster, so the three are one context. Ugaritic pdy (II) is a personal name, spelled syllabically pa-di/dì-ya, etym. unc. (DULAT 653); Padi is also the king of Ekron in Sennacherib's annals (RINAP 3, Sennacherib 4). DE writes the final ī. Rival: pa-de, a divine recipient at Knossos (KN Fp 1, Fp 48; DMic II 65–66), which Landau compares with PA-DE (Landau, Namen 94, apud DMic II 66).
entries.source: di Mino; DULAT; DMic II; RINAP 3; Pagan 1998; GlOS 2

entries.meaning: Taanach (place name); rival a personal name

cognates.Hebrew: Taʿnak 'Taanach', melek taʿnak ʾeḥād 'the king of Taanach, one' (Josh 12:21; HALOT 1770)
cognates.Akkadian: {uru}Ta-aḫ-n[a-k]a, Amarna, EA 248:14 (RGTC 12/2, 281, s.v. *Taʿannaku)
cognates.Egyptian: Tʿnk in the Thutmose III list, Urk IV 650:10 (RGTC 12/2, 281)

entries.note: HT Wc 3004 and HT Wc 3005, two roundels by one scribe, each reading TA-NI-KA with SE (GORILA II 73): one context. Taanach is Hebrew Taʿnak (HALOT 1770; Josh 12:21; 17:11; 21:25; Judg 1:27) and Amarna URU Taḫnaka, EA 248:14, 'perhaps biblical Taanach' (Moran 1992, index). The name is a taqtal of ʿ-n-k, Arabic ʿanak 'closure of a door' (Boehmer, apud HALOT 1769, which calls it questionable). ʿ is unwritten, NI writes the a, and a Canaanite town on Haghia Triada roundels is unexplained. Rival: a local personal name.

entries.meaning: personal name '(DN) has helped', hypocoristic

cognates.Amorite: ia-še-ia (GlOS 2, 379); JIŠʿ-IJA (see note)

entries.note: KN Zg 55, a steatite disk seal (CMS II 2, no. 213): face a a boar's head and knife, face b JA-SA-JA, the whole text, SA underlined in Younger's text (Younger, Linear A Texts, Other Texts: Knossos). Amorite JŠʿ 'to help', jišʿum 'help', and the hypocoristic name Jišʿ-ija (Gelb 1980, 22; no. 3768): ʿ unwritten, -JA the hypocoristic ending. Rival: an abbreviation of JA-SA-SA-RA (Younger). One attestation. See JA-SI and JA-SI-E.
entries.source: di Mino; Gelb 1980; GlOS 2; Younger, Linear A Texts

entries.meaning: Ridāyu 'Helper, Escort' (personal name, hypocoristic)

cognates.Arabic: ridʾ 'a helper, an aider' (Lane 1065); ridʾan, Q 28:34
cognates.Eblaite: |r-d-ʔ/y| 'to lead' in names: rí-dam-ma-lik, ìr-da-um, ìr-da-ma-lik (GlOS 2, 156)

entries.note: LACH Za 1, a limestone vessel from Tel Lachish, Level VI: ]-MI(?) · RI-DA-U · SE ¾, right to left, RI-DA-U whole between dividers (Finkelberg, Uchitel and Ussishkin 1996, 195–203). The frame of KN Zb 27 DI-NA-U · VIN 17, the closest parallel: name, commodity, number. Arb. ridʾ 'helper, aider' (Lane 1065), with U writing the hypocoristic -āyu as in DI-NA-U Dīnāyu, the ʾ unwritten. Hebrew Raddai (1 Chr 2:14) is the same name type. Rival: the name of a vessel or its contents, from ri-da-(wa)-*65 round *309 on TY 2 (GORILA V 76), groups the GORILA I reading does not keep. West Semitic names carry the root as 'to lead': Ebla rí-dam-ma-lik, ìr-da-um (GlOS 2, 156), Ugaritic rdn (DULAT 721), Akk. redû 'to accompany, lead'. Weak point: 'help' is the Arabic, Sabaic and Geʿez sense. RILA-S1 D 5 lists the inscription as doubtful. One attestation.
entries.source: di Mino; Lane; Harding 1971; Finkelberg, Uchitel and Ussishkin 1996; GlOS 2; DULAT

entries.meaning: Lyktos (place name); compare Egyptian Ri-ka-ta

cognates.Egyptian: rkt on the Kom el-Hetan Aegean list of Amenhotep III, oval 12, identified with Lyktos (Cline and Stannish 2011, 9–10)
cognates.Linear B: ru-ki-to, the town, KN Da 1288, Da 1289, Db 1279 and others

entries.note: HT 146 .4 RI-KA-TA 30, the last of four entries of 30 (]QE[ 30, RI-*305 30, MA 30); RI word-initial, TA dotted (GORILA I 241). The Kom el-Hetan list of Amenhotep III (statue base C, no. 9) writes Ri-ka-ta beside the names read as Amnisos and Knossos; Astour takes it as 'most probably identical with the Cretan Lyktos' and explains Likata as a status absolutus beside LB ru-ki-to (Astour 1966, AJA 70, 317). r/l merger; the three vowels match the Egyptian form, not LB ru-ki-to. Lyktos lies far from Haghia Triada. Rests on the dotted TA. One attestation.

entries.meaning: offering pit (for the dead)

cognates.Akkadian: apu B 'hole, opening in the ground', NA ritual pit for offerings to the dead (CAD A/2 201)
cognates.Hebrew: II ʾôb 'spirit of the dead' (HALOT s.v.); baʿălat ʾôb (1 Sam 28:7)
cognates.Hurrian: abi 'trou, fosse' (Laroche 1980, 34)
cognates.Hittite: a-a-pi 'sacrificial pit' (HALOT s.v. II ʾôb, after Rabin)

entries.note: KN Ze 16, the only word, incised at eye level on the last block of the dromos of the Kephala tholos, before the burial chamber (GORILA IV 138; Owens 1998–99, 148–149). A and PI clear; nothing before A or after PI, and the divider Owens reports after PI is not drawn. Akkadian apu B 'hole, opening in the ground', the NA ritual pit where food for the spirits of the dead is laid and honey, oil, beer and wine poured (CAD A/2 201); at Emar an offering is made before the abū (Milgrom 2000, 1768); Hebrew II ʾôb 'spirit of the dead', which Rabin derives from Hittite a-a-pi 'sacrificial pit' (HALOT s.v.; baʿălat ʾôb, 1 Sam 28:7). The word travels (Hurrian abi, Laroche 1980, 34; Hittite a-a-pi; Luwian āpit-), so it names the pit, not the writer's language; final I matches abi and needs the genitive -i in Akkadian. Rival: a personal name. One attestation.

entries.meaning: Kubariya, a town of Ugarit, (wool) of Kubariya: a section heading; rival Gubliya 'the Byblian'

cognates.Ugaritic: kbry, a town of Ugarit, syllabic URU ku-ba-ri-ia-a, RS 25.455 A+B I 4 (DULAT 424)
cognates.Akkadian: Kubariyā (RGTC 12/2, 165)

entries.note: HT 24a .1 KU-PA₃-RI-JA · KI-MA+RU[, the heading of a wool inventory; PA-SA-RI-JA heads the second section at .4. Kubariya, a town of the kingdom of Ugarit: alphabetic kbry (KTU 4.800 II 18), syllabic URU ku-ba-ri-ia-a in the town list RS 25.455A+ I 4, as van Soldt reads it, where Arnaud read URU šu-ma-ri-a (DULAT 424; RGTC 12/2, 165). KU-PA₃-RI-JA writes ku-ba-ri-ia sign for sign, PA₃ for b. The same list names Baṣīru at I 10 (RGTC 12/2, 53). Rival: Gubliya 'the Byblian', Gubla with the gentilic -iya: Amorite GUBL-AJ-I and GUBL-AJIT-UM (Gelb 1980, nos. 1793–1795); Akkadian Gublaya 'Byblian' at Ugarit (ORACC P503838); Hebrew gibli 'Gebalite'; Ugaritic gbl 'Byblos' (DULAT 290), with RI for l. One document.

entries.meaning: the Baṣirean, gentilic of Baṣīru, a town of Ugarit (Ug. bṣry): a wool section heading

cognates.Ugaritic: bṣr, a town of Ugarit, syllabic URU ba-ṣi-ri, RS 25.455 A+B I 10, 'inaccessible place' (Watson, apud DULAT 240); gentilic bṣry (DULAT 240)
cognates.Akkadian: *Baṣīru (RGTC 12/2, 53)

entries.note: HT 24a .4 PA-SA-RI-JA ·, all four signs whole, heads the second wool section as KU-PA₃-RI-JA Kubariya heads the first (GORILA I 43). Baṣīru, a town of Ugarit: alphabetic bṣr, gentilic bṣry, syllabic URU ba-ṣi-ri (DULAT 240; RGTC 12/2, 53). Both towns stand in the same lists: RS 25.455A+ I 4 and I 10, KTU 4.800 II 18 and II 29. PA for b; -JA the gentilic -iya, as bṣry. One document.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'burning, kindled'

cognates.Amorite: DALQ-UM, DALAQ-UM (Gelb 1980, nos. 1396, 1462), under DLQ 'burn': dalqum, dalaqum (Gelb AS 21, 17)

entries.note: HT 93a .6 DE-JU-KU 1½, whole and undotted, in a grain list between VIR+[·]-I 6 and O-TI-[·] 3 (GORILA I 147). Amorite DALQ-UM and DALAQ-UM (Gelb 1980, nos. 1396, 1462) and the root DLQ 'to burn' in Gelb's glossary; Hebrew dālaq 'burn'. JU writes l. Rival: √d-l-g 'leap' (Hebrew dālag), with KU for g. One document.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'glory' (feminine)
entries.note: ZA 10b .3 MA-KI-DE-TE 5, intact, between MA-ZA 5 and SA-MA 5 in a name list (GORILA III 171). Safaitic MJDT beside MJD (Harding 1971, 528); Hebrew meged 'excellence' and Magdîʾēl (Gen 36:43). With ME-KI-DI (ZA 14) the feminine and masculine of one name at one site, as Harding's MJDT and MJD. Rival: Arabian MQʿDT 'posterior, seat' (Harding 1971, 560), with ʿ unwritten. One document.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'glory' (masculine)
entries.note: ZA 14 .1 ME-KI-DI 1, intact, the first entry of a name list, before *21F-*118 1 and QA-TI-JU 8 (GORILA III 181). Safaitic MJD, feminine MJDT (Harding 1971, 528); Hebrew meged 'precious gift' (Deut 33:13; HALOT 543). The masculine of MA-KI-DE-TE (ZA 10b). Rival: Ugaritic mkt, which DULAT queries as 'immolation, offering' (DULAT 539). One document.

entries.meaning: personal name, hypocoristic in -ya

cognates.Amorite: PATIḤ-UM, PATIḤ-AH (Gelb 1980, nos. 5160–5161), under PTḤ 'open' (Gelb AS 21, 28)

entries.note: HT 6a .2–3 PI-TA-JA 24, intact, in a fig list after DA-TA-RA · TE · NI 15 (GORILA I 13). √p-t-ḥ 'open' with ḥ unwritten: Amorite PATIḤ-UM, PA-TE-ḪU-UM, and PATIḤ-AH, PA-TI-ḪA (Gelb 1980, nos. 5160–5161), Hebrew Pəṯaḥyāh. Rival: the Egyptian personal name pt.jj (Ilin-Tomich 2025, s.v.). One document.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'bear' with -ān

cognates.Akkadian: dabû, dabbu 'bear', in Old Akkadian personal names before the literary texts (CAD D 17; AHw 148)

entries.note: HT 115b .2 DU-PA₃-NA 1, whole and undotted, after TI-NU-JA · NU-WI · GRA ½ and before KU-RU-MA · I ½, on a palimpsest (GORILA I 191). Amorite DABIN-UM (Gelb 1980, no. 1411) and the root DBB in Gelb's glossary; Arabian DBN (Harding 1971, 234). Rival: Harding's own gloss, dibbān 'fly'. One document.
entries.source: di Mino; GlOS 1; CAD D; Lane

entries.meaning: personal name, 'thistle' (Hebrew Dardaʿ)

cognates.Hebrew: Dardaʿ, a wise man, wəkalkōl wədardaʿ bənê māḥôl 'and Calcol and Darda, sons of Mahol' (1 Kgs 5:11; HALOT 230)

entries.note: An entry with a numeral on four Haghia Triada tablets: HT 10a DA-RI-DA 8 before ME-ZA 3, in the KU-NI-SU list (GORILA I 21); HT 85a DA-RI-DA 12, first under A-DU · *307+*307 · VIR+[·] (GORILA I 131); HT 122a DA-RI-DA 1, last before KU-RO 31 (GORILA I 207); HT 93a DA-RI-DA *406VS 2 (GORILA I 147). Hebrew Dardaʿ (1 Kgs 5:11), with ʿ unwritten, from dardar 'thistle' by dissimilation (HALOT 230). Rival: a place or work unit, since 12 on HT 85a stands against 1 on HT 122a.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'antelope'

cognates.Hebrew: Dîšôn, Horite and Edomite clan, wədîšôn wəʾēṣer wədîšān (Gen 36:21); dîšôn 'aurochs, antelope', among the clean animals (Deut 14:5) (HALOT 221)

entries.note: HT 108 .2 DI-NA-RO 2 DU-SU-NI 4[, whole and undotted, a recipient in the grain list under KI-RE-TA-NA (GORILA I 175). Hebrew Dîšôn and Dîšān, clans of Seir (Gen 36:21), and dîšôn 'antelope' (Deut 14:5). Rival: a Hurrian name in -nni, as DA-KU-SE-NE. One document.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'chick'

cognates.Eblaite: zu-zu, PN, ṣūṣu 'chicken' (Pagan 1998, row 5285; ARET 8 525, ARET 20 22)

entries.note: HT 1 .2 ZU-SU 70, whole and undotted, the second entry under QE-RA₂-U, after KI-RO 197 and before DỊ-DI-ZA-KE 52 (GORILA I 3). The personal name zu-zu at Ebla, read ṣūṣu 'chicken' (Pagan 1998, row 5285), and at Late Bronze Ugarit (RSO 7, 3, lower edge 3; ORACC P347841). SU writes ṣ as usual, ZU as ZA does in TU-MI-TI-ZA-SE. Rivals: an opaque Zuzu, with SU for z; an institutional name in the same quantified slot. One document.

entries.meaning: personal name, '(a bird)', Akk. būṣu; rival an institution; a recipient
entries.note: A recipient at two sites: HT 123+124b .2 PI-SA 4 in a terebinth list, clean on a palimpsest face (GORILA I 213), and KH 6 .6 PI-SA[ at a line end, broken after, before CYP+D ½ (GORILA III 27). Bu-ṣí (F), with PI for b and SA for ṣ, which Huffmon sets with Bu-ṣi-ya under Akk. buṣ- (Huffmon 1965, 151 n. 37): būṣu C '(a bird)', with the Old Babylonian names Bu-ṣu-um, Bu-ṣa-a, Bu-ṣi-ia (CAD B 349). Rival: an institution receiving allocations.

entries.meaning: entity name: yidu 'strength' with TI

cognates.Eblaite: i-du-na yidu-na 'our strength' and other yidu names, i-du i₃-la yidu-ʾila 'strength is god' (Pagan 1998, rows 2460–2470)

entries.note: HT 104 .2–3 I-DU-TI 20 ½, I at the end of .2, DU-TI at the head of .3, all three signs whole and undotted, the ½ dotted (GORILA I 171). Eblaite names built on yidu 'strength', as yidu-na 'our strength' (Pagan 1998, Ebla personal names, row 2466); TI is unexplained. Rivals: I-DU followed by TI as an ideogram, which GORILA's note allows; Ida, written I-DA-A on KO Za 1. One document. See I-DU-NE-SI and JA-DI.

entries.meaning: ring text ending with the personal name ʾAyaku

cognates.Amorite: ʾAjak-u, written A-JA-KU (Gelb 1980, no. 320)

entries.note: KN Zf 13, gold ring HM 530: 19 signs in a spiral from the outer band inward, no dividers; RI (12, 15), MU (16) and KU (19) underdotted (GORILA IV 152–153). The last four signs are A-JA-KU, ʾAyaku (Amorite ʾAjak-u, Gelb 1980, no. 320); the first fifteen carry no reading, and the segmentation is not marked. Rival for the ending: Akkadian ajakku, a temple structure (CAD A/1 224–25). One document.

entries.meaning: skin, fleece (a hide with its wool)
entries.source: di Mino; CAD P; Kogan 2011; SED I; CAD B

cognates.Akkadian: paru A (parru, baru) 'skin, hide' (CAD P 209); pāru, parru, bāru 'Haut' (AHw 836)
cognates.Arabic: farw- 'fur'; farwa 'a skin, but not unless having upon it fur or wool' (Lane 2390)
cognates.Syriac: partā, pl. parrē 'bran, husk; scurf of the head' (Brock. 591)

entries.note: PH 3a .3 ]MA+RU ⅓ · PẠ-RẠ ⅓ (GORILA I 291): after the wool ligature MA+RU and the MA ligatures *556, *557 and *563, with the wool entry's ⅓ measure; a fractional measure fits a material counted by weight. PA and RA at their primary values, the geminate unwritten, both signs dotted. parr(u) 'skin, fleece': Akk. pāru, parru 'skin, hide' (CAD P 209; #1995). Rivals: *parʕ- '(loose) hair of the head' (Akk. pērtu, Heb. päraʿ; SED I No. 218), head hair rather than a traded material; *ɣapar- 'stiff hair' (Kogan 2011, 223) with its first syllable unwritten. HT 128a .1 *326 PA-RA TU-RU-NU-SE-ME GRA 10, with no quantity of its own (GORILA I 221): there a personal name, or *barr- 'grain' (Heb. bār; Akk. burru '(a cereal)', Mari, CAD B 330) with PA for /b/. Weak point: a two-sign word, so the PH 3a context, not the spelling, selects the sense.

entries.meaning: Tegi 'Beautiful' (personal name; Hurrian tagi/tegi 'beautiful')

cognates.Hurrian: tagi 'beau', RS voc. te-gi-še 'beau prix'; onom. Tagi(b)-šarri, Tagu(b)-šini, Taguya (Laroche 1980, 249–50); bare name Taki 'good', ta-gi (Mari, VHN 290), ta-ki (Šušarrā), ta-ki-e (Kaneš) (Monti 2017, 299, 413, 456); Amarna ¹ta-gi, ¹ta-a-gi, a Hurrian name (Hess 1993, no. 164)

entries.note: HT 13 .3–4 TE-KI 27½, after TE-TU 56 and before KU-ZU-NI 18, under KA-U-DE-TA VIN · TE · (GORILA I 27). HT 122a .3 TE-KI 2, before QA-*310-I 3 (GORILA I 207). HT 85a writes TE-KE 3 in the same set of units (DA-SI-*118, KU-ZU-NI), counted under VIR. Hurrian tagi 'beautiful' (Laroche 1980, 249) as a bare-stem name, as Amarna ¹ta-gi (Hess 1993, no. 164); the Ras Shamra form te-gi-še has e in the first syllable, as TE-KI does. Rival: PS *diḳ(ḳ)- 'small' (Ug. dḳ, DULAT 275). Two attestations.

entries.meaning: Tegi (personal name; spelling of TE-KI)

cognates.Hurrian: Taki 'Good': ta-ke-e, Šubat-Enlil (Monti 2017, 351); ta-gi, Mari (ibid., 299); ta-ki, Šušarrā (ibid., 413); ta-ki-e, Kaneš (ibid., 456)

entries.note: HT 85a .5 TE-KE 3, whole and undotted, sixth of seven entries under A-DU · *307+*307 · VIR+[?] ·, after KU-ZU-NI 5 (GORILA I 131). HT 13 lists DA-SI-*118, KU-ZU-NI and TE-KI in the same order; TE-KE is TE-KI with the e/i alternation. See TE-KI.

entries.meaning: personal name; Ugaritic tt, syllabic te-et-te, tu-tu

cognates.Ugaritic: tt PN, etym. unc., syllabic te-et-te, tu-ut-ti, tu-tu (DULAT 869)
cognates.Akkadian: Tette, {1}te-et-te, king of Nuḫašše, RS 17.334 (Kinlaw 1967, 119)
cognates.Hurrian: Tuttu, tu-ut-tu, Mari (Monti 2017, 308)
cognates.Egyptian: tt.w, 12th Dynasty to Thutmose III (PNM v6, personal_names_id 142606772; Ranke I, 385.27)

entries.note: HT 13 .3 TE-TU 56, whole and undotted, the largest share of the KA-U-DE-TA VIN · TE list (KU-RO 130½), beside TE-KI, KU-ZU-NI and DA-SI-*118 (GORILA I 27); HT 7a .5 TE-TU 1, TE over an erasure, under QE-TI · VIR+[?] (GORILA I 15); HT 85b .2–3 TE-TU[, broken after TU (GORILA I 133). Counted one man on two rosters: a person. Ugarit has the personal name tt, syllabic te-et-te, tu-ut-ti, tu-tu, etym. unc. (DULAT 869); Tette, king of Nuḫašše (Kinlaw 1967, 119). A pet-name type found across languages: Egyptian tt.w Tetu (Ranke I, 385.27), Hurrian Tuttu at Mari (Monti 2017, 308), Hittite Tuttu (LAMAN 4579). Rival: Egyptian Teti (Ttj). Two whole witnesses.

entries.meaning: official, commissioner (title); rival: the personal name Qīpu

cognates.Akkadian: qīpu (qēpu) s. 'official; administrator of a region, a city, a temple', from MB on, Ass. qēpu, lex. LÚ qe-e-pu (CAD Q 264); qīpu adj. 'trustworthy, trusted (person)' (CAD Q 263); qiāpu 'to believe, trust'
cognates.Nuzi: QĪPU, Ki-pu, slave of the palace (Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943, 88)

entries.note: HT 9a and 9b, the wine roster: QE-PU 2 on both faces, one of two entries unchanged (with DI-NA-U 4) while the total falls from 31¾ to 24 (GORILA I 19). QE writes q and the Assyrian ē, PU the -pu. An Akkadian title, qīpu (qēpu) 'official' (CAD Q 264), in a recipient slot beside the names Padī and Dīnāyu. Rival: the name Qīpu.

entries.meaning: Pašše (personal name; Hurrian pašš- 'send')

cognates.Nuzi: pašš 'send', with pa-aš-še, Mari 6:20; "paššija … Hypocoristic for Paššip-tilla" (Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943, 243); PAŠŠIJA, PAŠŠIŠŠE, PAŠŠI-TILLA (ibid., 112)

entries.note: HT 18 .1 PA-SE GRA+QE 20, OLE+KI 2, *304 3, a section before SA-RA₂ GRA 10, NI 10; HT 27b PA-SE · VIN+WA · SA 4, RE 70[, parallel to ]MI-DA · VIN+WA · SA 7. A section holder that never carries its own quantity. The bare name of PA-SE-JA Paššiya, as Paššiya is the hypocoristic of Pašši-tilla at Nuzi (Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943, 112, 243). Cf. PA-SE-JA.
entries.source: di Mino; Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943

entries.meaning: Paššiya (personal name; Hurrian hypocoristic on pašš- 'send')

cognates.Nuzi: PAŠŠIJA, Pa-aš-ši-ia, two bearers, one the son of Pula-ḫali who also bears Pašši-tilla (Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943, 112); "Hypocoristic for Paššip-tilla" (ibid., 243)
cognates.Hurrian: pašš- 'mander', Mitanni letter pa-aš-ši-en; paššithi 'messager' (Laroche 1980, 197–99); PN Paššitḫe, pa-aš-ši-it-ḫe 'messenger' (Karana; Monti 2017, 392)

entries.note: The matched roundel pair HT Wc 3001 (PA-SE-JA ½) and HT Wc 3002 (PA-SE-JA), Scribe 107 (GORILA II 72): one context. Uncounted: HT 93a .8 ]PA-SE-JA 20, broken before, PA dotted, or ]PI-SE-JA (GORILA I 147). The base PA-SE Pašše heads HT 18 and stands on HT 27b as an entry parallel to MI-DA (· VIN+WA · SA n): name and -ya short form in one archive, as Pašši-tilla and Paššiya at Nuzi. SE writes the stem vowel i. Cf. LB pa-sa-ja, a spice recipient (KN Ga 953).
entries.source: di Mino; Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943; Laroche 1980; Monti 2017

entries.meaning: Dašurat 'Old (f.)' (woman's name; Amorite dašuratum 'old')

cognates.Amorite: DAŠUR-AT-UM, DA-ŠU-RA-TUM, FN (YOS VIII 51 2, 14; Gelb 1980 no. 1489); DAŠUR-UM, DA-ŠU-RU-UM (no. 1490); DAŠUR-AH+ʿAŠTAR, DA-ŠU-RA-EŠ₄-DAR, FN (no. 1488); ʿAMM-I+DAŠUR, AM-MI-DA-ŠUR? (no. 729); dašurum, dušurum, fem. dašuratum, dašura 'old' (Gelb 1980, 17); Sippar da-šu-ra-tum, da-šu-ru-um (de Boer 2014, 341, 367)
cognates.Arabic: daṯara, aor. -ṯuru, inf. duṯūr, of a trace of a dwelling 'it became effaced… and it became old'; of a man 'he became overcome by old age and emaciation'; dāṯir 'effaced' (Lane 851)

entries.note: SY Za 6, on the wall of a chalice-shaped serpentine libation table below the rim: one group of four signs, no divider (Muhly and Olivier 2008, 209–210). SE uncertain; DA (SA not excluded), RA and TE probable. DA-SE-RA-TE writes DA-ŠU-RA-TUM sign for sign without mimation: SE writes š, TE the feminine -t. Amorite š writes PS *ṯ, so dašur- is Arabic daṯara 'became old' (Lane 851). The sole word on a libation table: the dedicant's name, or 'the Old One (f.)' as an epithet. Rival: SA for DA. One attestation. See DA-TA-RA.
entries.source: di Mino; Gelb 1980; de Boer 2014; Lane

entries.meaning: Ar-tae (personal name; Hurrian ar- 'give')

cognates.Nuzi: AR-TAE, A-ar-ta-e, var. Ar-ta-e, Ar-ta-a-e, A-ar-da-e (Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943, 33); ar- with -tae, from ar 'give' (ibid., 203)

entries.note: HT 29 .5 A-RE-DA-I 2, whole and undotted, RE written over an erased sign, the whole tablet over an erasure (GORILA I 55). An entry of two units after [?]-KI-TA 2 and before KA-DU-MA-NE 1, on a tablet with PA-JA-RE. Nuzi writes the name A-ar-da-e beside A-ar-ta-e (Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943, 33): RE writes ar- with a dead vowel, DA the -da- of that spelling. Rival: DA-I dayu as a second element, with A-RE unexplained.
entries.source: di Mino; Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943

entries.meaning: the one of Šakmu (Shechem) (gentilic in -SE on the toponym)

cognates.Hebrew: šǝkem 'shoulder, mountain ridge'; Šǝkem Shechem, gentilic haš-šikmî (Num 26:31)
cognates.Amarna: KUR ša-ak-mi 'the land of Šakmu', Shechem (EA 289)
cognates.Amorite: ŠKM: Šākim, DN (Gelb 1980, 33); ŠAKIM-UM, ŠA-KI-MU-UM (no. 5804)
cognates.Egyptian: skmimi, Shechem, Execration Texts, Brussels E6 (Streit 2017, 64–65)

entries.note: ZA 15a .7 *364-KE-MA-SE 5, the last entry of the wine issue headed *47-KU-NA, after SA-MI-DA-E 4 (GORILA III 183). Intact, no dots. SigLA reads the first sign A364, the Zakros form of *324. At *324's value ṮA, ṯa-ke-ma writes ṯkm, PS *ṯVkm-; Shechem is Skmimi of the Execration Texts (Brussels E6; Streit 2017, 63). -SE as on RU-MA-TA-SE beside bare RU-MA-TA, and on MI-ZA-SE on the same face: town and gentilic, as Šǝkem and šikmî. Rivals: the Amorite name Šakim (ŠA-KI-MU-UM; Gelb 1980, no. 5804); at the rival value SO, so-ke-ma gives the same root.
entries.source: di Mino; Gelb 1980; DULAT; Streit 2017; Ferrara, Montecchi & Valério 2022

entries.meaning: ʾAkiru (personal name; Amorite ʾAkir-, cf. ʾikkār 'plowman')

cognates.Amorite: ʾAKIR-UM, A-KI-RU-UM (KISURRA B 7+); ʾAKIR-I, A-KI-RI (VAS VIII 14 37); ʾAKIR-AH, A-KI-RA, FN (Gelb 1980 nos. 338–340)
cognates.Akkadian: ikkaru 'plowman, farm laborer; farmer', Sum. lw. (CAD I/J s.v.)

entries.note: ARKH 4b .4 A-KI-RO 3, after the numeral ]9 that closes the entry of .3–4 and before ZA-SI-ZU[ ]3, in a list of whole-number entries with no logogram on the face (GORILA III 14–15). Intact and undotted. A-KI-RO spells the Amorite A-KI-RU-UM, A-KI-RI and A-KI-RA sign for sign (Gelb 1980, nos. 338–340), RO for the case vowel; Gelb lists the names, and the noun ʾikkār 'plowman' behind them is di Mino's reading. Rivals: the Akkadian name Ikkaru; A + KI-RO 'owed'. See I-KI-RA and I-KA.

entries.meaning: Azzuya (woman's name; Hurrian hypocoristic on az(z)-)

cognates.Nuzi: AZ(Z)UIA, A-zu-ia, var. Az-zu-ia, a woman (Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943, 41); az(z), Hurrian, in women's names (ibid., 208)
cognates.Hurrian: Azzuāya, az-zu-a-ia, f. (Mari, VHN 81); base Azzu 'woman', f. (Mari, Karana; Monti 2017, 234, 386)

entries.note: HT 11a .3–4 A-SU-JA 1, A at the end of .3 and SU-JA on .4, whole and undotted, the first entry after KU-RO 10 (GORILA I 23). Spelled as Nuzi A-zu-ia: SU writes zu, JA the hypocoristic -ya. Rival: Ugaritic PN ùsy (DULAT 111).
entries.source: di Mino; Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943; Monti 2017

entries.meaning: corvée workers, labour gang (personnel term)

cognates.Akkadian: massu 'corvée worker': idi LÚ.MEŠ ma-zi 'wages for the corvée workers' (Wiseman Alalakh 246:6; CAD M/1 s.v.)
cognates.Hebrew: mas מַס 'corvée, labour gang': wayyaʿal ham-melek šəlōmōh mas 'King Solomon raised a levy' (1 Kgs 5:27)

entries.note: ZA 10b .2–3 MA-ZA 5, after U-*49 6 and before MA-KI-DE-TE 5 (GORILA III 171), in a list that counts A-MI-TA ʾamita 'handmaid' 3. MA-ZA writes ma-za on primary values: Alalakh's z spelling, the geminate unwritten. A labour gang issued in a list, as Alalakh issues wages to the ma-zi (CAD M/1 327). Rivals: the Eblaite name ma-za (Pagan 1998); the Hurrian name mzy, ma-zi-i (DULAT 600). See ME-ZA and MI-ZA-SE.

entries.meaning: messenger, courier (title)

cognates.Akkadian: kallû 'messenger', LÚ ka-al-la at Ugarit (RS 16.188 r. 7; CAD K 83–84)

entries.note: HT 88 .4 KA-JU 1, both signs whole and undotted, the second of six one-unit entries after KI-RO, between KU-PA₃-PA₃ 1 and KU-PA₃-NU 1 (GORILA I 139). JU at its primary value lu: ka-lu, the geminate unwritten. A title in a roster of one-unit entries, as Ugarit issues decanted wine to the courier, yn ḥsp l ql (KTU 4.213:27; DULAT 689). Rivals: Ugaritic ql 'swift (courier)', with KA for q; kalû 'lamentation priest' (CAD K 91).

entries.meaning: perfumer (title); rival rōkēl 'trader, merchant'

cognates.Hebrew (rival): rōkēl 'trader': hā-rōkĕlîm beside the goldsmiths (Neh 3:31–32); ʾabqat rôkēl 'the merchant's powders' (Song 3:6)

entries.note: HT 98a .4 RO-KE ½, whole and undotted, between TE-*301 ¾ and KA-RI-*310-I ¼, in a list of fractional issues with TA-NA-TI; wine on face b (GORILA I 161). The qōṭēl participle with Canaanite ō, as RO-E rōʿē; KE writes q, the final ḥ unwritten. Ebla rāqiḥ 'oil-perfumer' (GlOS 2, 165) and Ugarit rqḥ 'perfumer, druggist' (DULAT 734) attest the title. Rival: rōkēl 'trader', with KE at k and the final l unwritten, as Linear B drops a word-final liquid (ma-te mātēr, PY An 607); unattested in the Bronze Age. See RO-QA and *401.

entries.meaning: land labourer, field worker; rival the personal name Šadī

cognates.Ugaritic: šdy (I) 'land labourer', nʿrm šdym (KTU 4.868:4); PN šdy (II), syll. ša-de₄-ya (DULAT 799)

entries.note: HT 111b .1 SA-DI 4[, whole and undotted, the numeral broken after (GORILA I 181), on a fragment broken above and below. SA writes š in the S-class merger. Ugaritic šdy (I) 'land labourer', as nʿrm šdym 'serving lads, labourers in the fields' (KTU 4.868:4; DULAT 799). A count of four fits a term for workers; the fragment gives no heading to choose between the occupation and the name. Rival: the name Šadī, Ugaritic šdy (II), ša-du-ya (DULAT 799), and Amorite ŠADW-IJA, ŠA-DI-IA (Gelb 1980, no. 5781).

entries.meaning: Asīya, personal name, '(DN is) my physician'

cognates.Akkadian: asû 'physician'; ì-lí-a-si-ia 'my god is my physician' (GlOS 1, 47)

entries.note: HT 115a .4 A-SE-JA with four fraction signs, whole and undotted, among the names of a palimpsest list under *47-NU-RA-JA and GRA+BOSm (GORILA I 189), between PA-RA-NE and KA-PO-RU. Asīya 'my physician', the short form of the Euphrates name ì-lí-a-si-ia 'my god is my physician' (GlOS 1, 47), from A-SE ʾāsē. The name is written a-sí-ia, sign for sign: a woman of the Mari palace (Ziegler 1999, 262), and men at early Old Babylonian Kiš and Dilbat (de Boer 2014, 398, 410). Rivals: the Nuzi name Aziya, A-zi-ia (Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943, 41); the Ugaritic name ủsy (DULAT 111). One attestation.

entries.meaning: siddāru 'Arranger' (personal name; spelling of SI-DA-RE)
entries.cognates: see SI-DA-RE
entries.note: GO 2 recto .3 SI-DA-RO with ¼, broken after the fraction, below single-sign entries SI[, KA ⅛, SI 2 and DA[ (Younger, Linear A Texts). SI-DA-RE (HT 17, HT 122a) with the final vowel o; JA-SI-DA-RA (PH 7a) carries the same stem. A second site, not a second context for SI-DA-RE. Rival: a commodity term, as the single-sign entries around it are: Eblaite GÀR.SAR = si-da-ru₁₂ 'a plant' (GlOS 2, 187). See SI-DA-RE.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'He of the Portion' (ḏā + √m-n-y); rival √m-n-n 'He of the Favor'

cognates.Ugaritic: ḏmn PN (etym. unc.), syll. ZI-me-ni, ZI-me-nu (RS 34.169:2) (DULAT 283); tmn (II) PN (etym. unc.), syll. ta-me-nu (RS 34.169:5) (DULAT 858)

entries.note: HT 117a .8 DA-MI-NU 1, whole and undotted, in the second list headed SA-TA, before DA-NE-KU-TI 1 (GORILA I 197). Ḏā-Mīnu 'He of the Portion': the determinative-relative ḏā, written DA as in DA-QE-RA ḏā-Qīra, + MI-NU, as one word, as DU-RU-WI ḏu-luwwī is, of the type of Amorite Zu-i-la 'He of God' and Zu-dIš-ḫa-ra 'He of Išḫara' (Gelb 1980, nos. 6596, 6598), with MI-NU from √m-n-y 'count, allot' (Amorite manawum, manūtum, Gelb 1980, 25; Arb. Manāt, Q 53:20), MI- for Amorite ma- as in MI-NU-TE against Ma-nu-tum (Gelb 1980, no. 4528). Rivals: √m-n-n 'bestow, favor' (Lane 3024), 'He of the Favor'; Ḏimenu, the Ugaritic name ḏmn, syllabic ZI-me-ni, ZI-me-nu (RS 34.169:2; DULAT 283), which DULAT leaves without etymology; Ugaritic tmn (II), ta-me-nu (RS 34.169:5; DULAT 858), which needs DA for t. Weak point: DA writes the accusative ḏā (Fischer 2002, §283), where Amorite and Ebla names open with nominative ḏū. Cf. LB da-mi-ni-jo, a shepherd at Knossos (DMic I 152–153).

entries.meaning: He of Naśiʾ (personal name heading HT 126a)

cognates.Amorite: Naśiʾ DN, written NA-SI: Niqmi-la-Naśiʾ NI-IQ-MI-LA-NA-SI (Gelb no. 5051), Yadur-Naśiʾ IA-DU-UR-NA-SI (no. 3218); ḏu 'he/she of', written ZU (Gelb 1980, 18)
cognates.Hebrew: nāśîʾ נָשִׂיא 'leader, prince' (HALOT 727): nəśîʾ ʾĕlōhîm נְשִׂיא אֱלֹהִים 'a prince of God' (Gen 23:6), wə-nāśîʾ bə-ʿammǝkā lōʾ tāʾōr וְנָשִׂיא בְעַמְּךָ לֹא תָאֹר (Exod 22:27), nəśîʾê maṭṭôt נְשִׂיאֵי מַטּוֹת (Num 1:16)

entries.note: HT 126a .1 DA-NA-SI · *318 ·, heading the tablet, before A-NA-[·] 1 and SI-DI-JA 1 (GORILA I 217). ḏā 'the one of', as in DA-MI-NU, + Naśiʾ, the Amorite god of NŠʾ 'to carry, to raise' (Gelb 1980, 27), whom Gelb's names write NA-SI sign for sign: IA-AḪ-WI-NA-SI, IA-DU-UR-NA-SI, NI-IQ-MI-LA-NA-SI, ZI-ID-KU-LA-NA-SI (nos. 2874, 3218, 5051, 6457). 'He of Naśiʾ', the type of Amorite Zu-dIš-ḫa-ra 'He of Išḫara' (Gelb no. 6598). NA-SI also closes U-MI-NA-SI, the heading of HT 117a and HT 28b. Rival: ḏā-Nasr, the god Nasr of Ḥimyar (Q 71:23; Faris 1952, 10), with r unwritten.

entries.meaning: He of the speckled (flock) (personal name); rival 'He of the head shepherd'

cognates.Ugaritic: ksp d nqdm 'silver of the head shepherds' (KTU 4.369:8); nqd 'head shepherd' (DULAT 630); syll. mu-qa-dī 'grazing rights' (PRU 6 116; UVST NQD¹)
cognates.Hebrew: nōqēd נֹקֵד 'sheep-breeder', of Mesha (2 Kgs 3:4); nāqōd נָקֹד 'speckled' (Gen 30:32)

entries.note: HT 117a .8–9 DA-NE-KU-TI 1, after DA-MI-NU 1 and before KI-DA-RO 1, in the second list headed SA-TA (GORILA I 197). ḏā 'the one of', as in DA-MI-NU, + naquddi, genitive of naqudd- 'speckled', Jacob's flock (Gen 30:32), TI writing di: 'He of the speckled (flock)'. KU-TI answers to -qudd-, as Hebrew nəquddîm (Gen 30:39; HALOT 719); Safaitic has the name Nqd (Harding 1971, 597). DA-MI-NU beside it answers to LB da-mi-ni-jo, a shepherd at Knossos. Rivals: nāqidi 'herdsman' (Ebla na-gi-du-um, GlOS 2, 92), as Ugaritic nqdm 'chief shepherds' with the same d in ksp d … nqdm (KTU 4.369:2–8; DULAT 253), whose a-i vowels miss NE-KU; DA-NE + KU-TI, neither part attested alone.
entries.source: di Mino; HALOT; Harding 1971; GlOS 2; DULAT

entries.meaning: Old (man's name); rival 'He of the gate'
entries.cognates: see DA-SE-RA-TE
entries.note: HT 6a .1–2 KA-PA · DA-TA-RA · TE · NI 15, heading a fig entry (GORILA I 13). HT 88 .6 DA-TA-RE 1, in the KI-RO roster before KU-RO 6 (GORILA I 139), the same name. daṯar 'old', the masculine of DA-SE-RA-TE Dašurat: Amorite DA-ŠU-RU-UM beside fem. DA-ŠU-RA-TUM (Gelb nos. 1490, 1489). TA writes ṯ as in TA-RA ṯa(ġ)ra, where DA-SE-RA-TE writes it SE. Rival: ḏā-ṯaġri 'He of the gate', ḏā as in DA-MI-NU + ṯaġr- as in TA-RA, a type with no attested name.

entries.meaning: Good (f.) (personal name)

cognates.Amorite: ṬAJB-AT-UM, DA-BA-TUM, a woman (Gelb 1980 no. 1409); ṭābum, fem. ṭābatum 'good' (Gelb 1980, 35)

entries.note: ZA 10a .4–5 DA-I-PI-TA 1, in a name list after A-DU-KU-MI-NA 1 (GORILA III 169); ZA 8 DA-I-PI-TA 2½, before KA-I-RO 4, by another scribe (GORILA III 165). ṭayyibat- 'good (f.)', fem. of qattil ṭayyib-: DA writes ṭ as in Amorite DA-BA-TUM Ṭaybatum (Gelb no. 1409) and Ebla da-bù 'good' (GlOS 2, 311); I writes yyi, the gemination unmarked. LB da-i-pi-ta heads a catalogue of men at Knossos (KN Bk 799), a man's name (DMic I 149): the name carried into Mycenaean Crete. Rivals: DA-I + PI-TA, DA-I dayyu 'enough' (HT 12) with PI-TA otherwise only inside PI-TA-JA; DA + I-PI-TA, I-PI-TA unattested. See OLE+TA.
entries.source: di Mino; Gelb 1980; GlOS 2; DMic I

entries.meaning: Timar the Levite (f.), priestess (woman's name and title); rival Tamar + WI-TE

cognates.Hebrew: timmōrā תִּמֹרָה 'palm-shaped ornament' (HALOT 1757), carved with cherubim in Solomon's temple (1 Kgs 6:29, 32, 35); PN Tamar תָּמָר (Gen 38:6); Lēwî, named by his mother Leah (Gen 29:34)
cognates.Minaean: lwʾt 'priestess': lwʾtn S¹lmy 'the priestess Salmay', daughter of a priestess (M 333, RES 3357); lwʾtn Mwʾl 'the priestess Mwʾl' and her property (M 358, RES 3697), Dedan (DASI)
cognates.Amorite: TAMAR-U, TA-MA-RU (Gelb 1980 no. 6027)

entries.note: PY R 1 .1–2 TI-MA-RU-WI-TE, a ligature and VIN 90, the only entry (GORILA I 322). TI-MA writes Tīmar 'palm', the final r unwritten before the l of luwwīt, both in the R-series, with the i of Heb. timmōrā 'palm-shaped ornament' (HALOT 1757). RU-WI-TE writes luwwīt, the feminine of luwwī as in DU-RU-WI (HT 25a). A name with a title, as Minaean lwʾtn S¹lmy 'the priestess Salmay', a priestess's daughter (M 333). Rival: TI-MA-RU Tamar, Amorite TA-MA-RU (Gelb 1980, no. 6027), with WI-TE from √w-d-d, as in WI-TE-JA-MU. See TO-MA-RO.
entries.source: di Mino; GORILA I; HALOT; DASI; Gelb 1980

entries.meaning: Strength is alive, the arm thrives (personal name); rival Yidu-nešše, Hurrian 'prosperity'

cognates.Eblaite: i-du na-sa, yidu-naḥša 'strength is alive'; i-du na, yidu-na 'our strength' (Pagan 1998, rows 2469, 2466)
cognates.Akkadian: naḫāšu 'to prosper' (CAD N/1 133); naḫšu 'healthy, prosperous', PN Na-aḫ-šum (CAD N/1 142)
