cognates.Hurrian: nešše 'prospérité', ne-eš-ši (Laroche, GLH 181), rival

entries.note: HT 13 .5–6 I-DU-NE-SI 5, the last recipient in the VIN · TE list headed KA-U-DE-TA, after TE-KI 27½, KU-ZU-NI 18, DA-SI-ṬA 19, before KU-RO 130½; lines .4–7 over an erasure (GORILA I 27). I-DU = yidu 'arm, strength', as in I-DU-TI; NE-SI = naḥši, ḥ unwritten: the Eblaite name i-du na-sa yidu-naḥša 'strength is alive' word for word (Pagan 1998, row 2469). Cf. Amorite E-DU-NA-SA (Gelb no. 1599), unanalysed. Rivals: Hurrian nešše 'prosperity', the vowels match, beside Hurrian TE-KI; Naśiʾ, the god of DA-NA-SI, 'Naśiʾ is strength'. See JA-DI and I-DA.

entries.meaning: (Little) kinsman (personal name, hypocoristic); rival ʾAmaya 'maidservant'

cognates.Ugaritic: PN ʿmy ʿAmmaya (KTU 4.16:4), syll. am-ma-ya (DULAT 164); PN ảmy (KTU 2.76:3), syll. am-ma-ia (RS 88.2158:31') (DULAT 73)
cognates.Amorite: ʾAMAT-AN, A-MA-TA-AN (Gelb 1980 no. 404), rival

entries.note: KH 14 .1 ]RA · A-MA-JA · CYP 6[, whole and undotted between dividers, a cyperus recipient (GORILA III 45). A-MA ʿamma 'kinsman' + hypocoristic -ya, as A-SU-JA, PA-SE-JA: the Ugaritic name ʿmy ʿAmmaya (KTU 4.16:4), syllabic am-ma-ya (DULAT 164). Rival: ʾAmaya, short for ʾamat- 'maidservant' (Ug. amt, DULAT 71), with t lost.

entries.meaning: House of the Throne, the crown estate (institution heading); rival the Hurrian name of PI-TA-KE-SI

cognates.Akkadian: bīt kussî, É.GIŠ.GU.ZA, '1. royal property (real estate), 2. royal service' (CAD K 593); grain to PN ša GIŠ.GU.ZA (CAD K 592)

entries.note: HT 21 PI-TA-KA-SE · TE · GRA 161, then OLE+U 11, OLE+E 3¾, *304 7¾, OLIV 1¼, the heading of a grain and oil account (GORILA I 39). bīt 'house of' + kissē 'throne': Akk. bīt kussî 'royal property' (CAD K 593), and grain booked to persons ša kussî 'belonging to the crown' (CAD K 592). PI writes bi as in DA-I-PI-TA. Its man is PI-TA-KE-SI (HT 87), bīt-kissi with the genitive. Rival: the Hurrian name Pidi-kešḫi.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'El is king'; rival Hurrian Šar-elli

cognates.Amorite: ŚARR-A+ʾIL, ŠAR-RA-DINGIR, Alalakh IV (Gelb 1980 no. 5846)
cognates.Ugaritic: šr (III) 'Prince, Sovereign', divine title: [š]lm ỉl šr (KTU 1.123:3; DULAT 829)
cognates.Hebrew: Malkîʾēl, the same sentence with mlk (Gen 46:17)
cognates.Hurrian: Šar-elli, the queen ṯryl, syll. šar-e-li (DULAT s.v. ṯryl; Laroche GLH 78), rival

entries.note: HT 20 .4 SA-RE-JU ⅛, after CAPm ⅛ and before TELA, in the list under PA-RO-SU beside KU-MA-JU and QE-KU-RE (GORILA I 36–37). ša-r(ʾ)ē-lu sign for sign: JU writes lu, the nominative of ʾēlu, and RE carries the ē once the ʾ drops at the join. Ugaritic šr 'Prince, Sovereign' is El's title in ỉl šr 'El, the Sovereign' (KTU 1.123:3; DULAT 829). Rival: Hurrian Šar-elli, syll. šar-e-li (DULAT s.v. ṯryl; Laroche GLH 78), whose -li mismatches JU. One witness. See SA-RU, I-RA₂, PI-RU-E-JU and DI-NA-RO.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Offspring of El'; rival 'Fruit of El'

cognates.Akkadian: pirʾu, pirḫu '1. shoot, 2. offspring' (CAD P 416); Pir-ḫi-ì-lí-šu 'Offspring-of-His-God', wr. Pi-ir-i-ì-lí-šu (CAD P 418)

entries.note: PH 2 .3 PI-RU-E-JU 60, between RA-O-DI-KI 60 and SE-SA-PA₃ 60, under the heading A-SE-TU-*21F 1 (GORILA I 288–289). pirʾ(u) + ʾēlu: the ʾ of pirʾu goes unwritten, and E-JU writes ʾē-lu as in SA-RE-JU. The name type is Akkadian Pirḫi-ilišu 'Offspring-of-His-God', also written Pi-ir-i-ì-lí-šu (CAD P 418). Rival: pir- 'fruit', 'Fruit of El', a type with no attested name. One witness.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'She is gracious'

cognates.Amorite: NAʿM-IJA, NA-MI-IA, fem. (Gelb 1980 no. 5001); NAʿM-IJA, NA-AḪ-MI-IA, with ḫ for ʿ (no. 4896); 3 f. sg. ta- in TA-BNIJ+ʿAŠTAR, TAB-NI-EŠ₄-DAR, fem. (no. 6055)

entries.note: PE 6 .2 TA-NA-MA-JE, alone on the line below the ruling, under .1 I-NA-[?]-TE (Younger, Linear A Texts, Other Texts: Petras). ta-nʿam-ay: ta- the 3 f. sg. prefix of women's names such as Amorite TAB-NI-EŠ₄-DAR (Gelb no. 6055), √n-ʿ-m with the ʿ unwritten, -ay the hypocoristic of Ugaritic nʿmy, nu-ú-ma-ya (DULAT 607). Rival: Ugaritic tnmy 'overflow (?)', an exact consonant match, once, in a broken line (KTU 1.1 IV 9; DULAT 860). One witness. See TA-NU-MU-TI.
entries.source: di Mino; Gelb 1980; DULAT; Younger, Linear A Texts

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Calm, at rest'; rival Zakūtu 'pure, innocent'

cognates.Akkadian: sakātu 'to be silent' (CAD S 74)
cognates.Amorite: Ya-ās-qī-iṭ-AN, 'rest' in a name, where Huffmon allows skt 'be calm' (Huffmon, APNM 253)

entries.note: HT 115a .3 SE-KU-TU ½, between NA-*21F-NE-MI-NA 1 and PA-RA-NE 1, a recipient (GORILA I 188–189). šakūt-u, a qatūl adjective of √š-k-t 'be quiet, rest' (semitic_roots 3250), on primary values: Hebrew hasket 'be quiet' (Deut 27:9; HALOT 756), Akkadian sakātu 'be silent' (CAD S 74). Rival: Zakūtu 'pure, innocent', the Ebla name za-ku-tu (Pagan 1998, row 5026) and the Neo-Assyrian queen Zakūtu, which needs SE for ḏ where the lexicon writes z with the Z signs. One witness.
entries.source: di Mino; HALOT; CAD S; Huffmon 1965; Pagan 1998

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Pampered'; rival Amorite Banuq

cognates.Amorite: BANUQ-UM, BA-NU-KU-UM, and BANUQ-AN, BA-NU-KA-AN (Gelb 1980 nos. 1132, 1131), rival

entries.note: ZA 14 .4 PA-NU-QE 2, after TU-MI-TI-ZA-SE 45 and before JA-WI[, a recipient among names (GORILA III 181). panūq, a qatūl passive of √p-n-q 'pamper, indulge' on primary values (Heb. pānaq, BDB 819; Syr. paneq 'pamper', Payne Smith 451). Rival: the Amorite name Banuq, BA-NU-KU-UM (Gelb no. 1132), which reads PA as ba. One witness.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Second(-born)'; rival Dīnuya

cognates.Amorite: ŠANIJ-UM, SA-NI-U₂-UM; ŠANIJ-I, SA-NI-I (Gelb 1980 nos. 5495, 5494); Dīnuya, √d-y-n 'judge' (no. S36), rival

entries.note: HT 115b .2 TI-NU-JA · NU-WI · GRA ½, the frame of side a's *47-NU-RA-JA · I · GRA+BOSm / NU-WI, so a person (GORILA I 191). ṯinu-ya, Ugaritic ṯn 'two, twofold' (DULAT 905) + hypocoristic -ya as in *306-TU-JA on the same tablet; Ugarit has the personal name ṯny (DULAT 911). TI writes ṯ, as in TI-DA-TA ṯādīta 'sixth' and TU-PI-TA ṯāpiṭu. Rival: Dīnuya, √d-y-n 'judge', which needs TI = d, while the judge words here are written DI (DI-NA). One witness.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'broom (bush)'

cognates.Hebrew: rōtem 'broom' (1 Kgs 19:4); Ritmâ, a wilderness encampment (Num 33:18)

entries.note: HT 115a .1–2 RỊ-TẠ-MẠ, all three signs underdotted in both copies, then NU-WI 2; the copie tabulaire joins RỊ-TẠ-MẠ-NU-WI, GORILA's note on .2 allows the divider (GORILA I 189). A person, as TI-NU-JA · NU-WI on HT 115b. rit-mā, TA's vowel echoing MA: Ritmâ, where Israel encamped (Num 33:18), beside NU-WI 'steppe-dweller'. Rival: Arabian rtm rathîm 'broken-nosed' (Harding 1971, 270), which needs TA for ṯ. One witness.

entries.meaning: (My) Might (personal name; lītu 'might, victory' + hypocoristic -āy); rival Rašiyya

cognates.Akkadian: lītu 'victory, victorious might, power', in personal names: ᵈŠul-gi-li-ti, ᵈŠamaš-li-tum, Bēl-li-tim-Marduk (CAD L 222–223)
cognates.Amorite: liʔy 'power': li-i-um, li-ú-um, li-i-ᵈda-gan; laʔiy 'powerful', with -aya at Ugarit: la-i-ia, la-i-ia-ya (GlOS 2, 6); rival RAŠIJ-JA, RA-ŠI-A, √r-š-j 'acquire' (Gelb 1980, no. 5264)

entries.note: KH 6 .4 ]CYP+[ ] J · RI-TA-JE CYP+D[, intact and undotted, a recipient in a list of CYP+D J allotments (GORILA III 26–27). RI li, the ʾ of liʾt- unwritten, TA t; JE the hypocoristic -āy, as in *306-TA-JE ʿaṭāye and the Ugarit names la-i-ia-ya (GlOS 2, 6). lītu 'might' names the god's victory in ᵈŠamaš-lītum and ᵈŠulgi-līti (CAD L 223). Rival: Amorite Rašiyya, RA-ŠI-A (Gelb 1980, no. 5264), √r-ṯ-y 'acquire' with TA for ṯ, against the vowels of RI-TA. RI the i of Amorite liʔy 'power', li-i-um, li-i-ᵈda-gan (GlOS 2, 6), beside the verbal laʾijum (Gelb 1980, 23). One attestation.
entries.source: di Mino; CAD L; GlOS 2; Gelb 1980

entries.meaning: personal name (f.), on √ś-y-m 'to place, fix'; rival Šimʿat

cognates.Amorite: ŚIJM-AT-UM, ŠI-MA-TUM, fem.; ŚIJM-AT+DAGAN, ŠI-MA-AT-D-DA-GAN, fem. (Gelb 1980 nos. 5893, 5888)
cognates.Mari: Šīmatum, ši-ma-tim, daughter of Zimri-Lim (FM IV, 283; FM V, 285)

entries.note: HT 96a .2 SI-MI-TA GRA 5, the first recipient under I-TI-TI-KU-NI · A-PA-RA-NE · A-*123-TE (GORILA I 156). śīmat, the women's name of Amorite ŚIJM-AT-UM, ŠI-MA-TUM (Gelb no. 5893): SI writes ś, which merges into the S series, and MI for ma is a vowel mismatch only. Rival: Hebrew Šimʿat (2 Kgs 12:22), with the ʿ unwritten. One witness. See SA-JA-MA.
entries.source: di Mino; Gelb 1980; GlOS 2; FM IV; FM V

entries.meaning: personal name; compare Amorite ʾAkkatum

cognates.Amorite: ʾAKK-AT-UM, A-KA-TUM (Gelb 1980 no. 329); fem. ʾAKK-AT-IJA (nos. 327–28); ʾAKK-ATAN-UM, A-KA-TA-A-NU-UM (no. 326)
cognates.Linear B: a-ka-ta-jo, a man's name (PY Eo 269, KN Dv 1331; DMic I 34)

entries.note: KN 32a .2 A-KA-TA, whole at the left edge, broken after (GORILA I 264–65). Sign for sign the Amorite name ʾAKK-AT-UM, A-KA-TUM (Gelb no. 329), with the stem of ʾAKK-AT-IJA and ʾAKK-ATAN-UM; Gelb gives the element no meaning. Linear B a-ka-ta-jo, a man's name at Pylos and Knossos (DMic I 34). One witness.
entries.source: di Mino; Gelb 1980; FM IV; DMic

entries.meaning: personal name, 'the Hired' (article ha- + SI-KI-RA); rival haśkira 'he rewarded'

cognates.Hebrew: Śākār, PN (1 Chr 11:35); names with the article, haq-Qôṣ (1 Chr 24:10), hal-Lôḥēš (Neh 3:12)
cognates.Amorite: ʾAškur, DN, AŠ-KU-RA-AN, AŠ-KUR-ᵈIM (Gelb 1980 nos. 947, 950), 'of uncertain origin' (Huffmon, APNM 172), rival

entries.note: KH 20 .1 A-SI-KI-RA · CYP+E ⅓, an entry before cyperus, parallel to ]DU-RE-ZA · CYP+E ½ (GORILA III 51). The article ha- (A, h unwritten, as in A-TU-RI-SI-TI) + SI-KI-RA Śikira 'Hired' (HT 8a), the pair of A-KI-DA-RO beside KI-DA-RO; Hebrew names take the article, haq-Qôṣ (1 Chr 24:10). Rival: haśkira 'he rewarded', an H-stem of the same root, and the Amorite DN ʾAškur (Gelb nos. 947, 950). One witness.

entries.meaning: woven (cloth), a textile entry; rival šittātu 'remainder'

cognates.Ugaritic: štt adj. f. 'spun, woven'; RS Akk. TÚG še-ta-ti (DULAT 839)
cognates.Akkadian: šatû adj. 'woven (cloth)' (CAD Š/2 207); šittātu 'remainder', pl. of šittu A (CAD Š/3 136), rival

entries.note: ZA 20 .2 SI-TE-TU 1, after DU-RE-ZA-SE MI · 4 and before SI-TU 6, in a list ending KU-RA 130 (GORILA III 193). šetātu, the feminine of Ugaritic štt 'spun, woven', written TÚG še-ta-ti at Ras Shamra (DULAT 839), beside SI-TU sūt 'garment' on the next line. Rival: šittātu 'remainder' (CAD Š/3 136). One witness.

entries.meaning: for the must, new wine (terminative -SE); at Khania with the article, A-DU-RE-ZA ha-tīrāṯ 'the must'; rival √d-r-š 'demand, requisition'

cognates.Ugaritic: trṯ 'must, new wine', also a DN (DULAT 867)

entries.note: ZA 10b .1–2 DU-RE-ZA-SE *131B 5, the word before its own logogram, where ARKH 2 .1–2 has KU-RA *131B 5 (GORILA III 6–7, 168–171). ZA 10a .5 DU-RE-ZA-SE 2 closes a list opened by TA-NA-TE; ZA 20 .1 ]DU-RE-ZA-SE[, RE dotted, broken at both ends, over SI-TE-TU, SI-TU and TE-AROM (GORILA III 193). Ugaritic trṯ 'new wine' (DULAT 867), Hebrew tîrôš 'must' (HALOT 1727): DU for t, stops unmarked for voice, and ZA for ṯ; the u and e against *tīrāṯ- are a vowel mismatch only. -SE the Zakros terminative, as MI-ZA-SE. At Khania with the article ha- (A, h unwritten, as A-SI-KI-RA on KH 20): ]DU-RE-ZA · CYP+E ½ on KH 20, broken before (GORILA III 53), A-DU-[·]-ZA CYP on KH 11 (GORILA III 39), and A-DU-RE[ on KH 4. Rival: √d-r-š 'demand, require', of dues in 2 Chr 24:6 (lōʾ dāraštā … ləhābîʾ 'you have not required … to bring').

entries.meaning: Yawpiʿ 'He has shone forth' (personal name)

cognates.Amorite: *wpʿ 'be brilliant', kept apart from *ypʿ (Huffmon, APNM 212); MU-WPIʿ-I muwpiʿi, written mu-bi-ḫi, the causative participle (Gelb 1980, no. 4729)
cognates.Hebrew: hôpîaʿ 'he shone forth' (Deut 33:2); PN Yāpîaʿ (Josh 10:3; 2 Sam 5:15)

entries.note: PE Zb 7, a pithos: JA-WA-PI beside a handle, the first word, closed by a divider before JA[ (RILA-S1 112). The causative prefix form yawpiʿ of w-p-ʿ, ʿ unwritten, the w kept after the prefix as in Amorite muwpiʿi and Hebrew hôpîaʿ. Weak point: RILA-S1 reads the third sign PI, Younger VIR (Younger, Linear A Texts), and the photographs do not decide it. One witness.

entries.meaning: for the fighting (terminative -SE), a levy of 45; rival tmtt 'team, crew'

cognates.Ugaritic: tmtḫṣ n. m. 'fight' (< m-ḫ-ṣ); tmtt n. f. 'group of men, team, crew', rival (DULAT 859)
cognates.Akkadian: mitḫuṣu 'fight, combat, clash of weapons', ana mitḫuṣi 'for battle' (KBo 1 1:41) (CAD M/2 138)

entries.note: ZA 14 .3–4 TU-MI-TI-ZA-SE 45[ ], the largest count on a list of personal names, a space lost after the numeral (GORILA III 181). Intact. tumtiṣ-, the t-noun of the Gt of m-ḫ-ṣ with ḫ unwritten and ZA for ṣ, as Ugaritic tmtḫṣ 'fight' (KTU 1.3 II 19; DULAT 859) and Akkadian mitḫuṣu 'fight, combat', in the prose of the Akkadian treaties of Ḫattuša (KBo 1 1:41, KBo 1 2:10) and the Assyrian annals (CAD M/2 138); TU's u is the tu- of the war noun tuqumtu 'battle, war, fight' (CAD T 481); -SE the Zakros terminative, as MI-ZA-SE: 'for the fighting', a levy of 45. ZA belongs to the stem in MI-ZA-SE and DU-RE-ZA-SE, so the -ZA-SE words take -SE alone. Rival: Ugaritic tmtt 'group of men, team, crew' (ảlpm tmtt 'bullocks (and) personnel', KTU 4.231:9; DULAT 859), which leaves ZA unread. One witness.
entries.source: di Mino; DULAT; CAD M/2; CAD T

entries.meaning: flute; here the flute-player, the trade of TU-QE-NU Tuqnu; rival Hurrian Tulbiya

cognates.Ugaritic: ṯlb 'flute', b knr w b ṯlb 'with the lyre and the flute' (KTU 1.108:4; DULAT 892)
cognates.Akkadian: šulpu 'stalk, a flute or other reed instrument'; ša šulpi 'a reed-instrument player' (CAD Š/3 256–57)
cognates.Hurrian: tlby, syll. tu-ul-bi-ia, PN (DULAT 856), rival

entries.note: HT 25a .3–4 TU-QE-NU / ZU-JU-PU₂ 1, the layout of .4–5 DU-RU-WI / I-KI-RA 1: a name at the line end, then the trade and one unit (GORILA I 44–45). ṯu-lu-pu sign for sign: ZU writes ṯu, JU lu, PU₂ pu, *ṯulp- 'reed flute'. Ugaritic ṯlb 'flute', beside knr, tp and mṣltm (KTU 1.108:4; DULAT 892). Akk. šulpu 'a flute or other reed instrument' and ša šulpi 'a reed-instrument player', listed after ša malilim and ša enbūbim (OB Lu A 244) and written after a name, PN ša šu-ul-pi (MDP 22 21 r. 10) (CAD Š/3 256–57). GORILA's tabular copy dots ZU and PU₂, and the left margin beside ZU is abraded. Rival: the Hurrian name tlby, tu-ul-bi-ia (DULAT 856), which needs ZU = tu. One witness.

entries.meaning: personal name: tuqnu 'good order, safety'; the flute-player of ZU-JU-PU₂

cognates.Akkadian: tuqnu 'safety, security'; PN Tuqunu-ēreš (CAD T 480)

entries.note: HT 25a .3, after A-RI-NI-TA 1, at the end of the line with no numeral; .4 ZU-JU-PU₂ 1 ṯulpu 'flute-player' gives his trade, the layout of .4–5 DU-RU-WI / I-KI-RA 1 (GORILA I 44–45). NU is complete at the preserved right edge, though GORILA I 45 brackets it. tu-qe-nu for tuqnu, √t-q-n 'to be in good order': the Ugarit PN tqn, táq-qa-na (DULAT 862); ta-qa-an at Alalakh and il-taq-nu at Ugarit (GlOS 2, 294); Akk. tuqnu 'safety, security', in the PN Tuqunu-ēreš (CAD T 480). QE writes qe for qu. Rival: Ugaritic tkn 'inspector, measurer' (GlOS 2, 294), which needs QE = ke. One witness.
entries.source: di Mino; DULAT; GlOS; CAD T

entries.meaning: personal name: ḥdṯ 'new'; Ḥudaṯu of ʾArāyu on HT 122b

cognates.Ugaritic: ḥdṯ (III) PN, syll. ḫu-da-ši, ḫu-dá-ši; ḥdṯn PN, syll. ḫu-ud!-ša-nu (DULAT 351; Huehnergard 2008, 230)

entries.note: HT 122a .1 U-DE-ZA 2, the first entry after ]RA-RI ·, in a list of names totalled KU-RO 31 (GORILA I 207); HT 122b .3 ]A-RA-JU-U-DE-ZẠ 2, Ḥudaṯu of ʾArāyu, the same count in the same account (GORILA I 208–209). u-de-za for ḥudaṯ(u): U writes ḥu with the guttural dropped, ZA ṯa. The Ugarit PN ḥdṯ, syllabic ḫu-da-ši, and ḥdṯn, ḫu-ud!-ša-nu (DULAT 351; Huehnergard 2008, 230). DE writes de for da.

entries.meaning: place name: a unit of men and livestock in the HT rosters; rival the Hurrian personal name Madi 'wisdom'

cognates.Amorite: MAʾD-IJA, MA-DI-IA, PN (Gelb 1980, no. 4453; cf. nos. 4454–55)
cognates.Linear B: ma-di (KN As 603.2, Db 1168); ma-di-qo (KN Bk 806, Db 1460, Dl 930); ]ma-di-jo[ (KH Z 3); ma-di-je (TH Av 101, Fq 214, 254, 258, 263)
cognates.Hurrian: Madi PN, madi 'wisdom' (de Martino 2011, 68), rival

entries.note: HT 97a .4 MA-DI 5 in the KA-RU list of men by place, after PA-I-TO 6 and NA-TI 4 (GORILA I 159); HT 118 MA-DI 15 at the head of the pig list; HT 85b MA-DI 1 in the KI-KI-RA-JA roster, after WA-DU-NI-MI 1; HT 3 MA-DI 2, HT 69 MA-DI 4, PH(?) 31a MA-DI *21M 1. Maʾdi, √m-ʾ-d 'to be plentiful', the Amorite name MAʾD-IJA, MA-DI-IA (Gelb 1980, no. 4453). Linear B has ma-di (KN As 603.2, Db 1168) beside the derived ma-di-qo, ]ma-di-jo[ (KH Z 3) and ma-di-je (TH Av 101, Fq 214, 254, 258, 263). Rival: the Hurrian personal name Madi 'wisdom', at Hattusa, Alalakh and Emar (de Martino 2011, 68).

entries.meaning: place name: Memphis, the seat of Kothar (Ug. Ḥkpt), a recipient of cyperus; rival 'the Memphite'

cognates.Egyptian: ḥwt-kꜣ-ptḥ 'Memphis' (DULAT 353)
cognates.Ugaritic: Ḥkpt, the residence of the god kṯr (DULAT 353)
cognates.Amarna: ḫi-ku-up-ta-aḫ (EA 84:37); ḫi-ku-ta-aḫ, the p unwritten (EA 139:8) (Belmonte, RGTC 12/2, 105)
cognates.Linear B: i-ku-to, a man in the dative (MY Oi 705.1)

entries.note: HT 35 .1 I-KU-TA at the end of the line after TI-TI-KU · *326 ·, its entry CYP 1 at the head of .2 (GORILA I 67); all three signs whole and undotted. ḥi-ku(p)-ta(ḥ): I writes ḥi with the guttural dropped, the coda p and the final ḥ unwritten. The Byblos letter EA 139:8 also leaves the p unwritten, ḫi-ku-ta-aḫ, where EA 84:37 has ḫi-ku-up-ta-aḫ (Belmonte, RGTC 12/2, 105). Ugaritic Ḥkpt is the seat of Kothar, Egyptian ḥwt-kꜣ-ptḥ (DULAT 353). Linear B i-ku-to is a man in the dative at Mycenae (MY Oi 705.1). One witness.

entries.meaning: personal name: ʿUtay with the -SE suffix, a recipient of cyperus; rival a Cretan name of another language (LB u-ta-jo)

cognates.Hebrew: עוּתַי ʿÛtay, PN (1 Chr 9:4; Ezra 8:14), the man of 1 Chr 9:4 = עֲתָיָה ʿĂtāyāh (Neh 11:4) (BDB 738–39)
cognates.Safaitic: ʿty PN, 8 bearers, Thamudic 1; 'Ar. ʿatiy, rebellious' (Harding 1971, 406)
cognates.Linear B: u-ta-jo, a man, the 'collector' of the KN D series (DMic I)

entries.note: KH 7b .2 U-TA-I-SE CYP+D ½[, intact at the left edge, then PA-NA-TU CYP+D ½ (GORILA III 31); KH 7a lists *313b-men and cyperus under E-NA-SI, I-JA-PA-ME · TA-TA and QA-TI-KI. ]U-TA-I-SI CYP+D[ on KH 16 (Scribe 1) is the same entry in the other hand's spelling, as A-SE beside A-SI and I-SE beside I-SI. ʿUtay, the hypocoristic of 1 Chr 9:4 and Ezra 8:14 (BDB 738–39), and the Safaitic name ʿty (Harding 1971, 406), U for ʿu; built as MA-KA-I-SE Makī-se, a name in -I with -SE. Cf. LB u-ta-jo, the Knossos 'collector' (DMic I; Killen, Mycenaean Greek, glossary, s.v.). Rival: a Cretan name of another language. One intact witness.

entries.meaning: store(house), an entry under SI-DA-TE 'provisions'; rival a personal designation in -uwa

cognates.Hebrew: bêt hāʾăsuppîm 'the house of the stores' (1 Chr 26:15); ʾăsuppê 'storehouses of' (Neh 12:25); a loan from Akk. asuppu 'anteroom' (HALOT 76)
cognates.Akkadian: asuppu, an outbuilding; É a-su-up-pu bīt kāri 'an a.-house and a storehouse', Nbn. 499:1 (CAD A/2 349)

entries.note: ARKH 2 .5–6 A-SU-PU-WA 4, the final WA over an erasure, an entry under the heading SI-DA-TE ṣēdat 'provisions', after ZU-*301-SE-DE-*21F-*118 6 (GORILA III 6–7). ʾa-su-pp-ū-a, the ʾăsuppîm 'stores' of 1 Chr 26:15, Akk. asuppu, a loan in Hebrew (HALOT 76). -PU-WA writes the glide before a final -a, as A-SI-SU-PO-A writes -PO-A (KH 9), and QA-RA₂-WA stands beside QE-RA₂-U. Rival: a personal designation in -uwa, since A-SI-SU-PO-A stands beside the person sign VIR+*307. One witness. See A-SI-SU-PO-A.

entries.meaning: the storehouse (heading of issues), the word of A-SU-PU-WA; rival a personal or place heading in -uwa

cognates.Hebrew: *ʾāsōp, pl. ʾăsuppîm 'stores', bêt hāʾăsuppîm (1 Chr 26:15, 17); ʾăsuppê haššəʿārîm 'storerooms' (Neh 12:25); a loan from Akk. asuppu 'anteroom' (HALOT 76)
cognates.Akkadian: asuppu, an outbuilding; É a-su-up-pu bīt kāri 'an a.-house and a storehouse', Nbn. 499:1 (CAD A/2 349)

entries.note: KH 9 .1 A-SI-SU-PO-A · VIR+*307[, nothing before the first sign, heading small issues of figs, cyperus, wine and *304 (GORILA III 35). The A-SU-PU-WA of ARKH 2, with SI-SU for the s and PO-A for the glide before final -a. SI-SU writes the ss of NB às-su-up-pu (VAS 1 70 ii 30; CAD A/2 349), SI's vowel dead, as DI-DE writes the dd of DI-DE-RU ʾaddīru. Rival: a personal or place heading in -uwa, beside the person sign VIR+*307. One witness.

entries.meaning: corvée gang, labour gang (personnel term); the word of MA-ZA

cognates.Akkadian: massu 'corvée worker': idi LÚ.MEŠ ma-zi 'wages for the corvée workers' (Wiseman Alalakh 246:6); LÚ.MEŠ ma-as-sa.MEŠ (EA 365:14) (CAD M/1 327)

entries.note: HT 10a .8 ME-ZA 3, the last issue under KU-NI-SU 'emmer', after DA-RE 16½, U-*325-ZA and DA-RI-DA 8 (GORILA I 20–21); HT 85b ME-ZA 1, among single entries under KI-KI-RA-JA beside QA-*310-I qaynī 'smith' (GORILA I 130–131). Alalakh writes the gang ma-zi and issues it grain (CAD M/1 327), as HT 10a issues ME-ZA 3. The word of MA-ZA mazza (ZA 10b); ME for ma is a vowel mismatch only. Rival: the Hurrian name mzy, ma-zi-i (DULAT 600).

entries.meaning: partners, the heading of a shares account

cognates.Akkadian: tappû, tappāu 'partner, colleague … business partner'; Bogh. and Alalakh tappûtu (CAD T 184)
cognates.Eblaite: da-ba-u₃ tappāʾu 'comrade', a personal name (Pagan 1998, row 1378)

entries.note: HT 104 .1 TA-PA · *505 ·, heading three entries, DA-KU-SE-NE-TI 45½, I-DU-TI 20½ and PA-DA-SU-TI 29, whose sum is KU-RO 95 (GORILA I 170–171). ta-pa(ʾu) on primary values, the geminate and final ʾu unwritten: the partners in a divided account, as Akk. tappû 'business partner' (CAD T 184). Rival: ṭap 'children' (#66), TA writing ṭ. One witness.

entries.meaning: herdsman, shepherd (title on a label)

cognates.Ugaritic: rʿy 'shepherd', in ration lists: rʿym tlt ddm 'shepherds: three cauldronsful (of flour)' (DULAT 716)

entries.note: PH 24, an MM II label, RO-E the only group, whole and undotted (GORILA I 310–311). rō-ʿē, the qōtēl participle as in RO-KE rōqēaḥ, ʿ unwritten: Heb. rōʿeh, Ug. rʿy 'shepherd' (DULAT 716). Rival: rōʾē 'seer' (#627). One witness. See RA-O-DI-KI.

entries.meaning: Father (hypocoristic personal name, ʾAdday); rival the kin title ʾad 'father'

cognates.Ugaritic: ʾad 'father', par. um 'mother' (DULAT 16); PN ʾady, syll. a-da-a-a, ad-di-ya (DULAT 23)
cognates.Amorite: /ʔad/ 'lord, father' (Huffmon APNMT 156, apud DULAT 16)

entries.note: ZA 10b .4 A-DE 4, whole, between SA-MA 5 and A-MI-TA ʾamita 'handmaid' 3, in a list that also counts U-*49 ʾummi 'mother' 6 (GORILA III 171). ʾAddē, Ugaritic ʾady, syll. a-da-a-a (DULAT 23): hypocoristic -ay contracted to -ē, the geminate unwritten. Rival: the kin title ʾad 'father' (DULAT 16), as U-*49 is 'mother' in the same list. One witness.

entries.meaning: provisions (section heading); same word as SI-DA-TE ṣēdat

cognates.Hebrew: ṣēdâ 'provisions': lātēt lāhem ṣēdâ laddārek 'to give them provisions for the way' (Gen 42:25); lāqaḥat ṣēdâ lāʿām 'to fetch provisions for the people' (Judg 20:10)
cognates.Ugaritic: ṣd /ṣēdu/ 'provisions, sustenance': bn dgn b-m ṣdk 'son of Dagan, with your provisions' (KTU 1.14 II 25–26; Huehnergard 2012, 130)

entries.note: KH 7a .4 SE-*305 ·, whole, heading the third section, KU-[·]-KO-E VIR+*313b [ ]18 / CYP+D 1, in the slot of E-NA-SI ʾenāš and I-JA-PA-ME · TA-TA (GORILA III 29). ṣē-dā, √ṣ-y-d 'provisions': Heb. ṣêdâ 'provisions for a journey' (HALOT 1021), Ug. ṣd /ṣēdu/ 'provisions, sustenance' (Huehnergard 2012, 156). The heading word of SI-DA-TE ṣēdat (ARKH 2) and MA-SI-DU maṣīdu (HT 43). Rival: the name of the section's leader. One witness.

entries.meaning: provision of (construct), before *21F-*118 ḥiṭṭa 'wheat'
entries.note: ARKH 2 .3–4 ZU-*301-SE-DE-*21F-*118 6, ṯannān ṣēd ḥiṭṭa 'the chariot soldiers: provision of wheat, 6' (GORILA III 6–7). The root of the tablet's heading SI-DA-TE ṣēdat and of SE-*305 ṣēdā (KH 7a). Rival: part of a name ZU-*301-SE-DE. One witness.

entries.meaning: Height (toponym), the bare form of RU-MA-TA rūmatā

cognates.Amorite: RUWM-AT-UM, RU-MA-TUM, personal name (Gelb 1980, no. 5306)

entries.note: HT 64 .2 ]NA 2 RU-MA, whole against the tablet's right edge; only GORILA's normalized box adds the bracket (GORILA I 118–119). rū-ma sign for sign as Heb. Rûmâ (2 Kgs 23:36). The bare form of RU-MA-TA rūmatā 'the Height' (HT 29, HT 99b), √r-w-m. Rival: a personal name of the Amorite RU-MA-TUM type (Gelb 1980, no. 5306). One witness.

entries.meaning: Female (Hurrian personal name); rival the line as a heading, 'female (ones)'

cognates.Hurrian: aštuḫḫi 'féminin', opp. turuḫḫi 'masculin', from ašte 'femme'; instr. aš-tu-uḫ-ḫa-a-i (Laroche GLH 62); Ugaritic alphabetic aštḫ-n (GLH 63); Nuzi ᶠAš-du-uḫ-ḫa-a-a (NPN 37, 206); Aštuḫa, aš-tu-ḫa, f. (Sippar, TCL 1 109:14; Monti 2017, 502)

entries.note: PH 2 .1 A-SE-TU-*21F 1, the first entry, above RA-O-DI-KI 60, PI-RU-E-JU 60 and SE-SA-PA₃ 60, whole and undotted (GORILA I 288–289). aš-tu-ḫa with *21F = ḫa, SE writing š with the e of ašte: the Nuzi woman's name ᶠAš-du-uḫ-ḫa-a-a (NPN 37), Hurrian aštuḫḫi 'feminine' (Laroche GLH 62). Rivals: the line as a heading, 'female (ones)', reading GORILA's 1 as the first stroke of RA (Younger, Linear A Texts); A-SE ʾaššē + an unread TU-*21F. One witness.
entries.source: di Mino; Laroche GLH; NPN; Younger, Linear A Texts

entries.meaning: Ḫaru (Hurrian personal name); rival the Semitic name Ḫayru 'Excellent'

cognates.Hurrian: Nuzi Ḫa-a-ru, [Ḫa]-a-ru(m), f. of Alkiya (NPN 55); element ḫaru, cross-referred to ḫar 'H.? Anatolian?', with Ḫa-ru-se-en-ni at Ras Shamra (NPN 214)
cognates.Eblaite: ha-ru₁₂ ḫayru 'excellent', the rival (Pagan 1998, row 2259); *ḫVyVr- 'be favourable' (semitic_roots no. 988)

entries.note: HT 9a A-RU 4¼, the last recipient of the wine list under SA-RO · TE · VIN, before KU-RO 31¾; HT 49a A-RU 1 in a name list with TU-SU-PU₂ Tešub. ḫa-ru sign for sign, ḫ unwritten as in E-PA-TU Ḫebat: the Nuzi name Ḫa-a-ru (NPN 55), an element NPN refers to ḫar, 'H.? Anatolian?' (NPN 214). Rival: the Eblaite name ha-ru₁₂ ḫayru 'excellent' (Pagan 1998, row 2259), which needs the coda y unwritten.

entries.meaning: Arum-adal (Hurrian personal name), ar=o=m-adal 'The Strong one gave him'

cognates.Hurrian: Arum-atal, ar=o=m-adal 'The strong gave him': a-rum-a-tal, Mari (VHN 73); a-rum-a-dal, Ašnakkum (Talon 1997:123); a-ru-um-ma-tal, Ḫabiru Prism III 24 (Monti 2017, 228, 363, 425)

entries.note: HT 28a .5 A-RU-DA-RA GRA 5 *304 2, whole and undotted, at the head of the line, then OLE+DI 3: a recipient in the A-SI-JA-KA list with JA-*21F, SA-RA₂ and I-TA-JA (GORILA I 53). Hurrian Arum-atal, ar=o=m-adal 'The strong gave him', attested whole: a-rum-a-tal at Mari (VHN 73, apud Monti 2017, 228), a-rum-a-dal at Ašnakkum (Talon 1997, 123, apud Monti 2017, 363), a-ru-um-ma-tal on the Ḫabiru Prism (Monti 2017, 425). Cuneiform a-rum-a- closes arum with its m, which Linear A leaves unwritten as a coda; DA-RA -adal with its a absorbed and RA for the final l, as in KU-KU-DA-RA. Weak point: the m stands before a vowel in speech, and the Ḫabiru Prism writes it. One witness. Cf. A-RU.

entries.meaning: place name, heading the HT 11a list under KU-RO 10

cognates.Ugaritic: ảrr, the town ʾArruwa on the Siyannu border, URU ar-ru-wa (DULAT 102)
cognates.Akkadian: {uru}a-ru-ra, a town in Assurnasirpal II's annals (RGTC 7/3, citing RIMA 2 101.1 i 47)

entries.note: HT 11a .1 A-RU-RA, whole: the mark after RA is the fracture edge of the broken corner, and RU is written over an erasure (GORILA I 23). It heads A-RU-RA ]3, KA-RO-NA 2, *322-RI 1, KU-RO 10. Ugaritic ảrr is the town ʾArruwa on the border with Siyannu, URU ar-ru-wa, whose soldiers head a list, spr ḫrd ảrr 'list of the soldiers of ʾArr' (KTU 4.683:1; DULAT 102). {uru}a-ru-ra spells the name sign for sign in Assurnasirpal II's annals (RGTC 7/3, citing RIMA 2 101.1 i 47). One witness.

entries.meaning: Hand (personal name); rivals Yadīn 'he judges', Yadiʿ 'he knows'

cognates.Amorite: JAD-IM, IA-DI-IM (Gelb 1980, no. 3205); JA-DJIN+HADD-U, IA-DI-IN-D-IM (no. 3206), the Yadīn rival

entries.note: PH Wc 39, an MM II roundel from Vano LI, JA-DI on face a, RO rōš on face b, whole and undotted (GORILA II 94). ya-di sign for sign as the Amorite name IA-DI-IM (Gelb 1980, no. 3205), mimation unwritten, *yad- 'hand'. Rivals: Yadīn 'he judges' (Gelb no. 3206 IA-DI-IN-), Yadiʿ 'he knows', each with a final consonant unwritten. One witness. See I-DA, JE-DI and I-DU-NE-SI.

entries.meaning: Tuya (personal name, hypocoristic in -ya); rival Ḏū-Yā 'He of Yah'

cognates.Nuzi: TUIA, Tu-ú-ia, var. Tu-ú?-ia (NPN 156); -tuja 'H. Perhaps a formative in Akituja' (NPN 268)

entries.note: HT 7a .3 DU-JA 4, whole and undotted, under QE-TI · VIR after I-RU-JA 3, a Hurrian -ja hypocoristic (GORILA I 15). tu-ya sign for sign as the Nuzi name Tu-ú-ia (NPN 156), its element -tuja Hurrian (NPN 268). Rival: Ḏū-Yā 'He of Yah', ḏū as in DU-RU-WI ḏu-luwwī and DA-NA-SI Ḏā-Naśiʾ, + JA = Yā(h), as JA-*21F Yāh (HT 28b). One witness.

entries.meaning: lord, master (title, an entry in a KI-RO roster); rival a personal name
entries.note: HT 55a .1 ]KI-RO · MA-RE 1, whole and undotted, the first of single entries owed (GORILA I 106–107). mā-rē, the -MA-RE of JI-NU-MA-RE 'wine-lords'; Aramaic mārēʾ 'lord', mārēʾ malkîn 'lord of kings' (Dan 2:47), and Ebla mar-a 'the lord' (Pagan 1998, row 3651). Ugarit's mrủ, mur-u, is a class name of uncertain etymology (DULAT 564). Rival: a personal name. Weak point: MA-RE stands alone among single entries owed. One witness. See MA-RI-TA₂.

entries.meaning: Šata (personal name, heading the second section); rival śadā '(those of) the field'

cognates.Nuzi: ŠATA, Ša-a-ta, var. Ša-ta, f. of Urḫi-tešup (NPN 126)
cognates.Ugaritic: šd (I) 'open field; field, plot, estate' (DULAT 795), the rival

entries.note: HT 117a .7 SA-TA ·, whole and undotted, heading the second section over five names with 1 each, in the place MA-KA-RI-TE · KI-RO · U-MI-NA-SI holds in the first (GORILA I 197). ša-ta on primary values, sign for sign as the Nuzi name Ša-a-ta, Ša-ta (NPN 126), which NPN files under the Hurrian element šat (NPN 252). Rival: śadā '(those of) the field', TA writing d as the T class allows, the root of SA-DI šadī (#1804; DULAT 795), since HT 87 and HT 117b put group terms in this slot. One witness.

entries.meaning: Tunu (Hurrian personal name, owner's name on a double axe)

cognates.Hurrian: element tun- 'H.', cf. tu-u-ni, du-u-ni (KUB XXV 44, 45) (NPN 269); Nuzi TUN-TEŠUP, Du-un-te-šu-up, var. Du-un-te-šup, f. of Arbi (NPN 158)

entries.note: KA Zf 1, a bronze double axe from Kardamoutsa (BM 1954,10-20.1), TU and NU · on either side of the shaft hole, whole and undotted (GORILA IV 149). tu-nu on primary values: the Hurrian element tun- (NPN 269), as in the Nuzi name Tun-tešup (NPN 158). One witness.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'He is light'; rival mənōrāya 'lampstand (man)'

cognates.Ugaritic: PN nryn, syll. nu-ri-ia-nu, short form nu-ri-ia (DULAT 634)
cognates.Eblaite: su-nu-ri₂ šū-nūrī 'he is my light' (Pagan 1998, row 4282)
cognates.Amorite: NU-RA nūram (Gelb no. 5085)

entries.note: HT 115a .1 *47-NU-RA-JA · I · GRA+BOSm, whole and undotted, the first entry of a palimpsest (GORILA I 189); HT 115b repeats the frame with TI-NU-JA, a person. NU-RA-JA is nūr-aya, as Ugaritic nu-ri-ia beside nu-ri-ia-nu (DULAT 634). With *47 = so: šū 'he', as Ebla su-nu-ri₂ šū-nūrī 'He is my light' (Pagan 1998, row 4282); SO for šū is a vowel mismatch only. Rival: with *47 = mo, mənōrā 'lampstand' (Ug. mnrt, DULAT 558) + -aya. One witness. See NU-RO, *301-U-RA and JA-I-NWA-RO.

entries.meaning: rounds, round cakes of (a commodity); talent; rival the personal name Qaqqaru

cognates.Ugaritic: kkr 'talent' (DULAT 430–31); kkr ḥlb 'a talent of cheese' (DULAT 355)
cognates.Emar: ka-ak-ka-ri, ka-ak-ka-ru kakkaru 'talent, loaf of bread' (Emar 387:5; Pentiuc 2001, 91)

entries.note: HT 20 .2–.3 QE-KU-RE · DI ½, whole and undotted, the second entry under PA-RO-SU in a list where every entry takes a fraction (GORILA I 37). kik-kᵊrē, a construct before the commodity sign DI, as Hebrew kikkᵊrê kesep 'talents of silver' (2 Kgs 5:5). QE at its k value; Ugarit writes the word with ka₄, the QA sign (DULAT 430–31). Rival: the name Qaqqaru, spelled QA-QA-RU elsewhere at Haghia Triada. One witness. See QA-KU-RE, KI-KI-RA-JA and KE-KI-RU.

entries.meaning: rounds of (a commodity); talent

cognates.Akkadian: kakkaru, Qatna [q]a-a[q]-q[a]-r[u] (EA 53:32), Alalakh ka-qa-ru (CAD K 49–50)

entries.note: HT Wc 3017, a roundel, face a QA-KU-RE · DI-*306 ·, face b CYP+D · *304+PA, all signs whole and undotted (GORILA II 77). The a-vowel form of QE-KU-RE kikkᵊrē, again before a DI- word. QA for k as Ugarit's ka₄-ka₄-r[u] (DULAT 430–31). One witness.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'My judgment' (short form of a √d-y-n name); rival the whole group WA-DI-NI, Ugaritic PN wḏny

cognates.Amorite: Dīnī-Haddu, DI-NI-A-DU, DI-NA-A-DU (Gelb nos. 1513, 1512)
cognates.Linear A: DI-NA-U Dīnāyu beside WA on HT 16

entries.note: HT Wc 3007 WA-DI-NI, the only text; HT Wc 3008 face a WA · DI-NI, the point after WA in GORILA's transcription, face b RU-JA-TA-DI; all signs whole and undotted (GORILA II 74). WA is the cloth sign, alone on HT Wc 3019 (WA ¼) and KH Wc 2124, and beside DI-NA-U Dīnāyu on HT 16. dī-nī 'my judgment', as Alalakh Dīnī-Haddu, DI-NI-A-DU (Gelb no. 1513). Rival: one word, Ugaritic PN wḏny, 'etym. unc.' (DULAT 929). Two witnesses.

entries.meaning: Ḫaluti (woman's name, seal owner); rival ʾālôt 'oaths, curses'

cognates.Nuzi: Ha-lu-ti, var. Ha-lu-u-ti, a woman's name (NPN 51)
cognates.Hebrew: ʾālāh, pl. ʾālôt 'oaths, curses' (Deut 29:20; 30:7; 2 Chr 34:24), the rival

entries.note: CR Zg 4, a steatite reel seal (CMS XII 96), face b A-RO-TE under a lozenge-net relief, face a I-DA-DA, read from the impression, the signs whole (Younger, Linear A Texts, citing Raison–Pope 1994, 242–243). A seal names its owner: Ḫaluti, the Nuzi woman's name Ḫa-lu-ti (NPN 51), on the Hurrian element ḫal(u)- (NPN 212–213), with A for ḫa as in A-RU Ḫaru. Cf. Linear B a-ro-te (PY La 622), obscure (Killen 2024, 935). Rival: ʾālôt 'oaths, curses' on primary values, the plural of ʾālāh (Deut 29:20; 2 Chr 34:24), whose ō needs the Canaanite shift. Nuzi spelling does not keep e and i apart (Wegner 2000, 38), so TE matches -ti; cf. Tigunāni Ḫalut, ḫal=o=t(ta) 'Carry me away!' (Monti 2017, 428). Weak point: A writes ḫa. One witness.
entries.source: di Mino; NPN; Killen 2024; Wegner 2000; Monti 2017

entries.meaning: Kutukkore (Hurrian personal name)

cognates.Hurrian: Nuzi KUTUKKA, Ku-duq-qa, var. Ku-tu-ug-ga, Ku-tu-uq-qa (NPN 93), the element kutukka H., cf. ku-du-uk-ku KUB XXVII 38 ii 10 (NPN 231; Laroche GLH 150); Kutukkeja, Ku-dug-ge-ia (NPN 93); -re 'H.? … Probably identical with -ri' (NPN 248)

entries.note: ZA 8 .2 KU-TU-KO-RE with a fraction, whole and undotted, an entry in the fig issue headed KI-RA · (GORILA III 165). ku-tu-k(k)o-re: the Hurrian base kutukk- of Nuzi Kutukka (NPN 93), with the suffix -re of Antare and Humere (NPN 248), the geminate unwritten. Base and suffix are each attested, not together. One witness.

entries.meaning: Tati-te, '(Teššup) loved' (Hurrian personal name, hypocoristic)

cognates.Hurrian: tad- 'aimer' (Laroche GLH 248); tat 'H. … Cf. tat, "love," in Tuš.' (NPN 263); Nuzi TATI, Ta-ti, and TATIP-TEŠUP, Ta-ti-ip-te-šup (NPN 150); -te, the 'shortened var.' of -teja, itself the hypocoristic of -tešup (NPN 264)

entries.note: PK 1 .3 TA₂-TI-TE 1, whole and undotted, before O-KA-MI-ZA-SI-I-NA, in a roster of names each counted 1 (GORILA I 281). ta-ti-te: Nuzi Ta-ti beside Tatip-tešup (NPN 150), with -te for -tešup (NPN 264), 'Teššup loved'. TA₂ writes a t-, its vowel open. One witness.

entries.meaning: Akipe-te, '(Teššup) brought' (Hurrian personal name, hypocoristic)

cognates.Hurrian: ag- 'amener, apporter', agi-, agib- in names, Akib-Tešub (Laroche GLH 36); Nuzi Akipei, A-ki-be-e-i, 'Probably < akip-' (NPN 14, 198); [A-ki]p-te-ia, A-ki-te-ia, and A-kip-te-šup (NPN 198); -te, the 'shortened var.' of -teja (NPN 264)

entries.note: KH 10 .3–4 A-KI-PI | E-TE GRA 90, run over the line end and printed as one word in GORILA's normalized line, after I-PA-SA-JA Ipšaja · QA-*118 (GORILA III 36–37). a-ki-pe-te: the Hurrian stem akip- 'brought' of Akip-tešup (Laroche GLH 36), A-KI-PI-E sign for sign as Nuzi Akipei, A-ki-be-e-i (NPN 14), + -te for -teja (NPN 264), as Nuzi [A-ki]p-te-ia (NPN 198). A recipient of grain beside the Hurrian Ipšaja. One witness.

entries.meaning: Ṣubʾu (personal name); rival ṣābu 'workers, troop'

cognates.Amorite: ṢUBUʾ-UM, ZU-BU-U₂-UM and ZU-BU-UM (Gelb 1980, nos. 6581–6582)

entries.note: HT 63 .1 SU-PU₂, whole and undotted, the third entry under *305 · TE 1, after KA-TI 1, against the tablet's upper right corner; no numeral survives, and GORILA's normalized line brackets the end, SU-PU₂[ (GORILA I 118–119). ṣu-bu, PU₂ for bu as in DU-PU₂-RE dubur, the final ʾu unwritten as in TA-PA tappāʾu: the Amorite name Ṣubʾu (Gelb 1980, nos. 6581–6582). Linear B su-po (KN Dc 5812) and su-pu-wo (KN C 912) are men's names at Knossos (DMic II 304). Cf. HT 8b .1 SU-PU₂-*188 1. Rival: ṣābu 'workers, troop' (#1332), a collective under the personnel sign *305. One witness.
entries.source: di Mino; Gelb 1980; Pagan 1998; DMic II

entries.meaning: for the corvée gang (terminative -SE); the corvée word of MA-ZA / ME-ZA
entries.cognates: see ME-ZA
entries.note: ZA 15a .4 MI-ZA-SE 3, first entry under ME+VIN in a wine issue, beside *364-KE-MA-SE Šakma-se (GORILA III 183). The corvée word of MA-ZA mazza (ZA 10b) and ME-ZA massu (HT 10a, HT 85b), MI for ma is a vowel mismatch only. -SE the terminative 'to, for': Akkadian -iš = ana + genitive (Huehnergard 2011, 311). Rival gloss '(men) of the corvée', -SE as the Luwian possessive -ass(a/i)- (Yakubovich 2015, 13); rival name the Edomite Mizzâ (Gen 36:13).

entries.meaning: ʾItniša (personal name), the Mari name IT-NU-ŠA; rival ʾitnī-ša 'her gift (portion)'

cognates.Amorite: IT-NU-ŠA, Mari (Gelb 1980, AS 21, 610, no. 3828)

entries.note: ZA 15a .2 I-TI-NI-SA 10, intact, second entry under the first wine heading, after QE-SI-ZU-E 57 (GORILA III 183). ʾi-t-n-ša sign for sign as the Mari name IT-NU-ŠA (Gelb 1980, AS 21, 610); NI for nu is a vowel mismatch only. Rival: ʾitnī-ša 'her gift (portion)', Ugaritic ỉtnn 'present' (DULAT 119). One witness. See JE-TA-NA, A-DU-NI-TA-NA and MA-TI-TI.

entries.meaning: Kati-tati (Hurrian personal name); rival katītat 'beaten (oil)'

cognates.Hurrian: kat-: Nuzi Kataia, Qa-ta-a-a, and Katiri, Qa-ti-ri (NPN 224); -tati: Ḫamar-tati, Šenna-tati, also Še-en-da-ti (NPN 263); tat 'love' (NPN 263)

entries.note: HT 12 .1 QA-TI-DA-TE · OLE+DI 5, the heading of an issue of oils, fats, wool and figs totalled DA-I 50 (GORILA I 25). qa-ti-da-te: Nuzi writes kat- with QA (Qa-ti-ri, NPN 224) and -tati with DA (Še-en-da-ti, NPN 263). A recipient heading a mixed issue, as A-PU₂-NA-DU on HT 14. Rival: katītat 'beaten (oil)', √k-t-t (#3644), Hebrew šemen kātît (Exod 27:20), an adjective only. One witness.

entries.meaning: Kapizzi (Hurrian personal name), 'kapizzi-jewel'; rival kupṯu 'headdress'

cognates.Hurrian: Kapizza, ka-bi-iz-za 'Like the kapizzi-jewel', and Kapizz(i)-atal, Šubat-Enlil (Monti 2017, 345–346)

entries.note: KH 5 .3 KU-PA-ZU, after WI-NA-DU · *301-NA ·, before a cyperus entry on .4 (GORILA III 25). ZU = zu, as in RU-ZU-NA: the Ugarit name ka-bi-iz-zi, Hurrian kabizzi 'jewel' (Monti 2017, 346), KU-PA for ka-bi a vowel mismatch only. DULAT 424 sets ka-bi-iz-zi beside kbs 'fuller', which ZU cannot spell. Rival on ZU = ṯu: kupṯu 'headdress', Ug. kpṯ, Akk. kub/pšu (DULAT 448–449). One witness.

entries.meaning: Kattike (Hurrian personal name), on kad- 'to say'; rival katki 'utterance'

cognates.Hurrian: kat, katt and the formative -ke, var. -ki (Inniki, Unniki, Zirriki), Nuzi Qa-ti-ri (NPN 224); kad- I, katt- 'to say' (Richter 2012, 195); Mari Katiya, Kattiri (Monti 2017, 255, 432)

entries.note: KH 7a .4 QA-TI-KI VIR+*313b 4, CYP+D ⅓, the entry under I-JA-PA-ME · TA-TA · (GORILA III 29). kat(t)- + the formative -ki (NPN 224), on kad- 'to say' (Richter 2012, 195). Nuzi writes the base with QA (Qa-ti-ri), as QA-TI-DA-TE Kati-tati. Rival: katki 'utterance' (Richter 2012, 196), a noun that cannot draw men. One witness.

entries.meaning: Kaw-tatta (Hurrian personal name), kaw- + tatt- 'love'; rival Ugaritic PN kwt

cognates.Hurrian: kaw, Qa-wi-in-ni (NPN 224); Kawiya, kav=i=ya (Monti 2017, 346); tat 'love', tatt, Allai-tatta (NPN 263); Tatta, tatt=a, Mari (Monti 2017, 302); Tatta, da-da, da-da-e, Terqa (Monti 2017, 325)
cognates.Ugaritic: kwn PN, 'the element kaw=', ka-ú-a-ni; kwt PN (DULAT 469)

entries.note: HT 13 .1 KA-U-DE-TA, heading the wine list VIN · TE · to RE-ZA, TE-TU, TE-KI, KU-ZU-NI, DA-SI-*118 and I-DU-NE-SI, KU-RO 130½ (GORILA I 27). KA-U = kaw-, as A-RA-U-DA ʾArwada: Hurrian kaw (NPN 224; Kawiya, Monti 2017, 346) + tatt- 'love' (NPN 263). Terqa writes Tatta da-da, da-da-e (Monti 2017, 325): D for t, and e beside a. Cf. Kawinni, written Qa-wi-in-ni, Qa-we-en-ni, Ka-wi-ni and Ga-wi-in (NPN 224), and Šenna-tati, written Še-en-da-ti (NPN 263). Both elements are attested, never together. Rival: the Ugaritic name kwt, which leaves DE (DULAT 469). One witness.

entries.meaning: Kawṯuni (Hurrian personal name Kaw-šuni); rival Kawṯān, Heb. Kûšān

cognates.Hurrian: kaw (NPN 224); Kawiya, kav=i=ya (Monti 2017, 346); -šuni in Awa-šuni, A-wa-šu-ni (NPN 208)
cognates.Ugaritic: Hurrian ảủpš, var. ảủpṯ, ảủpṯn, syll. a-up-šu (DULAT 4); kṯn PN, ku-ši-nu; kṯn TN, cf. Heb. kwšn (DULAT 467)

entries.note: HT 26b .2–3 KA-U-ZU-NI 4, a count of men under VIR+[?] 9, between ]-RO-NI 3 and KI+MU 12 (GORILA I 47). ka-u-ṯu-ni: Hurrian kaw (NPN 224) + -šuni (Awa-šuni, NPN 208), the Hurrian š in ZU = ṯu as Ugarit writes ảủpš also ảủpṯ (DULAT 4). Same base as KA-U-DE-TA Kaw-tatta. Rival: Kawṯān, the place name kṯn, Heb. Kûšān (DULAT 467; Hab 3:7). One witness.

entries.meaning: Redis (Egyptian personal name rdj⸗s), 'the one she has given'; rival Safaitic RDS 'Breaker'

cognates.Egyptian: rdj⸗s, r:D37-s, r:di s, m. and f., 11th Dyn. to SIP (PNM: Cairo CG 23045, Louvre C 31, Berlin ÄM 1190, RILN 10); sꜣt-rdj⸗s, rdj⸗s-n⸗j
cognates.Safaitic: rds PN, Ar. radasa 'to stone, break' (Harding 1971, 275)

entries.note: HT 85b .4 RE-DI-SE 1, eighth of eleven single-unit entries under KI-KI-RA-JA ·, between ME-ZA 1 and WA-DU-NI-MI 1; written on .3, erased, and written again on .4 (GORILA I 133). Egyptian rdj⸗s: ⸗s written -SE as in DI-DI-KA-SE, rdj 'give' as in PA-TA-DA. Same name as RA-TI-SE (HT 6b), which also stands beside WA-DU-NI-MI. Semitic scripts write Egyptian d with ṭ, never d (Hoch 1994, 427), and Linear A, with no ṭ series, writes it DI here and TI there. Rival: Safaitic RDS, Ar. radasa 'to stone, break', one witness (Harding 1971, 275).
entries.source: Ilin-Tomich 2025 (PNM v6), s.v. rdj⸗s; Hoch 1994, 427; Harding 1971, 275; di Mino

entries.meaning: Ratis (Egyptian personal name rdj⸗s, the name RE-DI-SE), 'the one she has given'; rival Safaitic RDS 'Breaker'

cognates.Egyptian: rdj⸗s, r:D37-s, r:di s, m. and f., 11th Dyn. to SIP (PNM: Cairo CG 23045, Louvre C 31, Berlin ÄM 1190, RILN 10)
cognates.Safaitic: rds PN, Ar. radasa 'to stone, break' (Harding 1971, 275)

entries.note: HT 6b .2 RA-TI-SE 1, after WA-DU-NI-MI 3 and a fraction, on a face written over an erasure (GORILA I 13). The name RE-DI-SE (HT 85b), which also stands beside WA-DU-NI-MI, with TI for Egyptian d: Semitic scripts write Egyptian d with ṭ (Hoch 1994, 427), and Linear A has no ṭ series. Rival: Safaitic RDS, Ar. radasa 'to stone, break' (Harding 1971, 275).
entries.source: Ilin-Tomich 2025 (PNM v6), s.v. rdj⸗s; Hoch 1994, 427; Harding 1971, 275; di Mino

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Mourner' (Akk. lallaru); rival Amorite Li-lu-ri

cognates.Akkadian: lallaru 'mourner, wailer', PN ᵐLa-al-la-r[u], OB Nippur (CAD L 48)
cognates.Amorite: Li-la-ru, Li-lu-ri, root LLR (Gelb 1980, nos. 4365, 4367)
cognates.Hurrian: lallari-, meaning unknown (Laroche, GLH s.v.)

entries.note: ZA 10b .5 RA₂-RO-RE 2, after A-MI-TA 3 and before PA-JA-RE 1 (GORILA III 171), all three signs whole. Akkadian lallaru 'mourner, wailer', a name at OB Nippur, ᵐLa-al-la-r[u] (CAD L 48); RA₂ writes l as in SA-RA₂ šarra, RO the second l as in KU-RO kull. Rivals: Amorite Li-la-ru, Li-lu-ri, root LLR (Gelb 1980, nos. 4365, 4367); Hurrian lallari-, meaning unknown (Laroche, GLH s.v.). One witness.
entries.source: CAD L 48; Gelb 1980; Laroche GLH; di Mino

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Pomegranate' (Ug. lrmn); recipient of pigs

cognates.Akkadian: lurmû 'pomegranate', MA lurimā'u lu-ri-ma-e, lurimtu EA 25 (CAD L 255 f.); PN Lu-ri-in-di-ya (HALOT 1242)

entries.note: HT 118 .4 RI-RU-MA 10, a recipient of pigs after MA-DI, QA-QA-RU and A-RI-SU (GORILA I 200 f.), all three signs whole. Ugaritic lrmn 'pomegranate' (DULAT 499); Middle Assyrian lurimāʾu, lu-ri-ma-e (CAD L 255 f.). RI writes l; the final n is unwritten. A man's name: Hebrew Rimmon (2 Sam 4:2), Akkadian Lu-ri-in-di-ya (HALOT 1242). Cf. PH(?)31b [·]-RU-MA-TI, Akkadian lurimtu. One witness.
entries.source: di Mino; DULAT; CAD L; HALOT

entries.meaning: ʾAddu-ʿazz (personal name), 'Addu is strong'; rival Hadas 'Myrtle'

cognates.Ugaritic: ʕz 'strong'; mt ʕz bʕl ʕz, 1.6 VI 17 (DULAT 193–194)
cognates.Akkadian: Enlil-ezzu, {d}en-lil₂-ez-zu (ORACC)
cognates.Amorite: ʿAzz-ʿammi, ʿAzzu (Gelb 1980, 568)

entries.note: PK 1 .2 A-DU-ZA 1, the first name below the ruling, after KA-QA 2 and before TA₂-TA-RE 1, in a list of names at 1 each (GORILA I 281). Addu + ʿazz 'strong', the god first as in A-DU-NI-TA-NA and A-DU-KU-MI-NA. ZA writes (ʿa)zz. Ugaritic sets the god before ʿz: mt ʿz 'Mot was strong' (KTU 1.6 VI 17; DULAT 194); cf. Heb. ʾElʿûzay (1 Chr 12:6), Akk. Enlil-ezzu. Phoenician ʿŠTRTʿZ 'ʿAštart is (my) Strength' sets ʿz after the god, beside ʿZBʿL (Benz 1972, 175, 222; Krahmalkov 2000, 392). Rival: hadas 'myrtle' (K0080), which needs ZA for s. One witness.

entries.meaning: chariot soldiers, archers (a troop drawing rations); rival a name ZU-*301-SE-DE

cognates.Ugaritic: ṯnn, pl. ṯnnm, syll. LÚ ša-na-ni, LÚ ša-na-nu-ma; rb ṯnnm 'chief archer' (DULAT 909)
cognates.Akkadian: šanannu 'archer(?)', MB Alalakh and Ras Shamra: 1006 ERÍN.MEŠ ša-na-an-nu (Wiseman, Alalakh 183:2); sheep belonging to the LÚ.MEŠ ša-na-an-ni-e (Alalakh 352:6); Hurrian pl. LÚ.MEŠ ša-na-nu-ḫē (Alalakh 350:9) (CAD Š/1 366)
cognates.Egyptian: snny, *ṯannānu 'chariot soldier, archer' (Hoch 1994, 261, no. 371)

entries.note: ARKH 2 .3–4 ZU-*301-SE-DE-*21F-*118 6, read ṯannān ṣēd ḥiṭṭa 'the chariot soldiers: provision of wheat, 6', under SI-DA-TE ṣēdat 'provisions', between A-SI-DA-TO-I 12 and A-SU-PU-WA 4 (GORILA III 6–7). *301 and *21F over erasures, no dividers. SE-DE ṣēd, √ṣ-y-d as SI-DA-TE. Ugarit lists the ṯnnm as a group with named members (KTU 4.68:70; 4.126:4), with a rb ṯnnm (4.382:5). ZU writes ṯ before any vowel or none, as in A-ZU-RA ʾAṯirat. Egyptian snny, 'of the chariotry', takes the arrow determinative (Hoch 1994, 262, no. 371). Alalakh allots sheep to the šanannu as a body (CAD Š/1 366). Weak point: the must list turns to wheat without a logogram; *21F-*118 takes its numeral without one on ZA 14 too (*21F-*118 1). Rival: one name ZU-*301-SE-DE + ḥiṭṭa 6. One witness.

entries.meaning: Kukkadal (Hurrian personal name), kukk- + adal 'strong'; rival ḳdr 'dark'

cognates.Hurrian: kukk, ᶠKukku, Kukkuia, ᶠKukk-urašše (NPN 90, 229); adal 'strong', Akkadian adallu = gašru (Laroche GLH s.v. adali), -atal, -adal in Zi-li-ip-a-da-al, Ḫa-ši-ba-da-al, Pu-ut-ti-ma-da-al (NPN 207); Mari Tawen-atal, tav=i=n(na)-adal 'Strong, pour (him)!' (VHN 297; Monti 2017, 302)
cognates.Linear B: ku-ka-da-ro, a man at Knossos, KN Uf 836.b (DMic I)

entries.note: HT 117a .7 KU-KU-DA-RA 1, all four signs whole and undotted, the first name under SA-TA Šata (GORILA I 197). Hurrian kukk- (NPN 229; ᶠKukku, Kukkuia, ᶠKukk-urašše, NPN 90) + adal 'strong' (Laroche GLH s.v. adali; NPN 207; Mari Tawen-atal 'Strong, pour (him)!', Monti 2017, 302), DA for d as Nuzi Zi-li-ip-a-da-al and Ur III Ḫa-ši-ba-da-al write it (NPN 207), RA for the final l. Linear B ku-ka-da-ro, a man at Knossos (KN Uf 836.b; DMic I), writes the a of adal. Both elements are attested, never together; Laroche counts Kuku among the Lallnamen (GLH Intro §6). Rival: ḳdr 'dark' (#1679) with KU-KU reduplicated, as KI-DA-RO Qidaru in the same roster. One witness.
entries.source: di Mino; NPN; Laroche GLH; Monti 2017

entries.meaning: the Kushite woman (origin label); rival kusītu 'robe'

cognates.Egyptian: Kꜣš 'Kush' (AED lemma 163680); ı͗kšj.t 'Kushite woman'; Coptic ⲉϭⲱϣ, ⲉϭⲟϣⲉ 'Kushite' (ThotBank 486)

entries.note: HT 117a .7–8 KO-SA-I-TI 1, complete, I dotted, the second of five under SA-TA Šata, between KU-KU-DA-RA and DA-MI-NU (GORILA I 197). KO writes the ō of Coptic ⲉϭⲱϣ 'Nubian', feminine ⲉϭⲟⲟϣⲉ (Vycichl 1983, 50, apud Kilani 2020), SA-I the gentilic glide of Amarna LÚ.MEŠ ka-ši-yi (EA 287:33), I-TI the feminine nisbe -īt: Kōšayīt 'the Kushite woman', an origin label as U-SU ʾUšu and U-DI-MI ʾUdmī on the same tablet. Rival: kusītu 'robe' (Ebla gu-zi-tum, Amarna ku-zi-ti, Ug. kst; GlOS 1, 325), a garment in a roster of persons, where KU-SI-TI is the expected spelling. One witness.

entries.meaning: Zizapa (Hurrian personal name), ziz- 'chest'; rival Amorite ʿIziz-ab

cognates.Hurrian: Mari Zizap(-)a, zi-za-ba (VHN 277), Zizapān, zi-za-ba-an, ziz=a=b=ān (Sasson 1974, 372; ARM XVI/1, 244); Zizi, ziz=i 'Chest' (Monti 2017, 319)
cognates.Amorite: ¹IZIZ-AB, ʿIziz-ab, the rival (Gelb 1980, no. 2677)

entries.note: PH 2 .4 SE-SA-PA₃ 60, the last entry before the break, intact and undotted (GORILA I 288–289). Mari Zizap(-)a, zi-za-ba (VHN 277), and Zizapān, ziz=a=b=ān (ARM XVI/1, 244), on the stem ziz- of Zizi, ziz=i 'Chest' (Monti 2017, 319). Sign for sign, PA₃ for b, SE for zi. Same tablet as A-SE-TU-*21F Aštuḫḫa. Rival: Amorite ʿIziz-ab (Gelb 1980, no. 2677), ʿzz + ʾab, with the initial unwritten. One witness.

entries.meaning: Tarinna (Hurrian personal name), stem tarinn-; rival trn 'mast'

cognates.Hurrian: Tarinnam, ta-ri-nam, tarinn(i)=a=m(e/a) (VHN 299; Monti 2017, 351); Tarinam, ta-ri-nam, Šemšara 2:98 (Monti 2017, 413); Tarinze, ta-ri-in-ze (VHN 299; Monti 2017, 301)

entries.note: HT 10b .1–2 TA-RI-NA 15, TA closing .1 and RI-NA opening .2, whole and undotted, on a face written over an erasure (GORILA I 21); after U-TI 1 and DA-RE 2, before *312-TA 6½. Hurrian stem tarinn(i): Tarinnam, tarinn(i)=a=m(e/a) (VHN 299; Monti 2017, 351), Tarinam at Šemšara (Monti 2017, 413), Tarinze (Monti 2017, 301). Sign for sign, the final -m unwritten. Rival: Ugaritic trn 'mast' (#2979), out of place in a grain list. One witness.

entries.meaning: Kariru (personal name, Nuzi Qa-ri-ru, Ka-ri-ru); rival karr- 'ram'

cognates.Akkadian: Nuzi Qa-ri-ru, Ka-ri-ru, Ka-ri-ru(m), Qa-ri-ri (NPN 80), 'Root qrr, "to burn"? Cf. Qar-ru-ru' (NPN 322)
cognates.Hurrian: 'H. if formed on kar' (NPN 223), the rival analysis

entries.note: HT Wc 3003, a roundel (HM 77), KA-RE-RO alone, all three signs whole and undotted, no ideogram (GORILA II 72). Nuzi Qa-ri-ru, Ka-ri-ru(m), Qa-ri-ri, at least six men (NPN 80); Gelb gives root qrr, cf. Qar-ru-ru (NPN 322), Purves a Hurrian kar- (NPN 223). Sign for sign, RE for ri. A word alone on a roundel as ZU-DI-RA on HT Wc 3011 and PA-SE-JA on HT Wc 3002. Rival: *ka/irr- 'ram' (#2220; Ug. kr, DULAT 449), the roundel's commodity, with the r written twice. One witness.

entries.meaning: Qumalu 'Louse' (personal name); rival kumru 'priest'

cognates.Safaitic: QML, personal name, 'Ar. qaml, louse', four witnesses; Thamudic QMLT, Qatabanic QMLM (Harding 1971, 488)

entries.note: HT 20 .1–.2 KU-MA-JU ¼, KU at the end of .1 after the heading PA-RO-SU ·, MA-JU at the head of .2, all three signs whole and undotted (GORILA I 37). Geʿez qʷəmal, Harari qumāy 'louse' (Leslau 1987, 432), the qʷ the u of KU; the Safaitic name QML 'louse' (Harding 1971, 488). JU writes lu. First entry under PA-RO-SU Parʿōš 'Flea'; SA-RE-JU Šarr-ēlu is another name in the list. Rivals: kumru 'priest' (Amorite kumrum, Gelb 1980, 23), which needs JU for ru; Amorite GML 'to please, to spare' (Gelb 1980, 19). One witness.

entries.meaning: Tatta (Hurrian personal name), stem tatt-; rival the Anatolian name Tata

cognates.Hurrian: ᶠTatta, ta-at-ta, tatt=a, three times at Mari (VHN 301; Monti 2017, 302); Tatta, da-da, at Terqa (Monti 2017, 325) and ᶠta-at-ta at Tuttul (Monti 2017, 335)
cognates.Hittite: Tatta (HKM 25 obv. 2; KBo 30.37 obv. i 7′) and Tata (KBo 50.67 obv. ii 25′), the Anatolian name (Hittite Personal Names 0.1), the rival

entries.note: KH 7a .3 I-JA-PA-ME · TA-TA ·, whole and undotted, a section heading with no logogram or number, before QA-TI-KI VIR+*313b 4 (GORILA III 29). Hurrian ᶠTatta, a woman at Mari (Monti 2017, 302), sign for sign with the geminate unwritten. Rival: the Anatolian name Tata/Tatta (Marizza and Cammarosano, Hittite Personal Names, s.v. Tata, Tatta). One witness.
entries.source: di Mino; Monti 2017; Marizza and Cammarosano

entries.meaning: Measurer (professional-title PN), of grain; rival a name on g-y-l 'to rejoice'

cognates.Arabic: kāʾil 'measurer', active participle of kāla 'to measure (grain)'; kayl 'measure' (Q 12:59–65)

entries.note: ZA 8 .6 KA-I-RO 4 B B, intact, the last entry of the fig list headed KI-RA · (GORILA III 165), with the largest share, two entries after MA-KA-I-SE. kāʾil 'measurer', active participle of √k-y-l 'to measure (grain)': Arb. kayyāl 'a measurer of corn', mikyāl 'a measure for corn' (Lane 3005), kayl 'measure' (Q 12:59–65). I writes ʾi, RO the final l as in KU-RO kull; A-I writes -ay- in DA-I-PI-TA on the same tablet. Rival: a name on √g-y-l 'to rejoice', Heb. gîl (HALOT 189–190). One attestation.

entries.meaning: personal name Qāti 'Hand'; rivals Gattī 'the man of the press, the Gittite', Qəhātî 'Kohathite', Kittî 'Kittian'

cognates.Eblaite: ga-ti /qāti/ 'hand', personal name (Pagan 1998, row 1975), in 6 texts (EbDA; ARET 1 15 v. 6, 2)
cognates.Ugaritic (rival): gt /gittu/ 'wine or olive press; farmstead, estate' (DULAT 307)
cognates.Hebrew (rival): gat 'winepress'; gentilic hag-Gittî 'the Gittite' (2 Sam 6:10; 15:18 hag-Gittîm)

entries.note: HT 63 .1 KA-TI 1, both signs whole and undotted, under the personnel logogram *305, after TE 1 and before the name SU-PU₂ (GORILA I 118–119). The name Qāti 'Hand', as Ebla ga-ti (Pagan 1998, row 1975); KA writes qa. Rivals: Gattī, gat 'press' with the nisbe -ī, the Ugaritic gt being both the press and the estate around it; Qəhātî 'Kohathite' (Num 3:27), the medial h unwritten; Kittî 'Kittian' (Gen 10:4 Kittîm), against the a of KA. One witness. See QE-TI.

entries.meaning: Gūda 'luck' (personal name), Amorite Guʾuda; rivals Kutta, qāʾid 'chief'

cognates.Amorite: GUʾUD-A, GU-U₂-DA, an Ur III name (Gelb 1980, no. 1791)

entries.note: HT 122a, after KU-RO 31: KU-DA 1, the one man that brings the two faces to PO-TO-KU-RO 97 (HT 122b; 31 + 65 + 1), a name added below the total. Amorite GUʾUD-A, written GU-U₂-DA (Gelb 1980, no. 1791), sign for sign with the glottal stop unwritten; KU writes gu. Sanmartín files gu-ú-da under gudd, gūd 'luck; DN' (GlOS 1, 175). Rivals: Kutta, Ku-ut-ta, a name NPN marks H.? (NPN 231); qāʾid 'chief' (#51; Sabaic qwd, Beeston 1982, 110). One witness.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'his shout of joy'; rival two names, RA-NA and TU-SU

cognates.Arabic: rannah 'a sound, voice, or cry, in joy or sorrow', pl. rannāt (Lane 1164)
cognates.Hebrew: rinnāh 'ringing cry', rinnātî, rinnātām; Rinnāh, a man of Judah (1 Chr 4:20; BDB 943)
cognates.Ugaritic: /r-n(-n)/ 'to shout, raise one's voice', ảrnn (KTU 1.82:6; DULAT 731)

entries.note: PK 1 .6 RA-NA-TU-SU 1, one word, written with its 1 and the next NI over an erasure, in a roster of names each counted 1 (GORILA I 281). rannat-u-šu: the verbal noun rannat- of √r-n-n 'cry out', nominative -u, and -šu 'his'; the geminate is unwritten. Arabic rannah keeps the a of RA; Hebrew rinnāh takes the same suffixes (rinnātî 'my cry', Ps 17:1). Neo-Babylonian Bānītušu, ᵐDU₃-tu₂-šu₂ (GCCI 1, 63; YOS 17, 316), joins a -t- noun to -šu the same way. -šu keeps PS *-su 'his', which the change to *-hu reached in most but not all West Semitic languages (Huehnergard 2019, 51, 72–73 n. 5). Rivals: two names, RA-NA and TU-SU (TU-SU stands alone on .6–7); Egyptian rnn 'jubeln' (DULAT 731), which leaves -TU-SU unread. One witness. See A-RE-PI-RE-NA.
entries.source: di Mino; Lane; BDB; DULAT; Huehnergard 2019

entries.meaning: herdsman of the small cattle (title, over a flock of 60); rival a personal name

cognates.Arabic: huwa rāʿī ad-daqāʾiq 'he is the pastor of sheep, or goats'; daqīqa 'small cattle', opposed to jalīla 'camels' (Lane 896)
cognates.Akkadian: rēʾû, rāʾû 'herdsman, shepherd'; reʾû unīqi 'shepherd of she-kids' (CAD R 303)

entries.note: PH 2 .1–2 RA-O-DI-KI 60, RA at the end of .1, under A-SE-TU-*21F (the female small-cattle sign) and beside PI-RU-E-JU 60 and SE-SA-PA₃ 60 (GORILA I 288–289). rāʿû diqqi: the contracted nominative rāʿû < *rāʿiyu 'herdsman', O writing ʿu, and the genitive diqqi of *diqq- 'small (cattle)', as in KA-NI-JA-MI qāniy-yammi. The same root as RO-E rōʿē (PH 24). Akkadian has the masculine noun diqqu 'small one' (CAD D 159), Ugaritic the masculine dq 'tiny, fine' (DULAT 275). Weak point: the spelling differs from RO-E. Rivals: a personal name; Hurrian -tiki (Papan-tiki, Monti 2017, 411), which leaves RA-O unread. One witness.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'the Foremost is judge' (Ugaritic PN ảwldn); rival ʾIl-dīn 'El is judge'

cognates.Ugaritic: ảwldn PN, etym. unc. (DULAT 128; 4.54:9, 4.129:5); ảwl 'priority, supremacy' (DULAT 128); bʕldn PN, syll. ba-aʔ-la-da/dá-ni (DULAT 207); dn 'judgment, case, sentence' (DULAT 273)
cognates.Arabic: ʾāla, ʾawila 'to precede, to be first' (Lane 126)
cognates.Linear A: O-RA₂ ʾŌl, DI-NE dīn; DI-RE-DI-NA ʾaddīr-dīnā, DI-NI Dīnī

entries.note: HT 6a .4 O-RA₂-DI-NE 2, all four signs whole and undotted, in a list of NI after MA-*321 10 and before KA-PA-QE 5¾ (GORILA I 13). Two elements: O-RA₂ ʾŌl 'the Foremost' < *ʾawl 'priority, supremacy', O writing ʾō < *ʾaw as in O-SU-QA-RE ʾō Sukar and RA₂ its primary value la; DI-NE dīn 'judgment' (semitic_roots S36). DULAT sets ảwl beside the name ('Cf. ảwldn', DULAT 128), and bʿldn shares its last element (DULAT 207): ʾŌl stands where ʾIl and Baʿl stand in ỉldn and bʿldn. Ebla glosses GABA.GÁL with a-wa-lum, ʔawal 'priority, supremacy', and Arabic has ʔawwal 'first' (GlOS 1, 53). Rivals: ỉldn ʾIl-dīn 'El is judge' (DULAT 52), O for ʾi; ảrdn, syll. a-ra-ad-ni (DULAT 96), RA₂ for ra. One witness.

entries.meaning: the Foremost (name element), from 'priority, supremacy'

cognates.Arabic: ʾāla, ʾawila 'to precede, to be first' (Lane 126)
cognates.Eblaite: ʾūl 'strength', a name element, √ʾwl 'to be strong, foremost' (Pagan 1998, elements 1971–1972)

entries.note: Attested only within O-RA₂-DI-NE ʾŌl-dīn (HT 6a .4). ʾōl < *ʾawl, O writing ʾō < *ʾaw as in O-SU-QA-RE ʾō Sukar, RA₂ its primary value la. Dietrich and Loretz read ảwl in 1.12 II 56 as an address, 'oh Erster!' (DULAT 128). Rival: ʾil 'god', as in ỉldn (DULAT 52), O for ʾi. One witness.

entries.meaning: judgment (name element)

cognates.Ugaritic: dn 'judgment, case, sentence' (DULAT 273); the last element of ảwldn, ỉldn, bʕldn (DULAT 128, 52, 207)

entries.note: Attested only within O-RA₂-DI-NE ʾŌl-dīn (HT 6a .4): dī-n, the final vowel dead. The same element as DI-NI Dīnī and DI-RE-DI-NA ʾaddīr-dīnā. One witness.

entries.meaning: dipas, a large handled vessel (Linear B di-pa)

cognates.Linear B: di-pa, dual di-pa-e, a neuter noun counted with *202VAS and *214VAS: KN K 740 (bronze), K 875, PY Ta 641 (DMic I s.v. di-pa)
cognates.Greek: δέπας, Homeric, borrowed from a Mediterranean language, as Mycenaean dipa confirms (Chantraine 1968, s.v. δέπας)
cognates.Arabic: dabbat 'vessel for oil' (semitic_roots no. 291; Lane 841), the rival

entries.note: PH 7a .1 DI-PA-JA, line-initial at the original left edge and whole; a short stroke stands apart after JA where the surface breaks (GORILA I 295, note .1). Linear B writes the vessel di-pa, given four handles, three or none on PY Ta 641 (qe-to-ro-we, ti-ri-jo-we, a-no-we): a vessel of some size rather than a cup (DMic I s.v. di-pa). Homeric δέπας keeps the word, borrowed from a Mediterranean language (Chantraine 1968, s.v. δέπας). DI-PA-JA writes the stem with -JA. Rival: Arabic dabbat 'vessel for oil' (semitic_roots no. 291). One attestation.

entries.meaning: personal name, Ruya + dādī 'my beloved'; Ruya alone on KN Wc 26

cognates.Ugaritic: ddy PN, syll. ta-di-e (DULAT 264); dd (I) 'loved one', 'the element /dādu/ in PNN' (DULAT 262); rwy PN, bn rwy, etym. unc. (DULAT 738)
cognates.Amorite: AQ-BU-DA-DI ʿAqbu-Dādī (Gelb 1980 no. 884)

entries.note: HT Wc 3008 face b, four signs whole with no divider, opposite WA · DI-NI (GORILA II 74): Ruya, the Ugaritic PN rwy (DULAT 738), with dādī 'my beloved' (TA-DI), TA writing d as in ta-di-e for ddy (DULAT 264). Ruya stands alone on the roundel KN Wc 26, face a, with NI-PI on face b (GORILA II 85). Ruya is |r-w-y| 'to be well watered', with Amorite ia-ar-wi-um and ru₂-ya |rôya / rūya| in an Egyptian place name (GlOS 2, 178). Rival: two names, RU-JA and TA-DI.

entries.meaning: my beloved, a name and name element

cognates.Ugaritic: dd (I) 'love', 'loved one' (DULAT 262); ddy PN, syll. ta-di-e, da-de₄-ya (DULAT 264)
cognates.Mari: di-di Didi PN, a carpenter (ARM 21 397; ARCHIBAB T16508)
cognates.Amorite: da-di-i, dādī 'my beloved', a Sutean (ARM 23 341; Buck 2018, 327)

entries.note: TA-DI within RU-JA-TA-DI Ruya-dādī (HT Wc 3008). The Ugaritic PN ddy, syll. ta-di-e and da-de₄-ya (DULAT 264); Hebrew Dōday (1 Chr 27:4) and Mari di-di, a carpenter (ARM 21 397). One witness. See DE-DI.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'my beloved'; rival the Hurrian name dḏy

cognates.Ugaritic: ddy PN, syll. DUMU da-de₄-ya, DUMU du-da-a-ya, da-dá-a, ta-di-e (DULAT 264); ¹da-di Dadi, ¹bin-da-de₄-ya Bin-Dadeya (Kinlaw 1967, 47, 37)
cognates.Amorite: da-di-i, dādī 'my beloved', a Sutean (Buck 2018, 327)

entries.note: HT 94b .2 DE-DI 1, both signs whole and undotted, in the KI-RO list of five one-unit entries, between PA-TA-NE and KE-KI-RU (GORILA I 153). The name Dedī 'my beloved', of √d-w-d: Ugaritic ddy, syll. da-de₄-ya, du-da-a-ya and ta-di-e (DULAT 264), and the Ugarit names Dadi and Bin-Dadeya (Kinlaw 1967, 47, 37); Amorite da-di-i dādī (Buck 2018, 327); Hebrew Dōday (1 Chr 27:4). Weak point: the comparanda write a or u in the first syllable. Rival: the Hurrian name dḏy, syll. ti-še-ia, te-še-ia (DULAT 264). One witness. See TA-DI.

entries.meaning: Utti (Hurrian personal name), stem utt-; rival the Anatolian name Utti

cognates.Hurrian: Uttija, Ú-ut-ti-[i]a, var. Ú-ti-ia, at Nuzi (NPN 169); the stem ut, utt marked H.? (NPN 273)
cognates.Alalakh: Utti, Ú-ti (AlT 414.7,17; Niedorf 2008, 309) and Ú-ut-ti (AlT 341.2,3; Niedorf 2008, 492)
cognates.Hittite: Utti (LAMAN 4804, after Laroche, NH 1456), the Anatolian name, the rival

entries.note: HT 10b .1 U-TI 1, whole; the stroke inside TI is a palimpsest trace (GORILA I 21). First entry, before DA-RE 2 and TA-RI-NA 15. Utti, as Alalakh Ú-ti (AlT 414.7,17; Niedorf 2008, 309) and Ú-ut-ti (AlT 341.2,3; Niedorf 2008, 492), and Nuzi Uttija, var. Ú-ti-ia (NPN 169), the geminate unwritten; NPN 273 marks the stem H.? Rival: the Anatolian name Utti (LAMAN 4804, after Laroche, NH 1456). One witness.

entries.meaning: the East, lit. 'the going-out (of the sun)', a name for eastern Crete; rival ṣīt 'issue, outlay'

cognates.Akkadian: ṣītum 'rise, rising (of sun), east; emergence, birth, origin; produce, product; lease; expenditure, loss' (Huehnergard 1997, glossary); NIM read ṣīti 'east' (ORACC CAMS/GKAB, P348764); Tâmtu ša ṣīt Šamši 'the Sea of the Rising Sun' (RGTC 7/3, s.v.)
cognates.Hebrew: môṣāʾ (מוֹצָא) 'going out; east', against maʿărāb 'west' (Ps 75:7); ṣēʾt (צֵאת) 'going out', kə-ṣēʾt ha-šemeš 'as the going-out of the sun' (Judg 5:31)

entries.note: ZA 26a .1 SI-TE · DI-DI-[, heading the tablet before *21F 13, intact and undotted (GORILA III 202–203); MIL Zb 3, a vessel, breaks through SI. √y-ṣ-ʾ: ṣīt, the sun's going-out, the East, as Akkadian ṣītum and Hebrew môṣāʾ (Ps 75:7). SI writes ṣ as in SI-JA-SE, and SI-TU sūt spells the closed syllable alike. The Kom el-Hetan list's damaged [sȝ]-i-tȝ-[y], tentatively Siteia (Cline & Stannish 2011, 10), compares; cf. Σηταία (DMic II 288; MGV I 243 s.u.) and Σήται (Ruijgh, Études 210 n. 559, apud DMic II 289 n. 5). Rival: ṣīt 'issue, outlay', Ugaritic ṣảt 'issue' (DULAT 764).

entries.meaning: (the men of) Unuḫu, a town named in a text from Ugarit (RS 17.251), location unknown

cognates.Akkadian (Ugarit): ᵘʳᵘÚ-nu-ḫi 'Unuḫu', LÚ ᵘʳᵘÚ-nu-ḫi 'man of Unuḫu' (RS 17.251 [PRU 4 236f.]:19f.; RGTC 12/2, 324)

entries.note: HT 26a .3–4 U-NU-*21F 5[, whole and undotted, the numeral broken after (GORILA I 47): the last surviving entry under the cup heading *406VAS+KE · *312-TE-TE, after TA-TI 21 and MI-KI-SE-NA 15; side b counts men (VIR) under the same heading. *21F writes the guttural: U-NU-*21F spells ᵘʳᵘÚ-nu-ḫi, the town of a witness, 'man of Unuḫu', in a legal text from Ugarit (RS 17.251 [PRU 4 236f.]:19f.; RGTC 12/2, 324, location unknown).

entries.meaning: Free-running Bull, a bull that roams free (personal name); rival Murr-darār 'Flowing Myrrh'

cognates.Akkadian: mīru A 'young bull', mīrtu 'cow' (CAD M/2 109); darāru A 'become free, move about freely, run off' (CAD D 109); andurārum 'freedom, manumission' (Huehnergard 1997, glossary)

entries.note: HT 117a MI-RU-TA-RA-RE 1, intact, in the roster under MA-KA-RI-TE · KI-RO, between U-DI-MI and TE-JA-RE Teyar, with MA-RU Maruʾ 'Fattened' on the same list. MI-RU mīru 'young bull' (CAD M/2 109), as MU-RU mūru; TA-RA-RE darār, Akkadian darāru 'become free, move about freely, run off' (CAD D 109), as DU-RA-RE durar, TA for d as in TA-DI dādī. Rival: Murr-darār 'Flowing Myrrh', Hebrew mor-dərôr (Exod 30:23; #K0153), MI-RU as MI+JA+RU murru.
entries.source: di Mino; CAD M/2; CAD D; Huehnergard 1997

entries.meaning: the Ashdodite, a man of Ashdod (gentilic)
entries.note: ARKH 2 .2–3 A-SI-DA-TO-I 12, intact, the largest share in the must list headed SI-DA-TE (GORILA III 7). ʾa-š(i)-da-dō-ī: SI-DA as syllabic Aš₂-da-di, TO the ō of Hebrew ʾAšdôd with T for d as in TA-DI dādī, -I the gentilic -ī as in KA-NA-NI-TI kanaʿanītī. Ugarit lists men by their town as PN aḏddy (KTU 4.635). The town is Tel Ashdod (RGTC 12/2, 3); Naʾaman 1997 places Ugaritic aḏdd at Enkomi on Cyprus (apud RGTC 12/2, 3).

entries.meaning: a town of the kingdom of Ugarit, on the Ugarit–Alalakh border (toponym); rival Aralu

cognates.Akkadian (Ugarit): ᵘʳᵘA-ra-yu (RS 34.131 [RSOu 7 Nr. 4]:40); ᵘʳᵘA-ra-[ya] (RS 20.143B [Ug. 5 Nr. 103]:4′) (RGTC 12/2, 30); DULAT 108 reads RS 34.131:40 URU a-ra-wa and restores a-r[a-yu at RS 20.143B:4

entries.note: HT 109 .4 A-RA-JU 123, after KU-RO 129, and HT 122b .3 A-RA-JU-U-DE-ZA 2, each at the broken left edge; GORILA brackets HT 109's KU-RO line alike, and both lines begin with A (GORILA I 176–177, 208–209). With JU's second value yu, the yod (Melena 2014, 16), A-RA-JU spells ᵘʳᵘA-ra-yu sign for sign: ʾArāyu, a town of the kingdom of Ugarit on the border between Ugarit and Alalaḫ (van Soldt 1994, apud RGTC 12/2, 30). Rival: Aralu under the primary value lu, nearest place Alalaḫ, ᵘʳᵘA-la-la-aḫ, one vowel off with the final ḫ unwritten (RGTC 12/2, 8). HT 122b, under JE-DI · *346 · VIR, writes it with U-DE-ZA, listed alone on HT 122a.

entries.meaning: She of Memphis: Egyptian woman's name Tꜣ-n.t-Mn-nfr

cognates.Egyptian: tꜣ-n.t-mn-nfr 'she of Memphis', a woman's name (PNM v6, personal_names_id 142613640; Ranke I, 360.14)
cognates.Hebrew: Mōp 'Memphis', miṣrayim təqabbəṣēm mōp təqabbərēm 'Egypt shall gather them, Memphis shall bury them' (Hos 9:6; HALOT 617)

entries.note: ZA 8 .3–4 TA-I-NU-MA-PA ∠, intact, after A-RI-NI-TA 'She-of-the-Lion' (GORILA III 165). The Egyptian woman's name tꜣ-n.t-mn-nfr 'she of Memphis' (Ranke I, 360.14; Ilin-Tomich 2025, s.v. tꜣ-n.t-mn-nfr), borne by three Memphite women from Amenhotep II to Sety I (Prosopographia Memphitica, persons 1509, 1828, 2490). TA-I writes the article with the j of its usual spelling, the pestle tj (ti n:t mn nfr; Ilin-Tomich 2025), tꜣy beside tꜣ (Allen 2014, §5.11), as DA-I writes ṭay- in DA-I-PI-TA on the same tablet. NU writes n(.t), MA-PA Memphis as Coptic ⲙⲛϥⲉ has it (Peust 1999, 254): the n a coda left unwritten, as in Linear B a-to-ro-qo anthrōqʷos (Ventris and Chadwick 1956, 45), the r lost as in Amarna na-ap-ḫur-ri-ia (Hess 1993, 116); Hebrew מֹף Mōp (Hos 9:6). Rival: a Minoan name. Weak point: the lost vowel between n and f is attested only in Coptic and Greek. One witness.
entries.source: di Mino; Ilin-Tomich 2025 (PNM v6); Prosopographia Memphitica; Allen 2014; Peust 1999; Ventris and Chadwick 1956; Hess 1993

entries.meaning: Hathor (Egyptian goddess)

cognates.Egyptian: Ḥw.t-Ḥr.w 'Hathor' (AED lemma 99960; Wb 3, 5.11)

entries.note: ZA 8 .1 KI-RA · A-TA-RE · NI ½, intact, heading the fig list (GORILA III 165). Egyptian Ḥw.t-Ḥr.w Hathor, Lady of the Sycomore, the fig tree, at the head of a fig list: nb.t-nh.t (AED lemma 450446; Wb 2, 282.14; LGG IV, 79), and Lady of the Southern Sycomore, nb.t-nh.t-rs.jt (AED lemma 855250), in the Old Kingdom title ḥm.t-nṯr Ḥw.t-Ḥr.w nb.t Nh.t rs.jt (Jones, Titles OK, no. 2025, apud AED lemma 853009). A writes the dropped ḥ, TA-RE t-ḥr. One witness.

entries.meaning: the cella of Ṣiduq, the Just One (heading an aromatic list)

cognates.Amorite: ṣaduq 'just, right, just case; DN': za-du-kum, a-bi-ṣa-du-uq (GlOS 2, 215); ṣidq 'justice, legitimacy; DN' (GlOS 2, 214); zi-id-ki-e-pa Ṣidqī-yapaʿ, Qaṭna (Buck 2018, 352)
cognates.Ugaritic: ṣdq (B) 'lawful, righteous; DN' (GlOS 2, 215); Ṣidqanu (Kinlaw 1967, 103); kbm 'a cult installation', š kbmh 'a ram in the k.' (KTU 1.106:15), set beside Akk. kummu (DULAT 423)
cognates.Phoenician: Sadykos, father of the eight Kabeiroi (Damascius, in Brown 1995, 36)
cognates.Akkadian: kummu A 'cella, private room (of a temple or palace)', É.NUN agrun = kummu (CAD K 533)

entries.note: HT 110a .1 SI-DU-*34-KU-MI, all five signs whole and undotted, heading the tablet before CYP+E 20, then KU-PA 1, KU-RO 100[, NI 15[ (GORILA I 178–179). Ṣiduqi-kummi 'the cella of Ṣiduq': DU writes the u of Amorite ṣaduq and Damascius' Sadykos, SI the i of Ṣidqiyyāhû and Arabic ṣiddīq; kummu 'cella' (CAD K 533). Weak point: *34 = qi is a proposed value. Rival: a sentence name on ṣaduq. One attestation.
